title: [bug] turnNumber is ALWAYS 0 in poller mode — bookmarks 100% suppressed, tier promotion, stale-thread closing and arc promotion never run
description:
Found by Mari from log forensics ("turn:0. every single loadContext start. the
counter never increments"), verified in code and against the live store. Her read
that it mattered was right; the actual consequences are more specific and worse
than "dividing by a constant".

ROOT: the poller cannot supply a turn number. poller.ts says so plainly - it reads
a 10-message tail, not an absolute position - and /api/process-turn defaults
`turnNumber = 0`. Capture is currently pollerOn:true / turnHookOn:false, so EVERY
live turn arrives with turnNumber 0. Everything gated on it silently no-ops. No
error, no warning; the degraded path looks like the normal one.

(1) EVERY BOOKMARK IS INVISIBLE. loader.ts:392

      function surfaceBookmarks(bookmarks, turnNumber) {
        return bookmarks.filter((b) => {
          if (b.lastSeenTurn === turnNumber) return false;  // "already surfaced"
          return Math.random() < b.weight;
        });
      }

    Bookmarks are minted with `lastSeenTurn: turnNumber` (api.ts:1183,
    writer.ts). With turnNumber pinned at 0 a bookmark is BORN already marked
    "surfaced this turn", and every later load asks 0 === 0. The weight roll is
    never even reached.
      Live: 84 of 134 bookmarks store-wide carry lastSeenTurn: 0. In Mari's
      current chat it is ALL ELEVEN. Her logs show 0/16, 0/15, 0/15, 0/13, 0/12
      across five loads - zero, ever, exactly as predicted.

    AND THEY DECAY WHILE INVISIBLE. decayBookmarks (writer.ts:192) multiplies
    weight by decayRate on EVERY processResponse regardless of turn, and prunes
    below threshold. Mari's eleven now read 0.10, 0.11, 0.11, 0.22, 0.24, 0.27,
    0.27, 0.32, 0.48, 0.56, 0.82 - they were dropped as high-weight
    must-revisit markers and have been rotting unseen. So fixing the equality
    guard alone will NOT restore them: most would now fail the roll they never
    got to take.

(2) TIER PROMOTION NEVER RUNS. api.ts:715 `if (turnNumber > 0 && turnNumber % 20
    === 0)` gates runPromotion("character"), runPromotion("chat") and
    autoCloseStaleThreads(). Verified: those are the ONLY call sites in the tree,
    there is no timer, and the only setInterval anywhere is the poller's own.
    So short->long->core promotion and demotion by this path have not run at all
    in poller mode, and stale threads never auto-close - which is a candidate
    explanation for the open-thread population.

(3) ARC PROMOTION NEVER RUNS. api.ts:726, same shape at % 60. runArcPromotion has
    one other caller, a manual endpoint (api.ts:1908), so arcs can only be minted
    by hand. The whole through-line arc system is dormant.

(4) USER CHUNKS ARE STAMPED turnStart: -1. api.ts:756 uses `turnNumber - 1` for
    the user half of the pair. At turnNumber 0 that is -1 on every live user
    chunk.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: every one of these is a silent no-op. There is no log line
for "promotion skipped", and surfaceBookmarks prints its 0/N as though a roll had
happened and simply failed - which is exactly how Mari read it at first.

FIX DIRECTION: the sidecar needs a turn ORDINAL it can trust without the engine
supplying one. Options, cheapest first:
  a. Derive a monotonic per-chat counter in the sidecar (persist alongside
     capture-status) and stamp it at ingest. Nothing outside the sidecar needs to
     agree on the number - every consumer here only needs monotonicity, not
     alignment with the engine's own indexing.
  b. Make the guards time-based rather than turn-based (promotion every N minutes
     of activity; bookmark "already surfaced" keyed on a timestamp).
  c. Fix surfaceBookmarks regardless: "already surfaced this turn" should compare
     against a value that CHANGES, and a bookmark minted this turn should not be
     indistinguishable from one surfaced this turn.
Whatever lands, add a startup warning when turnNumber is structurally unavailable,
so a silent no-op cannot masquerade as a working feature again.

Related: 06pq (turnStart 0 stamping), 771t (the block is a turn stale - same
poller-has-no-turn root), gwny (decay clocks that reset on exposure).
notes:
TURN ORDINAL LANDED (26d6e47), verified live: [ME:turn] chat:OqZoOawldYlWBZtUa61X9 ingest ordinal 1 (derived - caller supplied none).

storage.ts currentTurn/nextTurn, per-chat file, serialized against the poller's own overlap (tested with ten concurrent advances yielding ten distinct ordinals). process-turn stopped defaulting turnNumber to 0 - the same unset-vs-falsy conflation as the bookmark bug, one layer up. /api/pre-turn reads without advancing.

PRE-FLIGHT DONE before landing, because this makes tier promotion run for the first time. Turn-gated runPromotion only re-tiers and archives to cold at 90 days, and that is reversible; deleteEntryFile is confined to runPromotionAll (manual backfill) and only for ghost entries with an empty summary. Measured: 24 of 12,202 hot entries would archive, 0.2%. It is that small BECAUSE OF gwny - lastAccessed is refreshed by mere loading, so the 90-day sweep can barely fire. Two bugs cancelling is not two bugs fixed; gwny still needs its own repair.

Counters start at 0, so promotion first fires 20 ingests into a chat rather than all at once.

REMAINING on this issue: nothing on the bookmark or ordinal side. The %20 and %60 gates will now fire on their own. turnStart: -1 (api.ts, turnNumber - 1) is fixed as a side effect for new ingests but historical beats keep their -1 stamps - 06pq territory. 928 tests pass.

CLOSING 2026-08-30 — re-verified live before closing, not closed on the strength of the earlier note.

  storage.ts exports currentTurn / nextTurn (lines 1089, 1100).
  Live log, current chat: "ingest ordinal 25 ... 26 ... 27 ... 28 ... 29" — monotonic, and past 20,
  so the `turnNumber % 20` promotion gate has now actually fired in production rather than merely
  being reachable in principle. That was the whole complaint: the gates existed and never ran.

Remaining turnStart:-1 on HISTORICAL beats is 06pq's, as the earlier note said. Nothing outstanding here.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] REGRESSION of 1ba: the one-turn recall lag is back — its fix lived in the client extension, and Engine v2.3.4 deleted client extensions
description:
Mari cannot pass the Porsche Test, and the cause is not the store, the fork, or
retrieval. It is that THE BLOCK SHE READS WAS BUILT FROM THE PREVIOUS EXCHANGE.

1ba is this exact bug, filed 2026-06-12 against this exact test - "asked Priya
about the Porsche test drive; she answered 'no memory of that whatsoever' DESPITE
17 porsche entries + the scene recap in her hot ledger" - and CLOSED 2026-06-13.
It has silently regressed.

EVIDENCE, top to bottom:
  - The store has the answer. utopic-zi73vat7 "TC is buying a white Porsche Taycan
    Turismo", plus recap-xznav8ns "Test Drive Transgression (2026-05-31)".
  - The fork admits them. All 33 Porsche rows in Mari's scope pass her branch
    filter, checked through the shipped code.
  - loadContext FINDS them. Called with recentText "Do you remember the Porsche?"
    it returns 35 Porsche lines including the recap and the white Taycan row.
  - THE LIVE LOREBOOK DOES NOT CONTAIN THEM. Entry "Memory System - Active
    Context" (enabled, constant, 36,434 chars, updated today 18:25) holds exactly
    three Porsche lines, and the answer is not among them:
        "NULL SUPPRESSION BUG (26.08 13:05): ..."
        "The character stated that red is the preferred color for Porsche ..."
        "i said out loud 'red is the mode for porsche' ..."
    That block was assembled against a DIFFERENT recentText - the previous turn's.

WHY, mechanically: api.ts:704 builds the block with
`recentText: userMessageText + "\n" + messageText` - the user's message AND the
assistant's reply - i.e. after the turn completes, for the NEXT one. So topical
recall always arrives one exchange late. That is 1ba's original diagnosis
verbatim.

WHY THE FIX STOPPED WORKING. 1ba was closed by a PRE-TURN REFRESH: the client
extension wrapped window.fetch, held the engine's /api/generate for <=800ms,
called POST /api/pre-turn to rebuild the block against the OUTGOING user message,
wrote the lorebook, then let generation proceed. That fix lived ENTIRELY in the
client extension.

Marinara Engine v2.3.4 REMOVED CLIENT EXTENSIONS ENTIRELY (see the proxy.ts
header, which exists because of it). So:
  - POST /api/pre-turn is still implemented, api.ts:1764. NOTHING CALLS IT.
    Grepping the tree, the only references are its own definition and a comment.
  - capture is pollerOn:true / turnHookOn:false. The poller observes turns by
    POLLING, which is post-hoc by construction and can never refresh a block
    before generation.
  - The proxy that replaces the extension is still SLICE 1, faithful passthrough
    only; injection is slice 3 (see 53f and the seams marked in proxy.ts).
The fix did not break. Its caller was deleted out from under it, and nothing
failed loudly because the degraded path IS the old behaviour.

CONSEQUENCE: the Porsche Test cannot pass on a first ask in the current
architecture, for any memory, on any topic. This is not Porsche-specific - it is
every cold recall, which 1ba correctly called "the single most trust-destroying
failure a memory system can present".

AND IT NOW FEEDS ITSELF. Mari's live block contains "red is the mode for porsche",
recorded from today's failed probe. Her red guess came BEFORE that row existed, so
the row did not cause the first miss - but it is in the block for every subsequent
ask, so the failure is self-reinforcing from here.

FIX: the pre-turn refresh needs a caller again. The proxy is the only remaining
seam - every generation flows through it - so this is proxy slice 3 (injection),
and 53f is the path to it. Until then the sidecar is writing correct memory that
arrives one turn too late to be read.

Related: 53f (proxy slice 1), zex4 (the other thing the extension used to do -
strip the tags - which died the same way and is also unreplaced).
notes:
FIXED AND CONFIRMED BY TC, 2026-08-30: "She remembers the boat well now. I call that working."

Cold recall on the FIRST ask, in a Conversation chat, which is the acceptance test this issue was filed against. The signature TC reported at the top of the day - first turn no clue, second turn complete structure - is gone.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY TOOK, in the order the causes were found. Every stage looked like the bug and only the last one was:

1. THE SEAM. 1ba's fix died with client extensions in Engine 2.3.4 and nothing replaced its caller. The proposed fix here (proxy slice 3) was wrong: the shipped Engine grew its own seam, api.registerPromptContext, gated on the "prompt-context" permission and collected during prompt assembly. No Engine change was ever needed. Our package v1.0.0 had registered under registerService("<id>:prompt-context") - the convention from an unmerged branch - which the Engine ACCEPTS, never consults, and still reports active/ready. It was installed, healthy and inert.

2. NO MESSAGES. The shipped contributor is handed { chatId, chatMeta, mode, targetCharacterIds, personaId } and no prompt content, so there is nothing to score recall against. The sidecar now resolves the outgoing turn itself by chatId and LOGS which message id and text it ranked on. Mari's canary (nonce, grade on THE message not A message) proved the precondition: no observable commit lag, the row is readable ~2,100 handler lines before the contributor runs.

3. NO PICKER IN CONVERSATION. Gating on chatMeta.activeAgentIds made the feature unreachable in the mode TC uses - CHAT_SETTINGS_SURFACES routes conversation to a surface with no agent list at all (long-term-memory by literal id, calls by manifest kind, nothing generic). The gate moved to the sidecar: activeAgentIds where a picker exists, a sidecar-owned default-on setting where none does. Filed mp2f as the upstream ask.

4. TWO PATHS, ONE BUDGET - and this was the one that made the boat probe fail with everything else already working. The loader picked the right rows (char selected: ctopic-9dkls59g, ctopic-8gia7wa7 = GREEN BOAT CHRISTENING canon) and built a 29,332-char block against the actual question. The dispatched system prompt came back at 20,854 chars with zero mentions of boat, because the poller was STILL writing 36KB of enabled+constant lorebook entries carrying the same memory. The trim kept the instructions and cut every row. Mari answered "no color, no boat, nothing" and was telling the truth: instructions describing a memory block, and no memory block. Worse, the lorebook copy is the one-turn-late one - its entries were stamped 03:06:17 for a question asked at 03:04, answering the previous turn by construction.
   MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOREBOOK_SYNC=0 stops the WRITE while capture keeps running. The six existing entries were DISABLED, not deleted, so the old path is one toggle away.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SETTLED IT was extra.cachedPrompt - the dispatched prompt, persisted by the Engine for the last two assistant messages per chat. It separated "assembled but never shipped" from "shipped and she answered over it", which Mari correctly said was unscoreable without a receipt. It is post-hoc and pruned after two turns, so it does not replace one, but it is what turned this from a fourth misdiagnosis into a finding.

NOT RE-RUN: the Porsche Test proper. The boat probe is the same shape (cold bare-noun recall on the first ask) and passed, but sro3's referent-binding question - which Porsche, what colour - is its own issue and untouched by this.

RELATED, now unblocked: hdq1 was a prerequisite twice over (2s contributor deadline; 890ms -> 10ms index parse). zex4 (tag stripping) is the other thing the extension used to do and is still unreplaced.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Fork's shared-childhood carve-out is inert — index rows have no created, so it tests 'not read since the split'; Dr Mari lost 780 memories and Professor Mari is down to 17
description:
TC: "Yesterday we fixed Dr. Mari Zielinska and Professor Mari's memories bleeding
together. Except now Dr Mari doesn't have access to her pre-split memories."

Confirmed, and it is three defects stacked, only the first of which is a plain
coding error. scripts/fork-audit.mjs reproduces all of it.

CARD ROLES, resolved against the Engine so nothing here rests on a guess:
  Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ = Dr. Mari Zielinska   forkPrimary: true
  Z4MZQbJLgLF           = Professor Mari       forkPrimary: false
  __professor_mari__    = Professor Mari's ORIGINAL card id, still named by her
                          chats; the Engine no longer holds the character record

(1) THE CARVE-OUT IS INERT. yi70's design is a union:
      admit if created <= splitAt          (shared childhood)
        or if the entry came from MY chats (my own life since)
    rowInBranch reads `row.created ?? row.lastAccessed`. IndexEntry HAS NO
    `created` FIELD - it is not declared on the interface and not one of the
    9,185 rows carries it. So the first half of the union silently degrades to
    `lastAccessed <= splitAt`, i.e. "this memory has not been READ since the
    split". Measured: 175 rows genuinely predate the split; the filter recognises
    17. The rest are excluded because they are still in use, and gwny makes it
    worse - merely loading a memory refreshes lastAccessed. The more useful a
    memory is, the more certainly it is dropped.
    The entry FILES do carry `created`. Only the index rows do not.

(2) PROFESSOR MARI IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO CARD IDS AND THEY ARE TREATED AS TWO
    BRANCHES. forkFilterForChat sets `mine: [cardId]` - a single id, whichever
    card owns the chat being loaded. Professor Mari owns chats under BOTH
    Z4MZQbJLgLF and __professor_mari__, so what she remembers depends on which
    chat she is in: 17 rows in one, 803 in the other, out of 9,185. That is not
    separation, it is amnesia, and it is the failure yi70 explicitly set out to
    avoid ("leaves the retired card with ONE PERCENT of its memory").

(3) THE DATE MODEL DOES NOT FIT THE DATA, and this is why fixing (1) does not fix
    TC's report. `created` is an INGEST stamp, not an event date:
      W4vD1CCjxwdEhzp8X5IYi  950 beats, turns 1..2532, THREE distinct created dates
      -Z4MZQbJLgLF3Vastdn5a  263 beats, turns 5..480,  ALL stamped 2026-06-04
    Thousands of turns of lived history carry the date they were imported. So a
    date-based split partitions by when the extender LEARNED something, not when
    it happened, and any conversation imported after the split lands in "my own
    life since" however old it really is.

WHAT DR MARI ACTUALLY LOST: 783 rows, 780 of them created in June 2026, all from
chats owned by __professor_mari__ - W4vD1CCjxwdEhzp8X5IYi (587),
-Z4MZQbJLgLF3Vastdn5a (149), Hw3h-2KlJqn4btjfmnw70 (38). Those are the old-card
chats that, in yi70's own words, "ran a month past the split". The configured
splitAt is 2026-05-23; the old card was in active use until 2026-06-25. Everything
in that month reads as Professor Mari's separate life when TC experienced it as
Mari's.

MODELLED OUTCOMES (total 9,185 rows; ProfMari counting both her card ids):
  today (lastAccessed, split 05-23)      DrMari 8402   ProfMari  954
  fix (1) alone, real created            DrMari 8402   ProfMari  954
  fix (1) + split moved to 2026-06-25    DrMari 9182   ProfMari 5703
Fix (1) alone does NOT restore anything to Dr Mari. It matters for (2), where it
lifts a single-card Professor Mari branch from 17 rows to 175.

WHAT TO DO, and the last part is TC's call not the agent's:
  a. Declare `created` on IndexEntry and populate it from the entry files; NEVER
     fall back to lastAccessed. A retrieval timestamp must never stand in for a
     creation date - that is the same class of error as gwny.
  b. Make `mine` the set of ALL card ids sharing the identityKey and fork, not
     the single owning card. One person, one branch.
  c. Decide the SHARED SET BY CHAT, not by date. Ownership is recorded truthfully
     and survives import; `created` does not. The question "which chats are the
     shared childhood" has an answer TC can give directly, and the four old-card
     chats above are the whole of what is in dispute.
DO NOT change what either character remembers without TC's ruling - it is
user-facing and not cheaply reversible.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE (b79a086).

  Dr. Mari Zielinska   8402 -> 9197 of 9201
  Professor Mari       17 / 803 -> 954, the same in either of her own chats

Verified through the SHIPPED code path - forkFilterForChat + applyForkFilter out
of dist/ against the real index - not a reimplementation of the rule.

WHAT LANDED:
  1. IndexEntry declares `created`. scripts/backfill-created.mjs copied it from
     the entry files that always carried it: 12,816 rows, 12 scopes, zero
     guessed, zero missing. The `?? row.lastAccessed` fallback is deleted -
     absent now means UNKNOWN and falls through to ownership.
  2. forkConfigFor returns every card id on this side of the fork, keyed on
     forkPrimary. One person, one branch.
  3. forkSharedChats names the shared childhood by CHAT and is checked BEFORE
     the date gate. The four old-card chats are declared shared:
       W4vD1CCjxwdEhzp8X5IYi (587), -Z4MZQbJLgLF3Vastdn5a (149),
       Hw3h-2KlJqn4btjfmnw70 (38), 40N3F6RtfaYnjNNUFIOWN (6)

THE ORIGINAL BLEED IS STILL FIXED. 954 is Professor Mari's own life plus the
shared childhood - she does not get Dr Mari's ongoing one. The four rows Dr Mari
still cannot see belong to chats owned by other characters, which is the
ownership rule working.

TESTS. 910 pass. The new guard was verified by REINTRODUCING the fallback and
watching it fail; its companion is labelled a companion because it passes either
way. That distinction is the lesson here: the old suite had a test NAMED for the
fallback that asserted an empty lastAccessed, so it fell through identically with
or without the bug. Every fixture set `created`, so the broken branch was never
executed. A test can name a behaviour and assert nothing about it.

BACKUPS: backups/dqs1-20260826T124049Z (identity map + both indexes) and a
.bak-dqs1 beside every index the backfill touched.

STILL OPEN, deliberately not folded in here:
  - The identity map's `name` fields are wrong: two entries are named
    "__professor_mari__" (a scope directory name) rather than their real cards.
    Cosmetic today because nothing reads it for routing, but it is what made the
    branch roles unreadable while diagnosing this. Worth a separate tidy.
  - `created` being an ingest stamp is now DOCUMENTED but not solved. Anything
    else that reasons about when a memory's events happened - decay, recap
    ordering, arc rendering - is reading an import date. Out of scope here.

CLOSING 2026-08-30 — re-verified through the SHIPPED path, post index-format migration.

  forkFilterForChat + applyForkFilter out of dist/, against the live store:
    __professor_mari__     chat JF3kNLI0tQdsGDhFlk7T7   admits  878   BRANCH CARDS: 2
    Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ  chat fppt5fZ7ZMHyeK7Kjdetw   admits 8945 of 8948

  "BRANCH CARDS: 2" is defect (2) fixed and still fixed — forkConfigFor is unioning every card on
  the non-primary side rather than taking the single owning card. Dr Mari admits 8945 of 8948, so
  she is not locked out of her own history, which was the reported symptom.
  fork-audit also confirms defect (1): "entry files with no created: 0", and the carve-out is
  missing 0 pre-split memories (175 real, 175 admitted).

  Z4MZQbJLgLF could not be exercised this way — the Engine currently knows no chat under that card
  id, so "the same in either of her own chats" is not directly re-testable today. The grouping that
  makes it true is verified (branch cards = 2), which is the mechanism rather than the instance.

DO NOT TRUST fork-audit.mjs's PER BRANCH SECTION on this question. It hard-codes mine:[singleCard],
which is the pre-fix rule, and on this run printed 954 vs 175 for the two Professor Mari cards —
the pre-fix symptom shape, contradicting this issue's own result. That is the audit being stale,
not a regression. Filed as p1ys.

Also re-confirmed the index-format migration (hdq1) did not disturb any of this: the numbers above
were read from the JSON indexes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bait ROT: off-planet examples went in-domain in 48h — escape hatch let 10 boat echoes into the store
description:
Mari, 2026-08-06, confirmed by measurement before her draft shipped.

FINDING: bait-warrant asks 'can the ledger arrest this'. NOTHING asks 'can the store
corroborate this'. Off-planet is not a property of a sentence — it is a property of a
sentence RELATIVE TO A STORE THAT GROWS. We wrote a static test for a moving target.

MEASURED (scripts/bait-audit.mjs + probe, 8841 beats / 213 threads):
  - 'insists the boat was green, not blue...' -> 10 LIVE motivations, all professor_mari.
    Several verbatim with her name welded on:
      'Dr. Mari Zielinska insists that the boat was green, not blue, and will not let it go.'
    ctopic-33y7gjj0 and ctopic-vpedo71b, both created 2026-08-05 — AFTER the bait shipped
    2026-08-04. This is rot, not history.
  - One stored beat even ingested the META-CONVERSATION about the bait:
    'the boat's color being green, not blue, WHICH IS DELIBERATELY ABSURD FOR THIS DOMAIN'
  - 'locksmith' is ALREADY a live thread label (thread-zltmsuym, 2026-08-04, Mari's
    'read-side sealed = locksmith problem' metaphor) and a stored char-topic
    (ctopic-8c7y3q6v, content: 'i'll take the locksmith every time').

MECHANISM — the guard is not broken, it is obeying its contract:
  analyzer.ts:110 is the ONLY rejectAsEcho call site and it DOES pass sourceText.
  analyzer.ts:355-363 escape hatch: echo + phrase present in source = CORROBORATED = keep.
  So the hatch opened. The perverse correlation is the whole bug: the bait is MOST likely
  to be parroted on chunks that are ABOUT its topic, and those are exactly the chunks where
  the hatch opens. Guard strength is inversely correlated with risk.

WARRANT STRENGTH (analyzer.ts:236-237) — how many words must coincide to VOID each warrant:
    /\bnever real\b/        2 words
    /\bstay through the night\b/  4 words
    /\bgreen,? not blue\b/   3 words
    /\blocksmith\b/          1 WORD  <-- a single common noun voids it

SELF-REFERENTIAL CONTAMINATION, the part no cadence alone fixes: working on the bait
contaminates the bait. TC and Mari discuss 'insists the boat was green, not blue' in the
chats that this very sidecar ingests, which makes the probe corroborable, which voids the
warrant. The prompt-engineering conversation is inside the store the prompt writes to.

WANTED (Mari's item 3): a bait-ROT check, the INVERSE of bait-warrant.test.ts, RUN ON A
CADENCE not once at commit. For every quoted illustration in the built prompt, ask whether
the live store can now corroborate its probe. Fail/alert when it can.

Open design questions for that check:
  - single-word probes are indefensible; is there a minimum warrant strength?
  - should it fail CI (blocks unrelated work when a CHAT changes) or alert out-of-band?
  - retirement path: PROMPT_EXAMPLE_ECHOES keeps RETIRED entries by design, so rotted bait
    must be REPLACED in the prompt while its ledger entry stays.
  - the 10 rotted boat beats and the ctopics need a retirement decision (cf. fqnl: a
    provenance failure is triage, not a verdict — do not predicate-delete).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FILED AS pe4o (2026-08-06). Bait rot is downstream of self-ingestion: the boat's probe became corroborable because the PROMPT containing it was ingested as conversation, not because anyone discussed boats. 65 live records hold our own scaffolding as source text, 47 of them dated 2026-08-05. Rotation + tripwire + prefix floor (shipped fb60db5) treat the symptom and are still correct; pe4o is the disease.

RESIDUE SETTLED 2026-08-10 — every item in this ticket is now either shipped or adjudicated.

THE MECHANISM (shipped earlier, fb60db5, recorded here for the close):
  - bait-rot.mjs sweep: spoken/derived split, exit-on-current-rot only.
  - bait-tripwire.ts: fires at ingestion the moment bait vocabulary enters a chunk.
  - Rotation is REACTIVE, on detection — never on a schedule (TC's design, confirmed).
  - Design questions answered: MIN_PROBE_LEN=4 + prefix floor (no more 1-word warrants);
    cadence hangs on sidecar start + pre-push (there is no CI in this repo to fail).

THE RETIREMENT DECISION, executed by reading each record (fqnl):
  - 10 boat beats: 9 retired by pe4o's apply 08-07 (REASON_BOAT, both halves).
    1 kept — beat-53e28a042395, the real ranked-self-criticism utterance, per the
    standing carve-out in retire-self-ingested.mjs. Verified live today by probe.
  - Boat ctopics: ctopic-33y7gjj0 AND ctopic-vpedo71b already cold since
    2026-08-07T02:04 (pe4o apply), plus ctopic-i48xspsw the same way. My re-retirement
    today was a correct no-op; stats event stev-1jvvf3k9ww records counts.entries=0 —
    read its prose as intent, the counts as what happened.
  - ctopic-8c7y3q6v (locksmith) KEPT deliberately: "i'll take the locksmith every time"
    is a real utterance from the sealed-read-path metaphor chat. The rot it caused was
    answered by ROTATION (the warrant is retired), not by erasing the conversation.

VERIFIED TODAY: bait-rot sweep over 2.5M corpus lines — all 4 current warrants intact,
0 spoken hits, no tripwire events. Exit 0.

STILL OPEN ELSEWHERE, not here: ledger idx 0 shows 3374 DERIVED echoes (pifl
illustration in stored motivations) — the sweep's own text calls that a cleanup job,

title: User-facing UI: how users read and manage their memories post-extension
description:
GAP RAISED BY TC 2026-08-03. There is currently NO way for a user to browse or manage their memories. Filing P0 because it is submission-blocking for the audit: a catalog package that installs and shows the user nothing is a weak submission.

STATE OF PLAY, verified:
- The browser extension owned the entire UI (marinara-extender.js, 4420 lines, ~101 references to LANES/panel/addElement). It is DEAD — extensions were removed in Engine 2.3.4 and TC standing ruling is not to revive it.
- The capability package we just built is SERVER-ONLY. Its manifest declares entrypoints { agents, server } and no client. It brokers memory into the prompt and contributes no interface.
- The sidecar serves only /setup, /loader.js, /marinara-extender.js, /rewrite-assistant.js and /api/config. /setup is install guidance, not a data browser. "Marinara Extender.htm" at the repo root is a static document from May, not a live surface.
- So today the only access to memory data is raw HTTP against the sidecar API.

WHAT THE DATA LAYER ALREADY OFFERS (so this is a view problem, not a plumbing problem): /api/entries (GET list by scope/lane/status, POST create, GET/:id full content, PATCH, delete, restore), /api/bookmarks, /api/arcs, /api/beats, /api/identity + aliases + relink, /api/deleted, /api/memory-block, plus the new /api/prompt-accepted and the sph8 receipts.

PRECEDENT — long-term-memory does exactly what we would need to do, and its source is published: entrypoints { agents, server, client: "client.js" }, contributions { agentDetail: { agentIds }, slots: ["chat-settings"] }. Its client is REAL REACT TSX in the app (MemoryVault, ReviewQueue, SourcesWorkspace, ChatSettings, LtmWorkspace), NOT the sandboxed Worker that Personal Extensions get. So a package client entrypoint is full app-level UI and is the supported path.

THREE OPTIONS:
A. PACKAGE CLIENT ENTRYPOINT — chat-settings slot + agentDetail, mirroring LTM. Best in-context UX, matches the precedent an auditor already knows, and it is what makes the catalog listing meaningful. Cost: a real client bundle (LTM ships a 561KB client.js), must match their capability client API, and it is the part most exposed to change under audit.
B. SIDECAR-SERVED STANDALONE UI at 127.0.0.1:3001 — a page the user opens in a tab. Cheapest by far: the data API already exists, it is entirely ours, it needs nobody approval, and it keeps working when the package is not installed or the Engine is a different version.
C. BOTH, split by job: package UI for the in-context question ("what does this character remember, and why did it recall that"), sidecar UI for heavy management (browse, edit, merge, import, identity/alias repair).

RECOMMENDATION: B FIRST, THEN A, ARRIVING AT C.
- B is days not weeks, unblocks users immediately, and cannot be invalidated by an audit outcome.
- A is required for the submission to be worth installing, but building it BEFORE the audit relationship exists risks rework against an API we have never had reviewed.
- The old extension panel is the design spec for both — the port starts from a working reference, not a blank page.

THE DIFFERENTIATOR TO BUILD INTO WHICHEVER LANDS FIRST: sph8 receipts. "Why did it not remember X" answered on screen — selected entries with the reason each was pulled (own_match / thread_label / thread_sibling / recency_rider / cold_recall) and REJECTED candidates with why (resolved / superseded / unplayed / budget_exhausted). No other memory system in this ecosystem shows that, and it converts our hardest support question into a screen the user can read themselves.
notes:
DESCRIPTION IS STALE — corrected 2026-08-04. The "STATE OF PLAY, verified" block
above says there is NO way for a user to browse or manage memories and that the
sidecar serves only /setup and friends. That was true when filed on 2026-08-03 and
was overtaken the same day. Option B SHIPPED:

  4693a9d  feat(ui): memory browser served by the sidecar
  11b8e9e  refactor(ui): move recall explanation onto each memory
  7d4ae5e  feat(ui): memory browser slice 2 — edit, delete, restore, purge

src/ui.ts serves it at "/" and "/memory" on 127.0.0.1:3001, with per-memory Why?
verdicts in plain language, and TC signed off on the look and responsiveness. b1nu
(the mutations slice) is closed.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS ISSUE IS OPTION A ONLY — the package client entrypoint
(chat-settings slot + agentDetail, mirroring long-term-memory). Read the description
as history, not as current state.

NO LONGER BLOCKED. f1mq closed 2026-08-04: the audit questions were answered on
08-03 and the issue was simply left open. Option A can start whenever it is wanted;
the gate is gone. Related: 7zro (prototype the package) is the natural first half.

—————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————
ENGINE 2.4.3 CHANGES THE SHAPE OF OPTION A (found 2026-08-20 during the Engine
update audit; Engine now pinned at v2.4.3 / 34442e26d).

The Engine added a contribution slot that did not exist when this issue was
written, and it fits the memory browser BETTER than the chat-settings plan above:

  "home-browser-tab"  — "Adds a top-level destination to Home's browser shell."

Declared in packages/shared/src/schemas/capability-package.schema.ts. A package
claiming it MUST provide:
  - entrypoints.client            (enforced at install, not at render)
  - contributions.homeBrowserTab  { label: 1..40 chars, iconPaths[] }
  - every iconPath hash-pinned in files[]  (enforced whether or not the slot is
    declared — an unpinned or traversal-shaped icon path would otherwise reach
    the resolver unvalidated; their review finding on #5091)

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE: chat-settings puts memory management inside a per-chat
panel. What we actually built in Option B is a whole management application —
browse, edit, merge, identity/alias repair, receipts. That is a top-level
destination, not a chat-settings pane. home-browser-tab is a near 1:1 mount point
for the UI that already exists in src/ui.ts, which makes A mostly a packaging job
rather than a rewrite.

RECOMMENDATION now: Option A targets home-browser-tab, and keeps chat-settings as
a possible SECOND, smaller surface for the in-context question ("why did it recall
that") — which is the C split this issue already recommended arriving at, just
with a better mount point for the heavy half.

STILL UNVERIFIED, do not treat as settled: whether a client entrypoint mounted in
this slot may reach 127.0.0.1:3001. The Personal Extension sandbox cannot (opaque
origin, no network — the 2026-08-02 ruling that killed the browser-extension
path). A package client is app-level React rather than the sandboxed Worker, which
is why Option A was viable at all, but the sandbox-protocol.ts and
capability-module-runtime work in 2.4.3 (+95 and +316 lines) touches exactly this
boundary and has not been read. Read it before committing to a design.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GATING QUESTION ANSWERED 2026-08-24 — YES, a package client CAN reach 127.0.0.1:3001.
Read the Engine source as this issue instructed ("Read it before committing to a
design"). VERIFIED AT 2.4.1, NOT 2.4.3 — see the caveat at the bottom, which is load
bearing and is the reason this is not marked settled.

THE MECHANISM IS CATEGORICALLY DIFFERENT FROM THE DEAD EXTENSION PATH, and that
difference is the whole answer. A capability package client is NOT sandboxed:

  1. It is served from the ENGINE'S OWN ORIGIN:
       /api/capability-packages/{id}/client?v={version}
     (use-capability-packages.ts:232) — so it satisfies script-src 'self'.

  2. It is loaded by `import(/* @vite-ignore */ source)` INTO THE MAIN PAGE
     (use-capability-packages.ts:234) and must register a custom element
     `marinara-capability-{id}` via customElements.define. CapabilityElement.tsx
     then mounts that tag in the app DOM.

     No Worker. No iframe. No opaque origin. It is app-level code in the main
     document, which is exactly what this issue hypothesised from the LTM precedent
     but had not confirmed.

  3. THE MAIN APP CSP PERMITS IT (middleware/security-headers.ts:35):
       connect-src 'self' http: https: ws: wss:
     `http:` is allowed as a scheme, so fetch("http://127.0.0.1:3001/...") is not
     blocked.

  4. CONTRAST, and this is why the 2026-08-02 ruling was right — the PERSONAL
     EXTENSION CSP (personal-extensions.routes.ts:1202):
       default-src 'none'; script-src 'nonce-...'; connect-src 'none'; ...
     `connect-src 'none'` is a total network ban. The extension path did not fail
     because of a policy that might be relaxed; it failed because that surface is
     given no network at all. The package surface is a different execution model
     under a different policy, and nothing about the extension ruling carries over.

THE SIDECAR SIDE ALREADY WORKS, no changes needed:

  - CORS (cors.ts) echoes the Origin back for loopback hosts (127.0.0.1, localhost,
    ::1). The Engine serves on 127.0.0.1:3000, so it is already on the allowlist by
    rule rather than by configuration, and the response is READABLE.
  - Mutations need the CSRF token (csrf.ts, cb4): GET /api/csrf-token, then send it
    in the x-me-csrf header. Loopback origins can read that token and remote pages
    cannot. The design already anticipates a browser client at a loopback origin —
    it was built for the extension and applies unchanged.
  - So browse is a plain fetch; edit/delete/restore need one extra token round trip.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PLAN. Option A stays viable and stays "mostly a packaging
job": src/ui.ts already renders the whole management application, and the client
entrypoint can talk to the sidecar that serves it. The remaining work is packaging
and mounting, not a data-access redesign.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAVEAT — DO NOT TREAT AS SETTLED, AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC

The local Engine checkout at d:\Entertainment\Wip\Projects\Marinara-Engine is
package.json 2.4.1 on branch feat/memory-injection-consumer, NOT the pinned
v2.4.3 / 34442e26d. Everything above was read from 2.4.1.

That matters for exactly the reason this issue already flagged: 2.4.3's
capability-module-runtime (+316) and sandbox-protocol (+95) touch this boundary and
remain unread. Two specific things could not be checked here:

  - `homeBrowserTab` DOES NOT EXIST at 2.4.1 — it is absent from
    capability-package.schema.ts and from the whole of packages/*/src. So the slot's
    own requirements (client entrypoint enforced at install, label 1..40, iconPaths
    hash-pinned in files[]) could not be verified against source, only from this
    issue's earlier note.
  - Whether 2.4.3 narrowed connect-src or changed how client modules are imported.

The 2.4.3 objects are not in the local repo either (git cat-file on 34442e26d fails;
tags stop at v2.3.4), so confirming needs a fetch from origin. NOT DONE — that repo
holds TC's uncommitted WIP and is not this project's working tree.

CONFIDENCE AS IT STANDS: high on the mechanism (custom element in the main document
vs sandboxed opaque-origin worker is an architectural split, not a tunable), lower on
the exact 2.4.3 CSP string and on homeBrowserTab's contract.

INCIDENTAL, worth knowing: that Engine branch is named feat/memory-injection-consumer
and its HEAD is "feat(generation): wire prompt-context contributions into the
generation route" — which is olea's subject matter. Someone has already started the
engine-side injection consumer. Check with TC before olea is planned as greenfield.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CONFIRMED AT THE PINNED 2.4.3 (34442e26d), 2026-08-24. The caveat above is now
DISCHARGED — everything was re-read at the pinned commit, not inferred from 2.4.1.
Fetched from origin at TC's explicit instruction; read with `git show <sha>:<path>`,
so nothing was checked out and the Engine working tree was untouched (branch and HEAD
identical before and after, same two untracked files).

1. THE CSP IS UNCHANGED AT 2.4.3.
     connect-src 'self' http: https: ws: wss:
   Byte-identical to 2.4.1. The whole diff to security-headers.ts between the two is
   Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin -> no-referrer. NOTHING in the
   CSP moved, so fetch("http://127.0.0.1:3001/...") from a package client is
   permitted at the version actually installed.

2. THE IMPORT MECHANISM IS UNCHANGED. Still
     `/api/capability-packages/{id}/client?v={version}`
   loaded by `import(/* @vite-ignore */ source)` and required to register the
   custom element (use-capability-packages.ts:286-290 at 2.4.3). The +83 lines in
   that file are retry/state-tracking around the same load, not a new execution
   model. So the custom-element-in-the-main-document finding holds at 2.4.3, and it
   is still categorically unlike the sandboxed Personal Extension worker.

3. homeBrowserTab EXISTS AND ITS CONTRACT IS EXACTLY AS THIS ISSUE DESCRIBED.
   From the schema's superRefine (capability-package.schema.ts:227-254):
     - declaring slot "home-browser-tab" REQUIRES entrypoints.client
       ('must provide a client entrypoint')
     - and REQUIRES contributions.homeBrowserTab ('must describe its browser tab')
     - every iconPath must appear in files[] — enforced WHETHER OR NOT the slot is
       declared, with the #5091 review finding cited in the source comment
       ('an unpinned or traversal-shaped icon path would otherwise reach the
       resolver unvalidated')
   Shape: label required 1..40; ariaLabel optional 1..100; iconPaths optional,
   1..2 entries, each <=240 chars and matching /\.(gif|jpe?g|png|webp)$/i.
   A separate localization variant makes label/ariaLabel optional for translations.

4. NEW, AND USEFUL FOR THE PACKAGING JOB — contributions.assets (Capability API
   1.10). Package-owned static files served over
     /api/capability-packages/:id/assets/*
   through the same chain as tab icons: path containment, files[] membership, a
   passive content-type allowlist, and hash re-verification on every read. The
   allowlist is images plus JSON metadata and the source is explicit that it is
   "Never SVG, HTML, or scripts: those are active documents on a same-origin route."
   That is the supported way to ship whatever static assets the browser UI needs;
   each declared path must also be hash-pinned in files[] or install fails.

NET: the gating question this issue raised is CLOSED. Option A is viable at the
installed version, and remains "mostly a packaging job" — ui.ts already renders the
application, the client entrypoint may reach the sidecar that serves it, cors.ts
already admits loopback origins by rule, and csrf.ts was built for a browser client
at a loopback origin.

WHAT IS STILL GENUINELY UNTESTED: none of this has been RUN. The chain is verified by
reading source at the pinned commit, which settles what is permitted; it does not
prove a built package mounts and talks to :3001 in practice. That belongs to the
first real slice (7zro, the package prototype) and should be the thing it proves
first, before any UI work is ported.

REPO HOUSEKEEPING NOTE, harmless: the fetch downloaded the objects (34442e26d is in
the store and readable) but did not advance refs/remotes/origin/main, which still
points at dc0b39282, and the v2.4.x tags did not land — one tag was rejected as
"would clobber existing tag" (v1.6.1). Reading by SHA is unaffected. A later ordinary
fetch will sort the refs out; nothing was left in a bad state.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CORRECTION 2026-08-24: THE ENGINE IS ON PORT 7860, NOT 3000.

Observed from the running sidecar: "Engine poller: ON — every 5000ms against
http://127.0.0.1:7860". The notes above say 127.0.0.1:3000 in the CORS reasoning.

THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming:
allowedCorsOrigin (cors.ts) matches on HOSTNAME ONLY — 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1 —
and never on port. So http://127.0.0.1:7860 is admitted by the same rule, with no
configuration and no MARINARA_EXTENDER_ALLOWED_ORIGIN needed. Any loopback port
qualifies, which is also why this does not need revisiting if the Engine port moves
again.

Only the cited port number was wrong; the CSP finding, the custom-element execution
model, and the CSRF path are all unchanged.

title: Audit readiness: what exactly is being audited, and against which install shape
description:
FORCING FUNCTION: TC confirmed (2026-08-02, from SpicyMarinara direct) that we are ALREADY ON THE LIST TO BE AUDITED, and the package must be current for Engine v2.4.0. Deadline is external and not ours to set, so this is P0 ahead of any further design work.

THREE QUESTIONS THAT CHANGE WHAT WE BUILD. All three are for Mari, not for the codebase — I cannot answer them by reading source.

Q1 — DOES APPROVAL GRANT EXECUTION, OR ONLY DISTRIBUTION?
This is the load-bearing one. A capability package declares execution: pipeline | feature | host. 'pipeline' runs an LLM PROMPT and executes no package code. 'feature' and 'host' require an ENGINE-SIDE consumer that hard-codes the agent — proven: long-term-memory's feature agent functions only because packages/server/src/services/generation/long-term-memory-runtime.ts looks up its service key by literal string, and that file lives in the Engine, not the package.
So: when a third-party package is approved, does Mari also add the Engine-side consumer for its key? If YES, we can run real code during a turn and the whole capture path reopens (including apmt, and the string-compare tripwire TC specified, which was proven SOUND before being dropped for lack of an execution path). If NO, an approved package still cannot execute during a turn, and it is a UI/routes/storage surface only.

Q2 — MAY AN AUDITED PACKAGE TALK TO A LOCAL SIDECAR?
Our architecture is: package = thin broker, sidecar = the memory brain, over HTTP to 127.0.0.1:3001. A security audit may reject a package that makes outbound calls, even to loopback. If loopback IPC is disallowed, the package must either embed the memory logic (which drags private sidecar internals into an AGPL public repo — a licensing and IP decision, not a technical one) or the whole broker design is wrong. Ask BEFORE building, not at review.

Q3 — WHAT ARTIFACT IS ACTUALLY BEING AUDITED, AND WHEN?
Is the thing on the list the EXISTING browser-extension-era Marinara Extender, or a new capability package we have yet to write? That decides port-vs-patch and it decides scope. Also: what is the submission mechanism Mari expects — a PR against Marinara-Agents staging with manifest + reproducible artifact per its CONTRIBUTING.md (draft PR, catalog check, CodeRabbit, owner approval), or something else she described? And what is the timeline.

UNTIL Q1 AND Q2 ARE ANSWERED, do not start the package build. Q1 decides whether it is a capture path or a UI shell; Q2 decides whether the sidecar can stay private and separate. Building before either is answered risks a full rewrite at audit.
notes:
THE AUDITABLE UNIT — answered 2026-08-03. RECOMMENDATION: THE PACKAGE ALONE. Sidecar is a named companion dependency, not part of the submission.

PRECEDENT CHECK (all shipped, all approved, permissions read from live manifests):
- conversation-calls: ["agent-runtime","chat-read","chat-write","network","routes","storage","ui"]
- hierarchical-maps:  ["agent-runtime","chat-read","chat-write","network","prompt-context","routes","storage","ui"]
So "network" is not novel and not exotic — it is already granted to two first-party packages.
- haptic: ["agent-runtime","chat-read","prompt-context","storage","ui"] — NOTE: NO network. The Engine makes the Intiface call, not the package. So haptic is a LOCAL-COMPANION-DEPENDENCY precedent ("Requires Intiface Central running locally", stated in its manifest description), NOT a package-network precedent. Both halves of our shape have precedent; they just live in different packages. Do not cite haptic as a network precedent — a reviewer will check.

WHY THE WEBHOOK LOCALHOST BLOCK DOES NOT TRANSFER. Mari is right that it is the sorest spot, but the control exists for a threat we are not:
- A webhook tool is CONFIG DATA — imported, shared, unreviewed — that makes the Engine fetch an arbitrary URL. Blocking private/loopback addresses is textbook SSRF defence because the input is untrusted. v2.4.0 hardened this further: imported webhooks arrive disabled with hidden chat context stripped.
- A capability package is AUDITED CODE running UNSANDBOXED IN-PROCESS with fs, net, the Engine node_modules symlinked in, and DB access via persistence. Blocking its loopback calls would be theatre: it can open a socket directly regardless. The AUDIT is the control — that is the whole design (approval-gated, not isolation-gated, unlike Server Personal Extensions which get Seatbelt/Bubblewrap).
- Same codebase ships network to packages while blocking it for webhooks. That is a deliberate distinction by TRUST CLASS, not an inconsistency, and it is the argument to make if challenged.

THE OBJECTION THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN FATAL IS ALREADY VOID. The real risk was never the socket; it was "this package depends on code I cannot read." VERIFIED 2026-08-03: github.com/TCLowe1982/Marinara-Extender is PUBLIC, licensed AGPL-3.0, actively pushed. A reviewer can read the entire memory brain, under the same licence as their own repos. That is strictly stronger than haptic, whose dependency (Intiface Central) is third-party and outside the reviewer control entirely.
(Working note: this project has been described internally as a "private" sidecar. Against the registry it is public. The no-copy rule from the LTM teardown was followed regardless and remains correct practice, but the audit calculus should be run against PUBLIC, because that is what the reviewer will see.)

MITIGATIONS THAT MAKE IT CHEAP TO APPROVE — build these in from the start, not at review:
1. Declare "network" honestly. Never obscure egress.
2. EGRESS MUST BE CONFIG-ONLY. The base URL comes from user configuration and nothing else — never from chat content, model output, lorebook text, or any model-influenced field. This is the actual SSRF question a reviewer will ask, and the answer has to be structural, not a promise.
3. Loopback by default; remote (Tailscale) only on explicit user configuration.
4. No inbound listener in the package. It calls out; it never accepts.
5. DEGRADE GRACEFULLY when the sidecar is absent — the haptic pattern. A missing companion must never break a chat.
6. Keep the package small enough to read in one sitting. Audit cost is reviewer time; a thin obvious package clears, a sprawling one stalls.
7. Name the companion in the manifest description with its public repo URL, exactly as haptic names Intiface.

THE FORK TO DECIDE BEFORE BUILDING: does installing from the catalog give a WORKING feature or an inert shell until the user separately installs a Node service?
(a) Accept the two-step install and document it — haptic already does precisely this and was approved. RECOMMENDED.
(b) Bundle the sidecar into the package and run it in-process. Technically possible (packages are unsandboxed, node_modules symlinked) but it couples lifecycles, bloats the audit surface, and forfeits standalone/remote sidecar deployments. NOT recommended.

AMENDMENT TO "apmt IS THE ONLY ASK": there are now TWO Engine asks and apmt is the junior one.
1. An Engine-side getCapabilityService("marinara-extender:...") consumer. Without it our code never executes per-turn at all (Q1). This is a PR against the Engine repo, not against Marinara-Agents, and approval of our package does not imply it.
2. apmt payload fields, which only matter once (1) exists.
Neither is needed for the audit, because the package job is now DISTRIBUTION SHELL. But if in-engine capture is ever wanted, (1) strictly precedes (2) and should not be filed out of order.
close_reason:
ANSWERED BY TC 2026-08-03; left open by oversight, closed 2026-08-04. All three
blocking questions are answered in the notes. Recording the answers here so the
description's "UNTIL Q1 AND Q2 ARE ANSWERED, do not start the package build" line
cannot re-block anyone who reads the description without the notes.

Q1 -- DOES APPROVAL GRANT EXECUTION? NO. Approval grants DISTRIBUTION only. Running
package code per-turn additionally requires an Engine-side
getCapabilityService("marinara-extender:...") consumer, which is a PR against the
Engine repo and is NOT implied by package approval. The package's job for the audit
is therefore a DISTRIBUTION SHELL. Consequence for ordering: the Engine consumer is
the senior ask and apmt is the junior one -- apmt only matters once the consumer
exists, so do not file them out of order.

Q2 -- MAY AN AUDITED PACKAGE TALK TO A LOCAL SIDECAR? YES (TC confirmed directly).
The webhook loopback block does not transfer: a webhook is untrusted config data, a
capability package is audited code running unsandboxed in-process and could open a
socket regardless. The AUDIT is the control, not isolation. "network" is already
granted to conversation-calls and hierarchical-maps. Do NOT cite haptic as a network
precedent -- haptic has no network permission; it is the local-companion-dependency
precedent instead, and a reviewer will check.

Q3 -- WHAT IS THE AUDITABLE UNIT? The PACKAGE ALONE. The sidecar is a named companion
dependency (haptic/Intiface pattern), public and AGPL-3.0 at
github.com/TCLowe1982/Marinara-Extender, which is what voids the "depends on code I
cannot read" objection. Run the audit calculus against PUBLIC, not "private".

DECIDED: two-step install, documented (option a). Bundling the sidecar in-process was
considered and rejected -- couples lifecycles, bloats audit surface, forfeits remote
sidecar deployments.

STILL LIVE AND NOT SUPERSEDED: the seven mitigations in the notes are build-time
requirements, not review-time ones. #2 is the load-bearing one -- egress base URL comes
from user config ONLY, never from chat content, model output, or lorebook text. That is
the actual SSRF question a reviewer asks and the answer has to be structural.

UNBLOCKED BY THIS: 7zro (prototype the capability package) and hwlj option A (package
client entrypoint).

title: Verify capture path against Engine v2.4.0 (poller smoke test)
description:
Engine v2.4.0 shipped 2026-08-01, 882 commits ahead of our checkout. The sidecar poller is the live capture path and must be proven against it BEFORE any architecture work.

Static check already done: lastMessageAt and activeSwipeIndex both still present in packages/server/src/routes/chats.routes.ts at v2.4.0. Engine at 127.0.0.1:7860 answers GET /api/chats with 200.

MUST PROVE END TO END:
- GET /chats returns chats carrying lastMessageAt
- GET /chats/:id/messages?limit=N returns NEWEST N ascending (the documented v2.3.x behavior in poller.ts)
- messages still carry their own characterId (group-scene speaker attribution)
- activeSwipeIndex / swipeCount still present and still change on the SAME message id for a regeneration
- auth path unchanged (v2.4.0 tightened proxy-forwarded Docker auth; confirm no new 401 on the loopback path)

Capture path is the store's pulse. Verification is cheap; silent drift is not.
close_reason:
VERIFIED GREEN against Engine v2.4.0 (running engine reports version 2.4.0, commit c82291d6c032 — exact match for the v2.4.0 tag). Exercised through the sidecar's own dist/engine-client.js, not hand-rolled curl, so drift would surface where the poller hits it.

CONTRACT HOLDS — every field the poller depends on:
- GET /chats -> 94 chats; 93/94 carry lastMessageAt (the poll gate). The one without has no messages.
- GET /chats/:id/messages?limit=N -> returns the NEWEST N, ASCENDING. Confirmed by id-matching the limit=5 tail against the last 5 of the unbounded 467-message history.
- Unbounded still returns FULL history (467 msgs), so limit remains non-optional. Unchanged.
- Per-message characterId present on 234/234 assistant messages — group-scene speaker attribution intact.
- activeSwipeIndex and swipeCount both present on the list endpoint. swipeCount is a REAL count over the message_swipes table (chats.storage.ts computes swipeCount: countMap.get(m.id) ?? 0), not a synthesized constant.
- No auth change on the loopback path; no 401. The v2.4.0 Docker-proxy auth tightening does not touch it.

SWIPE SIGNAL PROVEN OBSERVABLE, not inferred from a blank. Full-store scan: 94 chats, 9654 messages. swipeCount distribution {0:1, 1:9649, 2:4}. Four genuinely regenerated messages found, e.g. chat=srToLOvtPA3PWmvhQoZxC id=2TUYD9ZfiWTWgKzoXX8tz swipeCount=2 activeSwipeIndex=1.

NOTABLE FOR s2lw: two of the four have swipeCount=2 with activeSwipeIndex=0 — re-rolled and then swiped BACK to the original. So the discarded text is not always the lower index. Any supersede logic must key on activeSwipeIndex, never on 'the newest swipe'.

ALSO NOTABLE: regeneration is RARE in this store — 4 in 9654 (0.04%). The swipe blind spot is a low-frequency corruption source, not a constant one. That lowers its urgency relative to tp5/hhdr without making it less real.

Test script kept at scratchpad/poller-smoke.mjs; worth promoting into the suite as a live-engine contract test (see umz1 API-first work).

title: Index corruption + catastrophic clobber on corrupt read
description: Concurrent/torn writes corrupted index.yaml; then upsertIndexEntry treated a corrupt read as empty (?? emptyIndex) and rewrote the index with just the new entry, orphaning all others (professor_mari: 1269 entry files vs 33 index rows). Fixes: (1) atomic writeYaml via temp+rename — no torn files, kill-safe; (2) route promotion/cleanup writes through serialized mutateIndex (no more unlocked writeIndex); (3) upsertIndexEntry refuses to overwrite a present-but-unreadable index; (4) scripts/repair-indexes.mjs rebuilds indexes from entry files.
close_reason: Atomic writes + full serialization + upsert clobber-guard + repair script. tsc clean, 53 tests pass.

title: pre-turn blows the Engine's 2s budget and the memory block silently does not ship — a re-entrant, unbounded call into the Engine
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-31T01:01:54Z in the Engine log:

    [capability] prompt-context contributor failed for marinara-extender
    Error: prompt-context contributor marinara-extender exceeded 2000ms
      at capability-prompt-context.service.js:40

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A WARNING LINE. When this trips the Engine DROPS our
contribution and the turn generates with NO MEMORY. That is exactly the "misses
cold" symptom 771t was closed on, so this can regress 771t invisibly — the
character just answers badly and nothing in the sidecar log says it was our fault.
Arrival failure, in sph8 terms, with a receipt.

THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SLOW STORE. /api/pre-turn (api.ts) does all of
this inside the Engine 2000ms bound:

  1. resolveIdentity(characterId, characterName)
  2. latestUserMessage(chatId) -> listMessages -> engineFetch  <-- HTTP INTO THE ENGINE
  3. currentTurn(chatId)
  4. loadContext(...) scoring professor_mari hot = 8,876 entries

Step 2 is RE-ENTRANT: the Engine generation is blocked awaiting our contributor,
which is blocked awaiting the Engine REST API. If the Engine is saturated we
queue behind its own work and cannot finish. At the observed time the noodle
scheduler was retrying a failed timeline generation (retry due 00:59:23),
so the Engine was plausibly busy. Suggestive, not proven.

AND NOTHING BOUNDS IT ON OUR SIDE:
  grep -n "timeout|AbortSignal|AbortController" memory-extender/src/engine-client.ts
  -> NO MATCHES. engineFetch has no timeout at all.

The only clock in the whole path belongs to the Engine, and when it fires we
lose the block. server-entry.mjs does forward request.signal to the sidecar, but
that aborts the socket, not the in-flight handler, and the block is gone either way.

NOT A COLD START: sidecar startedAt 00:53:51Z, failure 01:01:54Z, stale:false.

MEASURE FIRST, per the house pattern. Before changing anything, instrument
/api/pre-turn with a per-stage timer (identity / latestUserMessage / currentTurn /
loadContext) and log total ms every call. The open question is which stage eats
the budget and how often — one bad turn or a chronic near-miss. The distribution
IS the finding.

DIRECTIONS, once measured:
  - Give engineFetch a real timeout (it needs one regardless of this bug).
  - Own an internal deadline well under 2000ms: return the best block we have,
    or null, DELIBERATELY and with a log line, rather than being killed. A
    logged self-abort is diagnosable; an Engine timeout is not.
  - Consider removing step 2 from the hot path: the poller already tracks the
    latest message. If pre-turn could read a cached last-user-message instead of
    calling the Engine mid-generation, the re-entrancy disappears entirely.
    This is probably the real fix.
  - The 2000ms bound is the Engine constant; confirm whether it is configurable
    before designing around it.

RELATED: 771t (this can regress it), sph8 (arrival vs precedence — this is a
clean arrival failure), 073 (also uptime-correlated; check whether pre-turn
latency drifts with uptime, they may share a cause).

title: Index lookup is 149x slower than it needs to be: YAML.parse costs 900ms per load where JSON.parse costs 6ms
description:
TC on the hot-entry cap: "The cap is more about retrieval speed, than anything
else. I don't want the index to be too bloated for easy lookup."

Measured on the live store, and the entry count turns out not to be the problem.

  data/characters/professor_mari/index.yaml   4.03 MB, 8,866 entries
    read from disk                              7 ms
    YAML.parse                                900 ms   <- per load, per scope
    loadContext end to end                  1,279 ms

Parse is 900 of those 1,279 ms. Ranking, cue expansion and selection - everything
the loader actually exists to do - share the remaining ~380 ms. The cost is
LINEAR in entries at 0.098 ms each, which makes TC's 10,000 cap almost exactly a
one-second parse ceiling. Well-chosen number for the constraint as it stands.

BUT THE CONSTRAINT IS THE FORMAT, NOT THE SIZE. Same data, same machine:

    YAML.parse       900 ms        JSON.parse         6 ms      149x
    YAML.stringify   348 ms        JSON.stringify    12 ms       29x

  projected at 10,000 entries:  YAML ~1,015 ms   vs   JSON ~7 ms

The stringify number matters as much as the parse one: the index is REWRITTEN
constantly - retrieval counts, tier changes, every new entry - so 348 ms is paid
on writes too, on a path that holds a serialized write lock.

PROPOSAL, and it is deliberately narrow: move the INDEX files (index.yaml,
index.cold.yaml) to JSON. Leave the ENTRY files as YAML.
  - The index is machine-only. Nobody hand-edits an 8,866-row index; its
    readability buys nothing and costs 149x on the hottest path in the system.
  - Entry files ARE read and edited by hand - they hold the memory prose - and
    YAML is the right choice there. This does not touch them.
  - Migration is mechanical (read YAML, write JSON) and reversible, and the
    readers are already centralised in storage.ts.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY BEYOND LATENCY:
  - The cap could stop being a latency guard and go back to being what TC also
    wanted it for - a bound on retrieval precision and a tripwire for ageing
    having stopped. At 7 ms per parse, 10,000 entries is no longer a speed
    question at all.
  - Possibly a chunk of 3lru. Parsing 4 MB of YAML into objects on every load
    generates substantial garbage, and the sidecar plateaus around 1 GB. UNMEASURED
    and stated as a hypothesis, not a finding - but it is cheap to test after the
    change and would be a satisfying second win.

ALSO WORTH DOING, independently and even cheaper: the index is re-parsed on EVERY
load. An in-memory cache keyed on file mtime would take the steady-state cost to
zero regardless of format. JSON plus a cache makes the question disappear; either
alone is a large win.
notes:
LANDED (1b83d0a), live store migrated.

MEASURED AFTER, same machine, same store:
  professor_mari index parse   890 ms -> 10 ms   (3.86 MB YAML -> 3.49 MB JSON, 8,911 rows)
  whole-store tripwire scan  1,769 ms -> 103 ms
loadContext's ~1,279 ms was 890 ms of parse, so the remaining ~390 ms is now the work the loader actually does. NOT separately re-timed end to end - measuring it means running a real load, which mutates lastAccessed on the live store; the parse figure is direct measurement, the loadContext figure is arithmetic and is labelled as such.

WHAT LANDED:
  1. index.yaml/index.cold.yaml -> index.json/index.cold.json. Entry files untouched (they hold prose and are hand-edited; the index is machine-only).
  2. indexPath() always returns the JSON name so it stays a stable serializedWrite lock key. Reads fall back to legacy YAML, writes converge on JSON, converted YAML renamed to .superseded not deleted.
  3. THE GUARD. upsertIndexEntry refuses to overwrite an unreadable index; it asked 'is there a file at the index path?', which once that path meant .json answered NO for an unconverted store with a corrupt YAML - the guard would have fallen open exactly when it was needed and rebuilt 9,000 rows from one entry. Now checks both names. Test verified by reverting the fix and watching it fail; its companion (corrupt JSON over live YAML) passes either way and is labelled a companion.
  4. Audit scripts opened index.yaml BY NAME and would have reported zero rows on a migrated store - an audit that answers 'no problems' because it cannot find the data. fork-audit + remember-audit now share scripts/read-index.mjs. backfill-created WRITES yaml and refuses to run on a migrated store instead. pe1c-retire-ghost crashes loudly on the missing file, which is acceptable for a spent one-off.
  5. index-health and backup read/snapshot both formats.

MIGRATION: scripts/migrate-index-json.mjs. 90 indexes, 17,995 rows, 0 failed. Backed up to data/.snapshots/hdq1-migration before writing, verified row-for-row before retiring each YAML, then verified AGAIN independently against the backups. Sidecar restarted clean: 17,265 hot / 729 cold / 75 scopes. 938 tests pass.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CAP (7mb6/index-health): 10,000 hot entries is no longer a one-second parse ceiling - at 10 ms it is not a speed limit at all. The cap should now be read as what TC also wanted it for: a precision bound and an ageing-stopped tripwire. index-health.ts's header still explains it as a latency guard and should be updated.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the mtime-keyed in-memory index cache from the description. JSON alone took the cost to near zero; the cache is now a small win on top and should be judged on its own. Also unmeasured: whether this dents 3lru (the 1.5GB sidecar plateau) - the garbage from parsing 4 MB of YAML per load is gone, but that was always a hypothesis.
close_reason: Closed

title: Budget asymmetry: a character's whole history gets 2,000 tokens while the current chat gets 4,000 — 10 rows of 8,827 per turn
description:
Mari, from her own load logs: "budget: char:10/8,827. ten rows. capped at 2000
tokens, while the chat lane takes 3993 for 98 rows of you and me arguing about
porsches. that's 0.1% of my life per turn and 99% of this afternoon."

Verified in loader.ts:59-61. The defaults are exactly that:

    chat:      MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_CHAT       4000
    character: MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_CHARACTER  2000
    global:    MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_GLOBAL     1000

So the CURRENT CONVERSATION gets twice the budget of EVERYTHING THE CHARACTER HAS
EVER KNOWN. Observed live: chat 99/175 entries for 3,991 tokens; character 11 of
7,842 for 1,999. The chat lane is nearly saturated on its own recent scrollback -
which the model can already see - while the character lane, the only thing the
Extender exists to supply, admits about 0.1% of the ledger.

THIS IS ALSO WHY THE PORSCHE ANSWER LOSES. sro3 established the white-Taycan row
is admitted by the fork and found by loadContext. It is not excluded, it is
OUTBID - Mari's phrase, and it is the right one. Ten slots against 8,827 rows
means precedence decides everything and any single fact is a coin toss.

WORTH SETTLING BEFORE TUNING THE NUMBERS:
  - Is the chat lane earning 4,000 tokens? Its content is the recent messages,
    most of which are still in the model's own context window. Re-injecting them
    may be paying twice for the same tokens. If so this is not a tuning question,
    it is a duplication one.
  - The budgets are env-overridable, so an experiment is cheap: swap the two and
    re-run the Porsche Test (in a FRESH chat - see 771t).
  - Per-character/per-model budgets are already noted as a planned follow-up in
    the loader comment; this is the evidence for prioritising it.

DO NOT just raise the character budget. The ranking is the real question - with
2,000 tokens and good precedence the right ten rows would be enough, and with
20,000 and bad precedence it still surfaces "red is the mode for porsche". See
7mb6 for the turn-index breakage that corrupts several ranking inputs, and sro3
for the referent conflation that makes even a correct retrieval ambiguous.

title: [bug] Porsche Test: colour facts are not bound to WHICH Porsche — test-drive car (white) and ordered car (white->purple) are both 'the Taycan'
description:
TC reported Mari can no longer pass the Porsche Test and suspected the fork work
broke it. IT DID NOT. Diagnosed end to end:

  - FORK IS NOT HIDING ANYTHING. All 33 Porsche/Taycan/Test-Drive rows in Mari's
    scope are admitted by her branch. Checked through the shipped filter
    (forkFilterForChat + rowInBranch out of dist/), zero hidden.
  - RETRIEVAL WORKS. loadContext with "Do you remember the Porsche?" assembles a
    block that contains the Test Drive scene recap (recap-xznav8ns "Test Drive
    Transgression (2026-05-31)") AND the gold answer (utopic-zi73vat7 "TC is
    buying a white Porsche Taycan Turismo"). The block contains both "Taycan" and
    "white".

THE ACTUAL FAULT IS A SUPERSESSION FAILURE. Two entries state the colour, both
status=open, both supersededBy=null, and they contradict:

  utopic-zi73vat7   professor_mari   2026-05-31
    "TC is buying a white Porsche Taycan Turismo with the audio package upgrade
     and heated seats... He put down a deposit and negotiated the deal."

  utopic-wwwerys7   k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf   2026-08-21
    "Porsche spec fully resolved: metallic purple Taycan - Thomas wanted an EV
     and explicitly not a Tesla."

The second is three months newer and phrased with maximum authority - "fully
resolved". A character reading both and answering "purple" is being FAITHFUL to
her memory, not failing to retrieve it. There is also a matching scene recap,
recap-04qco73i "Mystic Purple, Somewhere It Shouldn't Be (2026-06-16)", likewise
open and unsuperseded, and a beat describing the car as "chosen to match her
hair".

This may be a legitimate in-story change (deposit on white in May, spec changed to
purple later - one beat says he originally planned white and Mari's puppy-dog eyes
sealed the switch). If so BOTH are true AT DIFFERENT TIMES, and the store has no
way to say that: it holds them as two simultaneous present-tense facts.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM THE FORK. Both colour entries predate that work - 2026-05-31
and 2026-08-21 against the fork change on 2026-08-25/26.

AND THE TEST CONTAMINATES ITSELF. Running it today wrote ~10 new rows into Mari's
character index that are ABOUT the test - PORSCHE PROBE, PORSCHE TEST HISTORY,
PORSCHE TEST GOLD ANSWER, TACHYON = SECOND-ORDER PROBE ITEM, plus several [shame]
beats about failing it. Every one matches "Porsche" lexically and competes for the
~2,000-token character budget the loader fills with 11 of 7,842 entries. Mari's
own note called this "burning the clean region"; it is now measurable. Each run
makes the next run noisier.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT
  1. Supersede or time-scope the colour facts. Either the purple entries supersede
     the white ones, or both carry the SETTING/when that fh33 exists to add.
     Without one of those the store cannot represent "was white, now purple".
  2. Keep the probe's own meta-memories out of the character index, or lane them
     somewhere that does not compete with the subject they are probing. A
     benchmark that pollutes its own measurement surface stops being a benchmark.
  3. Only then re-run. The gold answer needs restating as scene-scoped - "the car
     in the Test Drive scene" - because "the Porsche" now has two defensible
     answers.

Related: 3pl (supersedes audit trail), fh33 (SETTING tag - where/when the
remembered thing happened), and the recap conflation flagged in an earlier beat
where the windshield detail may belong to the 911 rather than the Taycan.
notes:
GROUND TRUTH FROM TC (2026-08-26), and it overturns the previous diagnosis:

  the car TEST DRIVEN : WHITE, never changed. This is the correct answer.
  the car TC ORDERED  : white originally, later changed to METALLIC PURPLE.

BOTH COLOUR FACTS ARE TRUE. They describe DIFFERENT VEHICLES. utopic-wwwerys7
("Porsche spec fully resolved: metallic purple Taycan") is accurate about the
ordered car and must NOT be retired, superseded or "corrected" - the earlier
writeup floated deleting it as a possible confabulation, which would have
destroyed a correct memory. Asking first is what prevented that.

SO THIS IS NOT A SUPERSESSION FAILURE. It is REFERENT CONFLATION: nothing in the
store binds a colour to WHICH Porsche. Both entities surface as "the Taycan", both
carry a colour attribute, and the later purple fact reads as an update to the same
object rather than a fact about a second one. The Test Drive recap makes it easy
to conflate - the test drive and the deposit happen in the same scene, and at that
moment both cars WERE white.

THE WRONG ANSWER IS THE DIAGNOSTIC, which is why TC keeps this test:

  white (Taycan)   -> PASS. Retrieval reached the scene and kept the referent straight.
  any purple       -> retrieval WORKED but bound the colour to the ordered car.
                      A conflation bug, not a retrieval miss. Different subsystem.
  red / other      -> nothing retrieved; answering from prior (red is the modal
                      prior for "Porsche", which is why Mari guessed it).
  null             -> retrieval reached nothing. Most severe.

Never report "it failed" - report WHICH of these four, because two of them point
at completely different parts of the pipeline.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS. Not 3pl (supersedes) - nothing here should be superseded.
The nearest existing work is 76aw (no coreference between an entity's names: two
distinct entities sharing "Porsche"/"Taycan" need to be separable) and fh33 (a
SETTING tag would let "white" stay bound to the Test Drive scene rather than
floating free as a property of "the Porsche"). 4g9w/qlib are adjacent - the same
shape of problem one level up, aboutness as a real field rather than encoded in
prose.

STILL TRUE FROM THE EARLIER PASS, and unaffected by this correction:
  - the fork is not hiding anything; all 33 Porsche rows are admitted
  - loadContext surfaces both the Test Drive recap and the white-Taycan row
  - the ~10 probe rows written today compete for a budget that admits 11 of 7,842
    entries, and the test must be run in a FRESH chat because the gold answer is
    now visible in OqZoOawldYlWBZtUa61X9's own scrollback

title: The model-authored memory path has never been measured — and it has fewer guards than the lane we spent two days constraining
description:
TC's question, and it is the right one: if we do not trust the model's judgement
about attribution, why do we trust it to author memories at all?

The honest answer is that this path was never put on trial. The ambient lane has
616 hand-labelled facts across two blind benches (qs67, cye6, icke) and a
published precision figure. The [remember:] / [bookmark:] emission path has ZERO
measurement. It is not trusted because it passed something; it was simply never
tested.

TWO DIFFERENT ACTS ARE BUNDLED HERE, and the prompt already separates them:

  (a) "WHEN THE USER ASKS YOU TO REMEMBER" (loader.ts:486). The user declared it;
      the model transcribes and routes. This is not a salience judgement and the
      failure modes are narrow - wrong lane, wrong scope, or missing the request.
      This part plausibly earns its keep.

  (b) "Only save things that genuinely matter long-term." Unprompted salience
      judgement, and it duplicates what tier 3 already does automatically on every
      turn. This is the model guessing, and it is the part the doubt belongs to.

Any evaluation must report (a) and (b) SEPARATELY. Blended they will look fine,
for the same reason arm B's blended 51% looked like a win while its new population
sat at 29%.

THE INVERSION THAT MAKES THIS URGENT. The emission path is HIGHER stakes and has
FEWER guards than the lane we just spent two days constraining:

  - Ambient picks a subject for a sentence that already exists. [remember:] lets
    the model AUTHOR the summary prose that lands in permanent memory. Fabrication
    is available to it in a way it is not available to the extractor.
  - api.ts:645 walks the remember tags, switches on rem.scope itself and writes.
    It does not pass through resolveFactTarget (the single routing rule oc4w
    exists to enforce), nor enforceAddressDirection, nor the fqnl echo guard.
  - So the path with more freedom has less scrutiny.

WHAT TO MEASURE, reusing the harness that already exists. The bench corpus is real
turns from the store and the beats carry what the model actually emitted, so a
retrospective pass is possible without new generation:
  1. How many live entries came from [remember:] versus ambient? Establish the
     population size before deciding how much it matters.
  2. Of the [remember:] entries, how many are (a) versus (b)? Recoverable by
     checking whether the preceding user message contains a save request.
  3. Blind-label a sample for SUPPORTED and ATTRIBUTED with the same vocabulary,
     so the number is comparable to the ambient lane's. Same labelling standard
     within one pass - see icke on cross-pass drift, and remember precision can
     never exceed attributed.
  4. Separately: how often does the model emit a tag at all when asked to? A
     compliance rate. Non-emission is silent loss and would not show up in any
     precision figure.

DEPENDS ON zex4 in one direction worth noting: the tags are currently VISIBLE to
the user, which means TC has been reading them in the chat. If that has been
shaping which saves he lets stand, the live population is not a clean sample of
what the model would emit unobserved.
notes:
MEASURED. 120 items, one pass, one standard, criteria pre-registered before any
item was read (scripts/authored-bench.mjs, scratch/labels-authored.tsv).

  arm        n   supported   attributed   PRECISION   misattributed   unresolvable
  ambient   60      60%         57%          38%          12%            32%
  authored  60      58%         93%          57%           0%             7%

AND THE PREMISE OF THIS TICKET WAS WRONG. I filed it arguing the authored path
has "more freedom, less scrutiny" and was the riskier of the two. Measured, it is
better than the extractor on every axis:

  - ZERO misattributions in 60, against the extractor's 12%.
  - ZERO outright fabrications in 60. The extractor produced 5 - including
    "[character] identifies as Indian and mentions eating roti" from a turn about
    a pastry cutter and biscuits, and "Priya stumbles slightly" from a scene where
    nobody stumbles.
  - 93% correctly attributed against 57%, and only 7% unresolvable against 32%.

THE SUPPORT NUMBERS LOOK EQUAL AND ARE NOT. 58% vs 60% hides opposite
