compositions. Of the authored arm's 25 support failures, 15 are NTL - the claim
is TRUE but drawn from an earlier conversation rather than the turn it was
flushed in. Only 6 are distortions and 4 are on-topic-but-absent. The extractor's
24 failures are 19 distortions and 5 fabrications. Same headline rate, completely
different failure mode: one recalls things from elsewhere, the other invents them.

WHY IT WINS ON ATTRIBUTION, mechanically: an authored memory NAMES its subject in
prose ("TC's full name is Thomas Charles Lowe", "Mari's go-to delivery order").
The extractor has to populate a separate subject field, and fails by putting a
vocative there ("Priya I love him so much" -> Priya loves), an object there ("I
make a sound into Thomas's chest" -> Thomas makes it), or a template token
("[character]", "unknown", "character"). Prose that says who it is about cannot
make that class of error.

SCOPE, and it is the important caveat: this is the TURN-LOCAL subset only - 182 of
1,003 authored memories, 18%. The other 82% are DIGESTS, multi-fact dated
summaries condensing conversations from days earlier, median 482 characters
against the extractor's 60. They cannot be scored against a single turn because
they were never derived from one, and for the same reason fqnl's echo guard has
nothing to bite on: a digest has no single receipt. THE RISK IN THIS PATH LIVES IN
THAT 82%, and it is still unmeasured. Verifying it needs a different method -
checking a digest against the conversation window it claims to summarise.

METHOD, stated so the numbers are read correctly:
  - NOT BLIND, and it could not be. The arms are different kinds of object and
    differ in length, voice and shape; authored memories carry no subject field at
    all, so the display leaks the arm. icke could blind A/B/C because all three
    were ambient facts. The guard here is pre-registration, not concealment.
  - The ambient 38% is NOT the published 43%. Different standard, re-labelled
    today, and a TURN-level support test rather than qs67's per-SENTENCE one -
    applied equally to both arms, which is what makes the pair comparable to each
    other and to nothing else.
  - Display truncation caused at least one near-miss: item 28 read as unsupported
    at reduced width and is fully carried in the complete block. Items marked "not
    in the visible text" are soft.
  - The [user] side of the pairing is unreliable for multi-beat messages - several
    items share one mismatched user block. Those were credited on the character
    block rather than penalised for the harness's bug.

title: [remember:]/[bookmark:] tags render to the user — the stripper lost its consumer when v2.3.4 removed client extensions, and the prompt still promises otherwise
description:
The memory block tells the model, in the instruction block it reads every single
turn: "Commands are stripped from output. Use sparingly." (loader.ts:509).

That is no longer true, and has not been since Marinara Engine v2.3.4 removed
client extensions entirely (see the proxy.ts header - the proxy exists precisely
because the sidecar can no longer observe or touch turns from inside the browser).
The stripping had a consumer then. It has none now.

THE STRIPPER STILL RUNS AND ITS OUTPUT IS THROWN AWAY. writer.ts processResponse
computes `clean = stripRememberTags(stripBookmarkTags(rawText))` and returns it -
and the only call site, api.ts:701, destructures `{ bookmarksExtracted }` and
discards `clean`. So every turn pays for the strip and nothing consumes it.

AND THE SIDECAR CANNOT RETROACTIVELY FIX IT. engine-client has no message edit -
PATCH exists only for lorebooks and their entries. By the time the sidecar sees an
assistant message (poller or turn hook), the engine has already stored and
rendered it with the tags in place. There is no path from here to a clean
transcript.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is user-facing: the tags are visible in the chat, permanently,
in the stored history. Anything the model emits per the vocabulary we taught it
shows up as raw prose in the middle of an RP scene.

WHERE THE FIX HAS TO GO, and the constraint it collides with. The proxy is the
only seam left, because generation now flows through the sidecar on its way to the
provider. But slice 4 is currently specified as a TEE, and proxy.ts:147 states the
rule plainly: "The tee must never gate or delay a chunk being written out."

Hiding a tag is not observation, it is TRANSFORMATION of the response stream, and
it cannot be done without delay: `[remember: ...]` cannot be recognised, let alone
removed, until the closing bracket arrives. So the stripper needs a bounded
lookahead that holds output back the moment it sees a candidate opening token and
releases it when the tag either completes (drop it) or fails to complete within
the bound (emit it verbatim). That is a deliberate, explicit exception to the
slice-4 constraint, and it should be written as one rather than discovered later
by whoever implements the tee and finds the two requirements contradict.

WORTH DECIDING AT THE SAME TIME: whether the tags should be in the response stream
at all. A model that emits structured metadata mid-prose is being asked to do two
jobs in one channel, and the only reason it works is a stripper that no longer
exists. See the sibling question of whether the emission path deserves the trust
it has - it has never been measured (the ambient lane has 616 hand-labels; this
path has none).

INTERIM, if the fix is not immediate: correct the instruction. Telling the model
its commands are stripped when they are not is a false statement in the prompt,
and the model has no way to discover it. Either strip them or stop promising to.
notes:
2026-08-30 — INHERITED FROM z9s, which closed with the retired inference-proxy epic (hq7). z9s was 'proxy slice 6: command stripping without the extension' and held two candidate mechanisms. The proxy one died with the epic; the OTHER ONE SURVIVES AND IS NOW THE LEADING CANDIDATE, so it is recorded here rather than lost with the closed ticket.

HOW THE EXTENSION USED TO STRIP, three layers:
  1. an auto-installed Marinara regex script
  2. CSS hiding
  3. a DOM TreeWalker
Layers 2 and 3 died with the extension. LAYER 1 DID NOT.

THE SURVIVING MECHANISM: Engine-native regex scripts still work in v2.3.4+, both per-character and per-preset. What was lost is only the AUTO-INSTALL, not the capability. So the options are (a) document a manual install step, or (b) have the sidecar create the regex script itself over the Engine REST API — (b) keeps it invisible to the user, which is the behaviour the prompt already promises.

SCOPE LIMIT, stated so it is not rediscovered: the Engine already strips native [remember:]/[bookmark:] before SAVING. So this only covers the streaming window and legacy XML tags — the tags flashing on screen mid-generation, which is the actual reported symptom.

title: Identity in the extractor prompt is the attribution lever — arm E moved misattribution 22%->12% with the shipping gate
description:
Arm E of the icke bench measured what the qs67 sweep was looking for. Telling the
ambient extractor WHO SPOKE the block and that the persona IS the user - nothing
else - produced the only measured improvement over the shipped baseline in the
configuration that actually ships (old gate).

  A  old gate + old prompt  (SHIPPED)   45% attributed   15% misattributed
  D  old gate + new prompt              40%              22%
  E  old gate + new prompt + IDENTITY   60%              12%

Within the D/E pass, which shares one labeller, one session and one standard and
is therefore a clean contrast, the header moved precision 28% -> 45% and halved
misattribution. E's precision ceiling is its attributed rate, 60%, so a
like-for-like re-label can only raise it.

WHAT ARM E ACTUALLY SENT, so this is not re-derived from memory. A header on the
user message, plus a clause in the system prompt telling the model to use it:

  WHO IS SPEAKING
  - The [user] block was spoken by the human player: TC Lowe, thomas lowe,
    thomas charles lowe, tc, tc lowe, holyknight3. Any of those names means the
    user.
  - NOT the player, despite the resemblance: thomas collier.
  - The [character] block was spoken by Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran.

The names come VERBATIM from the declared identity (egj3, data/user-identity.yaml)
including the stored lowercase, and the exclusion line comes from its "excludes"
list. Nothing was invented for the bench, which is why the live path can reproduce
it. The exact clause and header builder are in scripts/ambient-precision-bench.mjs
(IDENTITY_CLAUSE and buildPrompt); dump them with BENCH_DUMP=1.

WHY IT WORKS, from the misattributed items it fixed: the extractor's failures are
overwhelmingly cases where a NAME appears in a sentence and is taken as the
subject regardless of grammatical role - a vocative ("Priya I love him so much"
recorded as Priya loving), or the object of an action ("I make a sound into
Thomas's chest" recorded as Thomas making it). Knowing who is speaking gives the
model the one fact that resolves "I" and demotes a bare name from
subject-by-default.

WHAT THIS NEEDS BEFORE IT SHIPS, none of it done:
  1. The live path does not have what the bench had. The bench was handed the
     speaking character's name per turn from the beat, and the declared identity
     from disk. classifyAmbient() receives a roster but is never told which
     character SPOKE the block. Check what the ingest path actually has there.
  2. Personas are not read at all yet (opyv, qhej). Arm E used the DECLARED
     identity as a stand-in for the persona; the real thing is per-chat - the
     chat row carries a persona id and it is unread, see poller.ts:78. Arm E is
     evidence the AXIS pays, not that the declared-identity file is the right
     source.
  3. It is unmeasured with the WIDE gate. B was the only arm with the wide gate
     and the new prompt; there is no gate-on plus identity cell. Do not assume
     the gains compose.
  4. TC reviews prompt text before it ships. The clause above is what was
     measured; changing a word makes it unmeasured again.

Blocked-by is deliberately not set: this is a lead with a number attached, not a
scheduled slice. It should be scoped against 4g9w/qlib (SUBJECT as a real field),
because if SUBJECT becomes structural the prompt may not be where this belongs.

title: Arm D: measure the DIRECTION OF ADDRESS prompt with the second-person gate OFF — the one configuration that was never run
description:
The precision bench ran three arms and the fourth is the one that decides two open
questions at once. Blocks both cye6 and qs67 slice 2.

    A  old gate + old prompt   43% precise, 15% misattributed   (ran)
    C  new gate + old prompt   55% precise, 15% misattributed   (ran)
    B  new gate + new prompt   62% precise,  7% misattributed   (ran)
    D  OLD gate + NEW prompt   ???                              NOT RUN

WHY IT MATTERS. The cye6 DIRECTION OF ADDRESS prompt block is currently OUT of the
build. It measured well — on the existing population it cut misattribution 15% ->
7% and raised precision 43% -> 62% — but only ever ALONGSIDE the wide gate, and
the gate is now off by default because it failed its own bar. Shipping the prompt
with the gate off is shipping a configuration nobody has measured. Arm D is
exactly that configuration.

AND IT IS ALSO qs67 SLICE 2's FIRST DATA POINT. The feature sweep established
there is no cheap surface rule for the 43% baseline (best single lift 1.46, best
conjunction 75%, and every usable rule confined to the second-person population
already handled). The lever that moves it is better INPUT, and the prompt block is
the only input change measured to move it at all. Arm D says whether it moves it
without the gate.

RUN IT AS: the same 60 turns, same seed (20260825), same model (dolphin3:8b), same
labelling vocabulary and the same blind harness. scripts/ambient-precision-bench.mjs
takes the arms as a literal; add D and re-run, then scripts/bench-label.mjs. The
existing labels stay valid because the blind ids are seeded — but D's facts are NEW
items and need labelling, so budget ~60-160 more.

WORTH ADDING IN THE SAME RUN, since the bench is already paid for: an arm that
tells the model WHO SPOKE and that the PERSONA IS THE USER. The sweep showed the
extractor is reliable when the sentence carries its own subject (subject "user"
wrong 11%, first person wrong 16%) and collapses when it must infer one — and its
only context for inferring is a [user]/[character] tag and a flat "Known
characters" list. It is never told which character spoke the block, nor that
"Thomas" and "the user" are one referent (qhej). Those are cheap to add and are
the strongest remaining hypothesis.

DO NOT re-derive the decision rule after seeing D. Precision is reported PER
POPULATION, never blended — blended, arm B scores 51% against A's 43% and looks
like a clean win while its new population sits at 29%.
acceptance_criteria: Arm D run on the same 60 turns, same seed, same model; its facts labelled blind with the same vocabulary; precision and misattribution reported per population against arms A and B. A decision recorded on whether the cye6 prompt block ships with the gate off.
notes:
RESULT. Arm D was run on the pinned 60 turns, same seed, same model; its 120 facts
(60 per arm, OLD population only) labelled blind with the same vocabulary.

  arm  configuration                      supp  attrib  PRECISION  misattrib
  A    old gate + old prompt  (SHIPPED)    92%    45%       43%       15%
  B    wide gate + new prompt              85%    67%       62%        7%
  C    wide gate + old prompt              90%    57%       55%       15%
  D    OLD gate + new prompt               73%    40%       28%       22%
  E    OLD gate + new prompt + IDENTITY    78%    60%       45%       12%

THE DECISION, and it is a NO: the DIRECTION OF ADDRESS block must NOT ship with
the second-person gate off. Arm D is worse than what already ships - 28% against
43% precision, and misattribution goes UP, 15% -> 22%. The 62% that arm B scored
was a JOINT effect of the wide gate and the prompt, not a property of the prompt.
Pulling it from the build in fe71f9f was correct, and it stays out.

D and E have NO NEW population at all, by construction: the old gate never admits
a second-person-only sentence, so there is nothing for the new cell to contain.
D/E compare to A and B on the OLD population only, which is where the decision
lives anyway.

THE NO SURVIVES THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE BROKEN IT. A/B/C were labelled on
2026-08-25 and D/E on 2026-08-26, by the same labeller in different sessions, and
the second pass was measurably STRICTER: notes rejecting a fact for importing
something "not in the sentence" run 3 across 180 pass-1 items versus 21 across 120
pass-2 items, and SUPPORTED drops 89% -> 76% with it. Precision is S && A, so that
drift depresses D and E on its own.

It does not matter here, because PRECISION CAN NEVER EXCEED ATTRIBUTED, and
attribution is what the import rule does not touch. D's attributed rate is 24/60 =
40%, so D's precision has a CEILING of 40% under any support standard however
lenient - below A's measured 43%. Arm D cannot beat the shipped baseline even if
every one of its supported-judgements were reversed in its favour. The verdict is
not sensitive to the drift; only the size of the gap is.
  Corroborating that the attribution convention itself held across the two
  sessions: the unresolvable ("?") rates match closely - 24/16/17 in pass 1
  against 23/17 in pass 2.

AND THE REAL FINDING IS ARM E. Telling the extractor who spoke and that the
persona IS the user is the lever the sweep was looking for:
  - within pass 2, where both arms share one labeller, one session and one
    standard - the clean contrast - the identity header moves precision 28% ->
    45% and HALVES misattribution, 22% -> 12%;
  - against the shipped baseline on the drift-robust axis, attribution goes 45%
    -> 60% and misattribution 15% -> 12%.
That is with the OLD gate, i.e. in the configuration that actually ships. E's
precision ceiling is 60%, so a lenient re-label could only raise it.

This redirects qs67. The feature sweep found no cheap surface rule and concluded
the lever is better INPUT; the prompt block was the only input change measured to
move anything, and D shows it does not move it alone. IDENTITY does. That is the
same axis as qhej (which Thomas) and opyv (read the cards) - the extractor cannot
attribute because it is never told who the participants are.

SPECIMENS, from the 20 misattributed, both showing attribution failing on a
sentence whose subject is unambiguous to a human reader:
  #44  "I make a sound into Thomas's chest ..."   -> recorded as THOMAS making
       the sound. The speaker acts; the named person is the surface the action
       lands on, and the extractor took the name.
  #50  "Priya I love him so much I think I am going to throw something."
       -> recorded as PRIYA expressing the love. The vocative was read as the
       subject; the speaker is someone else entirely.

NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS PASSES, stated so nobody quotes it: the absolute PRECISION
figures for D/E against A/B/C. The attribution and misattribution figures are
drift-robust and the D-vs-E contrast is within-pass. If a like-for-like precision
number is ever needed, A/OLD's 60 items must be re-labelled under the pass-2
standard first.
close_reason: Closed

title: The ambient extractor is 43% precise and the broken axis is ATTRIBUTION, not extraction — 92% supported, 45% correctly attributed
description:
FIRST EVER MEASUREMENT of the tier-3 ambient extractor, 2026-08-25 (cye6 slice 3).
496 facts hand-labelled blind to arm, over 60 real turns, on production's model
(dolphin3:8b). Nobody had ever measured this stage; the adjacent figures in the
repo all belong to other paths.

THE HEADLINE: the extractor is 43% PRECISE on its existing population, and the
broken axis is ATTRIBUTION, not extraction.

    baseline (arm A, pre-cye6 gate and prompt), n=60
      SUPPORTED   92%   the fact IS in the sentence
      ATTRIBUTED  45%   the subject is who the sentence is about
      PRECISION   43%   (both)
      MISATTRIB   15%   filed on the WRONG person

The model almost never fabricates. It gets the SUBJECT wrong more than half the
time. So better than half of everything this stage writes into the store is a
true statement filed against the wrong person — which is the failure 4g9w, qhej
and hhdr have all been circling from different sides, now with a number on it.

THE DOMINANT FAILURE MODE, and it is one shape, seen in ~40 of the 125
misattributions: SPEECH-ACT FRAMING. Given a character's line about the user, the
model writes a fact about THE SPEAKER instead of about the person spoken about:

  "but you don't have the mathematical formalism."
    -> "Dr. Mari Zielinska points out the user lacks mathematical rigor"
       subject: Mari                            (the fact is about the USER)

  "you built a system around the bug instead of pretending you'll stop being you"
    -> "The character has developed a workaround for their tendency to make
        mistakes"    subject: Dr. Mari Zielinska
       (this is TC building the Extender around his ADHD — a real, load-bearing
        user fact, recorded as a fact about Mari)

  "the philosophy department rejected the word multiverse as nonsensical and you
   walked out."  -> "Dr. Mari Zielinska left the philosophy department"
       (the USER walked out)

  "you watched an RPG-7 come at your vehicle."
    -> "The character witnessed an RPG-7 heading towards their vehicle."
       subject: "character"

The prompt ALREADY says "attribute by content, not by block label". It does not
hold. This is the prompt law again: an instruction is the weakest rung, and the
model has proximity, not valence — the speaker's name is right there in the block
label and the subject slot wants a name.

SECOND FAILURE MODE, ~35 of the 125: the PLACEHOLDER SUBJECT. The model returns
"character", "[character]", "listener", "speaker", "unknown" instead of a name.
makeSubject correctly refuses these (q5pk is closed), so the fact is stored with
NO aboutness at all. Refusing is right; the loss is real:
  "The Domain shapes what you can know about reality"  -> subject "speaker"
  "i don't actually know what goes in biscuits"        -> subject "[character]"
  "Priya I love him so much"                           -> subject "[character]"
A real relationship fact, a real character trait and live worldbuilding, all
stored about nobody.

WHAT THE NEW PROMPT DID, and it is genuinely encouraging: the DIRECTION OF
ADDRESS block cut misattribution on the EXISTING population from 15% to 7% and
raised precision from 43% to 62%. Decomposed across three arms on the same
sentences:
      A  old gate + old prompt   43% precise, 15% misattributed
      C  new gate + old prompt   55% precise, 15% misattributed
      B  new gate + new prompt   62% precise,  7% misattributed
The prompt halved misattribution where the population was already understood. It
did NOT help on second-person lines (29% vs 31%, inside the 2-point noise band) —
it helps where it was not needed and does nothing where it was.

THE FIX IS NOT ANOTHER PROMPT LINE. Two rungs are available and neither has been
tried:

  RUNG 3, route-and-mark. A fact whose supporting sentence is second-person and
  whose subject is the SPEAKER is grammatically impossible — "you" never refers
  to the person saying it. In the [user] block the speaker is one known person so
  this is already enforced (enforceAddressDirection). In the [character] block the
  speaker is not currently known to classifyAmbient, only the roster is. IF THE
  SPEAKING CHARACTER WERE PASSED IN, the same arithmetic closes the ~40-case
  dominant failure mode outright, and it is available at the call site: api.ts
  already has characterName. That is the single highest-value change on this list.

  RUNG 2, refuse at the boundary. A subject that is not a name is already refused
  by makeSubject. What is NOT refused is a subject that names the SPEAKER of a
  second-person sentence. It could be.

NOT IN SCOPE, and deliberately so: raising SUPPORTED. 92% is fine and is not what
is hurting the store.

METHOD NOTE for whoever re-measures: precision must be reported PER POPULATION.
Blended, the wired arm scores 51% against baseline 43% and looks like a clean win;
per-population it is 62% on the old sentences and 29% on the new ones, and the
blend hides the entire trade. Bench: scripts/ambient-precision-bench.mjs (seeded,
quarantined, three arms) and scripts/bench-label.mjs (blind labelling).

RELATED: cye6 (the gate that this defect forced back to opt-in), 4g9w/qlib (the
subjects field this now has a use for), qhej + hhdr (the referent bleed, here
quantified at 15% of everything the stage writes), q5pk (the placeholder
population, refused at the boundary but still being produced at ~35 per 496).
acceptance_criteria: The speaking character is passed into classifyAmbient and a fact whose supporting sentence is second-person may not name its own speaker as subject — enforced in code, counted, surfaced on the [ME:ambient] line. Precision RE-MEASURED with the same bench, same seed, same labels vocabulary. Misattribution on the baseline population below 8%.
notes:
SLICE 2'S FIRST DATA POINT IS IN, and it redirects the slice. The sweep concluded
there is no cheap surface rule for the 43% baseline and that the lever is better
INPUT. The prompt block was the only input change ever measured to move anything -
and icke's arm D shows it does not move it alone: with the gate off it scores 28%
against the 43% baseline, worse than doing nothing.

IDENTITY DOES MOVE IT. Arm E - the same prompt plus a header naming who spoke the
block and that the persona is the user - reaches 60% attributed and 12%
misattributed against the baseline's 45% / 15%, in the shipping gate
configuration. Within-pass, where the contrast is clean, it moved precision 28% ->
45% and halved misattribution.

That puts the broken axis on the same footing this ticket already named. qs67 says
the failure is ATTRIBUTION, not extraction (92% supported, 45% attributed); arm E
says attribution recovers when the model is told who the participants are. The
misattributed items show why - the extractor takes a NAME as the subject
regardless of grammatical role, so a vocative ("Priya I love him so much" -> Priya
loves) and an object ("I make a sound into Thomas's chest" -> Thomas makes it)
both mis-file. Knowing the speaker resolves "I" and demotes a bare name from
subject-by-default.

Follow-up carrying the numbers and the exact measured prompt text: avii. It wants
scoping against 4g9w/qlib first - if SUBJECT becomes a real field, the prompt may
not be where this belongs.

title: Live tier-3 ambient routing is a DUPLICATE of resolveFactTarget and drifted within a day — still mints [about: X] prefixes, writes no subjects[]
description:
resolveFactTarget (facts.ts:73) carries the comment 'Mirrors the live tier-3 routing in api.ts'. That is exactly backwards as a safety property: there are TWO copies of the subject-routing rule, and qlib's fix (aboutness as a FIELD, not a prose prefix) landed only in the copy that the live per-turn path does not call.

api.ts:889 — the ordinary live turn — has its own inline routing block. It still does:

    summary = truncateSummary(`[about: \] \`)

and calls createEntryIfUnique with NO subjects[]. So every ambient fact captured from a live turn is written in the pre-qlib shape.

EVIDENCE, 2026-08-25: 1,552 entry files in the live store carry an [about:] prefix. The newest three were minted 10:37:47 and 13:13:52 (-0500), the last of them five minutes before shape boundary #1 (18:18:41Z). It stopped because TC has been in a work session, not because anything closed it — the code path is unchanged and armed.

Their subjects are 'She', 'I', and '[character]' — i.e. the q5pk population, still being created, by the one path makeSubject cannot see.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING: cye6's decision to admit second-person candidates was recommended on the explicit ground that 'subjects[] now exists to record the attribution, so a wrong call is visible and correctable rather than silently misfiled'. On this path it does not exist. Widening the candidate gate over a router that cannot record aboutness adds volume to a blind spot.

FIX, rung 1 (the failure cannot be represented): delete the inline block and call resolveFactTarget. One routing rule, one place. The duplicate is the defect — not the prefix, which is only what the duplicate drifted into.

NOT IN SCOPE: the 1,552 existing prefixed rows. Those are awgj's two-phase migration, which is blocked on qhej by TC's ruling and must stay that way.

RELATED: qlib (the fix that landed in the wrong copy), q5pk (the placeholder population being recreated), cye6 (blocked on this), awgj (the backfill).
acceptance_criteria: api.ts tier-3 has no routing logic of its own; it calls resolveFactTarget. A live ambient fact is written with subjects[] and no [about:] prefix. Test pins that the live path and resolveFactTarget cannot disagree.
close_reason: Fixed in 0fa1819. api.ts tier-3 now calls resolveFactTarget; the inline duplicate is deleted. absorbAboutPrefix at createEntry's mint point makes the prefix unwritable — stripped, X moved into subjects[] via makeSubject (non-names refused and counted), absorption counted. 7 new tests in about-prefix.test.ts pin both the pure function and the storage boundary, including the nested [about: [character]] case (373 live entries) and the tier-2 [emotion] prefix that must survive untouched. 881 tests pass, tsc clean. The 1,552 existing prefixed rows are untouched — awgj's two-phase migration, still blocked on qhej.

title: A GET request silently MIGRATED a data directory — resolveIdentity mints and moves on unknown input, from a read-only endpoint
description:
CAUSED AND REPAIRED 2026-08-25. I did this to the live store while working ud30, and
the repair is done, but the hazard is real and unfixed.

WHAT I DID: GET /api/retired?characterId=professor_mari

'professor_mari' is an IDENTITY KEY, not a character card id. That endpoint calls
resolveIdentity(characterId, characterName), which for an unrecognised id MINTS A NEW
KEY and MIGRATES the existing data directory onto it:

    [identity] migrated data dir: professor_mari -> professor_mari_2
    [identity] registered: professor_mari -> "professor_mari_2"

Result: the entire professor_mari store (7,050 beats, 8,417 hot entries, 425 cold,
6,916 char-topics, 1,382 user-topics, 551 threads) was moved out from under its key,
a fresh empty scope was created in its place, and live capture began writing into the
empty one. Nineteen minutes later it had taken one real turn.

NOTHING WAS DESTROYED and it is fully repaired (scripts/repair-professor-mari-identity.mjs,
verified file-by-file against a backup of both scopes, zero missing, no duplicate index
rows, the one real turn folded back in). This ticket is about the MECHANISM, not the
incident.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT USER ERROR

1. A GET MUTATED PERSISTENT STATE. Read endpoints must not create identities or move
   directories. Whatever the argument was, a read is the wrong place to discover it.

2. THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND SUCCEEDS. The request returned 200 with a plausible empty
   result. There is no error, no warning in the response, and the only evidence is two
   lines in a log nobody was reading. I did not notice for thirteen minutes, and only
   then because an unrelated query returned 0 rows.

3. THE INPUT WAS PLAUSIBLE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. Identity keys and card ids are
   both opaque strings, both appear in this codebase's paths and logs, and
   'professor_mari' is the string a person reads off the data directory. An interface
   that accepts either and silently treats one as the other will keep being handed the
   wrong one. Note the store ALREADY holds three card ids mapping to professor_mari
   (__professor_mari__, Z4MZQbJLgLF, Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ) — so the distinction is
   load-bearing and invisible at the call site.

4. IT IS ALREADY A KNOWN HAZARD, recorded in bd memory
   (demo-test-sidecar-rule-learned-the-hard-way): 'resolveIdentity() would CREATE map
   entries and migrate data dirs for unknown IDs — unacceptable in a dry run.' The
   knowledge existed; the guard did not. That is the advisory-guard shape one level up:
   the danger was DOCUMENTED rather than PREVENTED.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIXES, ranked by the house law (close it structurally first)

  RUNG 1 — the bad state cannot be represented. Give the two id kinds distinguishable
    shapes, or take an explicit discriminator, so 'identity key passed as card id' is
    a type error rather than a silent migration. Biggest change; check whether the
    Engine's card ids have a stable shape first (they look like 21-char nanoids —
    'Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ' — while identity keys are snake_case slugs, which may be
    enough to tell them apart cheaply).

  RUNG 2 — refuse at the boundary. resolveIdentity gains a READ-ONLY mode, and every
    GET uses it: resolve if known, 404 if not, NEVER mint. Only explicitly
    write-intent paths (a real turn arriving for a new character) may create. This is
    the smallest correct fix and probably the one to ship first.

  RUNG 3 — if it must mint from a read, say so loudly in the RESPONSE, not the log.

  ALSO: an id that already EXISTS AS AN IDENTITY KEY should never be treated as an
  unknown card id. That single check would have refused this exact call, and it is
  three lines.

ACCEPTANCE: no GET can create an identity or move a directory; passing an existing
identity key where a card id is expected is refused rather than migrated; a regression
test covers exactly the call that caused this (characterId=professor_mari).

RELATED: ud30 (what I was building when it happened), wct1 (the retirements that
survived it intact), and the demo-sidecar memory that documented the hazard years
before it bit.

title: 4g9w slice 1: SUBJECT as a real field — stop encoding aboutness in the summary string
description:
IMPLEMENTATION SLICE of 4g9w, opened 2026-08-25 at TC's direction. 4g9w is the design
and stays open as the parent; this is the first shippable piece.

WHY THIS ONE. Five open P1s are the same missing field wearing different hats — qhej
(user_topics cannot say WHICH Thomas), su6h (extraction anti-correlated with evidence),
hhdr (referent bleed across the user/character membrane), 0qx6 (persona tier, which
4g9w says must not be built as a fourth SCOPE), cye6 (direction-of-address has nowhere
to put the subject it resolves). None of them can be closed properly without an
aboutness axis, and patching any of them individually means writing rules. This is the
structural close, per TC's house law: prefer the shape in which the failure cannot be
expressed.

BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT THIS SLICE DOES: it does NOT close those five. It gives them the
axis they are all blocked on. Each still needs its own work afterwards.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE FIELD ALREADY EXISTS — AS PROSE. THAT IS THE BUG.

resolveFactTarget (facts.ts) already computes aboutness and, when it cannot resolve the
subject to a character key, writes it into the SUMMARY TEXT as a '[about: X]' prefix.
3,380 entries carry one. So the code has wanted this field all along and has been faking
it in a string — the exact copy-instead-of-pointer shape TC ruled against for cards on
the same day.

Of those 3,380, only ~612 carry a usable name. The other 2,768 are q5pk's placeholder
garbage ('character', '[character]', bare pronouns, 'unknown'). Small migration, total
proof of need.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE — two decisions made deliberately, both recorded here because they are hard to
reverse across a serialization boundary

    interface SubjectRef {
      name: string;                                        // as observed in source
      key?: string;                                        // canonical entity/identity key when resolvable
      kind?: 'user' | 'persona' | 'character' | 'third-party';
    }
    subjects?: SubjectRef[];   // on Entry, IndexEntry, CreateEntryInput

  DECISION 1 — AN ARRAY FROM DAY ONE, even though the common case is one subject.
  4g9w lists 'one subject or several?' as open ('Mari and Priya argued' is about both).
  Adding an OPTIONAL field is backward-compatible here — citesChatId and bodyTerms both
  did it — but CHANGING ITS TYPE later is not, and this codebase has already been
  burned by exactly that (the EntryStatus audit: storage layers parse-and-cast with no
  runtime validation, so a changed shape round-trips silently). Array costs nothing now
  and removes the migration entirely.

  DECISION 2 — NAME AND KEY ARE SEPARATE FIELDS, never one string. Mixing resolved keys
  and raw observed names in a single field is 'cannot tell which', which is the shape
  this project keeps getting hurt by. It is also the card-pointer discipline applied
  again: keep what was OBSERVED separate from what it RESOLVED TO. It matters
  practically because entities.yaml has no refresh trigger (89l3), so resolution
  legitimately fails for new entities and must be distinguishable from 'never tried'.

  'kind' is the field that actually serves qhej and 0qx6: user vs persona vs character
  is precisely the distinction that put TC in Texas. Optional in this slice, populated
  only where it is known for certain.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCOPE — SLICE 1 ONLY

  IN
    1. SubjectRef + subjects?: on Entry, IndexEntry, CreateEntryInput.
    2. A subject-validity guard that REFUSES non-names at the boundary — placeholder
       tokens ('character', '[character]'), bracketed literals, bare pronouns,
       'unknown'. This closes q5pk structurally rather than by cleanup: the bad state
       stops being representable. Rejections COUNTED and logged, not silently dropped
       (advisory-guards-do-no-work).
    3. resolveFactTarget emits the field instead of the '[about: X]' summary prefix.
    4. Tests, including the q5pk placeholder population as fixtures.

  OUT — deliberately, each its own slice
    - Migrating the ~612 existing prefixed entries (needs a disposition for the 2,768).
    - Any retrieval/relevance change. The field is written and not yet read.
    - Backfilling subjects onto the rest of the store.
    - cye6's direction-of-address, which CONSUMES this field once it exists.

  The 'absent means unknown, never means none' rule from bodyTerms applies: an entry
  with no subjects field has not been assessed, and must never be read as 'about nobody'.

ACCEPTANCE: subjects survives a write/read round-trip on both Entry and IndexEntry;
no new entry can be written with a non-name subject; the rejection rate is visible in
logs; no '[about:' prefix is written into a summary any more; existing entries without
the field behave exactly as before.

PARENT: 4g9w. UNBLOCKS (does not close): qhej, su6h, hhdr, 0qx6, cye6. RELATED: q5pk
(closed structurally by item 2), 76aw (entity index supplies the keys), 89l3 (that
index has no refresh trigger).
notes:
SLICE 1 SHIPPED 2026-08-25 on branch 4g9w-subject-field. 840 tests pass (+37), tsc clean.

WHAT LANDED
  src/subject.ts (new)  SubjectRef { name, key?, kind? }, the validity guard, and
                        refusal counters by reason.
  storage.ts            subjects?: SubjectRef[] on BOTH Entry and IndexEntry.
  dedup.ts              subjects on CreateEntryInput; createEntry normalizes once and
                        writes to the entry file and the index row.
  facts.ts              resolveFactTarget returns the field; the '[about: X]' summary
                        prefix is no longer written. Refusals logged per run.
  __tests__/subject.test.ts (new, 37 tests) using the live q5pk population as fixtures.

TWO THINGS THE TESTS CAUGHT THAT REASONING DID NOT
  1. Two existing scene-facts tests asserted the OLD prose-prefix contract. They were
     updated to assert the new one, not deleted — they are the regression fence.
  2. readEntry takes the index row's relative PATH, not an id. My first round-trip test
     read the entry file with an id, got undefined, and looked exactly like a
     serialization bug in writeEntry. It was not: writeEntry spreads the whole entry and
     strips nothing. Worth remembering before anyone 'fixes' writeEntry.

NOT DONE, each its own slice
  - Migrating the ~612 real '[about: X]' prefixes into the field.
  - A disposition for the 2,768 placeholder-tagged entries (q5pk's existing population;
    the guard stops new ones, it does not clean old ones).
  - Populating kind beyond 'user' and 'character'. Notably ingestSceneFacts still has no
    personaName field, so resolveFactTarget's persona branch remains dead code on that
    path — that is why 68 '[about: Thomas]' entries exist and why kind='persona' is never
    emitted in production yet. That gap is qhej's half.
  - Nothing READS subjects yet. Retrieval, the confound sweep, and cye6's
    direction-of-address all consume it later.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
COUNTS IN THE DESCRIPTION ARE WRONG — corrected 2026-08-25, see q5pk for the full
reconciliation. '3,380 entries carry a prefix' and '~612 usable names' were GREP HITS,
double-counted across the entry file and its index row plus stale .tmp and receipts
copies. The real figures:

    1,494  DISTINCT entries carry an [about: X] prefix
      181  have a VALID name (89 distinct subjects) -> the migration list (awgj)
    1,313  are non-names (1,237 placeholder, 74 pronoun, 2 bracketed) -> q5pk

Nothing about the SHIPPED CODE changes — the guard classifies by value, not by count.
What changes is the size of the migration, which is ~3.4x smaller than advertised.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CARDINALITY CORRECTED 2026-08-25 (second time today, same root cause). Any "68
[about: Thomas]" above is a GREP-HIT count and is wrong. Reconciled by parsing:

    23  DISTINCT ENTRIES with subject exactly "Thomas"   <- the real number
     3  "Thomas Collier"   2  "real-thomas"   2  "thomas"   1  "Thomas" + apostrophe
    31  total distinct entries whose subject contains "thomas"

The 73 raw hits decompose as: 23 entry files + 23 index rows + 14 receipts/ copies
+ 12 BEAT TEXT quoting the tag syntax (Mari pasting a store audit back into the
conversation — not entries at all) + 1 supersession-candidates.yaml. Note also that
grep -o counts OCCURRENCES rather than files, so even per-bucket figures are matches.

THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE BECAUSE ANYTHING WAS RECOUNTED BY HAND. 22 came out of the
corrected census — the same run that produced 181/1,494. The error was that the
headline number was corrected and this sub-number was left standing in these notes,
so two figures for one population were published side by side. Restating every
derived count when a census is corrected is the actual discipline that was missing.

TWO THINGS THIS EXPOSED:
  1. THE CASE VARIANTS ARE A MIGRATION DECISION, not noise. FIVE distinct subject
     strings for one referent across 31 entries: "Thomas" 23, "Thomas Collier" 3,
     "real-thomas" 2, "thomas" 2, and one possessive form. (This line first said
     four-across-29 while listing five — corrected.) awgj must decide whether they normalize to a
     single subject — and "Thomas Collier" is the delicate one, because
     user-identity.yaml EXCLUDES that form from TC by declaration.
  2. IT IS A LEAK RATE, NOT A CONSTANT. The census counted 22 at ~12:40; the parse
     counted 23 forty minutes later. The old dist keeps minting prefixed rows until
     the sidecar is cycled. The 181 and 1,313 figures are timestamps, not totals.

The two follow-ups this ticket listed as separate slices both already exist as their own issues — awgj (migrate the valid prefixes, ruled to run LAST, after qhej) and q5pk (disposition for the placeholder-subject population). Nothing dangling; the axis the five blocked P1s needed now exists.

title: The live ambient gate is blind to SECOND PERSON — 15,681 sentences (32% of what it could see) discarded for addressing the user directly
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 while answering TC's question 'did it not get recorded because it was
in the character card?'. The answer is no, and chasing it down found the actual mechanism
behind su6h's omission half.

extractCandidates (ambient.ts) pre-filters every LIVE turn to candidate sentences before
the LLM ever sees them. A sentence survives only if it matches ONE of two patterns:

    FIRST_PERSON_RE   /\b(I|my|me|we|our|I'm|I've|I'd|I'll)\b/i
    NAMED_SUBJECT_RE  /^[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)?\s+(is|was|said|told|...)/

There is no SECOND PERSON. Not 'you', not 'your', not "you're". So the gate can see a
character talking about THEMSELVES, and a character talking about a THIRD PARTY BY NAME,
and is structurally incapable of seeing a character talking TO THE USER ABOUT THE USER —
which is the single most common way a fact about the user gets stated in a roleplay.

MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE STORE (164,733 sentences, all characters):

    inside the length/question window        118,405
    PASS the person test                      33,411   28.2%
    DROPPED though second-person              15,681   13.2%

    → the gate throws away 31.9% of the sentences it could otherwise have
      admitted, purely for addressing the user directly.

THE WORKED CASE — Thomas's origin (su6h). 23 origin-sense sentences in the store; run
them through the live gate and 3 survive, none of which actually states the origin (they
pass on incidental 'my'/'we'). Every clear statement dies, and most die INSIDE the length
window, on the person test alone:

    68ch  DROP  "you're from independence, missouri, dead center of the dialect zone."
    81ch  DROP  "sweeping every field: description is independence MO, army vet, ..."
    23ch  DROP  "Independence, Missouri."
    36ch  DROP  "A kitchen in independence, missouri."
    96ch  DROP  "Who played timpani and keyboard percussion in a high school band
                  room in Independence, Missouri."

That 81-char line is Mari READING THOMAS'S CHARACTER CARD ALOUD into the transcript on
2026-07-29 — the card's own text, in the beat stream, inside the length window, dropped
for saying 'description is' instead of 'I am'.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WHAT THIS IS *NOT*, so the next person does not re-litigate it

  NOT the card. The sidecar has never fetched a card (zero references to
  /api/characters anywhere in src/) so the card cannot have suppressed anything.
  That was the hypothesis under test; it is refuted.

  NOT the extractor, and NOT the judge. Run TODAY against the real beat text,
  classifySceneFacts produces the origin fact and judgeDurableFacts KEEPS it —
  3 for 3, including a clean 'Thomas is a former satellite technician from
  Independence, Missouri, and his surname is Collier.' Both stages work. They are
  simply never reached on the live path.

  NOT scene-facts either. ingestSceneFacts has exactly three call sites
  (api.ts:907 long user story, :1278 chat import, :1517 story jobs). None is the
  ordinary live turn. Live turns go through the tier-3 classifyAmbient path, and
  that is where this gate sits.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY ADDING you|your TO THE REGEX

Two reasons, both hard:

  1. IT WOULD WIDEN THE SCOPE OF EVERY DOWNSTREAM PRECISION NUMBER. Admitting
     15,681 more sentences is a ~47% increase in candidates reaching the ambient
     LLM. Every precision figure downstream was measured WITHOUT them. This is
     exactly the 'rule breadth survives its scope' failure already recorded in
     bd memory (code-filter's shell-command rule measured safe at chunk level,
     then ate blockquotes and dialogue once per-line routing widened it). Widening
     invalidates the measurement and requires re-measuring, not assuming.

  2. SECOND PERSON IS DIRECTIONAL AND THE GATE HAS NO SPEAKER. 'you're from
     Independence' said BY a character means the fact is about THE USER. The same
     words said BY the user mean the fact is about THE CHARACTER. extractCandidates
     takes a bare string and has no idea who is talking, so admitting second person
     without threading the speaker through would produce referent bleed at scale —
     the exact hhdr/qhej failure that put TC in Texas. The speaker IS available at
     the call site; the function just never receives it.

So the real work is SPEAKER-AWARE ATTRIBUTION: admit second person, and use the
direction of address to assign the subject. That is the fix. The regex edit is the
trap.

SUGGESTED FIRST SLICE, measure-first per house law: thread the speaker into
extractCandidates and emit the second-person candidates to a REPORT ONLY — do not feed
them to the LLM or write anything. Count how many are about the user vs about a
character, and sample the disagreements. That number sizes the fix and is not yet known.

ACCEPTANCE: second-person sentences reach the ambient extractor with a correct subject,
downstream precision RE-MEASURED at the new scope (not inherited), and the Independence
case captured end to end as the regression fixture.

RELATED: su6h (this is the mechanism behind its omission half — the anti-correlation is
explained by the gate seeing self-description and missing being-described), qhej + hhdr
(referent bleed — the failure mode a naive fix would amplify), opyv (reading the cards
would have caught the same fact by a different route; both fixes are worth having),
4g9w (SUBJECT vs SCOPE — the structural home for direction-of-address).
notes:
ICKE ANSWERED THE OPEN QUESTION, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Arm D - old gate + the
DIRECTION OF ADDRESS prompt, the configuration that would actually ship - scores
28% precision against the shipped baseline's 43%, and misattribution rises 15% ->
22%. The prompt block does not ship with the gate off. Pulling it in fe71f9f was
correct and it stays out.

The 62% arm B scored was a JOINT effect of the wide gate and the prompt. Neither
half carries it alone: C (wide gate, old prompt) is 55%, D (old gate, new prompt)
is 28%. Only together do they reach 62%, and the gate half already failed its own
bar in slice 3.

The verdict is immune to the labeller drift between the two labelling sessions,
because precision can never exceed the attributed rate and D's attributed rate is
40% - below A's measured 43% precision. D cannot beat the baseline under any
support standard.

So cye6 ends where slice 3 left it: the gate stays opt-in, and the prompt half it
was measured with does not follow it into the build. The finding, the code and the
tests all stand; what is refuted is the SHIP, not the observation.

The lever that did move the shipping configuration is identity - see avii.
close_reason: RESOLVED AS REFUTED — the observation stands, the ship does not. Arm D (old gate + DIRECTION OF ADDRESS prompt, the only configuration that would actually have shipped) scored 28% precision against the shipped baseline's 43%, with misattribution rising 15%->22%. The 62% that arm B reached was a JOINT effect: C (wide gate, old prompt) 55%, D (old gate, new prompt) 28% — neither half carries it alone. The verdict survives the labeller drift between the two labelling sessions, because precision can never exceed the attributed rate and D's attributed rate is 40%, below A's measured 43% precision: D cannot beat baseline under any support standard. So the second-person gate stays OPT-IN and the prompt half does not follow it into the build (pulling it in fe71f9f was correct). The finding, the code and the tests all stand as the record of why. The lever that DID move the shipping configuration is identity — see avii. NOTE: the cye6->qs67 dependency was removed before closing rather than forced, because the refutation makes it moot — cye6 was going to build ON qs67's attribution fix and there is now nothing to build. su6h, which depended on this, is thereby unblocked, but its path via the gate is dead and it should be re-approached from the identity direction.

title: Read the cards: personas and character cards are BASE FACT and the sidecar has never read either
description:
RULING (TC, 2026-08-25): 'Personas and character cards should be treated as base
fact.' Cards are authoritative ground truth, not another corroboration source. A
derived entry contradicting a card loses to the card; a fact stated in a card needs no
further attestation.

THE SIDECAR HAS NEVER READ THEM. Both are plain HTTP on the Engine it already polls
every 5 seconds:

    GET /api/characters                    character cards ( .data is a JSON string )
    GET /api/characters/personas/list      personas
    GET /api/characters/personas/active    the active one

Verified live 2026-08-25 against the running 2.4.3.

ONE RULE FIXES A FABRICATION AND AN OMISSION THAT LOOK LIKE OPPOSITE BUGS. Both
halves of su6h's anti-correlation were checked against the cards the same day:

  KRAKOW (fabrication). Mari's character card (Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ) contains
  'Polish' and does NOT contain Krakow anywhere. The store nonetheless holds
  ctopic-82p9tylw, 'Dr. Mari Zielinska's identity as a researcher from Krakow', with
  ZERO supporting source text — it took a hand audit to deny it on 05.08, and the
  denial is still sitting beside the claim rather than replacing it. A card check
  would have refused it at write time, months earlier, with no audit at all.

  INDEPENDENCE (omission). Thomas's persona card (T5qPktvQZjpwWxMFWx1DA) reads
  'Thomas Collier: 26, white, 5'10, from Independence, MO, Army veteran (satellite
  technician)'. The store recorded that origin ZERO times despite 21 RP assertions.
  It was in a structured authoritative field the whole time.

EVERY CORROBORATION TEST IN THIS PROJECT HAS A HOLE WHERE THE CARDS SHOULD BE, and
this is the general form of the n9bv Porsche note. Scoring a claim 'uncorroborated'
against beat text alone measures 'nobody said it in a logged turn' and reports it as
'it is not true in this world'. Those are different claims and only the first has ever
been measured. Anything that adjudicates truth — rejectAsEcho's escape hatch, the
thread-label corroboration check, fact-support scanning, the reconcile curator —
should be re-examined once cards are readable.

DESIGN NOTES, and the hard parts:

  1. BASE FACT IS NOT THE SAME AS TRUE-EVERYWHERE. Cards are authoritative about the
     entity they describe, in the contexts that entity is played. They are not global
     truth. Mark's Porsche is base fact about Mark; it says nothing about TC.

  2. PERSONAS ARE SCOPED (TC, same ruling). Mark exists ONLY to interact with Lara and
     interacts with no other character. So a persona card is not a global user fact —
     it is a fact about a persona, valid in that persona's chats. This is the axis
     0qx6 and 4g9w are both missing, now with a concrete containment rule to model.

  3. AND IT NESTS. Within the context of Mari, Mark is a FICTIONAL CHARACTER WRITTEN
     BY TC, not a person who lived any of it. Same entity, different ontological
     status depending on which chat it appears in — 7pcm case (b) exactly. Card-as-
     base-fact must not launder Mark's biography into Mari's ledger as lived
     experience; in that context the base fact is 'TC wrote a character called Mark',
     not 'Mark was in Iraq'.

  4. CARDS DRIFT. They are edited. A fact seeded from a card should record that it
     came from one (and which version), or the store will hold stale base facts with
     no way to tell them from attested ones. personaVersion exists on the persona
     payload; character cards carry their own versioning.

  5. DO NOT BULK-BACKFILL ON DAY ONE. Seeding every card field as a fact would write
     hundreds of entries into a store whose decay clock was only just fixed (gwny) and
     whose lanes cannot yet say which persona a fact belongs to (0qx6/4g9w). Read
     first, adjudicate against what is already there, and measure the disagreement
     before writing anything.

SUGGESTED FIRST SLICE, cheap and diagnostic rather than structural: fetch the cards
and REPORT the disagreements — every derived entry that contradicts a card, and every
card fact absent from the store. That number is the size of the problem and nobody has
it. It writes nothing.

RELATED: su6h (both halves), 0qx6 (persona tier), 4g9w (subject vs scope), 7pcm
(fiction provenance), n9bv (the corroboration corpus hole), uwyf (Krakow audit),
fqnl (provenance).
design:
RULING (TC, 2026-08-25): STORE A POINTER, NOT A COPY.

When a card states a fact, do not extract that fact into the store as its own
entry. Store a REFERENCE to the card field it came from, stamped with the card's
version, so the correct date is recoverable if the card later changes.

WHY THIS IS THE STRONGER FORM, and not just a storage detail:

  1. A COPY DRIFTS; A POINTER CANNOT. TC edits cards. A fact copied out of a card
     on 06-03 and a card edited on 08-21 are two different claims wearing the same
     words, and nothing in the store can tell them apart. A pointer always reads
     current.
  2. IT CLOSES jagj's LAUNDERING LOOP AT THE SOURCE. 'A copy cannot corroborate its
     source' is already house law. A copied card fact looks like independent
     attestation the moment it is one row among many; a pointer is self-evidently
     the card itself and can never be miscounted as corroboration OF the card.
  3. IT MAKES CARD EDITS AUDITABLE FOR FREE. Every pointer carries the version it
     was written against, so after an edit the stale ones are a query, not an
     archaeology project. This is the versioning coupling already flagged in the
     description, satisfied by construction rather than by discipline.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
MEASURED FIELD INVENTORY (live Engine 2.4.3, 2026-08-25) — everything needed exists

  GET /api/characters            9 cards
    outer: id, data, comment, avatarPath, spriteFolderPath, embedding,
           createdAt, updatedAt
    data (JSON string, v2 card spec): name, description, personality, first_mes,
           scenario, mes_example, creator_notes, system_prompt,
           post_history_instructions, tags, creator, character_version,
           alternate_greetings, extensions, character_book

  GET /api/characters/personas/list   4 personas
    name, personaVersion, versioningEnabled, description, personality, scenario,
    backstory, appearance, creator, creatorNotes, tags, isActive,
    createdAt, updatedAt, id

  Thomas persona: personaVersion 1.2, versioningEnabled true, updated 2026-08-21,
  id T5qPktvQZjpwWxMFWx1DA. description opens 'Thomas Collier: 26, white, 5'10,
  from Independence, MO, Army veteran (satellite technician).'

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE VERSION FIELD IS NOT A DATE, AND updatedAt IS NOT PROOF OF AN EDIT

TC's instruction was to note the version 'so you get the correct date'. Both halves
of that need care, and neither is free:

  character_version IS AUTHOR-MAINTAINED. It is a v2-card-spec string TC bumps by
  hand. Observed: 1.0.2, 1.0.1, 1.0, 1.0.3 — and TWO OF NINE CARDS HAVE NO VERSION
  AT ALL (Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, Aurora). Priya is a primary character. So a
  design that keys on the version alone has no key for two of the cards that matter
  most, and silently gets a stale one whenever an edit ships without a bump.
  personaVersion is better — all four personas carry one and versioningEnabled is
  true on all four.

  updatedAt MOVES FOR REASONS THAT ARE NOT CONTENT EDITS. Stephanie Collins, Alice
  Chen and Alex Navarro all read exactly 2026-07-16; Priya and Mari both read
  2026-08-25. Identical timestamps across unrelated cards are the signature of a
  batch write, not of three independent hand edits — and 2.4.3 added embedding
  columns to this table, which is a plausible toucher. NOT PROVEN, stated as the
  reason not to trust the field: verify against the Engine source before relying
  on updatedAt to date anything.

  THEREFORE THE POINTER CARRIES THREE THINGS, not one: the card/persona id and
  field path; the declared version (character_version / personaVersion); and a
  CONTENT HASH of the field text as read. The hash is the only one of the three
  that cannot lie about whether the content changed. Version answers 'which
  revision did the author intend', updatedAt answers 'when did the row move', hash
  answers 'is this still the text I read' — keep all three and do not collapse them.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DO NOT TRIGGER THE CARD READ ON A PHRASE — MEASURED, AND IT DOES NOT WORK

The idea arose from beat-39fe8fbb7da3 (2026-07-29), where Mari reads Thomas's card
aloud: 'sweeping every field: description is independence MO, army vet, eternal
optimist.' Scanning all 9,472 beats for that shape:

     4  'description is'        <- only ONE is a card readout; the other three are
                                   'the grader description is so specific', 'a
                                   raspberry pi whose job description is still
                                   UNKNOWN', 'the one thing whose job description
                                   is a standing death threat'
     1  'sweeping every field'
    11  'backstory is'          <- mostly ordinary prose about story craft
     2  'personality is'
    99  'character card'
    10  'the card says'
     8  'your card'

One true positive on the proposed trigger, at 25% precision, from a population of
one. That is the unsystematic-search failure mln9 is a standing warning about, and
a literal-phrase gate is the keyword rule that ticket banned.

AND THE TRIGGER IS UNNECESSARY. Reading a card is a single unauthenticated GET
against 127.0.0.1 that the sidecar already talks to every 5 seconds. There is no
cost to gate. Read the cards on a cadence (and on demand), cache by content hash,
and the readout beat stops being a trigger and becomes what it always was — one
more piece of transcript. If a card readout is worth detecting at all it is for
provenance (the card was demonstrably in context at that time), which is a
different and much weaker requirement than 'this is how we learn the card exists'.

ACCEPTANCE ADDENDUM: no card-sourced fact is written as a standalone entry; each is
a pointer carrying {cardId | personaId, field path, declared version, content hash,
read-at timestamp}; a card edit makes every pointer written against the prior hash
queryable in one pass; and the two version-less cards (Priya, Aurora) are handled
explicitly rather than defaulting to a stale or empty version.

title: Extraction is ANTI-correlated with evidence: Thomas's origin stated 21 times in RP, recorded 0 times; Mari's Krakow stated 0 times, recorded as fact
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at TC's instruction to extend the Krakow method to RP SOURCE TEXT,
not just derived fields. 9,453 beats scanned.

THE PAIR IS THE FINDING. Two origin facts, opposite evidence, opposite outcomes:

                        stated in RP source text    recorded as a derived fact
  Thomas: Independence MO          21                          0
  Mari:   Krakow                    0                          1  (still live)

The extractor produced a biography nobody asserted and failed to produce one asserted
twenty-one times. That is not low recall — recall that misses hard cases is ordinary.
This is ANTI-CORRELATED with the evidence, which is a different and worse property,
and neither number is visible from inside the system.

INDEPENDENCE, MISSOURI — 21 ORIGIN ASSERTIONS IN SOURCE TEXT. 35 beats contain the
string; classified by sense: 21 origin, 6 'Independence Day' (July 4th homonym),
8 abstract noun ('finger independence', 'independence of witness', 'backup requires
independence'). The origin set is unambiguous — 'you grew up there', 'your hometown',
'you're from independence, missouri, dead center of the dialect zone', 'Thomas
Collier, former satellite technician, Independence, Missouri', 'a kitchen in
independence, missouri', 'his desk in Independence', 'Your parents I want to meet.
Independence, Missouri.'

DERIVED: 2 entries mention it, NEITHER as biography.
  recap-q80a6ope   a scene recap, incidental ('Thanksgiving in Independence')
  utopic-5g4dz5e9  records his IDIOLECT (perfer/prefer) and cites 'Independence MO =
                   Midland zone' as EVIDENCE FOR THE DIALECT, not as where he is from
So the store knows his dialect is Midland because of where he is from, and does not
know where he is from. The premise was used and discarded.

WHO SAYS IT MATTERS, and is the likeliest mechanism. Of the 21:
    13  Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran
     3  Dr. Mari Zielińska
     2  Narrator
     1  Mari
     2  user            <- only two typed by TC himself
The persona's biography is established almost entirely IN THE CHARACTERS' MOUTHS. If
the fact lane privileges user-spoken statements when deciding what is true about the
user/persona, it would omit exactly this population. STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A
FINDING — it fits the numbers and has not been tested. Test it before building on it;
the Krakow case is a standing warning about confident stories that fit.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES THE OMISSION WORSE, from TC: Thomas is the IN-CHARACTER PERSONA,
distinct from TC the real person. TC is from Nodaway County; Thomas is from
Independence and keeps an apartment in the Iowa town where Prescott State is. The
store records TC's home county and NOT the persona's origin — so the half that is
purely in-fiction, and therefore only knowable from the RP, is the half that was
dropped. Also note beat-3539625477c3 names him 'Thomas Collier', and
data/user-identity.yaml EXCLUDES 'thomas collier' from TC by declaration. The membrane
is declared and the extractor still lost the persona's side of it.

AND THE STORE HOLDS BOTH SIDES OF ITS OWN CONTRADICTIONS. ctopic-82p9tylw still reads
'Dr. Mari Zielińska's identity as a researcher from Kraków' while ctopic-anvpzajo

title: user_topics cannot say WHICH Thomas — three Texas entries about the persona filed as facts about the human (a 4g9w specimen)
description:

Texas. Checking that against the store turned up three entries that say otherwise —
all live, all retrievable, all false.

    utopic-j8itu2vd  'User likely lives in Texas'                          status: open
    utopic-ntgxdp4b  'Lives in or has connection to Texas; unsure of weed
                      legality there'                                      status: open
    utopic-kftzlm70  'considers Texas warm in winter, implying familiarity
                      with colder climates'                                status: open

All three created 2026-06-02. All three in USER_TOPICS — the lane that means A FACT
ABOUT THE HUMAN.

THE SOURCE LINES ARE ROLEPLAY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Each entry carries the text
it came from, and none of it is TC talking about himself:

    '"At least Texas is warm in the winter." I say non-chalantly.'  -> kftzlm70

The second still has its narration attached ('I say non-chalantly') — it is a line in
a scene. The analyzer took a character's dialogue and filed it as biography of the
player. That is hhdr's REFERENT BLEED ACROSS THE USER/CHARACTER MEMBRANE, caught with
its receipt intact, and it is a cleaner specimen than hhdr's own example because the
source text is preserved and unambiguous.

THE STORE CONTRADICTS ITSELF AND CANNOT TELL. On 2026-08-04 it recorded
utopic-3vncpvcw: 'TC's home county = NODAWAY COUNTY, MISSOURI', and utopic-51q5g9vz
puts his wife's family in Kirksville, Missouri. Both true, both live, both sitting

WHY THIS IS NOT uwyf, though it was found while checking uwyf: ambient.ts:59 uses 'I

RESIDUAL RISK, not demonstrated: once these false facts exist, they could CORROBORATE
an echo of the ambient.ts Texas example, converting a safe off-planet example into a
corroboratable one. Bleed manufactures a false fact; the false fact then licenses an

read them, do not sweep), the Missouri record left intact, and a note on whether the

is the real question and it is UNSIZED — three is what one correction surfaced, which

fix that would make this class harder), 76aw (coreference), uwyf (corrected, not this).
