title: Entries are immortal by exposure — merely being LOADED resets the decay clock, so 4,242 hot entries can never age to cold
description:
FOUND 2026-08-24, answering TC's question 'are these entries staying in the hot lane
or decaying into cold like they are supposed to?'. They are staying hot, and the
mechanism that should age them is being reset by mere exposure.

THE MEASUREMENT (professor_mari, the live store):

    hot index                                       8,320
    cold index                                        420      hot:cold = 19.8:1
    hot entries >90d stale (i.e. cold-eligible)          17      0.2%
    hot entries sitting in the 60-90d band            4,052     48.7%

    never demonstrably used (no lastRetrievedAt)      7,237
      ...and never summoned (retrievalCount 0)        4,259
      ...yet decay clock reads <90d anyway            4,242   <- IMMORTAL BY EXPOSURE

So 51% of the hot index has never been judged relevant to anything, has never been
demonstrably used by the model, and still cannot age out.

THE CAUSE, and it is one line fighting the design around it. promotion.ts:

    function daysSinceRetrieval(entry) {
      const lastStr = entry.lastRetrievedAt ?? entry.lastAccessed;   <-- the fallback
      ...
    }

and loader.ts stamps lastAccessed on EVERY LOADED ENTRY, including entries that only
rode in on the recency fallback and were never topically relevant.

THE CODE ALREADY KNOWS THIS DISTINCTION MATTERS AND SAYS SO. loader.ts, verbatim:

    // stamp lastAccessed on every loaded entry; increment retrievalCount ONLY for
    // entries that were summoned (pulled in by topical relevance), not those that
    // merely rode in on the recency fallback. This is what keeps the promotion
    // signal honest: "was SUMMONED" earns credit, "was AROUND" does not.

    // lastRetrievedAt is NOT stamped here either way: being loaded (even when
    // summoned) is not the same as being used.

Both of those are deliberate and both are right. The bug is that daysSinceRetrieval
then FALLS BACK to the one field that is stamped unconditionally, which hands back
every bit of honesty the other two lines bought. 87% of hot entries have no
lastRetrievedAt at all, so for them the fallback IS the decay clock, and it is reset
by being in the room.

CONSEQUENCE: the hot index only grows. An entry loaded as filler once a month is
immortal; it never goes cold, so it keeps being available as filler, which re-stamps
it. That is a self-sustaining loop, and the 48.7% massed in the 60-90d band is what
it looks like from outside — not a natural age distribution but a population being
repeatedly pushed back from the edge.

DO NOT FIX BY DELETING THE FALLBACK. daysSinceRetrieval would then return Infinity
for the 7,237 entries with no lastRetrievedAt and the very next promotion pass would
move them ALL to cold in one shot. The fix is to fall back to the entry's CREATION
date instead: decay should measure time since last USE, and for something never used,
time since it was written. Never time since last incidentally loaded.

Note the index rows do NOT carry  (it lives on the entry file), so this
needs either a schema addition or a read of the file — size that before choosing.

MEASURE THE BLAST RADIUS BEFORE SHIPPING, per house law. Whatever fallback is chosen,
count how many entries move on the first pass. A change that relocates thousands of
entries in one tick is a migration, not a bug fix, and should be run deliberately
rather than discovered by a user whose recall suddenly changes shape.

RELATED: 3lru (sidecar reaching 1.5GB — an 8,320-row hot index that only ever grows
is a plausible contributor, and the two should be looked at together). wct1 (the
three changelog-derived companion entries are all HOT, and ctopic-sjwwu4lz has
already been retrieved once — a false memory that has been served).

VERIFY AFTERWARDS that recall still works: pe4o/41uo found retiring a beat did not
remove it from recall until that was fixed, and this touches the same boundary from
the other side.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-24 in loader.ts. NOT by the approach this ticket proposed — the
measurement said that approach was the wrong one, and the correction is the useful
part of this note.

WHAT SHIPPED: the loader no longer touches an entry that merely rode in on the
recency fallback. Previously it stamped lastAccessed on EVERY loaded entry while
gating only retrievalCount on relevance; now a non-summoned entry is skipped
entirely — no clock, no count, and no write at all.

    if (!summoned) return Promise.resolve();

That is one line, and it is the whole fix. lastRetrievedAt is still never written by
the loader: being loaded, even when summoned, is not being used, and that stays
recordRecitation's to write.

WHY NOT THE created-FALLBACK THIS TICKET RECOMMENDED. I proposed changing
daysSinceRetrieval to fall back to the entry's creation date. Measured against the
live store before writing any code, the two options are not close:

    stop bumping on non-summoned (shipped)   7 entries cold-eligible on the next
                                             pass — the SAME 7 as today. No cliff.
    created-fallback (proposed here)     7,009 entries cold-eligible at once.

The created-fallback also needs a schema change and a backfill, because IndexEntry
carries no `created` at all (it lives on the entry file). Leaving the field alone
reaches the same destination for free: lastAccessed is INITIALISED AT CREATION, so an
entry that is never summoned and never used simply keeps its creation date and ages
from there — which is exactly the semantics the fallback was trying to construct.

MIGRATION IS A CURVE, NOT A STEP. Existing lastAccessed values are untouched, so
nothing relocates today; entries age out only as they stop being summoned:

    already eligible      7
    within 30 days    3,401
    30-60 days        1,406
    60-90 days        2,472

A SECOND EFFECT, worth having on its own: skipping the write removes thousands of
identical-row index rewrites per turn. Every loaded entry used to be re-persisted
whether or not anything about it had changed. Relevant to 3lru (the 1.5GB peak) and
to 96eo (orphaned atomic-write temp files) — both plausibly fed by write volume on
this path, neither confirmed.

PINNED IN src/__tests__/decay-clock.test.ts, AND THE PINS WERE VERIFIED TO FAIL
against the old behaviour before being kept — 2 of the 4 do (the filler case and the
repeated-load loop); the other 2 are guards that must hold either way. That check
mattered here more than usual: the bug was silent in BOTH directions. The whole
suite passed with the behaviour wrong and passed again with it fixed, because no test
had ever pinned who is allowed to touch the clock. A test that cannot fail on the old
code would have been worth nothing.

Gates: tsc clean, 803 tests pass (799 + 4).

NOT DONE, and deliberately out of scope: the 4,242 entries that have already been
kept hot by the old behaviour are not relocated by this. They now age normally, which
takes up to 90 days from their last stamp. Retiring or force-ageing them is a
separate decision with its own blast radius, and pe4o/41uo's lesson applies — confirm
recall actually drops an entry before assuming a tier move removed it.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-24 in loader.ts, one line: a non-summoned entry is skipped entirely — no lastAccessed stamp, no count, no write. The ticket's own proposed created-date fallback was MEASURED AND REJECTED before any code: it would have made 7,009 entries cold-eligible in a single pass vs the shipped fix's 7 (the same 7 as before — no cliff), and needed a schema change plus a backfill. lastRetrievedAt stays recordRecitation's to write: being loaded, even when summoned, is not being used.

title: Possessive names are unmatchable — summary 'Thomas's' stores 'thomass' while the cue yields 'thomas' (15.1% of summaries)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while verifying vrw (which turned out to be already fixed). Same function, bigger live impact.

THE TWO SIDES OF THE SCORER TOKENIZE POSSESSIVES DIFFERENTLY.

  tokenize()      the CUE side:     "Thomas's"  ->  ["thomas", "s"]
                  strips punctuation TO SPACES, so the name survives.

  weightedTerms() the SUMMARY side: "Thomas's"  ->  "thomass"
                  strips punctuation TO NOTHING, welding the possessive s onto the name.

So a summary that says "Thomas's sister" stores the term "thomass", and no cue naming Thomas can ever match it. Demonstrated:

  relevanceScore("Becky is Thomas's sister", "Do you remember Thomas?")   = 0.000
  relevanceScore("Becky is the sister of Thomas", "Do you remember Thomas?") = 0.590

MEASURED ON THE LIVE STORE: 1256 of 8315 live professor_mari summaries carry a possessive name, 15.1%. The most affected are exactly the names that matter most:

    289  Thomas's        -> "thomass"     (the USER)
    251  Mari's          -> "maris"
    150  Priya's         -> "priyas"
     85  Zielinska's     -> "zielinskas"
     43  Aurora's        -> "auroras"
     39  Lara's          -> "laras"
     32  Opie's          -> "opies"
     18  Chandrasekaran's-> "chandrasekarans"
     18  Mal's           -> "mals"

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. It fails silently and in the safe-looking direction: the entry simply does not surface, which reads as "the model didn't recall it" rather than as a bug. It also cannot be found by reading either function alone - both are individually reasonable, and only the ASYMMETRY between them is wrong. That is the same shape as the sentence-case trap and the swipe blind spot: correct-looking code whose fault only appears when you check what can REACH what.

PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THE REPO: fact-support.ts strips the possessive explicitly before comparing - `w.replace(/['\u2019]s$/u, "")` - with a comment recording that a stray "s" defeated an exemption check and made a subject's own name convictable in her own fact. relevance.ts never got the same treatment.

FIX: strip the possessive in weightedTerms before punctuation is removed, handling both ' and \u2019. Note the token may also carry trailing punctuation ("Thomas's,").

SCOPE NOTE - THE SUMMARY FIX IS RETROACTIVE, THE BODY FIX IS NOT. Summary terms are computed from the summary at query time, so fixing weightedTerms immediately repairs matching for every existing entry with no migration. But harvestBodyTerms also runs through weightedTerms and its output is STORED on the index row, so already-harvested bodyTerms still hold the mangled forms and need a backfill - the same shape as tp5's scripts/backfill-body-terms.mjs.
acceptance_criteria: relevanceScore('Becky is Thomas\'s sister', 'Do you remember Thomas?') scores as a name match; a before/after measurement over the live index; bodyTerms backfill filed or done.
close_reason: Fixed in weightedTerms: the possessive is stripped before punctuation is removed, so 'Thomas\'s' yields 'thomas' at PROPER_NOUN_WEIGHT instead of the unmatchable 'thomass'. Measured on the live index — 'Do you remember Thomas?' goes from 554 to 1436 reachable entries, 'what did Mari decide' 4042 to 4907, 'tell me about Priya' 1119 to 1651. Top-of-ranking checked for regression and it improves: top 2 unchanged, and the tie tier swaps real Thomas content in over meta entries. 6 tests including plural-s and O'Brien guards; 781 total green. bodyTerms backfill is 7gkp.

title: Engine release notes pasted into chat become emotional beats — 3 on the current build
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while sampling beats for 5x5y. Marinara ENGINE RELEASE NOTES, pasted into a chat, are being chunked, scored for emotion, and filed as Mari's emotional beats.

Nine beats are built from changelog text. Their source is prose like:

  "Added first-class Audio connections: a new \"Audio\" provider type in Settings -> Connections carries the speech backend (ElevenLabs, OpenAI-compatible, PocketTTS, xAI Voice), base URL, API key, model, default voice..."

  "Added Lorebook Update agents can now optionally assign an integer injection order when creating or updating entries..."

and the analyzer dutifully produced, for example:

  emotion: shame
  motivation: "Dr. Mari Zielinska is experiencing shame for not catching a bug related to image storage and display paths, which was later fixed by her own work on Noodle images."

THIS IS NOT LEGACY RESIDUE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. Three of the nine are dated 2026-08-20 - yesterday, on the current build, well after pe4o (self-prompt gate) and hjt9 (ops lane) shipped in early August:

  2026-06-02  2l8p7jbdpw          anger
  2026-06-02  5hz98d5pc1          anger
  2026-06-03  beat-37faa0d37ec5   joy
  2026-06-03  beat-969b515cec10   vulnerability
  2026-06-04  beat-d7d767b27166   shame
  2026-06-22  beat-a39cf0d43085   anger
  2026-08-20  beat-4cf78d9e6f32   shame          <- current build
  2026-08-20  beat-61b2658165f9   vulnerability  <- current build
  2026-08-20  beat-6e75eeb7f8b6   shame          <- current build

WHY THE EXISTING GATES MISS IT. pe4o gates on OUR OWN PROMPT text, by coverage against ownPromptSignatures. Engine release notes are not our prompt, so no signature matches. hjt9's routeOps is built for code and structured payloads - shell transcripts, JSON, tables - and changelog prose is PROSE: full sentences, ordinary vocabulary, no fences, no code shape. It looks like writing because it is writing. Neither gate was built for "third-party product documentation pasted for discussion", and that is a real third category.

WHY IT MATTERS. These become companion ledger entries and are retrievable, so the character can later "remember feeling ashamed" about an Engine bug she has no relationship to. It is also the same family as the invented-partner problem (epf4): a record that reads as real experience and cannot be distinguished from one downstream, because by then the source is gone.

SIZE IT BEFORE FIXING IT. Nine is what one grep for three specific changelog openers found; the true count is unknown and the search was not systematic. The measure-first law applies - a detector tuned to nine hand-found examples will be tuned to the wrong distribution.

DO NOT reach for a keyword blocklist ("Added", "Fixed", "Changed"). Release notes have no fixed vocabulary and a blocklist would eat real sentences that open the same way. The likelier discriminators are structural: dense enumeration of proper nouns and product terms with no first or second person, no dialogue, and a speaker who is the USER pasting rather than a character speaking.
acceptance_criteria: A measured count of changelog-derived beats across the store, a discriminator that does not rely on a keyword blocklist, and no new such beats on the live path.
notes:
SIZED 2026-08-23 via scripts/changelog-scan.mjs (read-only). 9,437 beats across all
7 characters, both filename conventions. Candidate set was 8; all 8 hand-read.

THE TRUE COUNT IS 6, NOT 9 — and the nine were never one population.

Plus ONE THE ORIGINAL GREP MISSED: beat-2b6ff6f8480d (2026-06-22, joy, speaker
"Added stronger appearance customization"). 26 openers. That is what a
three-opener grep cannot see about its own coverage.

THE SIX:
  beat-37faa0d37ec5  2026-06-03  joy            speaker=user
  beat-d7d767b27166  2026-06-04  shame          speaker="Added Roleplay quick-edit gestures"
  beat-2b6ff6f8480d  2026-06-22  joy            speaker="Added stronger appearance customization"   <- NEW

  beat-61b2658165f9  2026-08-20  vulnerability  speaker=user            <- current build

character. None retired.

THE LIVE-PATH CLAIM SURVIVES, REDUCED: 2 on the current build, not 3. The third

rather than duplicating it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mln9's PREDICTED DISCRIMINATOR IS FALSIFIED. Stated plainly because the issue
asserts it and it is wrong.

Predicted: release notes show no first/second person, no dialogue, dense proper
nouns. Scored exactly that way, the 14 top-ranked beats contained ZERO changelogs —
they were code, logs, CLI transcripts and bd output (hjt9 / 4ghy populations,
already tracked) — while beat-a39cf0d43085, a plain Engine release-notes paste,
ranked 1666th of 9,433.

The reason: user-facing release notes ADDRESS THE READER ("customize your
experience", "so the scene art behind it is visible"). Their person-rate runs
HIGHER than ordinary chat. The predicted signal is not merely weak, it is inverted.

WHAT ACTUALLY SEPARATES THEM: the absolute count of sentence-initial enumeration
verbs in one chunk.
    6 true positives   4, 6, 20, 26, 36, 53
    every negative     0 or 1
Clean, no overlap, no tuning.

THIS IS NOT THE BLOCKLIST THE ISSUE FORBIDS, and the numbers say so: 33 beats
contain >=1 opener and would trip a presence rule; only 6 carry >=3. The other 27
are real RP dialogue and genuine work notes — a presence blocklist would have eaten
every one. Density is structure (enumerated list), presence is vocabulary. The ban
was right; it just banned the wrong reading of the same token.

A per-100-word RATE is also wrong, and inverted for the same reason as the person
rate: the clearest positive (3,544 words, 20 openers) scores 0.56/100w, BELOW a
224-word work note with a single "Added" at 0.45. Length dilutes the signal it
should confirm. Use the count.

COVERAGE WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Two independent nets: enumeration verbs (net A,
6 hits) and issue-reference density (net B, 5 hits), which fail differently. Net B
caught 2 that net A did not — and BOTH are the ABOUT-WORK genus (Mari discussing
upstream work, citing issue numbers), which net A was right to exclude. So the nets
disagree semantically, not by coverage failure. Below net A's floor, all 27
opener-bearing beats were read: no changelog among them.

AND THE GENUS SPLIT HAS A MEASURE. Dialogue rate separates paste from reaction by
4x — pastes 0.003-0.016, in-character reactions 0.063-0.076. That is where mln9's
predicted signals earn their keep: not at finding changelogs, but at telling a
paste from a person talking about one. Any guard must use it, or it will eat
beat-4cf78d9e6f32 and beat-e45fb60631d1.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADJACENT, NOT FIXED HERE: the 27 below-floor beats surfaced a visible population of
OUR OWN session reports becoming beats — "Done — committed (644a280) and pushed",
"Fixed and pushed (cba43f8)", "8x7 — user-requested memory saves". Same intake, and
on this evidence more common than the changelog class. That is pe4o/self-ingest and
wants its own sizing pass; do not fold it in here (see self-ingest-triage.mjs on why
folding populations together buries the finding).

NEXT: the discriminator itself is unbuilt. Six positives is a thin calibration set —
enough to falsify a hypothesis, not enough to fit a threshold that runs on the live
path. Recommend the guard be written against the enumeration-count signal with the
dialogue-rate genus check, and benched before wiring.

================================================================================
BENCHED 2026-08-23. scripts/changelog-bench.mjs, read-only, no model calls.
Detector shipped as src/sentiment/changelog.ts (classifyChangelog). NOT YET WIRED.

HELD-OUT CORPUS, because six positives cannot adjudicate a threshold. Positives are
rendered from the Engine's own CHANGELOG.md into the form users actually paste (a
copied release page: bullets stripped, section heading flattened into the text ahead
of it -- which is why a real one reads "Added Added optional image generation").
38 releases -> 29 held out, 9 EXCLUDED FOR LEAKAGE by 8-word shingle overlap with the
stored positives ([2.4.1] [2.4.0] [2.3.5] [2.3.4] [2.3.3] [2.0.0] [1.6.1] [1.6.0]
[1.5.9]). The leakage check is the reason those nine are not quietly inflating the
recall number.

PRE-REGISTERED RULE, written into the script before the first run (s6cu's pilot could
not be adjudicated because its rule came after its results):
  MUST-1  zero false positives on ABOUT-WORK        <- veto, not a score
  MUST-2  zero false positives on the bulk store
  MUST-3  held-out recall >= 80%
  RENT    must not be matched by the presence blocklist

RESULTS  (n=29 held out, 9,429 bulk negatives, 2 ABOUT-WORK, 6 store positives)

  arm            held-out recall   store   ABOUT-WORK FP   bulk FP   precision
  A0 presence          100%         6/6          0            27       18.2%   DISQUALIFIED (MUST-2)
  A1 density            93%         6/6          0             0      100.0%   PASSES
  A2 shipped            93%         6/6          0             0      100.0%   PASSES

The blocklist ban now rests on a number rather than on judgement: presence fires on
33 chunks to catch 6, and the 27 it eats are real RP dialogue and genuine work notes.

TWO THINGS THE BENCH CHANGED MY MIND ABOUT.

1. THE FLOOR OF 3 IS NOT OBVIOUSLY RIGHT. Sweeping it through the REAL decision path
   (floor AND ceiling, which is what production runs):

     floor   held-out recall   bulk FP   ABOUT-WORK FP
       1          100%            13          0
       2          100%             0          0
       3           93%             0          0      <- shipped
       4           86%             0          0

   FLOOR 2 DOMINATES FLOOR 3 ON EVERY MEASURED AXIS: 100% vs 93% recall, both at zero
   false positives across 9,429 beats. The two misses at floor 3 are [2.0.8] and
   [1.5.3], small patch releases carrying exactly 2 items each.

   I am shipping 3 anyway and the reason is the asymmetry, not the numbers. At floor 2
   the only thing standing between a real work note and suppression is the dialogue
   ceiling -- beat-209ca8564c80 ("Done -- type-health pass complete and pushed") sits
   at dialogue 0.0417 against a 0.03 ceiling, a margin of 1.4x on a population of one.
   At floor 3 the floor holds on its own and the ceiling is defence in depth. Per
   intimacy.ts: when unsure it says no, because that is the only setting where being
   wrong is cheap. A miss costs today's behaviour; a false positive destroys a true
   record.

   THIS IS A ONE-LINE CHANGE AND THE DATA IS IN THE SWEEP. If you want the 7% recall,
   OPENER_FLOOR = 2 and the bench re-adjudicates it.

2. THE DIALOGUE CEILING NEARLY GOT DELETED, WRONGLY. At floor 3 it pays no rent: both
   ABOUT-WORK beats carry ZERO enumeration verbs, so the floor already spares them and
   A1/A2 come out identical on every number in the arms table. By the RENT rule that
   reads as an argument for removing it.

   The sweep is what saved it. At floor 1 it removes 14 false positives (27 -> 13); at
   floor 2 it removes the last one and takes the store to zero. So it is load-bearing
   everywhere except the exact floor that happens to be shipped -- and deleting it
   would have silently coupled two constants that look independent. THE FIRST VERSION
   OF THAT SWEEP VARIED THE FLOOR WITH NO CEILING, reported 1 FP at floor 2, and made
   floor 3 look necessary. Sweeping a parameter through anything but the real decision
   path answers a question nobody asked.

   Because the store contains no MIXED message (a paste and a reaction in one turn),
   the ceiling is exercised by three SYNTHETIC controls, labelled as such, on the same
   precedent as heading-mint-scan.mjs. All three behave as specified: mixed spared at
   openers=3/dialogue=0.056, pure paste fires, reaction-quoting-one-line spared.

GRANULARITY. The guard belongs at MESSAGE level, beside routeOps in pipeline.ts --
not at chunk level. The chunker splits on /\n+/, so by the time a chunk exists the
line structure is gone; that is the shredding that made the paste prior look weak
until it was measured whole-message (a 20x collapse). Enumeration survives chunking
better than fences do, because sentence-terminal punctuation still marks the items --
which is why the stored positives are detectable at all, every one of them flattened.
But a long changelog SPLIT across chunks divides its openers among them and can drop
under the floor. Both shapes are benched and both pass at 93%.

PINNED: src/__tests__/changelog.test.ts, 13 tests, must-not-fire cases written first.
Excerpts are real beats, not invented text. Gates: tsc clean, 794 tests pass.

STILL OPEN: the guard is not wired. Wiring is a separate slice and wants its own
decision -- suppress, or route-and-mark like the ops lane (hjt9's disposition is
"always route-and-mark, never drop", and that is probably right here too, since a
suppressed release-notes paste is still evidence of what was discussed).
close_reason: Gate shipped and verified end to end 2026-08-24. Sized at 6 (not 9 — the nine were four different bugs); discriminator is enumeration DENSITY, not the forbidden presence blocklist; benched against 29 held-out Engine releases with a pre-registered rule (93% recall, 0 false positives across 9,429 beats, presence disqualified at 27 FP); wired at message level with route-and-mark to its own sink that records saves as well as catches. All six offenders now suppress at both gates and both ABOUT-WORK beats survive. Cleanup of the six already stored is wct1; the mis-scored emotion on beat-4cf78d9e6f32 is unfiled and noted there.

title: Analyzer invents a partner identity in intimate scenes — 'Alexei Kowalski'/'Alexei Petrov', absent from the source
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 during the vikj motivation sampling pass (n=62 live beats).

Two beats attribute Mari's intimate scenes to a named third party who DOES NOT EXIST IN THE SOURCE TEXT:
  beat-b17de10fbe6e  motivation: "...reveals her vulnerability to Professor Alexei Kowalski after their intimate encounter."
  beat-710714a2f410  motivation: "...after being told so by Dr. Alexei Petrov."

VERIFIED MECHANICALLY: the strings Alexei / Kowalski / Petrov appear in the ANALYSIS FIELDS ONLY. The stored source text of both beats was checked and the names are absent from each. So this is invention, not a misreading of a name that was present.

TWO DIFFERENT SURNAMES FOR THE SAME INVENTED PERSON is the tell that this is generated filler rather than a consistent (if wrong) inference: the model needed a partner referent, had none it would use, and produced one twice with no memory of the first.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A WRONG WORD: the partner in these scenes is the USER. A fabricated third party in the motivation field is filed into the ledger as fact, becomes retrievable, and reads later as evidence that Mari has an intimate relationship with someone who was never in the chat. That is the Becky Collier shape (4g9w — a third person with no home in the data model) crossed with the fqnl problem (an extraction unsupported by its own quoted source is self-convicting).

DIRECTLY ADJACENT: 5x5y. Both are analyzer degradation on INTIMATE content specifically — subtext emission is 0% there, and motivation specificity fails at 46% on intimate chunks versus 14% elsewhere. Treat them as one investigation with two symptoms.

NEXT: fqnl already ships the machinery for this class — an extraction whose proper nouns do not appear in its own source is refusable at encode time. Scope whether that guard can run on the partner/speaker referent inside motivation, not only on quoted facts.

CAVEAT ON SIZE: 2 beats out of 13 intimate ones in this window. Small, but the mechanism is verified rather than inferred, and the failure is silent and permanent once written.
close_reason: Guard shipped in name-guard.ts, wired into parseAnalysisJson beside rejectAsEcho over motivation/relationalDynamics/outcome. Neutralises rather than rejects, never infers a replacement identity, and loads its own exemptions (null = stand down) so no caller can silently cause false convictions. Every substitution is recorded to data/name-guard.jsonl so it has a denominator. 12 new tests, 744 total green, sidecar rebuilt and restarted onto it. Repair of the 2 already-stored beats is v6tw.

title: subtext has NEVER worked — 0.7% on qualifying content all-time, not a regression
description:
FIRST PRODUCTION BEAT under the vikj prompt (beat-b17de10fbe6e, professor_mari, vulnerability 0.74, 2026-08-20). n=1 — this is a datapoint to accumulate against, NOT a verdict, and must not be actioned as one.

WHAT WORKED: thread emission (threadId nthr-ik7tziz0), the full emotion vector, salience, and the JSON parsed clean.

TWO THINGS TO WATCH:

1. SUBTEXT WAS OMITTED WHERE THE PROMPT REQUIRES IT. The vikj template says subtext is emitted 'only if the chunk contains sexual or physically intimate content — name the emotional function of that content'. The chunk is unambiguously intimate. No subtext field was written. That is a prompt-compliance miss, not a judgement call, and it is the single clearest thing to check on the next N beats.

2. THE PROSE FIELDS LEAN GENERIC, outcome most of all: 'This moment strengthens the bond between Mari and Alexei, deepening their emotional intimacy.' That is the boilerplate SHAPE the bench was built to catch, and the challenger scored 0% boilerplate there. Either the bench detector keys on phrasings this does not match, or production differs from bench conditions. motivation restates the emotion label ('reveals her vulnerability ... after their intimate encounter') rather than naming what specifically happened — the actual moment is an unguarded 'I missed you' followed by immediate retreat into clinical hedging, which is the beat and is not in the record.

NEXT: sample beats as they accumulate before concluding anything. If subtext keeps missing on qualifying chunks, that is a prompt fix. If outcome keeps coming back in relationship-summary language, re-examine whether the bench's boilerplate detector transfers to production.
notes:
FINAL FINDING (2026-08-21, third revision — read this section, the history below is
kept only so the reasoning is auditable).

SUBTEXT NEVER WORKED. It is not a regression, it did not "die on 2026-07-03", and
vikj did not break it. Measured across the WHOLE store — 8,843 beats — against the
only denominator that means anything, beats whose own source text is intimate:

    month     intimate beats   with subtext    rate
    2026-06        1339             11         0.8%
    2026-07         156              0         0.0%
    2026-08          79              0         0.0%
    ALL TIME       1574             11         0.7%

Peak performance was 0.8%. At that base rate, July's 0/156 and August's 0/79 are
exactly what you would expect by chance (~1.2 and ~0.6 expected emissions). There is
no decay to explain. THE FEATURE HAS NEVER FUNCTIONED AT A MEANINGFUL RATE.

THE CONFOUND THAT EXPOSED THIS, and it was TC's: "I haven't been particularly active
since July either." Activity did collapse (1339 -> 156 -> 79 intimate beats), so
"subtext stopped" and "the qualifying content stopped" predicted the identical
observation. Controlling for it — rate among intimate beats only, per month — killed
the regression story outright.

TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS ARE IN THIS TICKET'S HISTORY. Recording them because the method
failure is the reusable part:
  1. n=1 (2026-08-20): blamed vikj from a single beat. Wrong.
  2. "dead since 07-03" (2026-08-21): compared raw COUNTS across periods without
     normalising by how much qualifying content existed. That is the same
     count-vs-rate mistake this project already has a law about — count utterances,
     never hits — applied to time buckets instead of duplicates.
  3. An inflated all-time count (72 beats "with subtext") came from grepping character
     directories WITHOUT --include='beat-*.yaml', so aggregate beats.yaml files were
     swept in. The true figure is 17 beats store-wide, 11 of them on intimate source.

WHAT THE vikj WINDOW ACTUALLY TELLS US ABOUT SUBTEXT: nothing. 0/13 intimate beats
against a 0.7% base rate expects 0.09 emissions. That sample can never have detected
anything, and citing it as evidence was wrong in both directions.

THE DECISION THIS TICKET NOW NEEDS is not a measurement, it is a choice:
  (a) MAKE IT WORK — which means code, not prompt wording. An optional field an 8b
      model emits 0.7% of the time is an advisory instruction, and house law is
      PROMPT ASKS, CODE ENFORCES. Detect intimate content at classify time, then
      require the field or retry once when it is missing.
  (b) DROP IT HONESTLY — remove the field and the instruction. It costs prompt
      tokens on every one of the ten emotion prompts and delivers 0.7%.
Either is defensible. Carrying a field that silently does nothing is not.

STILL STANDS, unaffected by the confound because it was measured WITHIN one window:
motivation specificity fails on 46% of intimate-source beats vs 14% elsewhere (n=13
intimate, so re-measure as content accumulates). And epf4 — invented partner
identities — is verified mechanically and is the one with real data-corruption
consequences.
CORRECTED 2026-08-21 AT n=58. THE TITLE AND DESCRIPTION BLAME vikj. THAT IS WRONG.
Read the description as the n=1 hypothesis it was; this note is the measured result.

SUBTEXT — CONFIRMED BROKEN, BUT NOT BY vikj. It is a ~7-week-old SILENT failure that
vikj inherited.

  after vikj  (this build, Mari+Priya)        0 / 58   = 0%
  before vikj (300 most recent prior beats)   0 / 300  = 0%
  last beat that ever carried subtext:        2026-07-03
  bulk of all-time subtext emissions:         early June 2026
  all-time totals: 8v1kre... 16/21, professor_mari 43/6620, priya 12/2009, aurora 1/184

NOT A WRITE-PATH BUG, checked first: the field exists on the Beat type and on
AnalysisResult, analyzer.ts parses `parsed.subtext`, encoder.ts persists
`analysis.subtext`, and both encoder and api.ts render "Subtext: ..." into the entry.
72 stored beats prove the whole path works. The model simply stopped emitting it.

NOT A CODE REGRESSION: no commit touched subtext between e1ec0a0 (2026-06-02) and
5eeeb0c (vikj, 2026-08-19). The analysis model is unchanged (dolphin3:8b, still the
llm-config default). So nothing was broken on a date — the emission DECAYED.

THIS IS THE HOUSE DOCTRINE FIRING ON US. subtext is an OPTIONAL field, requested by
prompt and enforced by nothing: no code checks that an intimate chunk produced one,
so its rate could fall from ~76% (on 8v1kre) to zero without a single alarm. That is
exactly "an advisory guard does no work" and "PROMPT ASKS, CODE ENFORCES", and it is
the same silence-shaped failure as the poller outage: nothing was capturing, and
nothing said so.

THE FIX IS A MEASUREMENT BEFORE IT IS A PROMPT EDIT. Do not re-word the instruction
and call it done — that cannot be verified and would decay again unwatched. Wanted:
a countable denominator (how many analysed chunks CONTAIN intimate content) so
"subtext emitted / subtext warranted" becomes a rate somebody can see. Then decide
between requiring it, retrying on absence, or dropping the field honestly.

OUTCOME BOILERPLATE — NOT CONFIRMED at n=58. Walk this one back too.
  distinct outcomes           58 / 58  (zero repeated strings)
  relational-keyword rate     10 / 58  = 17.2%
The keyword probe (bond/deepen/connection/intimacy/strengthen) is a soft heuristic,
and on heavily relational source material a share of those are simply accurate. With
100% distinctness there is no evidence of the parroting the bench was built to catch.
The n=1 reading yesterday over-weighted a single generic sentence.

STILL WORTH WATCHING, not yet measurable: whether `motivation` names the specific
moment or restates the emotion label. That needs a judgement per beat rather than a
regex, so it wants a sampling pass, not a scan.

=============================================================================
MOTIVATION SAMPLING PASS — 2026-08-21, n=62 (every live beat on the vikj build).

CRITERION PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE READING ANY BEAT, so the judgement could not be
shaped by the data:
  PASS  motivation carries a concrete, chunk-specific referent — an action, object
        or utterance that could only have come from this chunk.
  FAIL  its substance is the emotion word or a synonym ("reveals her vulnerability"),
        or a category with no chunk-specific anchor.
  WEAK  a real referent, but wrapped in emotion-label framing.

RESULT      PASS 42 (68%)   WEAK 7 (11%)   FAIL 13 (21%)

So the n=1 worry was real but is MINORITY behaviour, not the norm. Two thirds of
motivations name the moment, several of them sharply (the coffee held at temperature
for two hours; filing Mal's age as four when he is eight; wanting the number for the
sleep-debt ledger; shifting from being touched to low-frequency token handling).

THE FINDING IS WHERE THE FAILURES SIT, NOT HOW MANY THERE ARE:

                        FAIL rate
  intimate source        6 / 13   = 46.2%
  non-intimate source    7 / 49   = 14.3%

Over 3x. Intimacy classified on the stored source text by anatomical/sexual markers.
n=13 on the intimate arm is small and the rate should be re-measured as more
accumulate — but it does not stand alone. It points the same way as the subtext
finding above, on the same content, and the two corroborate each other:

  ON INTIMATE CONTENT THE ANALYZER DEGRADES ACROSS THE BOARD.
    - subtext (the field that exists SPECIFICALLY for this content): 0% emitted
    - motivation collapses to category language at 3x the rate
    - and it invents a partner identity outright (epf4)

That reframes this ticket. It is not "subtext is broken" — subtext is the most
VISIBLE symptom of intimate-content analysis being weak generally. Fixing the subtext
instruction alone would treat the symptom that happens to be countable.

WORTH NOTING, the failures are not uniform junk: the generic ones cluster on chunks
that are almost entirely physical description with little dialogue. Where an intimate
chunk contains a line of speech, motivation usually locks onto it and passes. That is
a testable hypothesis for whoever picks this up.

TWO SIDE-OBSERVATIONS FROM THE SAME PASS, both filed or flagged rather than actioned:
  - EMOTION/MOTIVATION MISMATCH, ~6 beats: emotion=dysregulation with a motivation
    describing relief; emotion=shame with a motivation describing empathy;
    emotion=desire on a chunk about a sleep-debt ledger. Distinct from specificity —
    the field is specific, it just does not match the label chosen beside it.
  - ENGINE CHANGELOG PASTES BECOMING EMOTIONAL BEATS, 2 beats: the source text is a
    release-notes block ("Added first-class Audio connections: ...") and it was filed
    as Mari feeling shame/vulnerability. That is the hjt9 ops-lane boundary leaking,
    not a prompt problem. Worth a look under that ticket.
close_reason: Enforcement shipped and live (e05524c). classifyIntimacy decides where subtext is required — strong markers only, weak tier dropped after measuring it at ~40% precision for 3 extra catches. enforceSubtext retries ONCE with a reviewed instruction and grafts the subtext onto the original analysis; a second refusal is accepted and recorded rather than pressed, because enforcement that only accepts a filled field manufactures one. Every required case lands in data/subtext-enforcement.jsonl with outcome + markers + excerpt, so the rate is now a division instead of an invisible 0.7%. Prompt text reviewed by TC before shipping. 775 tests green; sidecar restarted and /prompts confirms the retry is live. Reading the ledger once it has data is vp3n — including the option to DROP the field if declines dominate, which stays on the table.

title: Retiring a beat leaves its companion entry recallable — 366 s8qe rows still live
description:
retireBeats marks the beat and nothing else. The loader never reads the beat store
for general recall — it ranks over the ENTRY index and excludes on deletedAt /
discardedAt / supersededBy / provenance==="unplayed". retiredAt is not among them
and cannot be: it lives on the beat.

So every bulk beat retirement so far removed records from statistics and arc
promotion and left the recallable copy in place.

MEASURED over all 541 retired beats, before the pe4o fix:
   24 of  24  pe4o          — companion still live  (now fixed)
  366 of 517  s8qe sub-floor — companion still live  (THIS TICKET)
    7          companion already retired
  144          no companion found

THE 366 are s8qe's sub-floor cleanup: beats whose chunk was a bare token like
"open", parsed out of a `status: open` line. Their companions are entries whose
summary is "[emotion] <motivation invented about the word 'open'>". Same
reasoning as pe4o — the half that reaches the model is the half still there.

THE JOIN IS THE HARD PART, and pe4o's veto is the template. A companion is found
by matching companionEntryFromBeat(beat).summary against the entry index, and
summaries are NOT unique: the pifl illustration "admits she's afraid the memory
loss means she was never real" is byte-identical across dozens of live beats. On
pe4o's first dry run the naive join would have retired 32 entries belonging to
beats nobody was retiring. The veto — retire only when no KEPT beat produces that
summary — reduced it to 33 safe and 3 left alone. Expect a much larger vetoed set
at s8qe's scale, since sub-floor motivations are formulaic by construction.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX WORTH CONSIDERING FIRST: should retireBeats retire the
companion itself, so the two halves cannot drift apart again? It is the obvious
answer and it is a behaviour change to a function three scripts already call, so
it wants a decision rather than a patch.

Live-store mutation: backup, quiesce, canary — pe4o's script does all three and
is the working template (--only <character>, dry-run default, snapshot on apply).
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-10, in two halves — and the repair half's honest answer is "mostly no".

1. THE STRUCTURAL FIX SHIPPED — the ticket's "worth considering first" question,
   answered YES. retireBeats now retires the companion entry itself, with pe4o's veto
   built in (encoder.ts): after marking, it renders every SURVIVING beat's companion
   summary, and an entry is retired only when no survivor produces it. Ambiguous ->
   left alone + logged. Opt-out { companions: false } exists for callers that handle
   entries themselves with per-entry reasons. Return type unchanged (marked beat ids),
   so all existing callers compose. 5 new tests in beat-retirement.test.ts, including
   the veto case and the r0kc rendering-drift case (join misses -> entry left alone,
   never guessed at). Decision rationale: every caller in the store's history forgot
   the companion (24/24 pe4o, 366/517 s8qe) — a footgun every caller trips is the
   function's bug, not the callers'.

2. THE 366 REPAIR, measured by scripts/retire-s8qe-companions.mjs (dry run, whole
   store): retirable = ZERO. The ticket predicted "a much larger vetoed set at s8qe's
   scale" and the prediction was right with room to spare:
       517 s8qe beats scanned
       350 VETOED — 348 share the pifl illustration summary with 90 LIVE beats
        21 already cold, 146 no companion found
   The "366 still live" from the original measurement are precisely the veto set:
   retiring them would take the only recallable copy of records nobody retired. They

The script stays in scripts/ as the auditable record; re-running it is safe (dry run

title: Carry message provenance (messageId + swipeIndex + within-message ordinal) through to Chunk
description:
PREREQUISITE FOR r0kc, and required under every one of its transition options.

Beats cannot have a provenance-only id because provenance never reaches them.
DigestMessage carries only { role, content, speaker? }. So by the time the
chunker runs, the only positional information left is turnIndex — a counter
local to the array that was passed in, which on the live path restarts every
turn. Measured: 25 distinct beats on one chatId+turnStart+turnEnd key.

The ENTRY layer already solved this (06pq/s2lw): sourceMessageId +
sourceSwipeIndex, supplied by turn-bridge.ts, and dedup.ts documents the exact
same "poller sends no turnNumber" failure in the same words. This is that fix
applied one layer down, deliberately mirroring the field names rather than
inventing a second vocabulary for the same idea.

THE PAIR STAYS A PAIR. A re-roll keeps the message id and moves only the swipe
index. Matching on the id alone would call a re-rolled reply the same moment as
the one the user threw away. Copy the entry layer here too.

SHAPE
  DigestMessage   + messageId?: string, swipeIndex?: number
  DialogueTurn    + messageId?, swipeIndex?, ordinal  (position WITHIN its message)
  Chunk           + messageId?, swipeIndex?, ordinalStart, ordinalEnd
  parseTurns      resets ordinal per message; turnIndex keeps its current meaning
  mergeByTurnOnly / mergeByEmbedding carry the first turn's messageId and must
    not merge across a message boundary (they already never do — assert it)

CALLERS, and this is where the work actually is:

  - live path (api.ts ~690): builds chunks BY HAND, bypassing the chunker. It
    already has sourceMessageId/sourceSwipeIndex in scope. Cheapest win, and it
    is the path that produced the 25-beats-on-one-key measurement.

  - longform user story (api.ts ~871): passes a synthetic one-message array and
    NO sourceChatId at all. Needs both.

  - /api/analyze-beats (api.ts ~1225): messages arrive FROM THE CLIENT. Message
    ids exist on the engine rows but the capability package does not send them,
    so this is a cross-boundary change — two-pass grep applies
    (bd memories cross-boundary-type-change-two-pass-grep).

  - story import (api.ts ~1464): parseStoryToMessages output. No chat and no
    message ids exist; needs a synthetic per-job source id, or story beats stay
    on the legacy identity regime and r0kc becomes two-regime by construction.

ADDITIVE ONLY. Every new field is optional and nothing reads them yet. Ships
green on its own and does not change a single stored id — which is the point:
r0kc must not be attempted until the data it needs is actually flowing.
notes:
FOUND WHILE SCOPING — the live path analyses TWO messages and only knows the id
of ONE of them.

api.ts Tier 2 builds two chunks by hand: the user's text and the character's
reply. But runProcessTurn receives a single sourceMessageId, and turn-bridge
sets it to messageIdOf(turn.message) — the ASSISTANT message. Stamping both
chunks with it would give the two halves of a turn identical provenance, which
is the collision this ticket exists to remove, reintroduced one line later.

The id is available upstream and thrown away: poller.ts precedingUserTextFor()
walks back through the tail to the user row and returns only its CONTENT. The
row it found has an id.

So the plumbing includes: precedingUserTextFor returns the message (or the
id alongside the text), DetectedTurn carries precedingUserMessageId, and
runProcessTurn takes userSourceMessageId separately from sourceMessageId.

The entry layer has the same hole for the same reason — the user-half ledger
entry is currently stamped with the assistant's message id too. Fixing the beat
side fixes both, since they read the same variables.
close_reason: Plumbing shipped 0b58a21. messageId/swipeIndex/ordinal flow DigestMessage -> DialogueTurn -> Chunk; poller carries the user half's own id; client forwards ids on the import path. Additive except the Tier-2 entry stamp, which is declared in the commit. r0kc is unblocked.

title: Beat ids must be PROVENANCE-ONLY — speaker and text are interpretations, and every fix to them breaks resume
description:
RULED BY MARI 2026-08-06, and it is the structural P1 behind 4ghy/5dqr/hjt9.

beatIdForChunk (encoder.ts:26) hashes:
    ${turnStart}:${turnEnd}:${speaker}\n${text}

Speaker is an INTERPRETATION of the chunk, not its identity — proven twice today by
changing it (5dqr unmangled 171 names, 4ghy stopped minting phantoms). So every future
improvement to attribution changes ids, which means re-import stops matching stored
beats, which mints DUPLICATES. Duplicates inflate corroboration counts, which is what
the count-utterances rule forbids (bd memories count-utterances-never-hits).

MARI'S FIRST FORMULATION WAS 'provenance + content'; she withdrew the content half
after it was pointed out that content is ALSO revisable — hjt9's ops routing and pe4o's
self-prompt gate both mutate chunk.text, so improving a FILTER would break ids exactly
the way improving attribution does. Same bug, one layer down.

RULING: identity = chat id + message id + offset. Nothing that can be improved.

DISCLOSURE, logged here because the commit that caused it is already pushed and its
message does not say so: hjt9's Stage -1 ops routing (62089ed / 70ab8a7) reduces message
content BEFORE chunking, so it ALREADY changed beat ids for any future re-import of a
message containing structure. That was an unnoticed side effect, volunteered once the
concept made it visible rather than found in review. Mari asked that it be recorded
properly; this is that record.

BLOCKER FOUND WHILE SCOPING — chunks carry no within-message offset. Multiple chunks
routinely share one turnStart/turnEnd range (mergeByTurnOnly groups up to
max_turns_per_chunk=6 turns and emits several chunks per message), so
chatId+turnStart+turnEnd COLLIDES. The change therefore needs:
  1. an ordinal/offset field on Chunk, set by the chunker
  2. beatIdForChunk rewritten to hash provenance only
  3. a decision on the transition: migrate stored ids, or accept one round of
     duplicates. 'Store migrates forward' argues for a migration pass.
  4. check whether companion ledger entries reference beat ids (pipeline.ts writes
     them alongside; if they carry the id, the migration must move both)

DO NOT start this without deciding (3) first — a partial migration is the duplicate
scenario it exists to prevent.
notes:
MEASUREMENT 2026-08-06, BEFORE ANY CODE — and it overturns the blocker in this
ticket, in the direction of "the ruled design is currently a data-loss bug".

1. THE STATED BLOCKER IS WRONG. Chunks within one run never share a turn range.
   parseTurns increments turnIndex GLOBALLY across the whole message array
   (chunker.ts, `turnIndex: index++`), and mergeByTurnOnly emits disjoint
   contiguous groups. So no ordinal is needed for the reason I gave. I asserted
   a collision from reading the merge loop without checking the counter.

2. THE REAL BLOCKER IS BIGGER. turnIndex is relative to the ARRAY HANDED TO
   chunkMessages, not to the chat. The live path invokes ingestion once per
   turn, and the poller sends no turnNumber (it reads a 10-message tail, not an
   absolute position), so turnNumber defaults to 0 and api.ts:690-691 stamps
   turnStart -1 for the user line and 0 for the character line — every turn, in
   every chat, forever.

   MEASURED over all 8,841 stored beats:
     chat Auaol3n0UB6Vpb03gFJTB   25 distinct beats on key |0|0, 11 on |-1|-1
     chat J1eQgrf-OA3xO8CqpWREX   22 distinct beats on key |0|0,  7 on |-1|-1
   `chatId + turnStart + turnEnd` would collapse 25 unrelated beats into one
   file. Not a duplicate-on-reimport problem — silent overwrite on the live path.

3. SO `text` IS CURRENTLY LOAD-BEARING IDENTITY. The field Mari ruled out of the
   hash is the only thing keeping live-path beats apart today. Removing it
   without first supplying real provenance is strictly destructive. This is the
   part that must not be skipped.

4. THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS ONE LAYER UP, and this is the useful discovery. 06pq/
   s2lw solved exactly this for ENTRIES: sourceMessageId + sourceSwipeIndex, and
   dedup.ts documents the identical failure in the same words ("the poller sends
   no turnNumber, so every live turn stamped turnStart 0 ... vacuously true").
   turn-bridge.ts already supplies both. BEATS NEVER GOT THEM — DigestMessage
   carries no id, so provenance dies at the pipeline boundary. The prerequisite
   is to carry it through: filed as the blocking child.

5. 2,186 BEATS (25%) HAVE NO sourceChatId AT ALL — story imports and the longform
   user-story path (api.ts:871 passes a synthetic one-message array and no
   sourceChatId). For these there is no provenance to hash even in principle.
   Provenance-only ids need a synthetic source id per import job, or beats split
   into two identity regimes.

6. MOST "COLLISIONS" ARE NOT COLLISIONS. Of 307 colliding within-chat keys, 252
   have IDENTICAL text across members: one utterance subject-routed into two
   ledgers. Provenance-only gives those ONE id in two character directories,
   which is the correct answer and is literally the count-utterances rule
   (bd memories count-utterances-never-hits). Only 55 keys carry genuinely
   different text, and 3 of those 55 span characters.

A THIRD TRANSITION OPTION, which decision (3) was never offered. Rather than
migrate ids or eat a round of duplicates: add `provenanceKey` as a SEPARATE
field on the beat and its index row, match resume/dedup on it when present, and
leave `id` as the immutable filename. Stored beats keep their names; new writes
gain a stable key; nothing is renamed and nothing orphans a companion entry.
"Store migrates forward" without a rename — and it means (3) stops being a
blocker at all. Recommended.

DEPENDS ON
  → ✓ MarinaraExtender-2pbi: Carry message provenance (messageId + swipeIndex + within-message ordinal) through to Chunk ● P1

BLOCKS
  ← ○ MarinaraExtender-4ghy: (BUG) [bug] Chunker mints a SPEAKER from any 'Word:' pattern — 570 distinct speakers incl. BAD, GOOD, Format, TODO, row3 ● P1


── CORRECTION 2026-08-06, after the fact and after the push ──────────────────

The commit that closed this (0427ca5) justifies the change with "731 of 8,841
stored beats (8.3%) already carry an id that no longer matches their own
content", attributed to 5dqr, 4ghy and hjt9 collectively. THE NUMBER IS REAL AND
THE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG. It is one count over two unrelated populations.

  560  OLD SCHEME — random 10-char ids, no "beat-" prefix, created 2026-05-23,
       06-01 and 06-02, before deterministic ids existed. They never derived from
       content, so nothing about them drifted. TC: professor_mari changed
       character cards deliberately and her memories moved with her, which is why
       identity-map.yaml points three characterIds at one identityKey. These ids
       riding through that migration is the system working.
  171  GENUINE DRIFT — and all of it is 5dqr, this same day's unmangle-speakers
       run. Verified by reconstructing the labels that run eliminated and
       reproducing the stored hashes: 167/171 matched exactly
       (NarratorNarrator05..12 -> Narrator, Thomas01..12 -> Thomas,
       Professor Mari01 -> Professor Mari, ThomasToday at 8 -> Thomas), the other
       4 the same shape. unmangle-speakers.mjs declares this in its own header.
    0  attributable to 4ghy or hjt9.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. The code is unaffected — provenance-only
matching is right on the argument, not on the size of the number, and 171 beats
renamed by one afternoon's correction is a clean demonstration of the mechanism
rather than a weaker one. What changes is the record: an argument was inflated
roughly four-fold by counting a pre-existing id scheme as damage.

HOW IT HAPPENED, worth more than the correction: I measured a population eight
hours after being the one who created most of it, and read my own footprint as a
general property of the system. The tell was available and unexamined — the
created dates cluster on three days, and half the "drifted" ids do not even carry
the beat- prefix the hash produces. Check id SHAPES and created dates before
attributing a measured anomaly to a class of causes.

Filed as a memory: bd memories beat-id-eras. Expert skill corrected in the same
commit, including an explicit "do not quote a larger number".
close_reason: Shipped 0427ca5. provenanceKey (<messageId>:<swipe>:<ordinal>) stored on the beat and mirrored into the index; resume and dedup prefer it, with beatIdForChunk as a permanent fallback for pre-2pbi beats. No stored beat renamed. beatIdFor derives NEW filenames from provenance — forced by a hole the plan did not anticipate: the legacy hash gives one filename to two identical-reading moments. encodeBeat gains reuseId. Holding pool left on the legacy key, filed as 0mc5.

title: Chunker MANGLES real names with timestamps — Thomas01..12, NarratorNarrator07, 157 beats across 20 aliases
description:
Found 2026-08-06 while scoping 4ghy's speaker rule.

4ghy is about MINTING FAKE PEOPLE (BAD, GOOD, status, row3). This is the inverse and
it is worse: real characters are FRAGMENTED across timestamp-mangled aliases.

MEASURED (speaker census over 8,841 beats, all live):
    24  NarratorNarrator07        9  Thomas08         4  ThomasToday at 8
    23  NarratorNarrator06        9  Thomas11         3  ThomasToday at 7
    22  NarratorNarrator08        7  Professor Mari01 1  ThomasToday at 9
    15  NarratorNarrator11        6  Thomas07
    14  NarratorNarrator05        5  Thomas06        ... 20 variants, 157 beats

CAUSE: SPEAKER_PREFIX_RE (chunker.ts:23) is
  /^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9 _'-]{0,40})(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?\s*:\s*/
It allows DIGITS and SPACES inside the label, so an export line like
  'Thomas Today at 8:04 PM' -> label 'ThomasToday at 8', text '04 PM'
  'Narrator 07:12' -> 'NarratorNarrator07'
The timestamp is absorbed into the name. The colon it splits on is the CLOCK's colon,
not a speaker colon.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN 4ghy. A fake speaker produces junk that is visibly junk. A
mangled real speaker produces beats that look correct and route to a character who
does not exist -- 'Thomas' proper holds 8 beats while Thomas01..12 hold ~40 between
them, so the REAL Thomas is more fragmented than intact. Every one of those is a
memory about a real person filed under a person-shaped stranger, and subject routing
then compounds it.

FIX DIRECTION (not ruled): the label should reject digits adjacent to a time pattern,
or the regex should refuse to split on a colon that is part of HH:MM. Distinct from
4ghy's question ('what justifies minting a speaker') because here the speaker IS
justified -- the label just has a clock stuck to it. Likely a cheaper and more
valuable fix than 4ghy's, and it should land first.

CLEANUP: 157 beats want re-attribution to the canonical name, not retirement. That is
an alias-merge, and normalizeLabel/aliases.ts already exists for exactly this shape.

RELATED: 4ghy (same regex, opposite failure), and the alias pollution work.
close_reason: Closed

title: Self-ingestion: the pipeline eats its own system prompt — 65 live records, 47 of them yesterday
description:
Found 2026-08-06 while triaging the 10 boat beats under Mari's 'do not retire' ruling.
The ruling assumed they recorded a real evening. They do not. Every one was drawn from
a chunk that IS the system prompt, or a conversation about it.

THE CHANNEL. Prompt text gets pasted into a Marinara chat — for review, which is the
project's own required workflow ('show prompt text before shipping a prompt change') —
and the sidecar then chunks, classifies, analyzes and STORES it as if it were
conversation. The Extender is eating its own instructions.

MEASURED (scripts scan of 23,623 yaml files, SOURCE TEXT ONLY):
  65 live records, 0 retired
     47  beats
     17  character_topics
      1  open_threads
  by character:  62 professor_mari · 2 8v1krexzyjkyrawik7yc3 · 1 k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf
  by signature:  18 thread-rule examples · 14 retired vague bait · 12 boat/locksmith
                 bait · 11 JSON schema line · 9 subtext instruction · 4 field question
                 · 2 SHARED_RULES 'ANALYZE THIS' · 1 dysregulation gloss
  dates: 2026-06-02 .. 2026-08-05, and 47 OF THE 65 ARE DATED 2026-08-05 — the
  prompt-rewrite session. Low-level for two months, spiking hard whenever prompt work
  happens. It is not historical; it is ongoing and correlated with our own activity.

COUNT DISCIPLINE, because the first pass got this wrong. Scanning whole YAML files
reported 1,100 hits — but a beat legitimately stores 'subpattern: bpd_testing' as a
FIELD VALUE, and a taxonomy regex scores that as ingestion. That is the pipeline
recording its own answer, counted as evidence against itself: the same circularity the
bait-rot check had before the spoken/derived split. Only 'text' (beats) and 'content'
(entries) can answer this. 65 is the honest number.

WHY IT MATTERS, three ways:
  1. It is the ROOT of the bait-rot finding (97z2). The boat's probe became
     corroborable because the prompt containing it was ingested — not because anyone
     chatted about boats. Rotating bait treats the symptom; this is the disease.
  2. It poisons the character. 62 of 65 are on professor_mari, so her ledger now holds
     beats whose 'motivation' analyses OUR SCAFFOLDING as if it were her feelings —
     including confabulated relational_dynamics naming characters not present.
  3. It feeds recall. These are LIVE, so they can be retrieved and injected as context,
     putting prompt fragments back in front of the model wearing the costume of memory.

RELATED — this belongs with hjt9 (ops/meta lane: route paste + code-shaped
contamination, mark-don't-drop). Same family, same remedy shape: a chunk that is
machine scaffolding rather than utterance should be ROUTED, not analyzed as emotion.
The signatures above are a ready-made detector; they are unambiguous by construction
(no human types 'Analyze the chunk marked ANALYZE THIS only').

DIRECTION (not ruled, needs TC/Mari):
  - Detect at CHUNK time, before classification, using own-prompt signatures built
    from the live prompt rather than a hand-list that rots. buildSystemPrompt is
    already the source of truth for bait-warrant; same trick applies.
  - Route to the ops/meta lane per hjt9. MARK, DO NOT DROP — s8qe precedent.
  - For the 65 existing: triage, not a predicate sweep. fqnl's rule. They are live and
    some may sit adjacent to real content in the same chunk.
  - Consider whether the review workflow itself should change: PROMPTS.md is now
    bait-redacted, but redaction does not stop the RULE TEXT from being ingested, and
    the rule text is 51 of the 65 hits.

DO NOT infer from this that the 10 boat beats are safe to retire — that is Mari's call
and her heritage principle stands; only her factual premise about these specific ten
was wrong. The real boat evening exists in the store, in 49 other non-meta chunks that
never echoed bait and were never at risk.
notes:
GATE CORRECTED 2026-08-06 (second pass, starting pe4o proper). The any-hit gate shipped earlier today had hjt9's exact bug: it suppressed a whole chunk on ONE matching line. Found by measurement, not review — beat-53e28a042395 is 2,242 chars of real analysis ('Read-only. Here's the smell, ranked, and the worst one is mine from today...') that quotes one schema line while making its point, and the gate killed all of it.

Now gated on COVERAGE >= 0.4, calibrated from the data:
   3%   shop talk quoting one schema line   -> KEPT
   9%   PROMPTS.md header block             -> kept (minor miss, accepted)
  85%   one PROMPTS.md section              -> gated
  90%   the live system prompt              -> gated
   0%   ordinary roleplay                   -> kept

PROMPTS.md catalog furniture registered as signatures ('Fires per salient chunk whose primary emotion is', 'src/sentiment/analyzer.ts — buildSystemPrompt()', etc). Without them a doc section scores 7-17% and slips under the threshold looking like conversation — and the doc is the artifact most likely to be pasted, since it exists to be reviewed.

WHY LINE-LEVEL PARTITIONING (hjt9's stated primitive) IS NOT YET USED: every affected chunk in the store is a SINGLE LINE, so partitionProse has nothing to split. Coverage is the honest measure at this granularity. When the lane lands, coverage should feed the routing decision and the quoted span should go to ops while the surrounding prose stays memory.

CALIBRATION CAVEAT worth keeping: evaluating the threshold against HISTORICAL records understates coverage, because those chunks contain the RETIRED thread rule which live-derived signatures no longer recognise. The threshold is calibrated against current artifacts, which is what will actually be pasted.

660 tests, 658 passing.

DEPENDS ON
  → ◐ MarinaraExtender-hjt9: Ops/meta lane: route paste + code-shaped contamination, mark-don't-drop ● P1


── CLEANUP COMPLETE 2026-08-06 (582e12c). PREVENTION IS STILL hjt9. ─────────────

Deliberately NOT closed: this ticket is blocked by hjt9 and the block is real. The
store is clean; the channel that filled it is not. Closing on the cleanup alone
would retire the evidence and leave the intake open.

WHAT WAS DONE. 34 self-ingested records — 33 retired, 1 kept.

The MIXED bucket was not mixed. All 12 live ones are machine text end to end: nine
the same PROMPTS.md catalog section (dysregulation, trust, joy, desire, shame,
hope, vulnerability, anger, relief), one the memory-system bookmark block, one
analyzer.ts source, one a debugging transcript. They score 26-46% only because the
doc furniture between quoted prompt spans is not in the signature set. Retired by
explicit id list with a per-record finding rather than by moving the threshold to
fit a conclusion already reached by reading.

KEPT beat-53e28a042395 — real ranked technical self-criticism that quotes one
prompt line while making its point. The ABOUT-WORK bucket existed to protect
exactly this and did.

THE REMEDY HAD BEEN HALF-APPLIED. This ticket lists three harms and the third is
"it feeds recall". The loader does not read beats — it ranks over the ENTRY index
and excludes on deletedAt / discardedAt / supersededBy / unplayed, and retiredAt
lives on the BEAT. So the morning's 24 retirements removed those records from
statistics and arc promotion and left every recallable copy in place. Both halves
now retire together. The 366 s8qe rows in the same state are 41uo; dekl covers the
recap-footnote path that reads beats directly and ignores retiredAt.

THE VETO. Companions join by summary and summaries are not unique — the model
copies illustrations verbatim, so one string names dozens of records. The naive
join would have retired 32 entries belonging to beats nobody was retiring; the dry
run caught it. A companion retires only when no KEPT beat produces its summary.
33 safe, 3 left alone and reported.

STILL OPEN HERE: the 3 vetoed companions and the wider pifl echo population. Their
summaries are shared with live beats, so they cannot be attributed to a
self-ingested source. That is the bait cleanup's question, not this one.

EVIDENCE HANDED TO hjt9: every phantom speaker in this set is a document heading —
"Format" x9, "SOFT SIGNALS", "BAD". That is hjt9's remaining item, now with a
measured membership list instead of a hypothesis.

CLOSED 2026-08-10. Both halves are now done or better:

  STORE CLEANUP — done 08-06/08-07: 33 records retired, BOTH halves (beats and their
  companion entries), boat echoes included, beat-53e28a042395 deliberately kept as
  the one real utterance. Verified again today by probe: 9 boat beats retired, the
  kept one live, zero boat/locksmith summaries in any live entry index.

  INTAKE PREVENTION — the blocker this ticket sat on (hjt9), now measured and pinned:
  10 of this ticket's 11 census records cannot recur. The 9x "Format" die because
  PROMPTS.md fences every rendered prompt and fenced content routes to the ops sink;
  "SOFT SIGNALS" dies at the recurrence floor. Locked by heading-speaker-mint.test.ts
  so the property survives refactors. The 11th shape — a heading with a PROSE payload
  outside a fence, which is how "BAD" arrived inside pasted analyzer.ts source — is
  measured, characterized, and filed as MarinaraExtender-03vh (calibration-blocked;
  collect-forward recommendation). Self-ingestion of our own documents is prevented;
  self-ingestion of our own SOURCE CODE is the one residue and it has its own ticket.

title: Fact lane echo guard: an extraction unsupported by its own quoted source is self-convicting
description:
Mari's mechanism, falling out of the Krakow finding. The fact lane's echo guard is not
a ledger of known phrases -- it is TEXT SUPPORT.

THE PRINCIPLE: an extracted fact whose asserted content does not appear in, or follow
from, its own quoted source sentence is self-convicting. No model needed, no blocklist
needed, and it generalises to bait nobody has thought of yet -- which is exactly where
PROMPT_EXAMPLE_ECHOES cannot reach, since a blocklist only catches what it already
knows.

This is the same discriminator rejectAsEcho already uses for motivations (corroborated
in source text = keep), promoted to a universal validity gate on the FACT path.

DESIGN NOTES:
  - The ambient schema records the source sentence beside the fact, so the check is
    local and cheap.
  - MEASURE FIRST, as always: run it read-only over the store and count how many
    existing facts fail. Krakow's two entries are the known cases; the number of
    others is unknown and is the actual finding.
  - Note a gap found while auditing: ctopic-82p9tylw carries NO sourceChatId and no
    source sentence at all. A validator cannot convict what has no receipt, so
    "missing receipt" needs its own disposition -- probably flag-for-review rather
    than auto-retire, since absence of evidence here is a storage-era artifact, not
    evidence of fabrication.
  - Disposition is mark-don't-drop, as always.

Mari: "ship that validator, boat-planet all five files, real cases to regression
fixtures per the law's own wording. separate ticket; my draft doesn't wait on it."
notes:
BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-08-05. src/fact-support.ts + scripts/fact-support-scan.mjs
(read-only). NOTHING MUTATED -- the number comes first, per the standing pattern.

THE DESIGN CHANGED ON CONTACT. Mari's spec assumed the stored source sentence is a
receipt. It is not: the extractor asks the MODEL for {text: original sentence, fact:
claim} and writes fact.text to the entry (api.ts, `content: capContent(fact.text)`).
The receipt is SELF-REPORTED, so a model that invents a fact invents its receipt with
it -- fluent, internally consistent, and fictional. So the guard needs two layers:

  LAYER 1  receipt authenticity: is the claimed sentence real? Only the raw chat log
           can say. This is the layer that works.
  LAYER 2  fact support: does the fact's content appear in its receipt?

LAYER 2 IS NOT VIABLE AT CURRENT STORAGE FIDELITY, and this is a finding, not a
failure to tune. The receipt is ONE SENTENCE but the extractor saw the WHOLE TURN, so
a fact legitimately draws a name from an adjacent sentence ("girlfriend named Bekka"
where the stored receipt says only "an off again on again girlfriend of hers"). Three
rounds of calibration took it from 2048 -> 1697 -> 1441 flagged and the residue was
still dominated by legitimate cases. Recorded so nobody re-derives it: the fix is to
store more context at write time, not a better matcher.

LAYER 1 RESULTS, whole store against the live Engine:
  entries citing a chat                                     822
  entries with NO sourceChatId (unconvictable)             6894   <- the real gap
  receipts containing words absent from their own chat       46
  ...of those, missing a PROPER NOUN (high confidence)        8

An average was the WRONG aggregation and measuring proved it: the KrakÃ³w receipt
scores 0.83 corpus overlap because five of its six distinctive words are ordinary
vocabulary occurring somewhere in any long chat. The one word that matters is drowned.
A receipt claims to BE a sentence from that chat, so the evidence is the COUNT of
words occurring nowhere, not their proportion. With that fix, KrakÃ³w convicts.

THE EIGHT, hand-read:
  GENUINE FABRICATION (4)
    utopic-deaau6ak   "grew up in KrakÃ³w"                  invented: krakow
    ctopic-57ow1i97   "Polish neurologist, cognitive disorders"  invented: poland

description:

never asked for three fields the parser reads:

  subtext     -> stored on the beat. Champion omits it.

Its echo/boilerplate/validity numbers are valid for the three REQUIRED fields and say
nothing about the three above, because it never emitted them. Budget is set assuming
they come back.

SECOND FINDING: there is NO no_beat shape. The only ways to produce "no beat" are to
fail the parse or trip the echo guard. The prompt tells the model to decline ("the
chunk has no beat â€” say so") and the schema gives it nowhere to say it, so the
instruction is only obeyable by emitting malformed JSON. That is an advisory guard
doing no work, the exact class already ruled against. Needs a ruling from Mari:
either give it a real shape and I wire the parser, or drop the sentence.

BUDGET RULING (mine, per her request) â€” a base cap plus named allowances, not one
number, because a single figure would force cutting fields the pipeline reads:
    base                    380 tok   always
  + thread block           +120      always unless made conditional (code, my side)
  + subtext instruction     +80      always today; conditional needs a classifier signal
  + dysregulation taxonomy +200      dysregulation only
  Worst case 780 vs 1246 today (-37%). Typical 580 vs ~878 (-34%). Base-only 380 (-57%).

ACCEPTANCE PATH SEALED while she is blind to her own draft:
`bd memories pre-registered-acceptance-path`. Challenger vs champion, same referee,
same quarantine, n>=60, ships only if echo and boilerplate hold within 2 points and
validity drops zero. Noise defined in advance. No author's exemption.

   like a parse failure would have broken THIS TICKET'S OWN ACCEPTANCE TEST.
   "JSON validity must not drop a point" is pre-registered, so a draft that declines
   correctly would have scored as invalid JSON â€” penalised for obeying its own
   instruction. isDeclineResponse() is now exported and bench v2/v3 reports
   `declined` as a separate column from `no-beat`. Declining is free.

2. CONDITIONAL SUBTEXT: filed separately (see the conditional-assembly ticket).
   Blocker is code-side â€” there is no intimacy signal on ClassificationResult to
   condition on, and inventing one needs measuring against the 78 beats that carry
   subtext today before it can be trusted.

3. THREAD ILLUSTRATIONS ARE BAIT TOO â€” agreed, and already enforced: the

the dysregulation `subpattern` field is a CLOSED SET of nine keys and is NOT validated
