title: [bug] Echo rate is U-shaped in chunk length — 21% under 500 chars. A FLOOR is owed before the cap
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-05, whole store, 8841 beats. This CORRECTS Opie's earlier claim that
the echo bug lived in the 6-8KB regime -- that was an artifact of where he sampled.

  chunk chars      n     echo%   distinct-motivation%
  0-500         2700      21%       80%      <- dominant
  500-1000      1906       3%       98%
  1000-2000     2738       4%       96%
  2000-4000     1170       7%       94%
  4000-6000      211      12%       91%
  6000-max       116      14%       90%

U-shaped, and the two arms are NOT comparable in size. The short bucket carries roughly
567 echoes; the 6000+ bucket carries about 16. The long tail is real and the cap is still
owed, but the dominant source of prompt-example echo is chunks TOO SHORT TO BE SPECIFIC
ABOUT -- the model is asked to name what happened in a moment that contains nothing, and
reaches for the nearest concrete thing, which is the prompt.

Note the distinct-motivation column tracks it: 80% at the short end against 96-98% in the
middle. Short chunks do not just echo, they repeat each other.

TWO SEPARATE FIXES, and the floor is the bigger win:
1. FLOOR. Below some content threshold, do not analyze at all -- return no beat rather
   than an invented one. Salience gating already exists but is emotion-keyed, not
   content-keyed; a 40-character line can pass it. The knee sits between 500 and 1000
   chars, where echo drops 21% -> 3%.
2. CAP. Above ~4000 chars specificity degrades again (12-14%). Split or window rather
   than truncate, so nothing is silently lost.

SEQUENCING (Mari): ship these BEFORE re-running the prompt bench. Judge the arms in the
world that will actually exist -- calibrating against a stratum scheduled for demolition
wastes the run. The knee measurement above IS the calibration data for where the floor
goes.
notes:
RESOLVED (floor) 2026-08-05. The premise in the description is CORRECTED by finer
measurement. Reproduce with `node scripts/chunk-floor-scan.mjs` (read-only).

THE 0-500 BUCKET WAS ONE SPIKE, NOT A SLOPE. Subdividing it:

  chunk chars      n     echo%    distinct-motivation%
  0-10           515    88.7%       15.9%     <- the entire pathology
  10-20           15     6.7%      100.0%
  20-50          100     4.0%       96.0%
  50-100         218     6.0%       93.1%
  100-500       1852     4.3%       96.0%

Everything from 10 chars up sits at the same 3-6% as the healthy middle. The
'21% under 500' figure was 515 beats at 88.7% averaged against 2185 normal ones.

WHAT THE SPIKE ACTUALLY IS. 502 of those 515 beats have the identical chunk text
'open' -- a `status: open` line parsed as dialogue by the chunker's Word: rule
(that is 4ghy, the root cause). The rest are 'POST', 'PATCH', README.md: code and
config fragments. All chat-sourced, June 2026, concentrated in 2 chats. Not an
ongoing live leak (1 beat since). The salience gate could not stop them because it
asks whether a chunk looks EMOTIONAL, and a single word can answer yes: 'open'
matches a vulnerability keyword, scores 0.59, clears the 0.40 threshold.

A 500-CHAR FLOOR WOULD HAVE BEEN A SERIOUS MISTAKE. Priced: it discards 2,099
unique real beats to catch 93 echoes beyond what a 10-char floor already gets.
Recorded because the issue as written recommended exactly that.

THE AXIS IS RAW TOKENS -- NOT CHARS, AND NOT CONTENT WORDS. Content words
(skeletonTokens) look equivalent and fail at exactly the sizes that matter: for a
short utterance THE FUNCTION WORDS ARE THE CONTENT. 'I love you,' has one content
word, the same as the junk token 'open' -- but three raw tokens against one. Real
beats a content-word floor would have silently destroyed, all from this store:
'I love you,' (salience 1.0), 'All of me,', 'I love it!', 'You are a LIAR,'.

  raw tokens      n     echo%    distinct-motivation%
  1             513    89.1%       15.6%
  2-3             5    20.0%      100.0%
  3+           8323     ~5%         ~95%

SHIPPED: min_chunk_tokens: 2 in config/sentiment-config.yaml, enforced in
classifyChunk() BEFORE scoring, so a structural pattern cannot smuggle a
sub-floor chunk through (the dissociation_grounding pattern scores a lone quoted
'ok.' at 0.75, and it is one token). Returns a clean no-beat -- empty scores,
null primaryEmotion -- because callers branch on primaryEmotion as well as
passesThreshold.

Cost at floor=2: drops 5.8% of beats, kills 457 of 867 echoes (52.7%) plus 22
repeats, loses 38 'unique'. Sampling those 38 shows most are further
open/POST/PATCH artifacts whose invented motivations merely failed to collide
exactly, so true collateral is well under that.

WHY SHIP IT WHEN rejectAsEcho ALREADY CATCHES THESE. That guard is a blocklist of
sentences we have already seen. The floor removes the CONDITION that produces
them, so the next invented sentence -- which no blocklist can know in advance --
is never generated at all. Defense in depth beneath 4ghy, not a substitute for it.

Tests: src/__tests__/content-floor.test.ts, with real store rows as fixtures on
both sides. Full suite green (573 passed).

CAP NOT DONE -- split out. The rising long arm is real but small.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] The analyzer returns the PROMPT'S OWN EXAMPLE as a motivation — 9% of all beats
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 while looking at the mislabelled threads (j82t) to see whether they
could be relabelled to an event. They could not, but this fell out of the same read.

ONE MOTIVATION STRING accounts for 645 of 8700 beats (7.4%):
  "admits she's afraid the memory loss means she was never real"
  spread: 4 CHARACTERS, 37 CHATS, 35 distinct DAYS, first seen 2026-06-12.
A near-variant ("Dr. Mari Zielinska admits she's afraid...") adds 16 more.

AND IT IS IN THE RECALL POOL. 542 LEDGER ENTRIES carry that phrase as their SUMMARY,
in character_topics, across at least 8v1krexzyjkyra and aurora. Those are the companion
entries encodeBeat writes for each beat, and companion entries are what the loader
injects. So:

  beat -> companion entry -> injected in the memory block -> the analyzer reads it in
  context -> emits it as the motivation of a NEW beat -> new companion entry -> ...

A closed feedback loop. The memory system is feeding itself its own output and treating
the echo as fresh emotional evidence. That is why it crosses CHARACTER boundaries --
Priya and Aurora both "admit" a fear that is Mari's, because they were shown Mari's
memory and the analyzer attributed what it read.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT:
- The emotion tag varies ([fear], [shame], [desire], [hope], [vulnerability]) so the
  summaries are not byte-identical and any exact-match guard misses them.
- dedup's incident rule REQUIRES a same-moment proof before skipping a similar beat
  (deliberately -- it exists to stop distinct moments collapsing on boilerplate). Across
  chats there is no such proof, so every copy is created. The guard is behaving as
  designed; the design assumed the analyzer would not emit the same sentence 645 times.

INTERACTION WITH TODAY'S 06pq FIX -- IMPORTANT, AND IT CUTS AGAINST ME:
Before 06pq, the poller sent no turnNumber, so turnStart was 0 on every live turn and
the same-moment test was VACUOUSLY TRUE within a chat. That accidentally suppressed the
2nd+ identical beat WITHIN a chat -- an unintended brake on this loop. 06pq made the
test honest (message+swipe), which is correct and fixes a real collapse bug, but it also
REMOVES THAT BRAKE. Expect this loop to amplify faster now, not slower, until it is
fixed. 06pq is not wrong; this is the thing that has to land beside it.

WHERE TO LOOK, in order:
1. The analyzer prompt: it is handed prior context and does not appear to be told that
   remembered material is NOT this turn's evidence. A beat must be derived from what
   just happened, never from what was recalled.
2. What exactly is in the injected block at analysis time -- if analyzeChunks sees the
   memory block or a window containing it, that is the leak.
3. A cheap structural backstop: refuse to encode a beat whose motivation is a near-exact
   match of an entry ALREADY IN the injected memory block for that turn. Unlike a global
   similarity rule this cannot suppress a genuine repeat, because it only fires on text
   we just showed the model.

CLEANUP is a separate decision (and large: 645 beats, 542 entries). Do NOT start it
before the loop is closed -- the store refills. Same rule as oknn.

NOTE the phrase is emotionally load-bearing for TC's RP, so this is not merely noisy
data: the characters' recorded inner lives are 7% one borrowed sentence.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-04. It was neither of my two theories.

NOT an injection feedback loop, and NOT an attractor intrinsic to the model. The
sentence is THE PROMPT'S OWN EXAMPLE. analyzer.ts:162, inside SHARED_RULES:

  "motivation must name the SPECIFIC content of THIS moment ... so two different
   moments can never produce the same sentence. Genre descriptions are forbidden.
     BAD:  "exposes her personal fear" / ...
     GOOD: "admits she's afraid the memory loss means she was never real" / ..."

The sentence chosen to illustrate "two different moments can never produce the same
sentence" became the most repeated sentence in the store. 669 beats.

THE EVIDENCE THAT RULED OUT THE ALTERNATIVES, in order:
- ZERO story-sourced beats echo it. The import path runs the SAME analyzer with a
  different context assembly. If it were the model, story beats would show it too.
- Only 1% (4 of 669) of the source chunks that produced it mention "never real" or
  "memory loss". The analyzer is not reading it back out of the text, so it is not a
  recall loop.
- Other fields vary sensibly around it -- an [anger] beat carrying a vulnerability
  motivation while relationalDynamics tracks the real text. One FIELD collapses; the
  rest of the analysis is fine.
- The chunks that trigger it are huge (6-8KB) and often not emotional at all: one was
  a discussion of pipeline.ts code. Given nothing specific to say, the model returns
  the nearest phrasing it has been shown, and the prompt is nearest.

BOTH SIDES OF THE ILLUSTRATION LEAK, not just the recommended one: 107 beats open with
a paraphrase of the BAD example ("The speaker is exposing their openness..."). Total
echoing a prompt example before the fix: 792 of 8703 beats (9%).

FIX, two parts, because either alone is insufficient:
1. The examples are reworded to an unrelated domain ("insists the boat was green, not
   blue"), labelled as illustrations of SHAPE, with an explicit instruction not to
   reuse their words and to report no beat rather than reach for a remembered phrase.
2. echoesAnExample() in analyzer.ts REJECTS an analysis whose motivation matches any
   example, returning null -- the existing unusable-analysis path. Rewording is not a
   guarantee; this is. The list deliberately KEEPS THE RETIRED EXAMPLES, because the
   old wording is what 669 stored beats echo and an older build or a re-analysis must
   still be caught.

REMEASURED AFTER THE FIX (guard applied to the existing store):
  BEATS   8703 total, 789 echoes (9%), 7914 real
     professor_mari  6433 / 496 echo (8%)
     priya ledger    2020 / 173 echo (9%)
     aurora           141 / 112 echo (79%)   <- 29 real, and 12 of those are story
     lara card         37 /   8 echo (22%)
     lara story ledgers 72 /  0 echo (0%)    <- import path clean, as predicted
  ENTRIES 14930 total, 547 with an echo summary (4%)
  39 chats produced at least one echo.

CONSEQUENCE FOR 7pcm (written-vs-played): aurora's "129 chat beats" is really 112 echo
plus 17 real. The confound TC named is real but an order of magnitude smaller than the
raw number suggested. 7pcm updated.

CLEANUP NOT DONE -- filed separately. 789 beats and 547 entries. Safe to do now that
minting is fixed, but it is a live-store mutation and TC's call.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] Poller never sends turnNumber — turnStart collapses to 0 and defeats the same-moment dedup guard
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 while starting s2lw. Distinct from s2lw, and a prerequisite for it.

turn-bridge.ts handleDetectedTurn() builds the /api/process-turn body as
{ characterId, characterName, participantIds, chatId, sceneTitle, messageText,
userMessageText }. There is NO turnNumber. api.ts:524 defaults `turnNumber = 0`, and
api.ts:645-646 then stamps every chunk from the poller path with turnStart 0 (the
assistant chunk) and turnStart -1 (the user chunk).

MEASURED IN THE LIVE STORE, 14833 index rows, 3891 carrying turnStart:
  turnStart=0   -> 462 rows
  turnStart=-1  ->  99 rows
  turnStart=1   ->  42 rows   <- and a normal spread beyond (2, 4, 6, 8, 14, ...)
The 0/-1 spike is the poller path. The spread is the IMPORT path, where a real turn
number flows. 561 rows sit on the degenerate value.

WHY IT MATTERS -- IT DEFEATS A GUARD BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS CASE. dedup.ts decide(),
character_topics + kind=incident, will only skip a similar incident when it can PROVE
the two are the same moment:

    const sameMoment =
      !!input.sourceChatId && input.sourceChatId === e.sourceChatId &&
      typeof input.turnStart === "number" && typeof e.turnStart === "number" &&
      Math.abs(input.turnStart - e.turnStart) <= SAME_MOMENT_TURN_WINDOW;
    if (sameMoment) return { action: "skip", against: e };

Its own comment says why the proof is required: "the analyzer emits identical genre
boilerplate for genuinely distinct moments (measured: 37% of Mari's vulnerability
beats collapsed, 78 byte-identical summaries)".

On the poller path turnStart is ALWAYS 0, so |0-0| <= window is ALWAYS true. The
proof is vacuous and the guard inverts: any two similar incident beats anywhere in
the same chat are treated as the same moment and the second is SKIPPED. The 37%
collapse the guard was written to stop is unguarded again on the live path -- and the
poller is now the live path.

Note the direction. This is the OPPOSITE failure from s2lw: s2lw is "a re-roll keeps
both versions", this is "distinct moments collapse into one". Same root cause -- the
poller supplies no per-turn identity.

FIX DIRECTION, and it should be decided WITH s2lw because they share the plumbing:
the true identity of a moment is the MESSAGE ID, which is exactly what a re-roll
preserves and what a new turn changes. Proposal: add an optional sourceMessageId to
Entry/IndexEntry (optional-field additions are backward-compatible -- bodyTerms and
the 4g9w serialization note), stamp it from the poller, and have sameMoment prefer
message-id equality when both sides carry it, falling back to the turnStart window
for import-path and legacy rows. A synthetic monotonic turnNumber from poller-state
would also fix the collapse but gives s2lw nothing.

DO NOT simply pass a fabricated turnNumber without deciding this -- it would paper
over the collapse while leaving s2lw with no retire key.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped 2026-08-04 in commit 6dcd005 alongside s2lw; the issue was left open by oversight. sourceMessageId + sourceSwipeIndex are stamped from the poller through process-turn, and dedup's sameMoment prefers the pair with a chat+turn fallback for import-path and legacy rows. Regression test in dedup-matrix.test.ts covers two live turns both at turnStart 0.

title: [bug] Summarizer drops the user's clause — first-person facts lost and made unretrievable
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the np4b confound sweep. This is FACT LOSS, not a phrasing complaint.

When a first-person clause is coordinated with a third-person clause, the summarizer keeps the third-person one and DROPS THE USER'S. Two verified cases, content vs summary:

  utopic-wzgh3ilg  (user_topics, characters/k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf)
    content: "I was in the Army, and Mari is Polish."
    summary: "Mari is Polish"
    -> The user's military service is gone. A character's nationality survived.

  utopic-jakzyxe9  (user_topics, chats/c7Ui03XMg6bV7lVXOyz-8)
    content: "It was my fourth sapper stakes, and Sgt Roger's 6th? 7th? Sgt Lynn had done it 5 times."
    summary: "Sgt Roger has completed sapper stakes between 6th and 7th time; Sgt Lynn has completed it 5 times."
    -> The user's OWN fourth sapper stakes is gone. Two third parties' counts survived.

WHY THIS IS SEVERE AND NOT COSMETIC. The dropped fact becomes RETRIEVALLY INVISIBLE, not merely mis-worded:
  - Retrieval scores the SUMMARY, so "Army" is not matchable from there.
  - tp5's bodyTerms would normally rescue a body-only term, but bodyTerms harvests NAMES ONLY (capitalised tokens). "Army" is capitalised and might survive; "my fourth sapper stakes" contains no name at all and cannot.
So the user asking "tell me about my time in the Army" may reach an entry whose summary is about a character's nationality, or nothing.

It also actively feeds np4b: the entry LOOKS like a misfiling (a fact about Mari sitting in user_topics) when the lane was right all along — the summariser removed the reason it was there. Any lane-mismatch detector will keep reporting these as errors.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, unverified: a summarisation prompt biased toward third-person declarative phrasing, likely with an instruction to avoid first person. That is correct for a memory ABOUT a character and wrong for one about the user, and the pipeline appears not to distinguish. Look at the digest/ambient summarisation prompts before changing anything.

WHAT A FIX MUST PRESERVE: the summary is what retrieval scores, so it has to carry the user's clause when there is one. "User served in the Army; Mari is Polish" is fine. Dropping either half is not.

VERIFY BY: re-running scripts/confound-sweep.mjs after a fix — several bucket-B entries in that report were flagged ONLY because their summary dropped the user's clause, so a real fix should visibly shrink the candidate list.
notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-04. Prompt fix + deterministic net, 19 new tests, full suite 498 pass.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, and it is NOT a prompt instruction to avoid first person --
no such string exists anywhere in the prompts. Both entries came from the tier-3
ambient path (ambient.ts, 2026-06-01), which stores content=fact.text (the quote)
and summary=fact.fact. Neither SYSTEM_PROMPT nor SCENE_FACTS_SYSTEM_PROMPT ever
told the model a SINGLE SENTENCE may carry two facts about different people, so it
picked one clause. SCENE_FACTS taught the reverse case (a fact may span several
sentences) but not this one. facts.ts (1dn) postdates both entries; not implicated.

FIX 1, primary: both prompts now teach the split, with the Army sentence as a
worked two-fact example.
FIX 2, net: src/user-clause.ts, applied in classifyAmbient + classifySceneFacts.
Restores the clause as a verbatim [user: ...] PREFIX -- prefix so it survives the
120-char truncateSummary cap; verbatim because I -> User needs verb agreement and
there is no safe local rule, the same shape as the sentence-case trap.

THE CONDITION THAT MEASUREMENT ADDED, and the number to remember. My first cut
fired whenever a first-person clause had content words absent from the summary.
Scanned live: 169 hits, and on inspection MOST WERE HEALTHY -- a user_topics
summary routinely leaves the subject implicit (Speaks three languages / Was
medicated through high school / has a memory system to stabilize). Absence of the
user is NOT evidence the user was dropped. So the survivor must now be positively
about someone else. Accepting a third-party mention anywhere left 39, still mostly
the user's own facts that happened to name someone (has difficulty remembering
character names, specifically Hargrove). Requiring SUBJECT POSITION -- an explicit
non-user subject, or a summary that OPENS with a roster name -- gives 4. Same
conclusion the confound sweep reached independently, in its own words: only the
subject position is evidence.

ALSO FOUND BY THE SCAN: the prefix was bounded per-clause but not in total. One
entry whose content is a whole transcript produced a ~2000-char prefix out of
forty individually-capped clauses. Now capped overall (2 clauses, 90 chars).

VERIFY STEP NEEDS AMENDING. This issue says re-run confound-sweep.mjs and expect
the candidate list to shrink. It will not: the fix protects NEW extractions and
rewrites no stored entry. Sweep baseline unchanged at 188 (120 character_topics,
68 user_topics). scripts/user-clause-scan.mjs is the read-only measurement that
actually answers the question: 4 candidates over 2883 user_topics entries, two of
which are utopic-wzgh3ilg and utopic-jakzyxe9, the verified cases from this issue.
The other two are stored-data artifacts the live path would not produce (no
speaker split, no extractor subject).

NOT BACKFILLED, deliberately. Two genuine entries is a hand edit, not a scripted
mutation of the live store, and the scan cannot reproduce the speaker guard
retroactively -- a stored entry has no User:/Scene: split. TC's call.
close_reason: Closed

title: SETTING tag on memories — where/when the remembered thing happened (Iraq 2004 vs War 20XX)
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-04: "So when I tell Mari about my war memories, she remembers they are from Iraq 2004, and Collier's memories are from War 20XX."

WHAT IT IS. A SETTING tag on a memory — where and when the remembered thing happened. Not where it was recorded, and not the narrative clock.

WHY THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. TC's example is the user/character membrane stated in the most tractable form anyone has managed yet. "Iraq 2004" vs "War 20XX" separates user-world from character-world by a property the TEXT ACTUALLY CONTAINS, where the name does not: 76aw proved Collier and Lowe never co-occur in a single entry, so nothing in the corpus distinguishes the two Thomases — but a year and a place are usually right there in the sentence. Setting is the world discriminator the doctrine amendment needs, in a form that can be extracted rather than declared.

NOT THE SAME AS timeContext. Entry.timeContext already exists — { timeOfDay, dayOfWeek, inferredFrom } from the soft clock (off by default, MARINARA_EXTENDER_TIMESENSE=1). That is narrative time-of-day AT CAPTURE ("it was evening when this was said"). Setting is where the remembered EVENT sits. Do not overload the existing field; a memory recorded on a Tuesday evening about Iraq in 2004 needs both and they are unrelated.

EVIDENCE IT IS ALREADY BITING, independent of TC's example:
- auz1 — outline places the pre-meet in Kansas, played entries place it in Boston. A live geography conflict with no field to record either claim against.
- The Cambridge ambiguity, which already produced a wrong ruling once: Oleana/Cambridge MA (Boston metro) vs Priya having studied in Cambridge, England. Same token, two places, and the store cannot tell them apart.
- fph4 (chronology lint, P1) cannot pick the right birth year for a shared name until something carries world/period.

THE STRONGEST USE IS A GUARD, NOT A RECALL AID. The dangerous failure is not "she cannot recall the Iraq story" — it is injecting an Iraq-2004 memory into a War-20XX scene, where the character confabulates across worlds. Setting can GATE injection the way provenance:"unplayed" already does: a memory whose setting contradicts the current scene is withheld rather than ranked. That mechanism exists and is proven; this would be a second consumer of it.

SHAPE (proposal, not settled): optional setting?: { place?: string; period?: string; world?: string } on Entry, mirrored onto IndexEntry if it must gate retrieval without opening files (it must, if it gates injection). ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, never "no setting" — the same rule bodyTerms needed, and the reason the tp5 backfill skips unreadable files rather than writing empty lists.

SERIALIZATION: an optional field is backward-compatible (bodyTerms proved this on 14k rows). Do NOT encode setting by widening an existing enum — see the EntryStatus audit.

POPULATION: realistically the LLM pass at ingest, shared with 76aw slice 2 and the same call that would supply world tags. Lexical extraction will find "Iraq" and "2004" but cannot decide they belong to the user's world rather than the character's; that judgement is the whole point.

RELATIONSHIP TO 4g9w: adjacent, not duplicate. 4g9w separates WHO a memory is about from who can recall it; this separates WHERE/WHEN it is set. Both are properties the lane axis was never able to carry, and both would be populated by the same ingest pass.

OPEN: does setting belong to the memory or to the ARC/scene it came from (scene-conclude already emits dated summaries)? Inheriting from the scene would populate a lot of entries for free and is worth checking before hand-tagging anything.

title: Memory scoping: separate SUBJECT (who it is about) from SCOPE (who can recall it)
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-04, from the Becky Collier misfiling (np4b).

THE OBSERVATION. Scope answers "WHO CAN RECALL THIS". It does not answer "WHO IS THIS ABOUT", and the store has nowhere else to put that — so aboutness has been forced onto the LANE axis, which offers exactly two subjects: user_topics (the human player) or character_topics (the scope owner). A fact about a THIRD person has no correct home.

THE CASE THAT EXPOSED IT: "Thomas's sister is Rebecca 'Becky' Collier" is a TRUE fact about Thomas Collier, stored under characters/professor_mari. Nothing is wrong with the scope — Mari is exactly who should be able to recall it. It was filed in user_topics, which asserts it is about the USER; character_topics would assert it is about MARI. Both are wrong, and there is no third option. The same gap produced the sons confound in the opposite direction (a fact about the user's real children filed in character_topics with the character's surname attached).

THE ALTERNATIVE TC CONSIDERED AND SET ASIDE: splitting scope into more tiers — Global/Subglobal | Character/Other-Character-Relationships/Other-Character-Mentions | Chat. TC's own read was that it "seems messy", and it is: it tries to make ONE axis answer TWO questions, so the tiers multiply (roughly 2x3 buckets) while most of the combinations do not correspond to a real distinction anyone would file against.

THE PROPOSAL: keep scope meaning VISIBILITY, and add SUBJECT meaning ABOUTNESS. One optional field naming the entity a memory is about, rather than a taxonomy. Scope stays chat/character/global (+persona), lane stays a kind-of-memory axis, and "who is this about" stops being inferred from the lane.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS:
- np4b becomes MECHANICAL. "A user_topics entry whose subject is not the user" is a script; today it needs a human to read every entry. Combined with egj3 (declared user identity) that is a real cleanup sweep instead of a judgement call.
- 0qx6 (persona tier) gets designed on the right axis. "Facts about the persona known to all characters" is the SAME aboutness problem wearing a different hat, and building it as a fourth SCOPE would bake the conflation in permanently. This is why 0qx6 should wait on the decision here.
- Retrieval gains a real filter — "what does Mari know about Thomas Collier" is answerable, where today subject is only implied.
- The raw material already exists: the entity index (76aw slice 1, data/entities.yaml) resolves surface forms to canonical entities, which is what a subject field would reference.

SERIALIZATION NOTE, learned the hard way on this codebase: adding an OPTIONAL field to IndexEntry/Entry is safe and backward-compatible (bodyTerms did exactly this). WIDENING THE SCOPE ENUM is not — see the EntryStatus audit and the supersededBy comment: unknown enum values round-trip silently through storage layers that parse-and-cast without validation. That asymmetry is itself an argument for the field over the tier split.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT:
- One subject or several? "Mari and Priya argued" is about both.
- Does subject need the WORLD tag (76aw doctrine amendment), or does the entity record carry it? Probably the entity record.
- Who populates it — the ingest pipeline, the curator, or backfill? Existing entries have no subject and the same "absent means unknown, never means none" rule as bodyTerms applies.
- Relationship to w4l (subject->target emotion ledger) and 19o (relationship topology): both already assume a subject notion exists. This would give them one to share.

NOT URGENT (TC): the current model "works well enough". Filed so the persona tier and the confound sweep are not designed around the gap.
notes:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LIVE SPECIMENS 2026-08-25, and the canon TC stated for the record.

THE STRUCTURE THIS TICKET EXISTS TO EXPRESS, from TC directly:

  TC      real-life, out-of-universe personhood. Nodaway County, Missouri; wife in
          Kirksville. Who he is when talking to Mari OOC.
  Thomas  the IN-CHARACTER PERSONA, sharing his first name. From Independence, MO;
          keeps an apartment in the Iowa town where Prescott State University is;
          is there because of Mari.

Two entities, one first name, and the store currently has one lane for both.

FOUR SPECIMENS, all live, all in user_topics — the lane meaning A FACT ABOUT THE
HUMAN:

  utopic-fv4yj2v8  "Thomas's family background ... a functional errand life in Iowa"
                   TRUE of the persona. Correct content, wrong lane semantics.
  utopic-j8itu2vd  "User likely lives in Texas"
  utopic-ntgxdp4b  "Lives in or has connection to Texas; unsure of weed legality"
  utopic-kftzlm70  "considers Texas warm in winter, implying familiarity with
                   colder climates"
                   All three drawn from the Priya arc (k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf =
                   Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran), which is Austin/Texas-set and in which
                   Thomas is a speaker. Plausibly true of THOMAS-in-that-arc; false
                   of TC, who lives in Missouri.

THE TRUE ONE IS THE BEST ARGUMENT. utopic-fv4yj2v8 is not a mistake to clean up —
its content is right. It is in user_topics because there is nowhere else to put a
fact about the persona, and it sits beside three doubtful rows for exactly the same
reason. A cleanup pass would delete the doubtful ones and leave the lane just as
unable to express the difference. THE DEFECT IS THE MISSING AXIS, not the rows.

AND THE DECLARATION CANNOT HELP EITHER. data/user-identity.yaml lists "thomas lowe"
and "thomas charles lowe" as aliases of canonical "TC Lowe" — correct, because that
IS TC's real name — so the one identity artifact the system trusts collapses the
persona into the person by construction. The standing ruling that bare "Thomas" must
NOT expand (inside an RP it means the character) is currently the only thing holding
the membrane, and it is doing far more load-bearing work than it looks.

GAP WORTH RECORDING: the store has NO record of Independence, Missouri. Thomas's
origin is not captured at all, while TC's home county is — so the persona is the half
that is both unexpressed and misfiled.

Tracked as a specimen in qhej; hhdr named the mechanism (referent bleed across the
user/character membrane); 0qx6 is the persona tier this needs underneath it.

title: Declare the USER's identity — the one entity that should never be inferred
description:
RAISED BY the 76aw slice 1 findings and TC 2026-08-04.

The user is the single highest-value entity in the store — nearly every user_topics entry is about them — and the only one whose identity is known, stable, and authoritative in advance. It is currently INFERRED like any other name, and inference is failing on it specifically:

- "thomas" collides 11 ways in the entity index, so the ambiguity cap now suppresses it entirely. Thomas Lowe, Thomas Charles Lowe and TC Lowe are all TC\x27s real names and SHOULD resolve to one person; suppression is safe but wrong.
- Thomas Collier (RP character) is generally called "Thomas" and has sometimes been called "TC" — persona blending by the model, not a real alias.
- One concrete corruption already exists: "TC\x27s sons: Henry Warren and Malcolm Bradley Collier" attributes the character\x27s sons to the user.

WHAT TO BUILD: an explicit user-identity record — the set of names and forms that mean the user, marked as user-world. Consulted by the entity index (so those forms resolve together and are exempt from the ambiguity cap, which exists for guesses, not for declarations) and by the mention resolver.

WHY DECLARED RATHER THAN LEARNED: the store contains no evidence that could separate the two Thomases — measured, Collier and Lowe NEVER co-occur in any entry. The discriminator cannot come from the text. It can come from the user in one sentence.

RELATED: this is the same machinery the persona tier needs (0qx6 — facts about the persona known to all characters), and the natural home for the world tag the 76aw doctrine amendment requires. Also the shape a declared character SPLIT would need (Desmond/Draymond Cole drifted from one character into two, which is history no text analysis recovers).

SURFACE: the memory browser is the obvious place to declare and edit it, alongside the identity/alias repair already planned for hwlj.
close_reason: Shipped. Live: 'what did TC say' reaches 256 -> 2023 of 2616 rows naming tc/lowe/thomas. Declared forms exempt from ALIAS_MAX_AMBIGUITY; exclusions stop the declared user meeting the inferred character through the shared 'thomas' token. Identity declared in the live store as TC Lowe. No UI yet (hwlj); np4b's sweep is now mechanical.

title: 76aw slice 1: mention-entity index + cue expansion (no LLM)
description:
Slice 1 of 76aw, scoped by measurement and two TC rulings.

RULING 1 (TC): all multi-word proper nouns are worth remembering — Marinara Engine, Elysium Grand, Porsche Taycan are entities of a different TYPE, not noise to filter. So the table is a general mention-entity index and entity typing is NOT a gate on indexing.

RULING 2 (TC): "Claude and Claude Code both refer to you. If characters get to be people, you can be too." So the Claude/Claude Code case is a CORRECT person entity, not the false positive I recorded it as. Removes the sharpest objection to the pronoun signal.

ERICA IS A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT (TC): her low pronoun rate (0.22, below Elden Ring) is because she is discussed ANALYTICALLY — the Erica Test is the failure we are trying to pass. That signature is caused by the bug, so building the detector to fit it would encode the failure. The independent-use signal catches her instead (0.38).

WHAT SHIPS:
- Extraction of capitalised multi-token runs, PER FIELD (summary and content scanned separately — a regex over concatenated text produced "Priya Chandrasekaran Outcome" by running a name into the next YAML key).
- A mention-entity store keyed on the canonical full form, holding surface variants and the counts the thresholds are derived from.
- PERSON tag = pronoun-proximity rate OR independent-use rate over threshold. The two signals fail in OPPOSITE directions (Erica: 0.22 pronoun / 0.38 independent; Mari Zielinska: 0.54 / 0.06), so either alone loses one of the two most important entities. Noise accepted per TC.
- ALIAS links gated separately by per-part independent use — this is the safety property and it is independent of type. Measured: Cathmore 0.38, Cole 0.72, Taycan 0.33 link; Ring 0.12, Grand 0.07, Zielinska 0.06 do not. The catastrophic case (Elden = Ring) is excluded by construction.
- CUE EXPANSION at retrieval: expand the CONVERSATION text with linked forms, not the stored rows. One expansion per turn instead of per entry, and it keeps the index from growing again after tp5 already cost 23%.

NOT IN THIS SLICE: LLM extraction (slice 2, and the only thing that can supply the world tags the doctrine amendment needs — user-Thomas vs character-Thomas is not a surface-form distinction); a review surface in the memory browser; distinctiveness weighting to replace raw independent use.
close_reason: Shipped 0efe8ca. End-to-end on the live store: 'tell me about Cathmore' reaches 24 -> 90 of 108 Erica-corpus entries; 'tell me about Erica' 89 -> 90. Index built from 14032 files: 231 entities, 146 with an alias. Erica Cathmore links both parts and picks up 'Gunnery Sergeant Cathmore' as coreferent. Residual 18/108 are the tp5 leftovers - the mention is never capitalised, so nothing is harvested to link.

title: .env unconditionally overwrites shell env, so a per-run override is impossible
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03, immediately after MarinaraExtender-1akw, and it is the ROOT CAUSE that made 1akw possible for someone who already knew the rule.

THE CODE (index.ts loadDotEnv):
  // .env always wins — overwrites stale system env vars (e.g. from Python venvs)
  if (key && val) process.env[key] = val;

Unconditional assignment. Not `process.env[key] ??= val`. So a value passed on the command line is read, then silently replaced by .env a moment later.

HOW IT BIT. Restarting a demo sidecar deliberately as:
  MARINARA_EXTENDER_DATA=<scratch> MARINARA_EXTENDER_PORT=3099 MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 node dist/index.js
started with the banner "Engine poller: ON — every 5000ms against http://127.0.0.1:7860". The flag was correct, the code reading it (`=== "1"`) is correct, and .env carries MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=1. The shell value never survived to the check.

The banner then prints "(disable with MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 if the extension is also running)" — advice the program has just made impossible to follow.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS. This inverts the precedence every other tool in the ecosystem uses: dotenv and every port of it deliberately do NOT override an existing process.env, precisely so a one-off run can differ from the stored config. Here it means:
- No per-invocation override of ANY setting, for tests, demos, or reproductions.
- The launch command LOOKS like it took effect. There is no warning, no log line, nothing that says "your flag was discarded".
- Anyone reading the code sees `MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER === "1"` and concludes the flag works, because it does — just not from where they set it.

Note the failure it caused (1akw) was a WRITE TO THE LIVE ENGINE from a scratch store. This is not a cosmetic precedence quibble.

THE STATED RATIONALE IS REAL BUT THE CURE IS WORSE. Stale vars leaking in from a Python venv or a parent shell is a genuine annoyance. But the fix costs the ability to configure a single run at all, and it fails SILENTLY, which is the part that does the damage.

FIX:
  if (key && val && process.env[key] === undefined) process.env[key] = val;
plus, to keep the original intent available, a loud line when a shell value shadows a .env value:
  [ME:env] MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0 from the environment overrides .env (=1)
so the venv-pollution case the comment worries about becomes VISIBLE rather than silently corrected. If some deployment truly needs the old behaviour, MARINARA_EXTENDER_ENV_WINS=1 can restore it — but it should be opt-in, not the default.

Also worth a test: loadDotEnv currently has no coverage of the precedence question at all.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: there is none from the command line. You must edit .env, run from a directory with a different PACKAGE_ROOT, or temporarily comment the line out.
notes:
CLOSED OUT 2026-08-04. TC authorised removing the shadowing credential.

The stale MARINARA_EXTENDER_API_KEY was a USER-scope Windows environment variable (not Machine). Backed up to C:\Users\holyk\marinara-extender-REMOVED-api-key.txt with restore instructions, then removed via [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(...,$null,'User').

VERIFIED: a sidecar started without it in scope now logs only '[ME:env] taken from the environment, overriding .env: MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER' — the deliberate flag, no credential warning — which is proof the .env key is the one in use, since the warning fires exactly when the environment shadows it. Already-running processes keep the old value until restarted; that is inherent to how env is inherited at spawn, not a gap.
close_reason: Shipped: b1nu in 7d4ae5e, bkdz in bb82696. Both pushed.

title: Memory browser slice 2: edit, delete, restore (the mutations)
description:
Slice 2 of hwlj. Slice 1 shipped read-only on purpose — editing memories is where a half-built UI does real damage, and reading answered the urgent question first (what is stored, why did recall behave that way).

WHAT THIS ADDS, all over endpoints that already exist and are already tested server-side:
- EDIT — PATCH /api/entries/:id (summary, content, status). Inline in the card, not a modal; the card is already the unit the reader is looking at.
- DELETE — DELETE /api/entries/:id. SOFT by default: the entry moves to cold and stays recoverable. The UI must SAY that, because the whole architecture rests on never destroying a memory on one action.
- DELETED VIEW + RESTORE — GET /api/deleted, POST /api/entries/:id/restore, per scope.
- PURGE — DELETE ?purge=true, reachable ONLY from inside the deleted view, and only behind an explicit confirm. This is the one irreversible action in the product.

CSRF: the page is served from the sidecar itself, so a same-origin fetch POST still carries an Origin header and needs the token. Fetch it at boot from GET /api/csrf-token and send x-me-csrf. The token is minted per process, so a sidecar restart invalidates it — refetch once on 403 and retry, the same recovery the old extension used.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS CARRIED FROM SLICE 1:
- Model the surface around the question, not the artefact (TC, on the Why? button). Edit and Delete belong ON the memory, beside Why?, for the same reason Why? did.
- Destructive actions must state their reversibility in plain language at the point of action, not in a doc.
- Status is editable because open_threads carry a real lifecycle (open/in_progress/done/deferred) and "done" is what removes a resolved thread from recall.

NOT IN THIS SLICE: create-new-memory (the store should be written by the pipeline, not typed by hand — a manual create path needs its own thinking about dedup and provenance), identity/alias repair, merge/supersede.
close_reason: Shipped in 7d4ae5e, pushed. Edit/delete/restore/purge over the existing endpoints, CSRF with stale-token retry, 10 integration cases pinning the round-trip and that soft-delete is soft.

title: Persona scope — a fourth tier between character and global
description:
DESIGN CALL FROM TC 2026-08-03. Add a PERSONA scope, sitting above character and below global.

THE DEFINITION, in his words: facts known about that persona by ALL characters who interact with them. Today the ladder is chat -> character -> global, and there is no home for "this is true of ME, and everyone who has met me knows it". Such facts currently land in one of two wrong places: character scope (siloed per character, so every character must independently relearn the same fact about the user) or global (leaks to every persona, which is worse — a fact about persona A becomes ambient truth while playing persona B).

THE LADDER AFTER THIS CHANGE:
  chat      — this conversation only
  character — what THIS character knows / their own arc
  persona   — facts about THIS persona, shared across the characters who have met them   <-- NEW
  global    — true everywhere, for every character and every persona

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "GLOBAL BUT SMALLER": global is currently the only cross-character tier and it is deliberately opt-in and rare (verified: no automatic writer ever targets global — ambient, facts, reconcile, holding-pool and arc-promotion write only character and chat). Persona is the tier that SHOULD receive automatic writes, because most durable facts a user establishes are about themselves. Getting this tier in is what lets automatic capture stop over-writing to character.

IT MUST BE EPISTEMIC, NOT FLAT — TC: "or with the secret system". Persona-scope must NOT mean "every character knows this". It means "this is a fact about the persona, whose visibility is governed". Depends on and feeds MarinaraExtender-1m9 (stateful entity-state lane + epistemic injection, who-knows-what incl. hiding):
- default: known to characters who have actually interacted with this persona
- gated: known to a named subset (told to one character in confidence)
- hidden: true of the persona, known to none — the user knows, the cast does not
A persona tier without the epistemic layer would leak secrets to every character on contact, which is strictly worse than the status quo. Do NOT ship the scope before the visibility model exists, or design it so the default is conservative (interaction-gated) and widening is explicit.

PLUMBING — the identifier is already available, at every layer we need:
- Engine capability host: persistence.getChat(chatId) returns personaId on CapabilityChatRecord. Our package can resolve it without any Engine change.
- Extension API v5 exposes personaId (behind read_active_persona) if we ever go that route.
- The sidecar contributor input already carries chatId, so the package can look personaId up and pass it to /api/pre-turn.

SURFACE AREA — this widens a serialized enum, which this codebase has already been burned by. See the EntryProvenance note in storage.ts: "widening a serialized enum breaks consumers silently". Touch list: Scope type + VALID_SCOPES, scopeDir/indexPath/entryPath, loadIndexes and selectEntries in loader.ts, a new MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_PERSONA (the three existing budgets are chat 4000 / character 2000 / global 1000), promotion.runPromotionAll, cleanup, cold storage, dedup targets, the identity map (persona identities are a separate namespace from character identities and must not collide), the receipts scope accounting, and the UI sidebar.
Back-compat: old stores have no persona dir and no persona entries. Absent must read as empty, never as an error.

OPEN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING:
1. Persona identity — personas can be renamed and recreated like characters. Do they need the same alias/relink machinery (/api/identity/relink) or can they key on the Engine personaId alone? Renaming is the common case and it must not orphan memories.
2. Group scenes — several characters, one persona. Interaction-gating needs a record of WHICH characters have met this persona. Does that live on the persona index or in the entity-state lane from 1m9?
3. Budget default. Persona facts are high-value and low-volume; likely a small budget (~1000) but it competes with character for the same prompt space.
4. Migration — is there a pass that identifies existing character-scope entries that are really about the user and offers to relocate them? Probably a later, human-gated tool, not an automatic sweep.

RELATED: 1m9 (epistemic layer, hard dependency for the visibility model), c0b7 (scope defaulting — fix that BEFORE adding a fourth value, or the malformed-scope path gains another way to be wrong), hwlj (UI needs a persona section in the sidebar).
notes:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE ROSTER IS REAL AND READABLE, 2026-08-25. FOUR PERSONAS EXIST IN THE ENGINE RIGHT
NOW, WITH DISTINCT AND CONFUSABLE BIOGRAPHIES.

Read from the running Engine, GET /api/characters/personas/list. This ticket has been
arguing for a persona tier in the abstract; here is the concrete roster it would have
to model, with only the identity-bearing fields quoted:

  TC      (WHiB43tunmDxNBNYJUkHh)  "Army veteran (supply clerk turned combat engineer
          after 9/11). Husband, father of two. Degrees in Psychology and Computer
          Science, minor in Humanities."
  Thomas  (T5qPktvQZjpwWxMFWx1DA)  "Thomas Collier: 26, white, 5'10, from
          Independence, MO, Army veteran (satellite technician). Degree in Computer
          Science, minor in Humanities."
  Mark    (Kn-DGK07yZfxih6azJWKQ)  "A 23-year-old medically retired Army veteran who
          served as a Satellite Communication Systems Operator-Maintainer. Deployed to
          Iraq, where an IED strike killed his friend Finch..."
  Dr. Mari Zielińska (oE2T6LZwvzxvviv4-GEpC) — Mari also exists as a persona.

WHY THIS IS THE ARGUMENT, not just background. THREE OF THE FOUR ARE ARMY VETERANS,
and two of them are SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS people. TC is a supply clerk turned
combat engineer; Thomas is a satellite technician; Mark is a satellite comms operator
whose Iraq/IED story is his defining event. These are not distant identities that
happen to share a user — they are near-duplicates differing in exactly the details a
summariser flattens first. Any lane that cannot name WHICH ONE is going to blend
them, and the blend will read as coherent, which is hhdr's chimera-fusion precondition
stated in advance rather than discovered afterwards.

THE EXTENDER HAS NO AXIS FOR THIS. data/user-identity.yaml holds ONE canonical
identity ("TC Lowe", aliases thomas lowe / thomas charles lowe / tc), and user_topics
means "a fact about the human" with no further discrimination. So four biographies
land in one lane and the only thing separating them is the standing ruling that bare
"Thomas" must not expand — a single alias rule doing structural work.

ALREADY VISIBLE IN THE DATA, three specimens, all live:
  utopic-fv4yj2v8  Thomas's Iowa errand life — TRUE of the persona, filed as a fact
                   about the human. Right content, no way to say whose.
  utopic-j8itu2vd  "User likely lives in Texas" — from the Priya arc, where Thomas is
                   the persona. False of TC.
  su6h             Thomas's origin: in his persona card AND said 21 times in RP,
                   recorded zero times.
The first two are the lane being unable to say WHO; the third is the persona's
biography failing to land at all. Both directions of the same missing axis.

A CHEAP WIN AVAILABLE NOW, independent of the full tier design: the persona card is
READABLE OVER HTTP from the Engine the sidecar already polls, and it carries the
origin, service history and age as structured fields. Whatever the persona tier
eventually looks like, the card is an authoritative seed that currently goes unread.

RELATED, and worth checking rather than assuming: n9bv flagged "Porsche test drive" as
an uncorroborated phantom thread. Mark's persona description contains a paid-off
Porsche bought with an enlistment bonus. That thread may be persona canon that the
corroboration check could not see because it never read the cards. Do not close n9bv
on the old reading without re-checking against this.

title: In-engine INJECTION is the strongest case for an engine-side consumer — outranks capture
description:
TC asked 2026-08-03 whether in-engine helps INJECTION or SEARCH. Injection: yes, decisively. Search: marginal. This RE-RANKS our engine asks.

INJECTION — THE STRONGEST CASE YET, stronger than capture.
The current path is documented as lossy in our own source. turn-bridge.ts header comment, verbatim: "The engine then injects that lorebook on the NEXT generation, which is why memory has always been one turn behind on this path." Flow is POST /api/process-turn -> { memoryBlock } -> syncMemoryToLorebook -> engine injects it on the FOLLOWING generation.

Three distinct wins from a pre_generation hook, in order of weight:
1. IT KILLS THE ONE-TURN LAG, AND THAT IS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT A LATENCY ONE. loadContext scores relevance against recentText. On the poller path recentText is the turn that ALREADY HAPPENED, so we retrieve against the previous exchange rather than the user message actually being answered. A pre_generation hook has the incoming message in hand. Every ranking improvement we make (tp5, sph8) is currently handicapped by scoring against the wrong text — fixing the scorer while the query stays one turn stale caps the gain.
2. IT RETIRES THE LOREBOOK HACK. preGenInjections is per-turn, ephemeral, correctly positioned, and leaves no persistent artifact. Today we mutate a shared lorebook the user can see, edit, and be confused by. The "prompt-context" permission exists in the manifest enum for exactly this purpose, and long-term-memory already works this way (recall -> text -> engine injects).
3. IT REMOVES A WRITE-THEN-HOPE RACE. We write the lorebook after turn N and trust it lands before turn N+1 assembles its prompt. Ephemeral injection has no such window.

SEARCH — MARGINAL, DO NOT BUILD FOR IT.
- Packages get CapabilityEmbeddingHost { spaceId, label, embed(texts, signal) } — credential-free embeddings using whatever the user configured. That would retire our own embedding config burden (embeddings.ts). Real, but small.
- NOT AVAILABLE OVER REST: probed the live engine — /api/embeddings, /api/embed, /api/vectors/search all 404, and no matching route files exist at v2.4.0. It is package-only, so the sidecar cannot borrow it today.
- resources.listLorebooks would help cross-referencing (relevant to bos, lorebook import).
- BUT our retrieval weakness is OURS: summary-only scoring (tp5) and single-lane ranking (sph8). Borrowing their embedder does not improve our ranking. The engine cannot fix a problem that lives in our scorer.

CONSEQUENCE — RE-RANK THE ENGINE ASKS. Previously apmt (messageId + activeSwipeIndex on the post_processing payload) was treated as the ask, then demoted when in-engine CAPTURE was ruled unnecessary. That ruling stands and is unchanged — it was about capture. INJECTION is a separate question and it lands the other way.
If we ever get ONE Engine change, ask for the INJECTION CONSUMER: an Engine-side getCapabilityService("marinara-extender:runtime") call in the generation path that takes our text and injects it, mirroring exactly what services/generation/long-term-memory-runtime.ts already does for long-term-memory. That single change fixes a documented correctness limitation. The capture payload fields fix a latency nicety.
ORDER: injection consumer FIRST. apmt stays parked and junior.

NOT A BLOCKER FOR THE AUDIT: the package is a distribution shell; none of this is needed to submit. But it is the thing worth asking for once a relationship exists.
notes:
LINUX MATRIX COMPLETE — 2026-08-03. 24 of 25 regression targets PASS on our branch. Both failures verified pre-existing on untouched upstream.

PASS (24): spatial, prompt, timezone, emoji, providers, jsonish, tts, issues, backup, extensions-security, professor-mari-shell-sandbox, agent-import-security, custom-tool-import-security, PROMPT-CONTEXT (ours), request-security, runtime-integrity, novelai-zip-security, image-result-security, expression-tools, REGENERATION-CONTEXT, sprites, static-cache, localization, docs.
Note the two that matter most for a generation-path change both pass: regeneration-context and prompt.

FAIL (2), BOTH REPRODUCED ON PRISTINE a986675bd BY CHECKING IT OUT AND RE-RUNNING — not inferred:
1. regression:roleplay — scripts/regressions/roleplay-streaming.regression.ts:237, "Echo Chamber should leave the native Roleplay scrollbar reachable". expected /const HUD_EDGE_GAP = 24;[^\n]*native chat scrollbar/u, actual a comment banner. Identical assertion and identical actual value on pristine upstream.
2. regression:noodle -> noodle-prompt.regression.ts:968, date-dependent schedule fixture ("No generated schedules are available for today").

PATTERN WORTH NAMING, because it shaped this whole session: BOTH upstream failures — plus the Windows one that turned out to be ours — are SOURCE-TEXT-SCANNING or DATE-DEPENDENT assertions rather than behavioural tests. roleplay-streaming greps client source for a literal containing a constant and a comment phrase; prompt.regression greps for a literal containing a bare \n (which is why CRLF broke it); noodle-prompt asserts against "today". Tests that assert on the SHAPE OF SOURCE TEXT or on the CALENDAR rot without the product breaking. Useful context if we ever offer fixes, and a caution for our own suite: none of the 388 sidecar tests should ever assert on source text.

WHAT WE MAY NOW CLAIM IN THE PR, all verifiable by a reviewer:
- tsc --noEmit clean on the server package
- our new regression:prompt-context passes on Windows AND Linux
- 24 of 25 regression targets pass on Linux on this branch
- the 2 failures reproduce on untouched upstream a986675bd; here is the method (checkout the base commit, re-run the single target)
- smoke:ui not run
WHAT WE MAY NOT CLAIM: a green `pnpm regression`. The aggregate is && chained and aborts at noodle regardless of our work.

VERIFICATION IS NOW COMPLETE. Remaining before submission is authoring, not testing: PR description, and the decision on whether to offer the shared-timeout-helper extraction as a follow-up commit.

title: Strip memory tags from the STORED message after capture (PATCH), not just from display
description:
PROBLEM (TC, 2026-08-03): memory tags are broadcast in the open.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, verified against the live engine 2026-08-03:
- The regex script "Marinara Extender: Strip memory tags" IS installed and enabled (id eYD3Ppl8Abgkyty4h05vw, placement ["ai_output"], promptOnly false), left over from the extension era.
- It WORKS. Tested against real stored content: 155 messages contain a tag, 155 strip cleanly, 0 leak. (An earlier count of "151 leaking" was my own shell-escaping mangling the pattern before testing — the engine was never at fault. Recorded so nobody re-investigates a non-bug.)
- BUT A REGEX SCRIPT NEVER TOUCHES THE STORED ROW. Engine docs, docs/extending/regex-scripts.md: "Only Display: change only what you see in the chat. The saved message and the text the model gets in later turns do not change." Apply mode is separate from placement.
- So the raw tag persists in the message row permanently. That is how I was able to grep 155 of them out of the API in the first place. It survives into exports, search, and — depending on apply mode — future prompt history, where it both burns context and teaches the model to emit more of them.

THE FIX, AND IT NEEDS NOTHING FROM UPSTREAM: PATCH /api/chats/:chatId/messages/:messageId with { content: string } exists (packages/server/src/routes/chats.routes.ts @ v2.4.0, ~line 1860 -> storage.updateMessageContent). After the reader captures a turn, rewrite the stored message with the tag removed. The tag then disappears from display, storage, exports and all future prompt history at once — strictly better than any regex apply mode.

WHY IN-ENGINE CAPTURE WOULD NOT DO THIS BETTER: persistence happens BEFORE post_processing (7zro ordering proof — the row is written at generate.routes.ts ~6353, the phase runs at ~6805+, and the Engine own rewrite path re-writes the row later at ~8867). So even in-engine it is write-then-rewrite, exactly like PATCH. The ONLY difference is that in-engine closes the window within the same request, while PATCH closes it a poll tick later. In-engine buys a shorter visible window and nothing else here.

FIRST, CONFIRM APPLY MODE on the installed script. If it is Only Display, the model is currently reading its own tags back in history every turn, which is a live context-pollution and tag-echo problem independent of anything cosmetic. Prompt-side stripping should be on regardless of this issue.

BUILD CARE — this rewrites user-visible history, so it is higher-risk than anything else the reader does:
- Strip ONLY the tag span. Never reflow, retrim, or normalise the surrounding prose.
- No-op when the strip would change nothing; never PATCH for its own sake.
- Order matters: capture MUST be durable before the strip. Losing the tag before ingesting it destroys the memory outright — worse than a visible tag.
- Swipes: updateMessageContent syncs to the ACTIVE swipe. Re-verify behaviour against a message with swipeCount > 1 before enabling; the standing invariant (key on activeSwipeIndex, never newest) applies here too.
- Concurrency: do not clobber a user edit made between capture and strip. Compare against the content we captured; skip if it moved.
- Make it reversible/opt-out — MARINARA_EXTENDER_STRIP_TAGS — because it mutates the user chat record.

RELATED: the Engine also has a native bracket-command parser (registerCapabilityConversationCommand + stripCapabilityConversationCommands, matching [tag] and [tag:...]), but its only caller is services/conversation/character-commands.ts — CONVERSATION MODE ONLY. It would not cover Roleplay, so it is not the answer here.

title: Upstream ask: put messageId + activeSwipeIndex on the post_processing agent payload
description:
TINY, SELF-CONTAINED UPSTREAM ASK. Deliberately filed SEPARATE from MarinaraExtender-lmcz (catalog/trust policy) — two small issues beat one bloated one, and this one is a code ask with receipts while lmcz is a policy ask.

THE ASK: include the persisted assistant messageId and its activeSwipeIndex on the AgentContext handed to post_processing agents.

WHY IT IS NEARLY FREE — receipts, breadcrumbs @ v2.4.0:
- packages/server/src/routes/generate.routes.ts is ONE sequential handler. At ~line 6353 it persists the assistant turn, branching explicitly: regenerate -> chats.addSwipe(input.regenerateMessageId, fullResponse) with savedSwipeIndex = createdSwipe.index; continue -> updateMessageContent with savedSwipeIndex from the row; otherwise -> chats.createMessage with savedSwipeIndex = 0.
- At ~6370 it ALREADY passes { messageId: savedMsg.id, swipeIndex: savedSwipeIndex, regenerate } into materializeAssistantSpatialState — the hierarchical-maps capability package anchor. So handing (message, swipe) to package code at this exact point is an established, shipped pattern.
- At ~6812 it computes latestAssistantMessageId.
- At ~7036 it builds postAgentContext = { ...agentContext, mainResponse, preGenInjections, parallelResults } — WITHOUT either value, which is in lexical scope twenty-four lines above.
So this is not a new capability. It is passing variables the handler already holds.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS FOR CONSUMERS: any post_processing agent that must attribute its output to a specific turn REVISION rather than to 'the latest text'. Today mainResponse (packages/shared/src/types/agent.ts, AgentContext) is a bare string: an agent cannot tell a first generation from a re-roll, and cannot name the row it is looking at. Consumers are forced to infer the anchor by reading back the last assistant message, which is an UNCONTRACTED correlation that upstream can silently reorder.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: add messageId: string and activeSwipeIndex: number to AgentContext, populated for post_processing (null/absent for pre_generation and parallel, which run before the row exists). Optionally regenerate: boolean, which the handler already computes as Boolean(input.regenerateMessageId).

KNOWN NON-GOAL: this does NOT cover swipe-back. Navigating between existing swipes runs no generation, so no agent phase observes it. Not asking upstream to solve that; a reconciling reader is the right answer on our side. Say so in the issue so the scope stays small and obviously cheap.

BEFORE FILING: same voice pass as lmcz. Do not bundle with the catalog question.
notes:
DECISION 2026-08-03: IN-ENGINE CAPTURE IS NOT A NEEDED CAPABILITY. Do not pursue. Keep this issue as documentation, not as queued work.

REASONING, heaviest first:
1. The READER IS MANDATORY REGARDLESS. Swipe-back runs no generation, so no in-engine hook can ever observe it (7zro ordering proof). Something must keep reading no matter what we build, which makes in-engine capture an optimisation layered on a mechanism we are keeping anyway — never a replacement.
2. ITS MAIN BENEFIT IS ALREADY FREE. The prize was anchoring to (messageId, activeSwipeIndex) instead of a time watermark. activeSwipeIndex is returned on the REST list endpoint — verified live in jaos, which found 4 genuine regenerations carrying it. The poller can anchor correctly TODAY with zero Engine changes. That work is s2lw and needs nothing from upstream.
3. WHAT REMAINS IS LATENCY ONLY — capture at the turn versus at the next poll tick. Real but small, and the reader reconciles either way.
4. THE COST IS TWO UPSTREAM ASKS PLUS A FRAGILE DEPENDENCY: an Engine-side getCapabilityService consumer, THEN these payload fields, plus the uncontracted persistence-vs-phase ordering we would have to guard with the string-compare tripwire. Against a benefit of "slightly sooner".

REVISIT CONDITION: if the audit relationship makes Engine PRs cheap and routine, this can be reopened — the receipts in this issue and in 7zro are already gathered and need no rework. Until then nothing in the roadmap waits on it.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: s2lw — anchor the reader on (messageId, activeSwipeIndex) and supersede on drift. No permission, no upstream, fixes the actual bug.
close_reason:
DECIDED NOT TO PURSUE 2026-08-03; left open by oversight, closed 2026-08-04. Its own
notes already say "keep this issue as documentation, not as queued work" -- but an
open P1 does not read as documentation, it reads as queued work, and it was sitting
in `bd ready` doing exactly that.

WHY NOT: (1) the reader is mandatory regardless, since swipe-back runs no generation
and no in-engine hook can observe it, so in-engine capture is an optimisation on a
mechanism we are keeping anyway; (2) the prize -- anchoring to
(messageId, activeSwipeIndex) -- is ALREADY FREE, because activeSwipeIndex is
returned on the REST list endpoint (verified live in jaos); (3) what remains is
latency only; (4) the cost is two upstream asks plus an uncontracted ordering that
would need the string-compare tripwire to guard.

REOPEN CONDITION: only if an Engine-side getCapabilityService consumer is built
first. That is the senior ask; these payload fields are junior to it and must not be
filed out of order.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH CARRYING: s2lw needs NOTHING from upstream. The poller can anchor
on activeSwipeIndex today.

title: Adopt LTM-style lane fusion + explainability in Extender retrieval (feeds tp5)
description:
Found during the long-term-memory teardown (5hpe): their retrieval is ahead of ours in exactly the place tp5 says we are weak. Recording it as a design target rather than letting the finding evaporate.

WHAT THEY DO (contract-level, no line anchors):
- FOUR RETRIEVAL LANES, each producing scored chunk hits: (1) direct metadata match on note-id patterns and #tags parsed out of the query, (2) BM25 over chunk text, (3) a keyword index, (4) graph expansion over note-to-note links seeded from the top lexical and keyword hits. Optional fifth vector lane when an embedding adapter and a usable vector index exist for the current spaceId.
- RECIPROCAL RANK FUSION across the lanes with per-lane weights (semanticWeight, lexicalWeight, graphWeight, keywordWeight), all settable per chat.
- BUDGETING as a distinct stage after ranking: maxChunks, maxTokens, a relevance score threshold, and exact-text dedupe.
- EXPLAINABILITY AS A FIRST-CLASS OUTPUT: every selected chunk carries its score, the lanes that surfaced it, and per-lane reasons; REJECTED candidates are returned too, each with a rejectionReason. Emitted as a debug event with counts.

WHY IT MATTERS TO US: our scoring reads entry.summary only and never sees the body (tp5). Even fixing that leaves us single-lane. The graph lane is the interesting one — it surfaces material the query never lexically matched, via links from what did match, which is precisely the recall our arcs/threads data already has the shape for and does not exploit.

DO NOT COPY WHOLESALE. Their input is weaker than ours (artifact-derived, never sees a raw turn), so lanes tuned for summary text may not transfer to turn-derived entries. Take the ARCHITECTURE — lanes, fusion, budget-as-a-stage, rejected-with-reasons — not the weights.

THE EXPLAINABILITY PIECE IS THE CHEAPEST WIN AND SHOULD LAND FIRST: 'why did this memory not surface' is currently answered by hand-grepping the store. Returning rejected candidates with reasons would have shortened several past triages, and it directly serves the three-cause triage (capture gap vs retrieval invisibility vs digest corruption).

RELATED: tp5 (summary-only scoring), and the ranking work implied by vrw.
notes:
ERRATUM to the phase-1 note above: one line lost a word to shell backtick substitution when it was written. It should read:

- selectEntries now returns traces + rejected + candidateCount. The greedy-fill SKIP BRANCH (the loop continue when an entry does not fit the remaining budget) — where a stored-but-unsurfaced memory used to vanish without trace — now records budget_exhausted. That was the single hardest case to tell apart from a capture gap.

2026-08-30 — THE CONFIRMATION HALF HAS A MECHANISM NOW, and it did not need an Engine change.

This issue wants injection to be explainable: assembling a block and shipping it are different events, and on the lorebook path they were indistinguishable. /api/prompt-accepted and confirmInjection were built for that and lost their caller when Engine 2.3.4 removed client extensions.

The shipped Engine persists the DISPATCHED PROMPT: assistant message extra.cachedPrompt is the array of messages actually sent (measured: 44-92 entries, system message 20-58KB). Retention is a rolling window of the LAST TWO assistant messages per chat - verified across six chats of 22-233 messages, identical pattern in each.

So the distinction this issue is built on becomes observable:
  block present in cachedPrompt -> it shipped; a wrong answer is PRECEDENCE
  block absent                  -> it never shipped; that is ARRIVAL

Proven on live data, not argued: a nonce was located at index 55 of 56 in a real generation's dispatched prompt over plain REST, and the same technique then diagnosed 771t's last cause - a 29,332-char block that the loader had filled with the right rows, absent from a 20,854-char dispatched prompt because a second memory path was spending the same budget.

LIMITS, stated rather than glossed: post-hoc, not pre-dispatch, so it cannot bound a live turn the way a receipt would; and pruned after two turns, so it must be read within two turns of the generation. It makes the tests SCOREABLE, which was the blocker. A real acceptance callback remains the better answer and is recorded on 771t as an upstream ask - now downgraded from blocking to nice-to-have.

title: Rewrite the expert skills API-first — contracts, not line numbers
description:
RULING (TC, 2026-08-02): the archaeology era is over. Skill references go API-first. Line numbers rot; contracts do not.

EVIDENCE THIS IS NOW URGENT: hkdq carried a 'patch targets line 503 and line 754 BY NUMBER' urgency that had to be RETRACTED as unverified. 1wpt cites openai.provider.ts lines 805-810 and 842 against an engine that has since moved 882 commits. Every line-anchored claim in the skills is now suspect by default.

WHAT API-FIRST MEANS:
- name the CONTRACT (endpoint, field, capability name, permission string, manifest key), never the coordinate
- version the contract when the engine versions it (capability API 1.2 vs 1.7; extension API v5)
- where a file must be named, name the module and the exported symbol, not the line
- record OBSERVED WIRE BEHAVIOR (request/response shapes) over source excerpts — wire survives refactors

SCOPE:
- .claude/skills/marinara-extender-expert/ (SKILL.md + references/*) — repo copy is canonical, then re-sync ~/.claude/skills/
- marinara-engine-expert — also gets the n4fd rework (built for extension authoring, wrong shape for contribution)

MUST CAPTURE FROM THE v2.4.0 SWEEP:
- extension API v5 context contract (chatId/characterId/characterIds/personaId; read_active_characters, read_active_persona)
- the sandbox reality: bare .js imports with capabilities: [] and gets the opaque-origin Worker
- capability package permissions + entrypoint contract
- poller's engine contract (/chats lastMessageAt, /chats/:id/messages newest-N-ascending, per-message characterId, activeSwipeIndex swipe semantics)
notes:
EXTENDER SKILL DONE 2026-08-20. Engine skill NOT done — leaving this ticket open for it.

COORDINATES REMOVED. All 29 `file.ts:NNN` cites in marinara-extender-expert are gone;
the only surviving match is the `file.ts:123` example inside the new rule itself.

MEASURED BEFORE REWRITING, and the result is the argument for the ruling:
  - all 22 named symbols still existed (IndexEntry, Entry, Bookmark, moveToCold,
    supersedeEntry, softDeleteEntry, atomicWriteFile, serializedWrite, assertSafeId,
    estimateTokens, removeEntriesBySourceChat, harvestBodyTerms, ...)
  - most line numbers had drifted — landing on `});`, on a blank line, on `: chatId;`
  - TWO were on the WRONG FILE: the skill cited `pipeline.ts` for the narrative boost
    and for stages 2+3, but the module is `sentiment/pipeline.ts`. The boost is
    NARRATIVE_POSITION_BOOST, cited as line 60, actually 68.
  - a few line numbers were still correct (storage.ts:42 -> `export interface
    IndexEntry {`, dedup.ts:65 -> the jaccard comment). THAT IS THE TRAP: survivors
    are indistinguishable from rot without checking every one, so a reader has no
    reason to trust any of them.
So the prose was accurate throughout and only the coordinates rotted. Symbols now
carry the reference; where a cite named no symbol, one was looked up and added
(runSentimentPipeline, NARRATIVE_POSITION_BOOST, runPromotion, the Tier/EntryStatus
unions, the /api/process-turn handler).

The rule is now written into SKILL.md so it binds future edits, not just this pass.

NEW FILE: references/capability-package.md — closes the "MUST CAPTURE" item for the
capability package permissions + entrypoint contract, read against Engine v2.4.3
(34442e26d, the pinned install). Contains the manifest identity/version gates

{server, client, agents, knowledge}, the COMPLETE nine-member permission enum, the

TWO FINDINGS IN THERE THAT MOVE OTHER TICKETS:
  - the `ui` permission EXISTS and is declarable — that is what hwlj was waiting on.
  - `network` is declared in the enum but NO enforcement site was found in

    way, because it decides whether a package client may call 127.0.0.1:3001 —

STILL OPEN UNDER THIS TICKET:
