  skip it. Audit each consumer: loader, promotion, cleanup, /api/scopes, digest,
  stats, the entity index builder.

  Retained readable for verification, per TC. Never enumerated, never loaded, never
  promoted, never swept.

WHAT HAPPENS TO yi70's READ FILTER: it becomes unnecessary for any identity that has
been physically forked, because the stores are separate. Keep the module — rowInBranch
IS the distribution rule this operation needs — but the loader filter should be removed
once a fork is executed, or it will silently filter an already-correct store twice.

ACCEPTANCE: fork is one operation, driven by data, that a user can run on any character;
each branch ends with its own store and its own identity key; the ancestor is
unreachable from every system path (verified per consumer, not assumed); the ambiguous
set is duplicated rather than lost; and the whole thing is reversible from the archive
if it goes wrong.

RELATED: yi70 (the read-time fork this supersedes — live now, keep until this ships),
pe1c (the 657-row ghost — the archive rule is its structural fix too), evs1 (a GET that
mints and migrates; same subsystem, and a fork operation must not go through it),
1akw/identity-map (the mapping this rewires).
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARCHIVE REQUIREMENT REFINED (TC, 2026-08-25): "It's ok if it is readable by humans,
and viewable from the memory tab. It should have a DEPRECIATED label or something
along those lines."

THIS CORRECTS THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE. I had written that the archive must be
"unreachable from every system path" and live outside data/characters/ so nothing
could enumerate it. Too broad. The line is not display-vs-hidden, it is:

    NOTHING THAT FEEDS THE CHARACTER may read it.
    ANYTHING THAT SHOWS A HUMAN THINGS may read it.

  MUST NOT touch it: the loader (hot and cold recall), promotion, the decay clock,
    cleanup/sweeps, capture and every write path, digest, stats, arc promotion,
    the entity-index builder.
  MUST show it: the memory tab, labelled DEPRECATED, read-only.

THE REPO ALREADY HAS THIS EXACT SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN, and it should be copied
rather than reinvented: provenance "unplayed" (EntryProvenance, storage.ts:28).
Author-established outline is stored at full fidelity, is visible in the memory
browser with an "outline — never recalled" pill, and is rejected in the loader at
BOTH paths (loader.ts:242 hot, :367 cold) because "a character that can remember an
unplayed scene is a confabulation machine". An archived scope is the same promise at
scope granularity: kept whole, shown to the human, never in the prompt.

STRUCTURALLY: EXCLUDE BY DEFAULT, DISPLAY BY EXPLICIT OPT-IN. This is the part that
must not be got wrong, because "included by default and every reader remembers to skip
it" is precisely how pe1c's 657-row ghost stayed live in the memory browser for months.

    listScopeIds("character")   NEVER returns an archived scope. Every existing
                                consumer (promotion, cleanup, /api/scopes) is then
                                correct with NO change, because they cannot see it.
    listArchivedScopes()        a separate call that ONLY the memory-tab endpoint
                                makes. Opting in is a deliberate act at one call
                                site, not a default that leaks everywhere.

  So the archive can stay under data/characters/ with an `archived: true` marker in
  its index, or live in data/archive/ — either works once enumeration is opt-in.
  Prefer whichever makes "a new consumer cannot accidentally include it" true by
  construction, since that is the actual requirement and the reason pe1c happened.

UI: DEPRECATED label on the scope in the character list, read-only (no edit, no
delete, no restore into recall — restoring an archived ancestor is the fork's undo
path, not a per-entry action), and a line saying what it is and when it was archived.
Reuse the discarded-tab pattern from ud30: show the REASON verbatim.

ACCEPTANCE ADDENDUM: an archived scope is listed in the memory tab with a DEPRECATED
label and browsable; and a test proves it is absent from listScopeIds, from a loaded
memory block, and from a promotion pass — asserted per consumer rather than assumed
from the directory location.

title: Identity FORK with a split point — the retired Professor Mari card still reads Current Mari's whole memory, and a date cutoff alone would leave her with 1%
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-25: 'I still have a character card that uses Professor Mari as
well. Sorta. I have one chat remaining from the original Professor Mari. She kinda
shares memory with Current Mari. Her memory should stop of Current Mari after the
split.'

HE ALSO ASKED WHETHER ANY OF THE pe1c FIXES WOULD DO IT. THEY WOULD NOT. pe1c is about
a stale INDEX (657 rows, no files). This is the identity MAPPING, a different mechanism
doing exactly what it was built to do. Nothing proposed there touches this.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE MECHANISM. identity-map.yaml collapses three card ids onto one identity key:

    __professor_mari__      -> professor_mari
    Z4MZQbJLgLF             -> professor_mari
    Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ   -> professor_mari    (Dr. Mari Zielinska, current)

That was CORRECT for a REPLACEMENT — the card changed, the character did not, and the
map is why she kept her memories (see the beat-id-eras memory). It is WRONG for a FORK,
where the old card is still played as a distinct entity. The system has no way to say
'these two cards were the same person until a date, and different people after it'.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 against the live Engine and store:
  - 10 chats still use characterId __professor_mari__. That card NO LONGER EXISTS in
    the Engine; the chats outlived it.
  - THE SPLIT IS 2026-05-23: the last old-card chat closed that day and the first
    Dr. Mari Zielinska chat was created the same day.
  - NINE of the ten ended on or before the split. ONE did not:
        Hw3h-2KlJqn4btjfmnw70  "Professor Mari"  created 05-25, last message 06-25
    A month of play AFTER the split, during which it loaded Current Mari's memory.

⚠ A PURE DATE CUTOFF IS THE OBVIOUS FIX AND IT IS WRONG. Measured:

      7,052  beats in the shared store
      6,983  created after 2026-05-23   (99.0%)
         69  at or before the split      <- ALL a naive cutoff would leave her

  Professor Mari would be left with 1% of her memory and read as amnesiac. That is not
  what TC asked for; it is what a literal reading of 'stop after the split' produces.

THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY MATCHES THE INTENT is a union, not a cutoff:

      Professor Mari's memory = everything up to the split
                              + everything from HER OWN chats after it

  Her own post-split chat produced 40 beats and 38 entries, all after the split. So she
  ends up with roughly 69 + 40 = ~109 memories: small, coherent, and correct for a
  character played briefly and then mostly retired. The cutoff is on SHARED history;
  her own continued life is hers.

OPEN QUESTION FOR TC, and it is the reverse direction he did not specify: should
CURRENT Mari still see those 40 post-split beats from the Professor Mari chat? They are
in her store now. Symmetry says no — that is Professor Mari's separate life after they
became different people. But TC only ruled on one direction, and retiring 40 real beats
from Current Mari is not a call to make by inference.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IMPLEMENTATION, two shapes:

  A. READ-TIME FORK (preferred). Give the identity-map entry an optional
     forkedFrom + splitAt. The loader, when resolving for a forked card, admits an
     entry if (created <= splitAt) OR (its source chat belongs to this card). No
     duplication, non-destructive, reversible by deleting two fields, and the shared
     past stays a single copy that cannot drift.

  B. COPY-ON-FORK. Give the old card its own identity key and copy the pre-split
     entries into it. Clean separation, but duplicates the shared history and the two
     copies then diverge silently — the exact problem the store already has with the
     657 ghost rows, recreated deliberately.

  A is the design. B is what gets built if nobody thinks about it.

  NOTE THE SUBJECT AXIS ALREADY LANDED (4g9w/qlib): entries now carry subjects[] with
  kind user|persona|character. A fork is the same question one level up — WHICH
  character is this about when two cards are the same person until a date. Worth
  checking whether the fork belongs on that axis rather than beside it.

ACCEPTANCE: the surviving Professor Mari chat loads only pre-split shared memory plus
its own; Current Mari is unaffected unless TC rules on the reverse direction; nothing is
duplicated; and the fork is expressed as data in identity-map.yaml, not as a code branch
per character.

RELATED: pe1c (the ghost index — adjacent, different, and NOT a fix for this), evs1
(resolveIdentity minting/migrating from a GET — same subsystem, third failure this
week), 4g9w/qlib (the subject axis), and the beat-id-eras memory, which records that
professor_mari changed cards deliberately more than once.
notes:
SHIPPED AND LIVE 2026-08-25. TC ruled the reverse direction: Current Mari should NOT
see the retired card's post-split memories either — "They should read more as sisters
who shared the same household, ie, the pre-split memories, rather than be shared." So
the fork is SYMMETRIC.

  identity.ts  IdentityEntry gains forkSplitAt + forkPrimary. Absent = not forked =
               today's behaviour. forkConfigFor(), forkSiblingsOf().
  fork.ts      (new) chat -> owning card cache (from the Engine, like personaNameFor),
               forkFilterForChat(), rowInBranch(), applyForkFilter().
  loader.ts    loadIndexes filters the CHARACTER index by branch. Chat index is
               per-chat and already correct; global is global.

THE HOOK IS THE CHAT, NOT THE CARD. loadContext receives a resolved identityKey and
cannot tell which card it is serving — but it receives chatId, and a chat belongs to
exactly one card. No call-site signature changed.

CONFIGURED: splitAt 2026-05-23 on all three professor_mari cards; forkPrimary on
Po_H0vIbkPUMbZmt7aUoQ (the one still in the Engine). identity-map backed up first.

MEASURED LIVE AFTER THE CHANGE:

                                sees          hidden   composition
    Professor Mari (retired)    742 / 8,431    7,689   16 shared + 726 from her 10 chats
    Dr. Mari Zielinska (cur)  7,702 / 8,431      729   16 shared + 0 from the retired card

  Confirmed end to end through GET /api/memory-block: the retired card's block is
  17,537 chars / 243 lines, the current card's 24,971 / 324. Different blocks, same
  identity key, same store.

⚠ MY OWN ESTIMATE IN THIS TICKET WAS WRONG BY 7x AND IS CORRECTED HERE. The description
predicted "roughly 69 + 40 = ~109 memories" for the retired card. The real figure is
742. I had counted only the ONE SURVIVING chat as "her own"; she has TEN — nine that
closed on or before the split plus the survivor — and every memory from all of them is
hers. The union rule was right; the arithmetic under it counted one tenth of the input.
COUNT EVERY CHAT A BRANCH OWNS, NOT JUST THE ACTIVE ONE. This is the same restatement
discipline that came out of the cardinality corrections earlier the same day: the
headline design survived, the derived number did not, and both need saying.

  Note the practical consequence is the opposite of the worry that motivated the union:
  she is not amnesiac at 1%, she has a coherent 742-memory life. The union was still
  necessary — a pure cutoff would have left her with 16.

STILL OPEN:
  - The cold index is NOT filtered. loadIndexes covers the hot path; a recall MISS that
    consults cold could still surface the other branch's memories. Small surface (cold
    is read only on a miss) but it is a hole and should close before this is called done.
  - Nothing stamps a branch at WRITE time. New memories are attributed by chat ownership
    at read time, which works and needs no backfill, but means a chat deleted from the
    Engine makes its memories fall to the primary. Acceptable now, worth revisiting if
    forks become common.
  - pe1c (the 657-row ghost index) is untouched and still awaiting TC's disposition; it
    is a different mechanism and this does not resolve it.

title: Discarded tab in the memory view — system-retired memories have no surface, and wct1 just put four more there
description:
ASKED FOR BY TC 2026-08-25, immediately after wct1 retired 6 beats and 4 companion
entries. Those four are recoverable and auditable — but only by someone who knows to
run a script, which is not a surface.

THERE ARE THREE RETIREMENT FIELDS AND THEY ARE DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. This is already
a ruling in the code (ui.ts, the 4z0h block): 'filing them under deletes would reassert
exactly the conflation that discardedAt exists to prevent.' Do not collapse them.

    deletedAt      THE USER deleted it            -> 'Recently deleted' view, restore + purge
    supersededBy   a newer fact replaced it       -> /api/retired, rollback
    discardedAt    THE SYSTEM retired it          -> NOTHING

The third is the gap. It is where a wct1-style cleanup lands, where a discarded swipe
lands (s2lw), and where anything the sidecar retires on its own behalf lands. The
user did not do it, so it must not appear under deletes; it was not replaced, so it
must not appear under supersessions.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is smaller than it looks:
  storage.ts  restoreDiscardedEntry() — already written, already guarded to
              discardedAt specifically, with a comment explaining why it is a THIRD
              restore rather than a flag on the other two. Reuse it; do not widen
              either existing guard.
  storage.ts  listDeleted() is the exact shape to mirror for listDiscarded().
  api.ts      restoreDiscardedEntry is reachable ONLY from the held-lane settle path
              (the entangled discarded-swipe records). There is no general restore.
  ui.ts       VIEWS map + state.mode is the tab machinery; 'deleted' and 'held' are
              the two working examples.

WHAT TO BUILD:
  1. listDiscarded(scope, scopeId) — cold rows with discardedAt, excluding rows that
     are also deletedAt or supersededBy so a row cannot appear in two views at once.
     MUST return retiredReason: 'why is this here' is the whole question a reader has,
     and wct1 wrote a real sentence into that field for exactly this purpose.
  2. GET /api/discarded, mirroring GET /api/deleted.
  3. POST /api/entries/:id/restore-discarded (or equivalent) wrapping the existing
     guarded function.
  4. A view + nav control. It is NOT 'Recently deleted' and NOT 'Held for review'.

DESIGN NOTES:
  - SHOW THE REASON VERBATIM. retiredReason is free text written by whatever retired
    the row; wct1's reads 'derived from a pasted Engine changelog, not a lived moment
    (mln9)'. A reader deciding whether to restore needs that sentence, not a code.
  - NO PURGE, at least not in the first cut. The user did not discard these, so the
    destructive action is the one thing they have no context for. Restore and read.
    'Machine text left in recall is recoverable; a real memory removed is not.'
  - MARK THE OVERLAP WITH 'Held for review' rather than hiding it. An entangled
    discarded-swipe row is BOTH discarded and awaiting a decision; showing it in this
    list with a marker is honest, hiding it makes the list silently incomplete.
  - EMPTY IS THE NORMAL STATE and should read as reassuring, not broken.

ACCEPTANCE: a discarded memory is visible with its reason, restorable in one action,
and a restored row returns to recall (verify it re-enters index.yaml, not just that
the button reports success — pe4o/41uo is the standing warning that a retirement can
be marked without taking effect). The four wct1 entries are the live fixture.

RELATED: wct1 (put the first four there), 4z0h (held-review lane — adjacent surface,
must stay distinct), s2lw (discarded swipes), a90l (the held lane), 3pl (rollback,
which is the supersession path and a different concept again).
notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-25.

  storage.ts  listDiscarded(scope, scopeId) — cold rows with discardedAt, EXCLUDING
              any that also carry deletedAt or supersededBy so one row cannot appear
              in two views and be restored from the wrong one. Returns retiredReason,
              retrievalCount and recitationCount.
  api.ts      GET /api/discarded, POST /api/entries/:id/restore-discarded (wrapping
              the existing restoreDiscardedEntry, which was already guarded to
              discardedAt and previously reachable ONLY from the held-lane settle path).
  ui.ts       'Discarded by the system…' as a PEER button beside 'Recently deleted…',
              and renderDiscarded. Reason shown verbatim. Restore only, no purge.

THE NUMBER IS THE FINDING: 363 discarded entries in professor_mari alone, and none of
them has ever had a surface. Not four. The wct1 rows are simply the newest; underneath
them sit whole populations retired by earlier cleanups, each carrying the sentence that
retired it —

  'unsupported biography: profession not attested anywhere in the corpus (fqnl)'
  'prompt-example echo on ingested scaffolding (pe4o/97z2) — no real boat scene exists'

Those were correct retirements. But TC has never been able to see any of them, review
one, or put one back, and that is 363 decisions made on his behalf with no way to audit
them. This is the same shape as 'nothing retires the loser of a settled question' —
except here the loser was retired properly and then became invisible.

DESIGN CALLS, all from the ticket and kept: no purge (the user did not discard these,
so the destructive action is the one they have least context for); reason verbatim
rather than mapped to a code; retrieved/recited surfaced because they change the stakes
of leaving something retired; empty state worded to read as reassuring.

NOT DONE: the overlap marker for rows that are ALSO in 'Held for review'. Held rows are
entangled discarded-swipes and appear in both lists; the ticket asked for a marker and
this first cut does not have one. Filed as remaining work rather than silently dropped.

title: Migrate the 181 valid [about: X] prefixes into the subjects field — TWO PHASE, and LAST
description:
RULINGS BY TC 2026-08-25. Both are conditions on HOW and WHEN, not suggestions.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RULING 1 — MIGRATE LAST, ALWAYS. THIS RUNS AFTER qhej, NOT BEFORE.

TC's reasoning, verbatim in shape: 'if you migrate now, those 68 rows land as unresolved
names, and the second pass has to tell "migrated before the persona branch existed"
apart from "genuinely never resolved," which is exactly the ambiguity you just spent a
whole slice designing out. Don't build the scar and cut yourself on it in the same week.'

CONCRETELY: 22 of the 181 migratable entries have subject 'Thomas' (plus 3 'Thomas
Collier', 2 'real-thomas'). Thomas is TC's PERSONA. ingestSceneFacts currently has no
personaName field, so resolveFactTarget's persona branch is dead code and those rows
would migrate with kind UNSET. Once qhej wires the persona branch, an unset kind becomes
genuinely ambiguous: does it mean 'this predates the persona branch' or 'the persona
branch ran and declined'? qlib's whole design premise is that absent means UNASSESSED —
migrating early manufactures a population where that is false, in the exact field built
to avoid it.

ORDER: qhej (persona kind) → any other kind-populating work → THIS.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RULING 2 — TWO PHASE. THE PREFIX IS THE GROUND TRUTH; DO NOT STRIP IT IN THE SAME PASS.

TC: 'write the field, LEAVE the prose prefix, verify against it, strip only after. The
prefix is your only ground truth for checking the migration and the instinct will be to
clean it in the same pass. Do not.'

  PHASE A   Write subjects[] from the parsed prefix. LEAVE the '[about: X] ' text in the
            summary exactly as it is. The store is briefly redundant on purpose.
  PHASE B   VERIFY: for every touched entry, re-parse the prefix and assert it agrees
            with the field — same name, expected kind, expected count. Report
            disagreements as a number before proceeding. A migration that cannot be
            checked against an independent copy is a migration nobody can audit.
  PHASE C   Strip the prefix from the summary, and ONLY then.

  Note the tension with 'a copy cannot corroborate its source': the prefix is not a copy
  OF the field, it is the field's SOURCE. Checking a derived value against the original
  it was derived from is the legitimate direction. Once phase C runs that check is gone
  forever, which is precisely why it is a separate phase.

  STRIPPING CHANGES SUMMARIES, WHICH CHANGES DEDUP. createEntryIfUnique scores Jaccard on
  the summary, so removing a shared 12-char prefix from 181 rows alters their similarity
  to each other and to future candidates. Probably an improvement (the prefix was noise
  in the signal) but it is a behaviour change and phase C must measure it, not assume it.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SCOPE: THE 181, AND NOT THE 1,313

  181 entries, 89 distinct subjects — top: Thomas 22, holyknight3 14, Ashley 9, opie 6,
  The Doctor 6, River Song 5, TC 4, Rebecca Collier 4, Jack Harkness 4.

  The other 1,313 are q5pk's non-names and are NOT migratable — there is nothing to
  migrate, the prefix names a placeholder or a pronoun. Their disposition is a decision
  in q5pk, informed by the measurement recorded there: all 1,313 are chat-scoped,
  untiered, status open, and have been RETRIEVED ZERO TIMES. They are inert. Decide
  whether phase C strips their prefixes too, or whether they are left alone entirely —
  do not fold that decision into this ticket silently.

  'holyknight3' (14) needs a ruling before it migrates: that is TC's account handle, so
  those rows may be user facts wearing a username rather than third-party facts. Check
  against data/user-identity.yaml, which already declares TC's canonical forms and
  deliberately EXCLUDES 'thomas collier'.

ACCEPTANCE: phases A, B and C are separate commits; phase B reports an agreement count
and a disagreement list before C runs; the dedup effect of stripping is measured; and no
entry ends with a subjects field that disagrees with the prefix it came from.

RELATED: qhej (MUST land first), qlib (built the field), q5pk (the 1,313 and their
counts), i83s (its orphaned .tmp files were 153 of the phantom hits in the original
miscount), 4g9w (parent).

title: capture-status.yaml has no write mutex — up to 5 concurrent atomic writes per millisecond, 152 orphaned .tmp files, and the poller watermark is what is being lost
description:
FOUND 2026-08-25. Noticed as litter in data/, measured into something with a mechanism.

THE SURFACE SYMPTOM: 152 orphaned '*.tmp-<pid>-<ms>-<rand>' files in data/, 2.2 MB,
oldest 2026-06-03, newest TODAY. Nothing ever cleans them up.

WHAT THEY ARE. atomicWriteFile (storage.ts) writes to a tmp, fsyncs, then renames.
The cleanup path is CORRECT — a final rename failure unlinks the tmp and rethrows. So
an orphan is not a failed write; it is a process that EXITED between open() and a
successful rename. The filename is therefore a forensic record: it carries the pid and
a millisecond timestamp of every such exit.

    146   capture-status.yaml     <- the poller watermark
      6   index.yaml
    ---
     67   distinct pids
     84   distinct (pid, millisecond) write instants

THE MECHANISM — CONCURRENT UNSERIALIZED WRITES TO ONE FILE. 152 files across only 84
distinct (pid, ms) pairs means the SAME process opened multiple tmps for the SAME path
in the SAME millisecond. 44 such groups, up to FIVE deep:

    5  capture-status.yaml.tmp-40368-1787185962376-*
    5  capture-status.yaml.tmp-38844-1787358682313-*
    5  capture-status.yaml.tmp-36576-1787671603352-*

capture-status.ts calls atomicWriteFile directly with NO serialization. Compare
lorebook-writer, which learned this lesson already and holds _lorebookWriteChain for
exactly this reason (see bd memory demo-test-sidecar-rule-learned-the-hard-way, where
the per-process scope of that mutex was itself the bug).

WHY CONCURRENCY TURNS INTO ORPHANS ON WINDOWS, stated as the leading hypothesis and NOT
yet proven: N simultaneous renames onto one target contend, so the losers hit the
EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES path and enter the retry loop — 10 attempts with 30..300ms backoff,
about 1.65s. That widens the window in which a process exit orphans the tmp from
microseconds to seconds, which is why the count is 146 and not 2. VERIFY THIS before
fixing: instrument the retry loop and count how often it is entered and how deep it
goes. If the retries are near-zero the hypothesis is wrong and the cause is something
else holding the process open.

RATE STEPPED UP SHARPLY, cause unknown:
    Jun 03 / 12 / 19 / 21 / 23     1, 1, 2, 1, 1
    Aug 19 .. Aug 25               6, 16, 13, 8, 8, 17, 10   (78 in seven days)
Do NOT read that as a regression on a date without checking survivorship first — older
orphans may simply have been cleared by a backup/restore or a data-dir rebuild, and the
June population is small enough that it proves nothing on its own. Establish whether
anything ever deleted them before attributing the step to a code change.

WHY IT IS MORE THAN LITTER. The file being lost is the POLLER WATERMARK. A lost write
does not corrupt anything — the real file stays at its last good value, which is the
whole point of the atomic pattern — but it means the watermark silently REVERTS. The
consequences run in both directions: a stale watermark re-ingests turns already
captured, which is precisely the mechanism by which one utterance becomes five beats
(see bd memory count-utterances-never-hits-dedupe-by-content-hash); an advanced one
would skip turns outright. dedup absorbs some of the first case and nothing absorbs the
second. ESCALATE TO P1 if re-ingest can be demonstrated from a lost watermark; filed at
P2 because the failure is currently inferred from the write pattern, not observed in
the beat store.

STRUCTURAL FIX, per the house law (close it so the state cannot exist, do not add a
cleanup sweep): serialize writes per PATH — a promise chain keyed on the file path in
storage.ts, so atomicWriteFile is safe for every caller rather than each hot file
having to remember its own mutex. That also subsumes the index.yaml orphans, which are
the same bug on a different file, and needs a join point at shutdown so an in-flight
write drains rather than orphaning (see bd memory background-write-discipline).
A startup sweep of stale tmps is a SECOND, lesser fix — do it as well, but do not let
it substitute for the serialization, or the litter disappears and the lost writes do not.

DO NOT DELETE THE EXISTING 152 UNTIL 073 IS CLOSED. They are the only record of these
exits that exists, and 073 is currently waiting on a spontaneous death to produce an
exit code. The pid+timestamp pairs here may correlate with the watchdog's own restart
log and give 073 its answer without waiting. Read them before sweeping them.

ACCEPTANCE: concurrent atomicWriteFile calls on one path are serialized and provably
cannot produce a second tmp for the same target; retry-loop entry rate is instrumented
and reported; shutdown drains in-flight writes; a stated disposition for the 152
existing orphans that is sequenced AFTER 073 reads them.

RELATED: 073 (silent sidecar deaths — these orphans are candidate evidence), 3lru
(process instrumentation), and the storage.ts hardening already recorded in
engine-pasta-devs-marinara-engine-has-a-recurring.
notes:
THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN — found 2026-08-25 while working qlib in the same file.

storage.ts ALREADY HAS serializedWrite(path, fn), a per-path promise chain, and
upsertIndexEntry already uses it. capture-status.ts calls atomicWriteFile directly and
simply never opted in. So the structural fix is routing the write through the mutex that
exists, not building one.

That also reframes the ticket: this is not 'a missing mutex' but 'a per-path lock that
callers must remember to use'. Per the house law, the stronger close is to put the
serialization INSIDE atomicWriteFile so it is correct for every caller by construction,
rather than fixing capture-status and leaving the next hot file to rediscover this. The
6 index.yaml orphans are the same bug on a path that DOES use serializedWrite, which is
worth understanding before assuming the mutex alone is sufficient — check whether those
6 predate its introduction.

Still needs the shutdown drain (a join point) and the retry-loop instrumentation named in
the description; the mutex addresses concurrency, not process exit.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DESCRIPTION ABOVE, both found while implementing 2026-08-25.
Read these before acting on anything written earlier in this ticket.

CORRECTION 1 — capture-status.yaml IS NOT THE POLLER WATERMARK. I asserted it was,
and built the severity argument (stale watermark -> re-ingest -> one utterance
becomes five beats) on top of that. WRONG.

  capture-status.yaml  is the LIVENESS EVENT signal — a timestamp of the last
                       successful ingest, surfaced on /api/health and in the
                       memory-browser header. Its own file header says so
                       explicitly: "A watermark advance is deliberately NOT
                       capture." It exists because the 08-04 poller outage ran six
                       days behind a STATE signal nobody looked at.
  poller-state.yaml    is the actual watermark, written via mutateYamlFile, which
                       ALREADY takes serializedWrite. Verified: zero orphaned .tmp
                       files for it, ever.

  SO THE REAL CONSEQUENCE IS SMALLER AND DIFFERENT. A lost capture-status write
  means the health page shows a STALE "last captured" time — a monitoring blind
  spot on the exact signal built to end a monitoring blind spot, which is a real
  bug and an ironic one, but it does NOT cause re-ingestion and cannot duplicate
  beats. Nothing in the beat store is at risk. DOWNGRADE the severity accordingly;
  the P1-escalation clause in the description is void, because the mechanism it
  was conditional on does not exist.

CORRECTION 2 — 'PUT THE SERIALIZATION INSIDE atomicWriteFile' WOULD DEADLOCK.
That was my earlier note and it is wrong. upsertIndexEntry already does
serializedWrite(indexPath) and then calls writeYaml(indexPath) -> atomicWriteFile
on THE SAME PATH. A lock taken inside atomicWriteFile would wait on the lock the
caller is already holding. storage.ts warns about exactly this shape in the
writeIndex comment ("intentionally NOT serialized ... to avoid deadlock") and I
proposed walking straight into it.

  THE CORRECT SHAPE: take the lock at the CALL SITE. serializedWrite is now
  exported, with the hazard documented at its definition so the next person does
  not repeat my suggestion.

WHAT SHIPPED: recordCapture now wraps its write in serializedWrite(captureStatusPath()).
Concurrency on the hottest file in the store is gone. 847 tests pass.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN:
  - The 6 index.yaml orphans. That path ALREADY held the lock, so the mutex is not
    a sufficient explanation and they need their own look — check whether they
    predate serializedWrite before assuming anything.
  - The shutdown drain (a join point so an in-flight write finishes rather than
    orphaning). Serialization addresses concurrency, not process exit, and process
    exit is what actually creates an orphan.
  - Retry-loop instrumentation, still unmeasured. The EPERM/EBUSY hypothesis in the
    description is still only a hypothesis.
  - Disposition of the 152 existing orphans, still sequenced AFTER 073 reads them.
    Note they also inflated two separate counts today by being read as live data
    (153 phantom [about:] hits), which is its own argument for clearing them once
    073 is done.


────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RETARGETED 2026-08-25, NOT RETIRED. Ruling: "the diagnosis is dead, the symptom
isn't. One utterance still exists at five weights and it now has zero cause."

The race diagnosis is dead — capture-status is telemetry, not the watermark, and
its writes are serialized now. But the SYMPTOM that started this ticket is
untouched: a single utterance still turns up carrying several weights, and after
the race was ruled out it had no explanation at all.

NEW PRIME SUSPECT, and it is not a race: THE MIRROR. Store diagnostic output
pasted into chat and ingested as dialogue. The store describes itself, the
description becomes a memory, and the memory then inflates the next measurement
of the thing it described. That is how 12 beats containing the literal text
"[about: Thomas]" got counted as if they were entries.

MEASURED BEFORE GUARDING (9,513 beats):

    840   deliberate capture syntax only ([remember:]/[bookmark:])  <- A FEATURE
    126   mirror signals only — the store's own ids, tags and logs
     21   BOTH in one beat  <- the hard case, ordinary shop talk citing an id

    by signal:  79 entry-id · 47 me-log · 31 ticket-id · 13 about-tag · 9 beat-id
    by month:   232 Jun · 376 Jul · 388 Aug   <- GROWING

WHAT SHIPPED: src/sentiment/mirror.ts + Stage -1b in the pipeline.

  REFUSE, DON'T FILTER. Route-and-mark into data/mirror-lane.jsonl with the FULL
  text before the message is emptied, refusals counted BY REASON, and both the
  refusals and the SAVES surfaced live in the [ME:pipeline] mirror-lane line. The
  saves matter as much: without them the ledger could show what was refused and
  never whether a real utterance was eaten.

  LINE-LEVEL WITH A COVERAGE GATE, never a chunk-level boolean. The 21 "both"
  beats are real conversation that happens to cite one of our ids — "the
  [remember:] tag writes character-scope because…" — and a chunk verdict would
  misfile every word wrapped around the thing it detected. That is the pe4o
  failure repeated, and the fix is the one pe4o already found.

  DELIBERATE CAPTURE SYNTAX IS NEVER A MIRROR LINE. 840 beats carry a
  [remember:]/[bookmark:] tag; that is the primary manual-capture path and
  refusing one would break it.

  NOT A KEYWORD BLOCKLIST. It matches SELF-MINTED IDENTIFIERS — ctopic-/utopic-,
  beat-<sha>, [ME:...], MarinaraExtender-<id>. Nobody types "ctopic-8f3k2a1b" to
  mean something. A human can say "about" or "remember" all day and never trip it.

THRESHOLD, AND THE TRADEOFF STATED RATHER THAN TUNED AWAY. MIRROR_COVERAGE = 0.4,
matching SELF_PROMPT_COVERAGE. Benched (scripts/mirror-bench.mjs): 137 chunks carry
a mirror line; at 0.4 it refuses 79 and keeps 58. KNOWN MISSES: two genuine log
pastes sit at 0.36 and 0.39, just under. KNOWN CORRECT KEEPS at the same depth:
Mari's "OH IT FINISHED. 263/263, 469 chunks, zero off-speaker errors" at 0.35, and
a real debugging exchange at 0.30. Dropping to 0.3 catches the two misses and eats
both of those. The threshold was NOT lowered to make the number look better.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET:
  - The 6 index.yaml orphans. That path ALREADY held the lock, so serialization
    does not explain them.
  - The shutdown drain. Serialization fixes concurrency; PROCESS EXIT is what
    actually creates an orphan, and nothing joins in-flight writes yet.
  - Retry-loop instrumentation — the EPERM/EBUSY hypothesis is still unmeasured.
  - ELEVEN UNSERIALIZED WRITERS remain, now visible because the raw function was
    renamed to atomicWriteFile_UNLOCKED_takeSerializedWriteYourself: receipts,
    soft-clock, stats-events, encoder, entities, identity, user-identity,
    story-jobs, setup, and a backfill script. Several are per-turn. Each is a
    candidate for the same orphan.
  - Disposition of the 152 existing orphans, still sequenced AFTER 073 reads them.

title: 1,313 demoted facts carry a non-name subject — the prompt's own placeholder emitted as a name, and nothing ever refused it
description:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while tracing su6h's omission. Incidental to that hunt, but large.

resolveFactTarget demotes a fact to chat scope and tags the summary '[about: X]' when
resolveNameToKey(X) cannot resolve the subject to a character key. The store holds 3,380
such entries. Ranked by subject:

    2,395   character
      373   [character
       68   Thomas
       62   she
       56   unknown
       40   him
       29   holyknight3
       19   the character
       19   I
       ...  111 distinct 'subjects' in total

2,768 of 3,380 — 82% — are the literal word 'character' or the bracketed placeholder
'[character]'. These are not names. The extractor is handing back the PROMPT'S OWN
PLACEHOLDER TOKEN as the subject of a fact, and the summaries confirm it:

    '[about: character] A character expresses the idea of experiencing ...'
    '[about: character] Someone did not apply patches to something referred ...'
    '[about: [character]] [character] is intentionally delaying progress, ...'
    '[about: [character]] [character] has a specific ritual or process for ...'

The second form is worse: the placeholder leaks into the FACT BODY too, so the entry
reads '[character] is anxious' — a sentence with no referent at all. Nothing downstream
can ever resolve these. They are retrievable, they occupy the chat-scope lane, and they
carry zero recoverable information.

THIS IS THE PROMPT LAW WEARING A NEW HAT. The placeholder is proximate text in the
prompt, so the model reaches for it when the chunk gives it nothing — the same mechanism
that made 792 beats echo a prompt example. Verify which prompt introduces the token
before changing anything, and check whether the [character] block label in the message
format is the source rather than the fact prompt.

AND THE GUARD DEMOTED WHERE IT SHOULD HAVE REFUSED. Demote-and-tag is the right response
to an UNKNOWN name. It is the wrong response to a value that is not a name at all — that
is a malformed extraction and should be dropped with a counter, not filed. 2,768 entries
accumulated behind a check that had already noticed something was wrong, which is the
looksCastList shape recorded in bd memory ('advisory guards do no work'): if a condition
is worth detecting it is worth refusing.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING in the same population: 62 'she', 40 'him', 19 'I', 13 'he',
12 'someone', 6 'we', 6 'himself' — bare pronouns as subjects, ~160 entries. Same class:
not a name, should never have been accepted as one. 'unknown' (56) and 'unknown character'
(14) are the model explicitly saying it does not know, which is honest and should be a
DROP, not a tag.

SCOPE NOTE: the 68 '[about: Thomas]' entries are a DIFFERENT bug and must not be swept
with these — Thomas is a real subject (TC's persona) that fails to resolve because
ingestSceneFacts has no personaName field, so resolveFactTarget's persona branch is dead
code on that path and bare 'Thomas' correctly does not expand to the user. Those entries
are correct data in the wrong place. These 2,768 are not data at all. File separately if
the persona-routing gap needs its own ticket.

SUGGESTED SLICE: (1) a validity check on the subject before it is ever used — reject
placeholder tokens, bracketed literals, bare pronouns, and 'unknown', with a counter so
the rate is visible; (2) find and fix the prompt surface leaking the token; (3) decide
what to do with the 2,768 already on disk — they are inert but retrievable, and 'nothing
retires the loser' is already a standing complaint in this store.

ACCEPTANCE: no new entry can be written with a non-name subject, the leak source is named
in the fix, the rejection rate is logged rather than silently demoted, and a stated
disposition for the existing 2,768.

RELATED: 4g9w (SUBJECT vs SCOPE — the missing 'who is this about' axis these entries are
failing to express), cye6 (found in the same trace), the-prompt-law-tc-2026-08-04-pifl
and advisory-guards-do-no-work-oknn-2026-08 in bd memories.
notes:
COUNTS CORRECTED 2026-08-25 — the original description's 3,380 / 2,768 were GREP HITS, not entries.

My mistake, and it is the 'count utterances, never hits' law broken in the one place it
matters most: an entry's summary is stored in the entry FILE and again in its INDEX ROW,
so a naive grep double-counts every entry, and stale copies in orphaned .tmp files and
the receipts audit trail inflate it further.

FULL RECONCILIATION of the 3,396 raw hits (recounted by distinct entry id):

    1,494   entry files (char-topics + user-topics)
    1,492   live index.yaml + index.cold.yaml rows
      153   ORPHANED .tmp index copies  <- i83s's litter, counted as if it were data
      257   receipts/ audit-trail copies
    ─────
    3,396   grep hits
    1,494   DISTINCT ENTRIES  <- the only real number

CLASSIFIED BY THE SHIPPED GUARD (rejectSubjectName, so these are the exact entries the
new code would refuse):

    1,237   placeholder   ('character', 'the character', 'unknown', 'someone', …)
       74   pronoun       ('she', 'him', 'I', 'he', 'we', 'himself')
        2   bracketed     ('[character]')
    ─────
    1,313   non-names
      181   VALID names, across 89 distinct subjects  <- the migration list

PROFILE OF THE 1,313, measured before proposing any disposition:

    lane      character_topics 1,302 | user_topics 11
    scope     chat 1,313  (ALL of them — they are the demoted population by definition)
    status    open 1,313
    tier      none 1,313
    created   2026-06-12 .. 2026-08-25

    RETRIEVED AT LEAST ONCE: 0.  Recited: 0.

That last line is the one that matters for disposition. Not one of these 1,313 has ever
reached a prompt — unlike wct1's ctopic-sjwwu4lz, which had retrievalCount 1. They are
inert: chat-scoped, untiered, never recalled, and now unreproducible. So there is no
urgency to delete them and no evidence of harm from leaving them, which argues for
handling them in the migration slice rather than as their own cleanup.

The created range ending 2026-08-25 means they were still being produced up to the day
the qlib guard landed. That guard is what stops the population growing; it does not
touch these.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CARDINALITY CORRECTED 2026-08-25 (second time today, same root cause). Any "68
[about: Thomas]" above is a GREP-HIT count and is wrong. Reconciled by parsing:

    23  DISTINCT ENTRIES with subject exactly "Thomas"   <- the real number
     3  "Thomas Collier"   2  "real-thomas"   2  "thomas"   1  "Thomas" + apostrophe
    31  total distinct entries whose subject contains "thomas"

The 73 raw hits decompose as: 23 entry files + 23 index rows + 14 receipts/ copies
+ 12 BEAT TEXT quoting the tag syntax (Mari pasting a store audit back into the
conversation — not entries at all) + 1 supersession-candidates.yaml. Note also that
grep -o counts OCCURRENCES rather than files, so even per-bucket figures are matches.

THE NUMBER DID NOT MOVE BECAUSE ANYTHING WAS RECOUNTED BY HAND. 22 came out of the
corrected census — the same run that produced 181/1,494. The error was that the
headline number was corrected and this sub-number was left standing in these notes,
so two figures for one population were published side by side. Restating every
derived count when a census is corrected is the actual discipline that was missing.

TWO THINGS THIS EXPOSED:
  1. THE CASE VARIANTS ARE A MIGRATION DECISION, not noise. FIVE distinct subject
     strings for one referent across 31 entries: "Thomas" 23, "Thomas Collier" 3,
     "real-thomas" 2, "thomas" 2, and one possessive form. (This line first said
     four-across-29 while listing five — corrected.) awgj must decide whether they normalize to a
     single subject — and "Thomas Collier" is the delicate one, because
     user-identity.yaml EXCLUDES that form from TC by declaration.
  2. IT IS A LEAK RATE, NOT A CONSTANT. The census counted 22 at ~12:40; the parse
     counted 23 forty minutes later. The old dist keeps minting prefixed rows until
     the sidecar is cycled. The 181 and 1,313 figures are timestamps, not totals.

title: Propose card edits when the story outgrows the card — human approval, diff, and stated supports; never automatic
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-25: cards should be updated occasionally to reflect major
changes to the story. NOT PREVIOUSLY FILED — searched every issue title, description,
notes and design field plus all 45 bd memories; the nearest neighbours are opyv (read
cards as base fact) and the lorebook write-back tickets, and neither touches the card
itself.

TC'S REQUIREMENT, verbatim in shape: 'All Card edits would need human approval. With a
diff explaining the changes made, and what the supports are for the change.'

So the deliverable is a PROPOSAL, never a write. Three parts, all mandatory:
  1. HUMAN APPROVAL   no auto-apply at any confidence, ever.
  2. A DIFF           field by field, old -> new, so the change is readable as a
                      change rather than as a new card.
  3. THE SUPPORTS     for every proposed edit, the evidence: which beats/entries,
                      with their source text and dates. An edit with no citable
                      support is not offered.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⚠ THE CIRCULARITY IS THE DANGER, AND IT MUST BE DESIGNED AGAINST FIRST

opyv rules that cards are BASE FACT — the thing derived entries are adjudicated
against. This feature proposes editing cards using evidence FROM THE STORE. That is a
loop, and it runs in the worst direction:

    a fabricated memory  ->  cited as 'support'  ->  written into the card
                         ->  becomes base fact  ->  now corroborates itself
                         ->  and licenses every future echo of the same claim

The Krakow entry is not a hypothetical for this. ctopic-82p9tylw asserts 'Dr. Mari
Zielinska ... from Krakow' with ZERO supporting source text, and it is still live
today. Feed that to a naive card-update proposer and it would offer 'add: from Krakow'
to a card that deliberately says only 'Polish' — completing the laundering that the
05.08 audit caught by hand. The fabrication would become the axiom.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE DESIGN, not optional extras:
  - SUPPORTS MUST BE SOURCE TEXT, never derived fields. A summary or motivation is
    the system's own output and cannot corroborate a change to the system's ground
    truth — 'a copy cannot corroborate its source', already house law.
  - Show the human the RAW UTTERANCES and who said them. The su6h count (21 origin
    assertions, 19 of them spoken by characters rather than by TC) is exactly the
    kind of distribution a reviewer needs to see, because 'the characters have been
    treating this as true for months' and 'the author established it' are different
    warrants.
  - An edit supported ONLY by derived entries should be shown as such and flagged,
    not silently ranked with the well-supported ones.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
REUSE THE MACHINERY THAT EXISTS — this is not a new review system

  apply-gate.ts       already implements a two-stage hold: domain-sensitive verdicts
                      (trauma first) ALWAYS hold regardless of confidence, everything
                      else holds unless high-confidence. Cards are simply the
                      unconditional case — treat a card edit as permanently sensitive,
                      so the confidence stage never runs. The doctrine there already
                      fits: 'when the downside is unrecoverable and the upside ~0,
                      never auto-apply, no matter how confident.' A wrong card edit is
                      exactly that shape, one level higher.
  reconcile-queue /   the held-for-review lane and its ledger already exist on disk.
  reconcile-ledger    'hold never means drop' is already the rule.
  4z0h                the held-review lane UI from the mockup — the surface this
                      would present in.
  3pl                 supersedes audit trail + rollback UI — a card edit MUST be
                      reversible, and this is where that lives.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SEQUENCING: opyv FIRST, AND IT PRODUCES THIS FEATURE'S WORK QUEUE

opyv's suggested first slice is a report of DISAGREEMENTS between cards and the store
— every derived entry contradicting a card, and every card fact absent from the store.
That report IS the list of places the story may have outgrown the card. Build the
reader, read the disagreements, and the proposer's input already exists. Building this
first would mean inventing the same comparison twice.

VERSIONING IS A HARD COUPLING, not a nicety. opyv already flags that a fact seeded
from a card must record WHICH VERSION it came from. The moment cards start moving,
every seeded fact needs that or the store fills with stale base facts indistinguishable
from current ones. Thomas's persona already carries personaVersion 1.2, so the field
exists; the discipline does not. Do not ship the writer before the reader records
versions.

SCOPE NOTE: personas and character cards are different objects with different write
paths (GET /api/characters vs /api/characters/personas/list). Do not assume one
implementation covers both, and note that a PERSONA edit is a claim about TC or one of
his personas, which is a more sensitive object than a character card.

ACCEPTANCE: a proposal surface that shows a field-level diff with per-change supports
quoted from SOURCE TEXT, applies nothing without an explicit human action, records what
was applied and from which card version, and is reversible. Plus a measured statement
of how many proposals were generated and how many the human accepted — an approval gate
nobody can audit is an approval gate that drifts into a rubber stamp.

RELATED: opyv (read cards as base fact — build first), su6h (the omission this would
have surfaced), 7pcm + 0qx6 (a card edit must respect persona containment: Mark's card
is base fact about Mark, and within Mari's context Mark is fiction TC wrote), 3pl
(rollback), 4z0h (review UI), a90l (deferred reconciliation lane).
notes:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CORRECTION 2026-08-25 — the supports rule as first written was wrong.

I wrote "supports must be SOURCE TEXT, never derived fields", implicitly ranking beat
text above the card. TC: "I did write the character card, so a human did say it. It's
there so I don't have to repeat it." The card IS a human utterance — the strongest
one, authored declaratively so it need not be repeated.

THE RULE RESTATED CORRECTLY. Supports must come from a tier above system-derived, and
must never be tier 3 ALONE:
  1  authored by TC declaratively (cards, his lorebook entries)      base fact
  2  typed by TC in conversation                                     strong
  3  model-generated character dialogue                              NOT independent
  4  system-derived (summaries, motivations)                         never a support

TIER 3 IS THE TRAP, AND IT IS SUBTLER THAN THE DERIVED-FIELD ONE I ORIGINALLY NAMED.
Character dialogue is canon-consistent BECAUSE the card was injected into that
character's context. So a proposer that counts character lines as evidence for editing
a card is reading the card's own echo back to itself — a second laundering path,
distinct from the derived-entry one, and harder to see because the text looks like
fresh testimony from a different speaker.

Concretely: 19 of su6h's 21 Independence assertions are character-spoken. As support
for "the card already says this", they are worthless — of course they say it, they were
told. As support for CHANGING the card, they would be actively misleading.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE from the original note: the circularity risk is real, the Krakow
entry is a live example of a fabrication that would be offered as an edit, and no
proposal should ever apply without human action. Only the ranking was wrong.

PRACTICAL SHAPE FOR THE REVIEW SURFACE: label every support with its tier and its
speaker, and show tier-1 conflicts first — "the card says X, the store says Y" is the
proposal worth a human's attention. "The characters keep saying X" is not, on its own,
a reason to write anything.

title: Sidecar memory reaches 1.5GB against a 93MB median — Windows RADAR flagged node.exe as a leaker twice
description:
FOUND 2026-08-24 while investigating 073. SEPARATE FROM THE DEATHS, and filed
separately on purpose: this is not what kills the sidecar, but it is a real problem
and 073's evidence is the only reason anyone noticed.

WINDOWS ITSELF FLAGGED IT. The Application event log holds two 'Windows Error
Reporting / RADAR_PRE_LEAK_64' reports naming node.exe 24.15.0.0 (2026-07-19 and
2026-08-19, one shared fault bucket). RADAR is Windows' resource-exhaustion detector
and PRE_LEAK is a memory-GROWTH warning — not a crash. These are the only node.exe
entries in the event log at all; there is not one Application Error.

THE NUMBERS, from start.ps1's Measure-SidecarProcess samples recorded at each of 30
deaths (working set of whichever node owns port 3001):

    n=30   min 73 MB   median 93 MB   max 1496 MB

So the usual resting state is under 100 MB and something occasionally takes it past
1.4 GB. Individual samples seen: 958 MB, 990 MB, 1496 MB.

WHY IT IS NOT THE CAUSE OF 073, so nobody re-merges them: the MEDIAN death happens at
93 MB, the log contains zero V8 OOM signatures ('FATAL ERROR', 'heap out of memory',
'Reached heap limit') even though stderr is merged into it, and death uptimes show no
relationship to memory at all (1.7 min at 112 MB; 62 min at 958 MB; 1250 min at
110 MB). 073's own note carries the full rule-out.

WHAT IT PLAUSIBLY DOES EXPLAIN: the machine-wide memory pressure RADAR was reacting
to. A background sidecar sitting at 1.5 GB is a problem on its own terms even if it
never dies of it.

WHERE TO LOOK FIRST — the sidecar holds several things that grow with corpus size and
are plausible: beat-embeddings.yaml is 8.1MB for one character and recap-embeddings
another 624KB, index.yaml 3.5MB; the entity index, alias maps and beat index are read
into memory; and the embeddings model (EMBED_MODEL via Ollama) plus any cached
tensors are the usual suspects for a hundreds-of-MB step change. The 73 MB floor
against a 1.5 GB peak suggests a per-operation retention rather than a slow creep --
find the operation before assuming a leak in steady state.

MEASURE IT BEFORE FIXING IT, per house law. Measure-SidecarProcess already samples
working set every 5 seconds and currently only prints at death; logging it on an
interval (or on a threshold crossing) would turn this from three anecdotes into a
curve, and would show whether it is a slow creep or a step. That is the cheap first
move and it needs no code in the sidecar itself.

RELATED: 073 (the deaths — different cause, ruled out above), 96eo (85 orphaned
atomic-write temp files, which an abrupt end to a large operation would also explain).
notes:
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GROWTH-RATE OBSERVATION 2026-08-24, from the gwny restart.

The node process was at 839 MB after 49 MINUTES of uptime (launched 16:36:48, killed
17:26 for a deliberate restart). Two more samples from the same day's log: 850 MB and,
earlier in the week, 958 MB / 990 MB / 1496 MB.

THAT IS FAST, and it reframes the shape of this bug. The 93 MB median at death made it
look like a rare excursion; 839 MB inside an hour says the climb is the NORMAL
behaviour and the low medians are simply short-lived processes that were killed before
they got going. Median-at-death measures how long processes live, not how fast they
grow. Sample WORKING SET AGAINST UPTIME, not against death events.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP unchanged and now better motivated: Measure-SidecarProcess already
samples working set every 5s and only prints at death. Logging it on an interval turns
this into a curve, which would settle slow-creep vs step-change in one session — and
at this rate a session is all it needs.

POSSIBLE CONTRIBUTOR NOW REMOVED, worth re-measuring against: gwny shipped the same
day (loader.ts no longer re-persists every loaded index row on every turn — thousands
of identical-row writes per turn are gone). That is write volume rather than retained
heap, so it should NOT be assumed to fix this; but any growth curve measured from now
on is measured against a different write load than the 839 MB sample above, and
comparing across that boundary would be comparing two different systems.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
INSTRUMENTATION WRITTEN 2026-08-24 (start.ps1). NOT YET ARMED — see the bottom.

The sample was already being taken every 5 seconds by Measure-SidecarProcess and
thrown away unless the process died. It now reaches the log two ways, answering two
different questions:

  [mem]       HEARTBEAT every 15 min -> the CURVE. Slow creep, or flat with steps?
  [mem:STEP]  an increase of >=150 MB between two samples 5 SECONDS APART, logged
              immediately -> names the OPERATION.

THE STEP WRITER IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A 73 MB floor against a 1.5 GB peak is the
shape of per-operation retention, not of gradual creep. A 500 MB jump inside five
seconds is one thing retaining one large object, and the line's value is its
TIMESTAMP: it lands in the same log the sidecar tees to, so the jump sits directly
beneath whatever the sidecar was doing at that moment.

CHOICES, so they can be re-tuned deliberately rather than fiddled with:
  - 150 MB step floor is well above jitter (resting state is 73-93 MB), so a hit
    cannot be noise. Tune DOWN only after reading what it catches at 150 — starting
    sensitive would bury the real steps in chatter.
  - 15 min heartbeat is ~96 lines/day, invisible in a 15MB log.
  - Uptime comes from the PROCESS's StartTime, not SidecarStartedAt. The launcher
    ATTACHES to an already-running sidecar when the port is busy (Start-Sidecar's
    port guard), and in that case SidecarStartedAt is the watchdog's start — it would
    report a 20-hour-old process as newborn, which is exactly the axis this needs
    right.
  - A step is only computed WITHIN one pid. Across a restart the baseline resets, so
    a fresh 90 MB process after a 600 MB one must not read as a -510 MB step (or, on
    the way back up, as a phantom jump).

VERIFIED IN ISOLATION rather than by waiting 15 minutes for a line: first sample
logs a heartbeat; +10 MB is silent; +500 MB same pid logs a STEP; +500 MB ACROSS a
pid change is correctly silent; 14 min is silent and 16 min heartbeats. start.ps1
parses clean and the log path resolves to the real file.

⚠ NOT ARMED YET, and this is the same trap as the 073 fix. The instrumentation lives
in start.ps1, so it only takes effect for a watchdog started AFTER the edit — the
worker/loop code is the watchdog's in-memory copy of the script. The live watchdog is
pid 16964, started 16:30:15, and the edit landed at 18:29:26, so it is running the old
code and writes nothing. (A second watchdog, pid 38036, did start at 18:30:09 with the
new code, but exited almost immediately — most likely a window opened and closed;
Start-Sidecar's port guard would have had it attach rather than spawn.)

TO ARM: quit the launcher and run it again. [R] restart is NOT enough — that calls
Stop-Sidecar/Start-Sidecar inside the already-loaded script and never re-reads the
file. Verify by grepping the log for "[mem]" within ~15 minutes of relaunch, or
immediately on the first healthy check.
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LIVE SPECIMEN CAUGHT 2026-08-26T01:42Z, and it is not the shape the ticket
assumed. Measured before killing it, which is the only reason it is on record.

  pid 15588   node dist/index.js
  started     2026-08-24 19:08:37 -05:00      age 25.6 HOURS
  private     1281.2 MB     (median 93 MB; peak working set 1096.9 MB)
  working set  527.8 MB
  handles     311           threads 24
  CPU         356.2s total over 25.6h — idle, not spinning
  LISTENER    NONE. Nothing on 3001 (netstat empty, curl HTTP=000, twice).

THE PROCESS WAS ALIVE AND THE HTTP SERVER WAS DEAD. That is a distinction this
ticket did not have. 3lru was filed as "memory reaches 1.5GB" and 073 as "the
sidecar dies"; this is a third state — bloated, running, and serving nothing.

AND THE POLLER WAS STILL RUNNING while the listener was gone:
poller-state.yaml's newest watermark is 2026-08-26T01:14:17.864Z with a file
mtime of 01:14:20.264Z, 28 minutes before the process was examined. The poller is
a setInterval and does not depend on the HTTP server, so capture kept working
while the panel, /api/health and every endpoint went dark. Anyone checking "is
the sidecar up?" by watching whether memories still appear would have said yes.

WHY NOTHING RESTARTED IT: no launcher process was running. The full process list
held only VS Code shells and three comfyui-mcp nodes — start.ps1's watchdog was
not up, so there was nothing to notice the dead listener. That is consistent with
the launcher having been quit and the sidecar surviving as an orphan, but the
ORDER is not established and should not be assumed.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and worth saying rather than implying: whether the listener
died or never bound after a restart; whether the 1.28 GB is cause or symptom of
the listener loss; and whether the watchdog's health check would have caught it,
since the watchdog was not running to try.

WINDOWS ERROR REPORTING has one node.exe fault in the last 7 days, 2026-08-19
17:00:56, fault bucket 1276469612830154952 type 5 — the same bucket already on
this ticket, not a new event.

STILL NOT ARMED: the [mem] instrumentation never ran on this process, because it
predates it. Killed at 01:43Z to do the pe1c repair. The next launcher start is
still the thing that arms it.

THE CHEAP DETECTOR THIS SUGGESTS: the watchdog must probe /api/health over HTTP
rather than checking that a pid exists. A live pid is not a live sidecar, and
this process proves the gap is reachable in normal operation.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INSTRUMENTATION ARMED 2026-08-25 20:48 LOCAL (TC relaunched the launcher), and it
answered the ticket's central question inside fifteen minutes. The shape is NOT
what this ticket assumed, and it is not a per-turn leak either.

THE CURVE, pid 22212, from the log:

  20:48:33  [mem]        91 MB   up 0.1 min   <- fresh process
  20:49:29  [mem:STEP] +268 MB -> 355 MB      up 1.0 min
  20:53:14  [mem:STEP] +163 MB -> 296 MB      up 4.8 min
  20:53:19  [mem:STEP] +208 MB -> 504 MB      up 4.9 min
  21:02:46  [mem:STEP] +231 MB -> 823 MB      up 14.3 min
  21:03:37  [mem]       911 MB               up 15.2 min

  91 MB + 870 MB of steps = 961; observed 911, so ~50 MB was reclaimed. The four
  STEPS account for essentially ALL of the growth. There is no creep component in
  this window — the start.ps1 comment's prediction ("per-operation retention, not
  gradual creep") is correct about the SHAPE.

EVERY STEP LANDS ON A COMPLETED TURN. Reading the sidecar lines immediately
before each jump: three of four sit on '[ME:bridge] turn ingested' or the
tier2/tier3 tail of one, the fourth on a loadContext assembling a context block.
Six turns ran in that window.

AND THEN IT STOPS, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. I was about to report
"~145 MB per turn" (870 MB / 6 turns). That would have been wrong, and the check
that killed it was asking for the DENOMINATOR before comparing:

  since the 911 MB heartbeat:  3 more turns ingested
                               0 mem STEPs
                               895 MB at 29 min, peak 1012 MB — DOWN from 911

Turns 7, 8 and 9 cost nothing. So this is not linear per-turn retention. It is a
fast climb to a HIGH-WATER MARK over the first handful of turns and then flat —
the signature of V8 growing its heap to accommodate a large working set (the
loader reports 3,023-3,029 character index rows loaded on EVERY turn, plus cue
expansion over 231 entities) and then never returning it to the OS.

SO THERE ARE TWO PHENOMENA HERE AND THE TICKET CONFLATES THEM:
  (1) FAST: 91 MB -> ~900-1000 MB in ~6 turns, in discrete ~200 MB steps. Bounded.
      Plateaus. This is heap warm-up against a big per-turn working set.
  (2) SLOW: the hung process examined earlier the same day was at 1,281 MB private
      after 25.6 HOURS. That is ~300 MB on top of the plateau over a day, which
      (1) does not explain and which this window is far too short to see.
Only (2) is a candidate for an actual leak. (1) is expensive, not leaking.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and neither has been done: a heap snapshot at the plateau
to see whether the 3,025-row index is retained per-turn or merely re-allocated;
and a long window with a turn count attached, so (2) can be normalised by
exposure instead of by wall-clock.

DO NOT quote "145 MB per turn" from anywhere. It was never true.
PLATEAU CONFIRMED OVER A FULL HOUR, pid 26552 (session 21:36:49, TC's own restart):

  21:39:22  [mem:STEP] +410 MB in one 5s sample -> 1001 MB   up  2.5 min
  21:52:01  [mem]      1002 MB                                up 15.2 min
  22:07:05  [mem]      1121 MB                                up 30.3 min
  22:22:07  [mem]      1036 MB                                up 45.3 min
  22:37:10  [mem]      1024 MB                                up 60.3 min

One 410 MB step at 2.5 minutes, then flat for an hour — 1002, 1121, 1036, 1024,
i.e. wandering inside ~10% with no trend. The 29-minute window recorded earlier
was too short to be sure; sixty minutes is not, and it says the same thing. Fast
climb to a high-water mark, then steady. This is the second independent process
to show it.

Note the step is BIGGER and EARLIER here than on pid 22212 (+410 MB at 2.5 min
versus four ~200 MB steps over 14 min). Same destination, different route — which
is consistent with heap sizing against whatever the first turns happen to load and
not with a fixed per-operation cost.

title: Retire the 6 changelog-derived beats mln9 found — the gate stops new ones, it does not clean the old

pipeline.ts and as defence in depth in classifyChunk). Its acceptance criteria were
about the LIVE PATH, and those are met: verified end to end, all six offenders now
suppress at both gates.

THE SIX ARE STILL IN THE STORE. They remain retrievable, so the character can still
'remember feeling ashamed' about an Engine bug she has no relationship to — which is
the harm the ticket was actually about. This is the companion cleanup, filed
separately for the same reason 4ghy split its census from its minting fix.

  beat-37faa0d37ec5  2026-06-03  joy            53 openers
  beat-d7d767b27166  2026-06-04  shame          36 openers   speaker minted from the changelog
  beat-2b6ff6f8480d  2026-06-22  joy            26 openers   speaker minted from the changelog
  beat-a39cf0d43085  2026-06-22  anger           6 openers
  beat-6e75eeb7f8b6  2026-08-20  shame          20 openers
  beat-61b2658165f9  2026-08-20  vulnerability   4 openers

`node scripts/changelog-scan.mjs` (read-only) — it now imports the shipped detector,
so the scan and the gate cannot disagree.

not a verdict. Of 8 entries flagged there on stale sourceChatId, 7 had true content
and a sweep would have destroyed them. Six records is small enough to read, and they
should be read before anything is written.

TWO THINGS TO CHECK WHILE RETIRING, both found during the mln9 sizing pass:

  1. THREE OF THE SIX CARRY A MINTED SPEAKER taken from the changelog's own first
     line ('Added Roleplay quick-edit gestures', 'Added stronger appearance
     customization'). Those speakers are in the 570-label census 4ghy tracks, and
     retiring the beat should not orphan or silently keep the label.

     beat did not take it out of recall until that was fixed; confirm the companion
     ledger entries go with them rather than surviving the beat.

AND DO NOT TOUCH THE TWO ABOUT-WORK BEATS: beat-4cf78d9e6f32 and beat-e45fb60631d1.
Both are Mari reacting in her own voice to real work, both are real utterances, and
both are pinned as must-not-fire cases in changelog.test.ts. beat-4cf78d9e6f32 IS
mis-scored (celebratory text filed as shame, with an invented motivation about 'not
catching a bug') but that is emotion mis-scoring on a genuine beat and wants its own
ticket, not a retirement.

two ABOUT-WORK beats untouched.
notes:
SCOPED 2026-08-24. All six beats verified LIVE (none retired, none on a thread), and
the companion-entry blast radius measured rather than assumed.

THE CLEANUP IS 6 BEATS + 3 COMPANION ENTRIES:

  beat-37faa0d37ec5  2026-06-03  joy            no companion entry
  beat-d7d767b27166  2026-06-04  shame          no companion entry

    [shame] Dr. Mari Zielińska feels a surge of shame when she realizes that her

OqZoOawldYlWBZtUa61X9, turnStart 2.

HOW THE COUNT WAS TAKEN, because the first attempt was wrong in the documented way.
Companion entries carry no beat id — companionEntryFromBeat derives them from the

the summary from the beat's motivation and that beat's motivation was the paste's
own text. So the manual scoping under-counted by one and retireBeats' veto caught
it. An entry whose entire content is "Added stronger appearance customization" is

  2. both ABOUT-WORK beats still LIVE                               PASS
  3. VETO CORRECTNESS — for each of the 4 retired entries, count of
     LIVE beats that would still produce that summary: 0, 0, 0, 0   PASS

     8,417 hot / 425 cold                                           PASS
  5. RECALL ACTUALLY DROPS THEM (the pe4o/41uo requirement) — all

  6. MINTED SPEAKER LABELS (the 4ghy overlap): "Added Roleplay

  7. snapshot taken before the write, recoverable at

execution, so TC was actively chatting and the sidecar was writing. retireBeats
does read-modify-write on beats/index.yaml and so does the encoder; its

This is the demo-sidecar lesson applied to a script instead of a second sidecar.

THE SCRIPT REFUSES RATHER THAN TRUSTS: scripts/retire-wct1-changelog-beats.mjs

(supersededAt/replacedBy), so discarded-to-cold entries have no HTTP surface.
