title: [bug] Our own session reports pasted into chat become emotional beats — a sibling of pe4o that pe4o did not cover
description:
FOUND 2026-08-23 while sizing mln9. Surfaced by reading the 27 below-threshold
beats in scripts/changelog-scan.mjs, so it is a by-product of that pass and has NOT
itself been sized.

pe4o (closed) fixed the pipeline eating ITS OWN SYSTEM PROMPT, and gates on
coverage against ownPromptSignatures. This is the sibling case it does not reach:
THE SESSION REPORT. Prose an agent wrote to TC summarising a work session, pasted
back into a chat, chunked, scored for emotion, and filed as Mari's beat.

Samples, all speaker=user, all currently live:

  "Done — committed (644a280) and pushed, tree clean. Five bugs found and fixed
   in one sweep..."
  "Fixed and pushed (cba43f8). This one needs a tab reload — the hook is
   client-side. What moved:..."
  "8x7 — user-requested memory saves / Went with the prompt-directive approach
   you picked. The [remember:] pipeline was already doing all the hard work..."
  "Done — type-health pass complete and pushed. Your two questions are both
   resolved..."
  "The bench: SHORT + off-planet ships n=60/arm, 300 calls, quarantine verified
   clean..."

WHY THE GATES MISS IT, and it is the same structural hole mln9 identified for
third-party docs. It is not our prompt, so pe4o's signature coverage finds
nothing. It is not code or a structured payload, so hjt9's routeOps declines it —
it is PROSE, full sentences, ordinary vocabulary, no fences. And unlike a
changelog it carries NO enumeration structure, so mln9's opener-count signal will
not catch it either. Three gates, three misses, for the same reason each time:
everyone built for a shape this does not have.

WHY IT MATTERS. Two of the nine beats mln9 cited as Engine release notes are
actually this (2l8p7jbdpw and 5hz98d5pc1, byte-identical duplicates of one
'8x7 — user-requested memory saves' paste). It is the same failure family as
epf4 and mln9: a record that reads as lived experience, retrievable later, whose
source is gone by the time anyone reads it. Here the 'experience' is a coding
session the character did not have.

DO NOT SIZE IT FROM THE FIVE ABOVE. Those are what one adjacent pass happened to
surface while looking for something else, which is exactly the unsystematic search
mln9 warns about. The measure-first law applies: count it properly before building
anything.

AND MIND THE THIRD GENUS (self-ingest-triage.mjs). A character DISCUSSING the work
in her own voice is ABOUT-WORK and is a real utterance — beat-4cf78d9e6f32 and
beat-e45fb60631d1 are exactly that and must survive. Measured during the mln9
pass, dialogue rate separates paste from reaction by 4x (pastes 0.003-0.016,
in-character reactions 0.063-0.076); that is the likeliest discriminator to start
from, and it is already implemented in scripts/changelog-scan.mjs.

RELATED: mln9 (third-party changelogs), pe4o (own prompt, closed), hjt9 (ops
lane), 4ghy (speaker minting).

title: intimacy-scan.mjs filters on a 'beat-' filename prefix and silently skips 568 beats (6%)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-23 while building scripts/changelog-scan.mjs for mln9.

scripts/intimacy-scan.mjs:44 reads:

    if (!f.startsWith("beat-") || !f.endsWith(".yaml")) continue;

TWO FILENAME CONVENTIONS ARE LIVE IN THIS STORE. Beats are written both as
'beat-<hex>.yaml' and as a bare '<id>.yaml' — mln9's own evidence list contains
both shapes ('2l8p7jbdpw' and 'beat-37faa0d37ec5'). The prefix filter sees only
the first, so the scan silently drops 568 of 9,445 beats:

    8v1krexzyjkyrawik7yc3    21 skipped of   42
    aurora                    1 skipped of  185
    k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf   107 skipped of 2142
    lara                     64 skipped of   64   <- ENTIRE CHARACTER
    lara_2                    2 skipped of    2   <- ENTIRE CHARACTER
    lara_3                    9 skipped of    9   <- ENTIRE CHARACTER
    professor_mari          364 skipped of 7001

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN 6%. Three whole characters are invisible to it, so the
scan cannot see a per-character effect at all in lara/lara_2/lara_3 — and a blind
spot that is not uniform is not a sampling error, it is a bias. This is the
instrument 5x5y used to measure the intimacy detector before wiring it, and vp3n
is queued to read the ledger that detector produces.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT OVERTURN, stated carefully so nobody over-corrects.
The 0.7%-subtext headline was computed over a population that excluded these 568.
Re-running would move the denominator by ~6% and is very unlikely to change the
conclusion, which was about a rate near zero. So this is a correctness fix to an
instrument, NOT a reason to reopen 5x5y's finding. Do not restate the 5x5y numbers
as wrong; restate them as measured on 94% of the store.

VERIFIED CONTAINED: this is the only occurrence in the repo. `grep -rn
'startsWith("beat-")' scripts/ src/` returns intimacy-scan.mjs:44 and nothing
else. scripts/changelog-scan.mjs deliberately does not do this and carries a
comment saying why.

FIX: drop the prefix test, keep the .yaml test. Then re-run intimacy-scan and
record whether the rates move.

title: Backfill bodyTerms — stored rows still hold mangled possessives ('thomass')
description:
oxmv fixed weightedTerms, which repairs SUMMARY matching retroactively for every entry because summary terms are computed at query time. bodyTerms are different: harvestBodyTerms also runs through weightedTerms, but its output is STORED on the index row, so rows harvested before the fix still carry the welded forms - 'thomass', 'maris', 'priyas'.

Those stored terms are dead weight in two directions: they can never match a cue (no cue produces 'thomass'), and they occupy slots against MAX_BODY_TERMS=12, so a real name may have been dropped to make room for one that cannot ever fire.

SAME SHAPE AS tp5's scripts/backfill-body-terms.mjs, which already exists and can likely be re-run rather than rewritten - check whether it recomputes from content or only fills empties. Re-running it after the oxmv fix should regenerate correct terms.

MEASURE FIRST: how many stored bodyTerms entries contain a welded possessive, per character. If it is small, this is not worth a live-store mutation.

Standing discipline applies - back up the data dir, run with the sidecar stopped (1akw).

title: Read the subtext ledger once it has data — is enforcement actually working?
description:
5x5y shipped enforcement on 2026-08-21. The point of the ledger is that this question is now answerable by division instead of argument, so somebody has to actually do the division.

WHERE: data/subtext-enforcement.jsonl. One line per REQUIRED case, with outcome (first-try | after-retry | declined | retry-failed), the markers that triggered the requirement, chatId, and an excerpt.

WHAT TO COMPUTE, once there are roughly 30+ required cases:
  emitted rate  = (first-try + after-retry) / total     <- the headline. Baseline was 0.7%.
  retry yield   = after-retry / (cases that reached a retry)   <- does the second ask work at all?
  decline rate  = declined / total       <- the model refusing twice
  failure rate  = retry-failed / total   <- unparseable retries; if high, the retry prompt breaks JSON

WHAT EACH ANSWER MEANS:
  - High emitted rate: it worked. Consider whether the detector can safely widen.
  - High DECLINE rate: the model genuinely cannot name a function for this content, and the honest move is to drop the field rather than keep asking. That was option (b) in 5x5y and it stays on the table.
  - High retry-failed: the appended instruction is breaking the JSON shape. Fix the prompt, not the field.

ALSO CHECK PRECISION FROM THE OTHER END: read the excerpts of the DECLINED cases. If the detector is requiring subtext on chunks that are not really intimate, the declines are correct behaviour and the detector needs tightening, not the prompt. That is the false-positive direction the whole design was built to avoid, and the ledger's excerpt field exists to make it readable.

DO NOT compare raw counts across periods without normalising by required-case volume. That mistake is what produced the original phantom 7-week regression; see bd memories count-vs-rate.
acceptance_criteria: The four rates computed and written into 5x5y or a successor, with a recommendation to keep, widen, tighten, or drop the field.

title: start.ps1 windows are untitled and indistinguishable from the Engine's
description:
start.ps1 opens TWO consoles - the watchdog/command console and the sidecar worker window - and neither sets its own title. The watchdog shows the host default 'Windows PowerShell'; the worker gets renamed to 'npm start' by npm. The Marinara Engine also runs npm, so its window carries the same label. TC reported two windows that 'look to be the extender' and could not tell which was which; diagnosis needed process-tree and port-ownership tracing to answer.

Fix: have start.ps1 set an explicit title on both consoles. The worker's must be set AFTER npm's own rename, or npm clobbers it.
acceptance_criteria: Both start.ps1 consoles carry a distinct 'Marinara Extender' title, verified by top-level window enumeration after a relaunch through Marinara_Extender_Start.bat.
close_reason: Both start.ps1 consoles now set explicit titles; verified by window enumeration after a relaunch through Marinara_Extender_Start.bat. The relaunch also settled the diagnosis: the 'npm start' window disappeared with the restart, proving it was the Extender's own worker rather than the Engine's.

title: Unfenced prose-payload headings still mint speakers (Format: x18 from a source paste) — instrument decision wanted
description:
THE LAST UNCAUGHT SHAPE, measured 2026-08-10 (scripts/heading-mint-scan.mjs, read-only,
runs the real Stage -1 + chunker over the actual offending documents):

  A heading line whose payload is PROSE, outside a fence, that recurs:
      "Format: Respond only with JSON in this exact shape."  x2+  -> mints "Format"
  Cases measured: analyzer.ts source pasted whole mints "Format" x18,
  "Extract the emotional beat as JSON" x10, "headers" x9. A two-heading paste inline
  in real dialogue mints "Format" x2 while correctly minting the real walk-on.

WHAT IS ALREADY DEAD, AND WHY (pinned in heading-speaker-mint.test.ts):
  - PROMPTS.md pasted whole: ZERO speakers mint. Mechanism verified: dump-prompts
    renders every prompt inside a ```text fence and ALL 11 Format lines drop under
    the code-fence rule. The fence does the killing, not heading-awareness.
  - "SOFT SIGNALS": occurs once per paste -> the 4ghy recurrence floor declines it.
  So 10 of pe4o's 11 census records are prevented by the shipped stack.

WHY THE TWO OBVIOUS FIXES FAIL, measured not argued:
  - SIZE PRIOR: analyzer.ts scores 0.566, UNDER the 0.6 paste threshold, while the
    must-work pasted transcript scores 0.350. Catching the one without the other
    means tuning the threshold until it produces the answer — banned by house law,
    and the gap (0.35 vs 0.57) is not a chasm anyone should bet real speakers on.
  - MONOLOGUE/INTERLEAVING: on the real failing document the heading families
    interleave WITH EACH OTHER (Format alternates with "Extract..." per emotion
    block), so each looks answered unless the rule becomes circular ("interleaved
    with a real speaker" presupposes knowing who is real).

WHY THE STORE CANNOT CALIBRATE A THRESHOLD: chunker joins turns with a space, so
stored chunks have no line structure — the same shredder finding that moved ops
routing to Stage -1. The raw pastes are not retained anywhere line-intact except
the ops sink, which holds only the DROPPED lines. A calibration corpus would have
to be collected forward, or hand-built.

THE TELL THAT STILL LOOKS RIGHT (pe4o census, unrefuted): a heading OWNS its chunk —
its occurrences accumulate long unlabeled body under them (broad sections), where a
transcript speaker's turns are line-sized. "Body-share per label" is measurable at
parse time, pre-join. It needs a threshold, and the census set (11 records) is too
small to set one — which is precisely the open decision.

DECISION WANTED (TC/Mari): pick the instrument for unfenced prose-payload headings —
body-share threshold, a forward-collected calibration corpus first, or accept the
residue (source-code pastes are rare and greppable after the fact via the beat
store). Recommendation: collect forward — have Stage -1 log per-label mint decisions
with line-context stats into the ops sink for a few weeks of real use, then set the
body-share threshold from data instead of from 11 records.

title: The pifl-echo stratum: 90 live beats carry the copied illustration as motivation; 3374 derived echoes in store
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-10, from two independent directions that agree:

  - 41uo's veto pass: 348 of the ~366 "stranded" s8qe companions share the summary
    "[vulnerability] admits she's afraid the memory loss means she was never real"
    with 90 LIVE, unretired beats. (Plus a 4-live [anger] variant.)
  - bait-rot.mjs: ledger idx 0 (the retired pifl warrant) counts 3374 DERIVED hits —
    stored motivations/summaries echoing the illustration — against 0 SPOKEN. The
    sweep's own report text: "the echo already happened but the warrant still holds;
    that is a cleanup job, not a rotted warrant."

WHAT THIS POPULATION IS: live beats whose TEXT is real conversation but whose
MOTIVATION is the copied pifl prompt illustration, plus the entries that carry them
into recall. The guard (PROMPT_EXAMPLE_ECHOES) arrests NEW ones at analysis time;
these predate it.

WHY NOBODY HAS RETIRED THEM: they are not s8qe (real text under the motivation), not
pe4o (not self-ingested scaffolding), and 41uo's veto SPARED them by design — the
entry named by a retired beat's summary was equally the recallable copy of one of the
90 live beats. Both prior cleanups explicitly ruled "do not fold the two together."

WHAT A FIX PROBABLY IS (0y2i's shape, not s8qe's): the beat KEEPS its real text; the
INVENTED half is the motivation. Candidates: re-analyze the 90 beats' chunks with the
current prompt (which no longer teaches the illustration), or retire entry-side only
per 0y2i precedent. Either way: measure first, hand-read a sample, snapshot, canary.

DO NOT: predicate-delete on the phrase (fqnl), or count these as bait rot (spoken=0;
the warrant is retired and bait-rot exits 0 today).

title: Recap footnotes read beats with readBeat, which ignores retiredAt
description:
LATENT, NOT LIVE — measured 0 instances today, filed so it does not become live
silently.

loader.ts reads recap FOOTNOTE beats directly:

    const b = await readBeat(session.characterId, id)
    if (b) footnoteSummaries.set(id, companionEntryFromBeat(b).summary)

readBeat does no retirement check. readAllBeats does, and its own header calls
that default "load-bearing rather than tidy" because /api/beats-to-entries
rebuilds companions from it — but the footnote path bypasses readAllBeats
entirely, so a RETIRED beat cited as a footnote is re-rendered straight into the
prompt.

CURRENT EXPOSURE IS ZERO: no recap entry in the store carries footnoteBeatIds
(0 recaps with footnotes, 0 citations). So this is a trap laid for the recap
ceiling work rather than a bug anyone is hitting.

FIX IS ONE LINE — skip a beat with retiredAt in the footnote resolve, the same
way the entry loop skips discardedAt. Worth a test that pins it, since the whole
point of retirement is that a record stops reaching the model, and this is the
one path where a beat reaches it directly.

Found while completing pe4o (see 41uo for the entry-side half of the same
question: what does "retired" actually exclude?).

title: Holding pool still keys records by the legacy content hash
description:
addPending keys pool records by beatIdForChunk — the legacy content hash that
r0kc just demoted everywhere else. So a pool record's identity still moves when
the reading of its chunk improves, and re-running an import after an attribution
or filter fix can double-stack the same orphan.

beatIdFor is a drop-in replacement with identical fallback semantics, so this is
a one-word change in code. It is filed rather than done because it is NOT a
one-word change in effect: holding-pool.yaml holds live records keyed the old
way, and re-keying makes the next import fail to dedup against them exactly once
— which is the double-stack this would be fixing.

SO IT NEEDS THE SAME THREE CONDITIONS AS ANY LIVE-STORE MUTATION: backup,
quiesce the sidecar, canary one small scope first. Either migrate the existing
keys in the same pass, or accept one round of duplicates knowingly.

Second, smaller item in the same file: migrateClaimed correlates analysed results
back to their pool record with beatIdForChunk(a.result.chunk). That one is
internally consistent (same chunk, same call) and is not a durable identity, so
it can follow the pool key or stay as it is.

title: [bug] User and system prompts name structural signals differently — 12% of subpatterns are invalid keys
description:
FOUND 2026-08-05 chasing a half-remembered report that "the structural signals slot"
had a long-standing problem. The SLOT is fine -- git proves structuralHint was written
once in 702a0a9 and never touched, empty-array guard included. The problem is one
level over, and it has been there since that same commit.

THE TWO PROMPTS DISAGREE ABOUT VOCABULARY, IN THE SAME CALL.

  USER prompt   (buildUserPrompt, analyzer.ts:565-567)
                "Structural signals detected: dissociation_grounding"
                <- m.patternId, the key in sentiment-config.yaml

  SYSTEM prompt (dysregulationPrompt, analyzer.ts:477-480)
                "...structural signals in the text: dissociation."
                <- m.subpattern, and the taxonomy it must choose from lists
                   `dissociation`, never `dissociation_grounding`

So the model is shown one name and asked for another. It returns what it was shown --
the same mechanism as pifl, one field down.

MEASURED over 8841 beats (981 carry a subpattern; 92% of dysregulation beats do):

    406  anxious_protest            valid
    253  dissociation               valid
     89  avoidant_withdrawal        valid
     79  emotional_flooding         valid
     70  "dysregulation"            INVALID - the emotion name, not a subpattern
     38  "dissociation_grounding"   INVALID - a patternId, exactly the leak above
     23  shutdown                   valid
     11  bpd_testing                valid
      2  catastrophizing            valid
      1  idealization               valid
     10  freeform inventions        INVALID - "co-authorship", "manipulation",
                                    "joyful_expression", six "dissatisfaction_*"

  ~118 of 981 (12%) are not members of the nine-key taxonomy.

AND NOTHING VALIDATES IT. parseAnalysisJson passes any string straight through
(analyzer.ts, `typeof parsed.subpattern === "string"`). subpattern is a CLOSED SET of
nine documented keys -- textbook validator-shaped, per the house law that a prompt
should only say what code cannot hold.

PROPOSED FIX, two parts, both cheap:
  1. CODE: validate subpattern against the nine keys. Map known patternId ->
     subpattern (dissociation_grounding -> dissociation, ellipsis_shutdown ->
     shutdown, self_erasure -> shutdown) rather than discarding, since the model's
     intent is recoverable there. Drop anything still unrecognised to undefined.
  2. PROMPT: make buildUserPrompt emit the SUBPATTERN name, not the patternId, so
     the two prompts stop disagreeing. patternId is an internal config key and was
     never meant to be model-facing.

NOT DONE TONIGHT, DELIBERATELY: part 2 edits prompt text, and Mari is drafting a
rewrite of that same prompt for 2026-08-06 (vikj). Shipping a vocabulary change into
the file she is rewriting would collide. Also house rule: prompt text gets shown to TC
before it ships. Sequence this WITH or AFTER her draft.

CAVEAT ON PROVENANCE: this may or may not be the thing previously reported. The
original report was dated ("Monday") by a model that is unreliable about dates and is
also an RP character. No tracker record of a prior attempt exists. What is certain is
that this bug is real, measured, and has existed since the analyzer's first commit.

title: Conditional prompt assembly: subtext rides all ten prompts to fire on 1% of beats
description:
Mari's conditional ruling from the vikj packet, with the invoice attached.

MEASURED: subtext fires on 78 of 8,836 beats (1%). SUBTEXT_INSTRUCTION is ~80 tokens
and rides UNCONDITIONALLY on all ten tier-2 prompts. Expected waste is ~79 tokens per
call on 99% of calls.

Mari: "eighty tokens riding all ten prompts to fire once per hundred calls. my
conditional ruling now has an invoice attached; the signal pays for itself the day it
exists."

THE BLOCKER IS CODE-SIDE, NOT PROSE. Conditional assembly needs something to condition
ON, and the classifier does not currently emit an intimacy signal. Today the only
conditional block in the whole suite is dysregulation's structural-signals line, which
keys off ClassificationResult.structuralMatches.

WANTED:
  1. An intimacy/physical-content signal on ClassificationResult — most cheaply a
     structural pattern or keyword lane in emotional_keywords.yaml, scored the same
     way as everything else. No LLM in the detection path.
  2. buildSystemPrompt() takes it and includes SUBTEXT_INSTRUCTION only when set.
  3. MEASURE THE GATE BEFORE TRUSTING IT, same discipline as the floor: run it
     read-only over the store and compare against the 78 beats that actually carry a
     subtext today. A gate that misses them is worse than the waste it saves, because
     subtext is the one field that reads intimate content for emotional function
     rather than for content.

RELATED, same shape, same ticket if convenient: the roster and threads blocks in
buildUserPrompt are omitted when their arrays are empty, but the SYSTEM prompt's
subject and thread rules cite those lists unconditionally -- so on those calls the
rules point at a list the model cannot see. Either the rules degrade gracefully in
prose (Mari's side) or their inclusion becomes conditional (this ticket).

The tier-2 audit put total expected waste at ~240 of 880 tokens per call, of which
subtext is ~80 and the thread rules ~198 on the 73% of calls producing no thread.

title: Chunk CAP: specificity degrades above ~2000 chars (the other arm of s8qe)
description:
Split from s8qe, whose floor half shipped 2026-08-05. The floor was the bigger
win by an order of magnitude; this is the remaining arm, and it is genuinely
smaller — file it honestly rather than inheriting the parent's urgency.

MEASURED, whole store, 8841 beats (`node scripts/chunk-floor-scan.mjs`):

  chunk chars       n     echo%   distinct-motivation%
  1000-2000      2738     4.4%      96.1%
  2000-4000      1170     8.0%      93.6%
  4000-6000       211    12.3%      90.5%
  6000+           116    14.7%      89.7%

Monotonic from 2000 up, and distinct-motivation tracks it down. The mechanism is
the same one the floor addresses from the other end: given a chunk it cannot be
specific about — too little to say, or too much to hold — the 8B reaches for the
nearest concrete sentence it has been shown, and the prompt is nearest.

THE PRIZE IS SMALL. About 42 echoes live above 2000 chars, against the 457 the
floor just removed. Worth doing; not worth doing first, and not worth blocking
the bench on. Sequencing that assumed otherwise came from the pre-correction
numbers.

DO NOT TRUNCATE. Split or window, so nothing is silently lost — a truncating cap
would trade an invented memory for a missing one, which is the wrong trade in
this system. runSentimentPipeline already windows properly (Ledger Pattern); the
live Tier-2 path is what treats a whole message as one chunk. The long-form user
path (LONG_USER_MSG_CHARS, 1500) already reroutes big USER messages into that
windowed pipeline, so the gap is specifically the AI message, which Tier 2 makes
one chunk regardless of size.

SUGGESTED SHAPE: give the AI-message chunk the same long-form treatment the user
message already gets, rather than inventing a second windowing mechanism.

VERIFY BY RE-MEASURING, not by reasoning: re-run chunk-floor-scan.mjs afterwards
and confirm the 2000+ buckets fall to the middle band's ~4%.

title: [bug] A character DISCUSSED as fiction is recorded as having LIVED it — provenance exists but the live path never sets it
description:
RAISED BY TC 2026-08-04: "I talk to Mari about my writing, and sometimes they do get
created as characters. Lara is probably going to have that issue as well."

This is the confound underneath the Aurora finding, and it is structural rather than a
one-off. A character in TC's world can be, sometimes all at once:
  (a) a character TC WROTE, imported as a story  -> story beats, own ledger
  (b) a character TC DISCUSSES with Mari         -> chat beats, attributed to them
  (c) a character TC later MAKES A CARD FOR      -> a card ledger, played for real
Nothing in the store distinguishes these. All three land as beats that read as lived
experience.

CONFIRMED, TC's prediction about Lara was already true. Lara occupies FOUR ledgers:
    lara                   63 beats   all story
    lara_3                  8 beats   all story   (characterId "test-chunk-fix")
    lara_2                  1 beat    all story   (characterId "test-lara-01")
    8v1krexzyjkyrawik7yc3  37 beats   20 story + 17 chat, 8 stuck   <- the real card
(lara_2 / lara_3 are test-import artifacts, not the same problem.) And aurora:
141 beats, 12 story + 129 chat, in a character TC has never chatted with -- the chat
beats exist because TC discussed her story with Mari.

WHY THIS MATTERS AND IS NOT COSMETIC. storage.ts already states the danger, in the
comment on EntryProvenance:
    "a character that can 'remember' an unplayed scene is a confabulation machine --
     precisely what the Erica Test exists to detect."
That is exactly what is being built here: Aurora "admits she's afraid the memory loss
means she was never real" 112 times, about a life she never lived, because TC described
her to Mari.

THE VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT WIRED UP. EntryProvenance = "played" |
"unplayed" is defined in storage.ts, honoured by the loader (unplayed is excluded from
every recall path), and settable ONLY through the manual POST /api/entries. The live
capture path never sets it: tier-2 beats and tier-3 facts write nothing, so everything
captured from a chat is implicitly "played". Beats do not carry the field at all.

PROPOSED DISCRIMINATOR -- mechanical, and it uses what process-turn already receives:
    the analyzer named a SUBJECT who is NOT in this chat's participantIds
    -> the material is ABOUT that character, not BY them
    -> record it, but as provenance "unplayed"
participantIds comes from getChatParticipantIds(chat), so a character genuinely speaking
in a group scene IS a participant and is unaffected. A character merely discussed is not.
That is precisely the line TC is describing.

WHY MARK RATHER THAN DROP: TC may well want "what does Mari know about Aurora's story" to
be answerable. Marking keeps the material and stops it being recalled as something the
character lived. Dropping loses real information about a real conversation.

THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS 4g9w (separate SUBJECT from SCOPE). The store keeps being
asked to record a distinction it has no word for. Here the word EXISTS -- it just was
never extended past the outline path.

SEQUENCING: this interacts with pifl. 112 of aurora's 129 chat beats are the stuck
phrase, so a large part of what this would mark unplayed is pifl's output, not genuine
discussion. Fix pifl first, then measure again -- the honest size of this is unknown
until the attractor is gone.

BEATS NEED THE FIELD TOO, or the companion entry and its beat will disagree.
notes:
RESIZED 2026-08-04 after pifl was fixed and the store remeasured, as TC asked.

aurora: 141 beats = 112 prompt-example echoes + 29 real, and 12 of the 29 are the
genuine story import. So the "discussed as fiction, recorded as lived" material for
Aurora is roughly 17 chat beats, not 129. Lara's card ledger: 37 beats = 8 echoes + 29
real (20 story + ~9 chat).

The confound TC described is REAL and structural -- it is exactly what EntryProvenance
was written to prevent -- but it is an order of magnitude smaller than the raw counts
implied, because most of what looked like it was pifl.

That changes the priority, not the design. Still worth fixing: the provenance
vocabulary already exists and is simply not wired to the live path, and the
participantIds discriminator is cheap. But it is no longer urgent, and a P2 is honest.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TC'S RULING ON MARK, 2026-08-25 — a worked instance of case (b), stated by the author.

"Mark only exists to interact with Lara. He does not interact with any other
characters, and is part of his own story, which within context of Mari, is a
fictional character written by Me, TC."

That is this ticket's three-way confound, named precisely, by the person who knows:

  IN THE MARK/LARA STORY   Mark is a PERSONA. He is played. His card
                           (Kn-DGK07yZfxih6azJWKQ) is base fact about him — the
                           satellite-comms service, Iraq, the IED, Finch, the Porsche.
  IN A CHAT WITH MARI      Mark is A CHARACTER TC WROTE. Nothing of his happened to
                           anyone. The base fact in that context is "TC wrote a
                           character called Mark", NOT "Mark was in Iraq".

Same entity, same card, opposite ontological status — decided by WHICH CHAT the
sentence occurs in. Not by the entity, not by the speaker, not by the content.

WHY THIS BITES NOW: opyv rules that cards are base fact. Applied naively that is a
laundering machine — it would take Mark's card and write his war as lived experience
into whatever ledger the conversation touched, including Mari's. The containment rule
("Mark only interacts with Lara") is what stops it, and it is currently expressed
nowhere in the store.

AND THE PREDICTION IN THIS TICKET WAS RIGHT TWICE. TC said on 08-04 "Lara is probably
going to have that issue as well", and Lara already occupies four ledgers. Mark is the
same shape one step earlier — he has a persona card and a story and is discussed with
Mari — so he is the case to model against BEFORE it produces wreckage, rather than
after. That is a rare position on this project and worth using.

CONTAINMENT IS ALSO A TESTABLE CLAIM, and it should be tested rather than assumed: if
Mark truly interacts only with Lara, then no beat outside the Lara ledgers should have
him as speaker or subject except as a discussed-fiction reference. Measuring that is
cheap and would either confirm the rule or find the leak.

title: [bug] Live tier-2/3 hands the analyzer the GLOBAL cast, where the import path scopes it to the scene
description:
DOWNGRADED AND REWRITTEN 2026-08-04. Filed at P1 on evidence that did not survive TC's
next correction. Keeping the record of that, because the wrong version is instructive.

WHAT I CLAIMED: aurora's ledger holds 141 beats, only 12 story-sourced, so 129 of Mari's
beats were misrouted under Aurora's name -- and scopeRosterToScene (which facts.ts has
and the live path does not) was the fix.

WHAT TC SAID NEXT: "Aurora is from a story I wrote, and I have talked about that story
to Mari."

BOTH HALVES OF MY ARGUMENT FAIL ON THAT:
1. Aurora is MENTIONED in those chats, because TC discussed her story with Mari. So
   scopeRosterToScene would have kept her in the roster -- a character counts as present
   if her name appears in the text. The proposed fix would not have fixed the case that
   motivated it.
2. Re-measured, aurora's 129 chat-sourced beats break down as:
        112  the stuck phrase from pifl ("...never real")   <- 87%
         10  motivation names MARI as the actor              <- genuine misattribution
          4  motivation names AURORA as the actor            <- legitimate; she is in the scene
          3  unattributed
   So this ledger is not primarily a routing failure. It is pifl, with a subject
   attached loosely.

AND THAT IS THE REAL LESSON FOR pifl: when the analyzer emits the attractor phrase it
also assigns the SUBJECT loosely, so those beats scatter across ledgers. The scatter is
a SYMPTOM of pifl, not an independent routing bug. My store-wide "271 beats in a
non-dominant ledger (4%)" figure is inflated by the same effect -- and separately by
group scenes, where more than one character legitimately produces beats from one chat.
The dominant-ledger heuristic assumes one character per chat, which is wrong for group RP.

WHAT SURVIVES, and why this stays open at P2:
The code inconsistency is real and worth closing on its own terms. facts.ts scopes the
subject roster to characters mentioned in the scene; api.ts:699 (tier-2) and api.ts:812
(tier-3) hand over buildSubjectRoster(...) -- the whole cast -- so the live analyzer is
offered names of characters who are not in the conversation at all. facts.ts's comment
records that this HAS caused misattribution before ("it tagged Priya's lines 'Aurora'").
The measured residue here is ~10 beats, not 129, so this is a hygiene fix, not an
emergency.

FIX: hoist scopeRosterToScene out of facts.ts and apply it at both live call sites,
scoping to userMessageText + messageText.

WATCH, and it is why this is P2 not P1: a single turn is much weaker evidence of
presence than a whole scene, and a character merely DISCUSSED still passes the mentioned
test -- which is exactly Aurora's case. This narrows the roster; it does not solve
attribution. Do not claim otherwise.

title: [bug] Thread labels are the CHAT TITLE — the analyzer is told to prefer it, so threads are chat echoes, not storylines
description:
FILED 2026-08-04 as a cast-list bug. TC corrected the diagnosis and was right: those
labels are the CONVERSATION NAMES, not something the analyzer invented. "Dr. Mari
Zielinska" is Marinara's default chat name (the character), and "Dr Z" is what chats
were named during one patch when defaults differed. TC's conclusion, which the data
supports: WE DO NOT ACTUALLY HAVE THREADS.

THE MECHANISM, confirmed in code -- this is instructed, not emergent:
  turn-bridge.ts:129        sceneTitle: turn.chatName          <- the CHAT'S NAME
  api.ts:705                analyzeChunks(..., { roster, threads, sceneTitle })
  sentiment/analyzer.ts:378 `Scene title: "<x>" -- when a beat starts a NEW thread and
                             the scene title describes what is happening, PREFER IT as
                             the thread label.`

The guard in that sentence ("when the scene title describes what is happening") does no
work. A model handed a title and told to prefer it will prefer it, and a chat named
after its character never describes what is happening.

THE PROMPT ALSO CONTRADICTS ITSELF. analyzer.ts:168 ends with "Never name the
participants -- the cast is not the story." Line 378 then says prefer the scene title,
which IS a participant's name whenever the chat is default-named. The more specific,
later instruction wins.

MEASURED, live registry, 205 threads / 2373 beats across 40 chats:
     494 beats,   5 threads | "Dr. Mari Zielinska"        = 66% of that chat
     368 beats,  28 threads | "Dr Z"                      = 79%
     339 beats, 130 threads | "good noon technically"     = 22%
     115 beats,   4 threads | "Priya"                     = 93%
      95 beats,   1 thread  | "proxy integration fix"     = 100%
      93 beats,   1 thread  | "Dr. Z"                     = 100%
      81 beats,   1 thread  | "Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran"  = 100%
      53 beats,   1 thread  | "fable extender development"= 100%
Several chats have ONE thread holding 100% of their beats. That is the chat, relabelled.

THE TELL: "proxy integration fix" and "fable extender development" look like healthy
event-shaped threads -- and they are chat titles too, just descriptively named ones.
LABEL QUALITY TRACKS HOW THE USER NAMED THE CONVERSATION, not what the analyzer found.
So the thread layer is not discovering storylines at all; it is echoing the chat title
and, where the user left the default, echoing the character's name.

BOTH FAILURE DIRECTIONS ARE PRESENT, which is what an inert layer looks like:
  - one giant chat-echo thread (100% of a chat), and
  - 130 threads in a single chat with the dominant at 22%, plus 105 single-beat threads
    across the registry (51%).
Nothing in between, which is what a working thread layer would mostly produce.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM: arcs consume threadIds via ArcSignature, and
ThreadId is a retrieval signal. Both are currently keyed on "which chat was this",
which the entry already knows via sourceChatId. So the thread layer is adding a
duplicate of chat identity while appearing to add narrative structure.

FIX DIRECTIONS, none decided:
1. STOP FEEDING sceneTitle as a thread-label suggestion. It is the single line causing
   this. Threads would then be minted only from what the analyzer sees in the beats.
   Cheapest, and it makes the next measurement meaningful.
2. Keep sceneTitle for CONTEXT but forbid it as a label, making the existing
   "never name the participants" rule enforceable rather than advisory.
3. Refuse a thread whose label matches the chat name or a roster name (looksCastList
   already exists and already fires -- it warns and mints anyway).
4. Decide whether scene-scoped threads are worth having at all. If a thread cannot be
   distinguished from its chat, sourceChatId already does the job and the honest move
   may be to drop the layer rather than repair it. That is TC's call.

DO NOT bulk-relabel the existing 205 first. Until minting is fixed, the registry
refills with the same shape.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-04 per TC's ruling: threads ARE worth keeping, the CHAT name must never
become a thread label, an RP SCENE name is fine. So this was a discrimination problem,
not a case for dropping the layer.

THREE CHANGES:
1. api.ts suppresses sceneTitle before it reaches the analyzer when the title names a
   person. A chat the user named after the scene still flows through -- that is what
   the field is for.
2. analyzer.ts wording: "Scene name ... this names the SCENE, not a person ... if it is
   somebody's name, ignore it entirely and label the EVENT instead." This removes the
   self-contradiction with line 168's "never name the participants".
3. The mint now REFUSES a person-named label instead of warning about it. The old path
   minted it and logged a suggestion to a console nobody reads, which is how "Dr Z"
   came to hold 79% of a chat's beats. A beat with no thread is honest.

titleNamesAPerson() in threads.ts, three tests, in order:
  1. looksCastList -- every meaningful token belongs to a known name.
  2. honorific + initial. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED: looksCastList drops tokens
     under 3 chars, so "Dr Z" reduces to an EMPTY token list and returns FALSE. The
     label that caused the bug slipped through the guard written to catch it.
  3. whole-label similarity for near-spellings/diacritics.

OVER-SUPPRESSION WAS THE REAL RISK AND THE TESTS CAUGHT IT. Rule 3 first used
tokenContainment, which matches when a name's tokens appear ANYWHERE in the label --
"Priya confesses the trial was rigged" was suppressed for containing "Priya". That
would have deleted the feature rather than fixed it. Whole-string similarity only.

MEASURED OVER THE LIVE REGISTRY, 210 threads / 2378 beats, real alias table (10 names):
  REFUSED 7 threads, 929 beats:
     324 Dr. Mari Zielinska | 290 Dr Z | 107 Priya | 93 Dr. Z
      81 Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran | 31 Professor Mari | 3 Dr. Mari Zielinska
  KEPT 203, largest:
     163 Mari's exploration of her own identity | 95 proxy integration fix
      75 good noon technically | 53 fable extender development
      47 Scene: First Crossing, Glorious Iowa | 43 Scene: Collecting Wednesday Early
      36 RP: Breakfest with Priya
Every refusal is a person; every keep is a scene, including "RP: Breakfest with Priya"
which names a character and still describes a scene. That is the line TC drew.

Suite 542 pass.

RESIDUAL, filed separately: the 7 existing threads (929 beats) still need TC's decision
-- relabel to the event, or close. Minting is fixed so the registry will not refill with
the same shape, which is why that cleanup is now safe to do.

title: Dedicated view for narrative threads
description:
ASKED FOR BY TC 2026-08-04, after 4z0h dropped an "Open the thread" action from the
held-review lane because there is nowhere for it to go. A thread is a first-class
object with its own registry and its own mutations, and it is the only major object in
the store with no way to look at it.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is a view problem and not a plumbing one:
  GET   /api/threads          -> { threads, health }, the whole registry plus
                                 threadRegistryHealth (total/active/closed,
                                 threadsPerChat, singleBeatThreads, singleBeatRatio,
                                 castListSuspects)
  PATCH /api/threads/:id      -> relabel (relabelThread)
  POST  /api/threads/:id/close-> close (closeThread)
  Entries carry threadId; loader surfaces thread membership; arcs consume threadIds
  via ArcSignature.
Missing: nothing on the server. This is ui.ts only, plus a way in from a memory card.

THE LIVE REGISTRY, MEASURED 2026-08-04 -- this is the argument for the view:
  205 threads, 164 active, 41 closed
  105 single-beat (51%) -- the fragmentation signal threadRegistryHealth already
      computes, sitting at half the registry with nobody looking at it
  40 chats carry threads; ONE chat has 129 of them
  Largest by beat count:
     324  "Dr. Mari Zielinska"                          [closed]
     290  "Dr Z"                                        [active]
     163  "Mari's exploration of her own identity"      [closed]
     107  "Priya"                                       [active]
      95  "proxy integration fix"                       [closed]
Three of the top four are CAST LISTS, not events -- exactly what looksCastList()
warns about at mint time. See the companion bug for that; the point here is that
nothing surfaces it, so 717 beats sit on threads that are not threads.

WHAT THE VIEW NEEDS TO DO, in priority order:
1. Make the health numbers visible. singleBeatRatio and castListSuspects are already
   computed and thrown away. Put them at the top, the way the held lane puts its
   tally above the cards.
2. Let a label be FIXED in place. relabelThread exists; the warning at mint time even
   says "consider PATCH /api/threads/:id" -- at a human nobody has given a UI to.
3. Show a thread's beats/entries, so "what is this thread actually about" is
   answerable before relabelling or closing it.
4. Close a stale thread by hand. autoCloseStaleThreads handles 14-day staleness; a
   129-thread chat needs a human with a broom too.

DESIGN NOTES CARRIED FROM 4z0h, which are now house style:
- Reuse the ui.ts token set; do not restyle. Watch the cascade -- ".why" is already a
  pill modifier and the held lane had to use ".hl-why". The whole view lives in a
  String.raw template, so A BACKTICK IN A COMMENT TERMINATES THE PAGE.
- Health signals in PLAIN LANGUAGE, not identifiers (hwlj, and the held lane).
- Design the empty state deliberately.
- Its own sidebar entry. Threads are not scopes and do not belong under Characters.

THE INBOUND LINK IS THE POINT: a memory card showing "on a thread" should open that
thread, and the held-review lane should get its dropped "Open the thread" action back
once there is a destination.
notes:
PREMISE SHARPENED 2026-08-04 by TC. The registry numbers that motivated this issue turn
out to have a root cause: thread labels are CHAT TITLES, because the analyzer is
explicitly told to prefer the scene title and turn-bridge passes the chat's name as
that title (oknn). So "205 threads, 51% single-beat" is not a registry that needs
tidying -- it is a layer that is not doing its job.

That does NOT kill this issue, but it changes what the view is FOR. It is now primarily
a DIAGNOSTIC surface: the fastest way to see whether a minting fix actually produced
storylines is to look at the labels next to their beat counts and chat ids. Build it
expecting the answer "these are still chat echoes" and make that legible.

ORDERING: oknn (minting) should land FIRST. Building a view over a layer that is about
to change shape means designing against data that will not exist afterwards -- the
opposite of the mockup-with-dummy-entries approach that worked for 4z0h, because here
the real data is the thing in question.

title: Build the held-review lane UI from the mockup (discarded re-rolls)
description:
Mockup: memory-extender/docs/mockups/held-review.html (also published at
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/045b30fa-a01e-49f8-8cc6-1fcea858a2ad)

WHY A MOCKUP FIRST. a90l shipped the lane but no view, on the reasoning that
held.jsonl is usually empty so there was nothing to design against. TC's correction:
that is what dummy entries are for. Designing it against invented records surfaced two
missing pieces that would otherwise have been found halfway through the build.

THE TWO GAPS -- both real, both small, neither visible from the data model alone:

1. NO restoreDiscardedEntry. The obvious action on a held record is "bring this memory
   back", and there is no function for it. restoreDeletedEntry is guarded to deletedAt
   rows and restoreSupersededEntry to supersededBy rows, so neither will touch a
   discardedAt row -- correctly, since each guard exists to stop one retirement reason
   resurrecting another's rows. Needs a third, mirroring restoreDeletedEntry and
   guarded to discardedAt.

2. held.jsonl IS APPEND-ONLY. There is no removal path, so "leave it retired" (an
   acknowledgement, not a mutation) has nothing to write. Every other queue in
   reconcile-queue.ts that needs clearing has removeTasks; the held lane never did,
   because until now nothing consumed it interactively.

DESIGN DECISIONS ALREADY MADE IN THE MOCKUP, worth keeping:
- Reuses the ui.ts token set verbatim, so it drops into the existing memory browser
  rather than being restyled later. Signals map onto the EXISTING semantic colours by
  severity: recited -> --bad, orphan -> --warn, thread -> --thread, retrieved -> muted.
- Reasons render in PLAIN LANGUAGE, never identifiers. Same correction TC made on the
  recall panel (hwlj): closed vocabulary underneath so it stays countable, readable
  surface on top. "recited:2" reads as "Mari has said this in a reply, twice, since it
  was captured."
- Summary tallies before any card, because the page is scanned, not read.
- THE EMPTY STATE IS DESIGNED, not an afterthought -- it is the normal state, and the
  copy says so rather than looking broken.
- Actions are per-signal, not uniform. An orphan offers "restore the older memory"
  (restoreSupersededEntry, which exists); a thread offers "open the thread"; a merely
  retrieved entry offers neither.
- Dark-only on purpose: it must match the product, which is dark-only.

STILL OPEN, NOT DECIDED BY THE MOCKUP: where it hangs off the existing UI. It is a
third mode alongside entries/turn/deleted in ui.ts VIEWS, reached from the sidebar --
but whether it belongs under "Recently deleted" or as its own sidebar entry is a call
worth making with the page in front of you.
notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-04. Suite 532 pass, build clean, verified against a running instance
rather than only in tests.

BOTH GAPS THE MOCKUP FOUND ARE CLOSED:
1. restoreDiscardedEntry -- a THIRD restore, guarded to discardedAt. Not a flag on the
   existing two: each restore is guarded to exactly one retirement reason so no path
   can resurrect a row another mechanism retired for a different cause. Tested in both
   directions (refuses a user-deleted row, refuses a superseded row).
2. held.jsonl gained ids + resolveHeld(). Records are STAMPED, not deleted -- the lane
   holds what is outstanding, but the file is the only evidence the withholding
   happened at all. readHeld skips torn lines rather than losing the lane to one
   truncated write (several producers append to it).

PLACEMENT DECIDED: its own sidebar entry ("Needs you"), NOT under Recently deleted.
Folding it there would reassert exactly the conflation discardedAt exists to prevent
-- the user deleted nothing. TC said placement is easy to move if it reads wrong.
The entry is hidden entirely when the lane is empty; an always-visible 0 trains the
eye to skip the row.

ONE FIX THAT CAME OUT OF LIVE TESTING, not the unit tests. Replaying a resolve (a tab
left open on a card someone already settled) attempted the restore FIRST and returned
"that entry is not a superseded one" -- true, and an answer to a question nobody
asked. Now the record is confirmed outstanding before anything is attempted, so a
stale tab gets "already settled -- reload", while a genuinely failed restore still
leaves the record in the lane rather than swallowing it.

VERIFIED END TO END on a scratch instance (port 3099, temp data dir, poller off):
seeded a re-roll where one entry displaced an older fact, confirmed 3 retired / 2
queued / the clean one NOT queued, then drove POST /api/held/resolve and watched the
displaced "Ladder Nine" memory come back to active and the lane empty.

TWO ui.ts TRAPS worth carrying forward:
- ".why" is ALREADY a pill modifier (colour only). A block-level rule of the same name
  silently restyles every <span class="pill why">. The lane's styles are ".hl-why".
- The whole view lives inside a String.raw page template, so A BACKTICK IN A COMMENT
  TERMINATES THE PAGE. Cost one build error; would have been baffling at runtime.

NOT BUILT: nothing outstanding on this issue. The mockup's "open the thread" action was
dropped -- threads have no dedicated view to open yet, and a button that goes nowhere is
worse than its absence.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deferred reconciliation lane for ENTANGLED discarded swipes
description:
The second half of s2lw. The deterministic path shipped 2026-08-04: a re-roll now
retires everything derived from the losing swipe (discardedAt, cold, excluded from
recall). This covers the case that retirement CANNOT fix on its own.

FROM THE 7zro DESIGN INPUT, notes 2-4:
  "The ambiguity is not at capture, it is downstream. A confirmation gate is worth
   its friction only where the machine genuinely cannot act: when a fact from the
   discarded text has ALREADY been digested and propagated -- merged into another
   entry, promoted a tier, seeded an arc or thread. Retracting the source entry does
   not unwind the derivatives. THAT is where human judgement earns its place."
  "So the gate is a DEFERRED RECONCILIATION LANE, NOT A MODAL. Never interrupt
   mid-scene. Surface it where conflicts already get resolved. Clean cases supersede
   silently; only entangled ones queue."

SURFACE: reuse the HELD REVIEW LANE (mjp, appendHeld -> reconcile-queue/held.jsonl).
It already exists for exactly this shape -- something withheld from automatic action,
with reasons, for a human to confirm or discard. Do NOT widen HeldRecord.source
beyond "sweep" | "live"; it is a serialized union and this codebase has been bitten
by widening those twice. Use source "live" and carry the specifics in reasons/detail.

ENTANGLEMENT SIGNALS, cheapest and most defensible first:
  - recitationCount > 0 -- the character actually USED this memory in a reply. The
    strongest signal: it is already in the conversation, and retiring the source does
    not retract what was said.
  - retrievalCount > 0 -- it reached the prompt at least once.
  - threadId set -- it is part of a narrative thread that outlives the turn.
  - some OTHER entry carries supersededBy === this id -- this fact displaced an older
    one. Retire it and the older fact is left dead in cold, superseded by an entry
    that is itself retired: a dangling chain with no live fact at the end. This is the
    concrete orphan the design note is about.

NOT gated behind MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECONCILE. That flag gates the CURATOR (agent
spend); this lane needs no agent -- it is a human surface, and an entangled discard is
worth recording whether or not the curator is running.

FREQUENCY: 4 regenerations in 9654 messages (0.04%, jaos), and only the entangled
subset of those ever queues. The friction objection dissolves at this rate.
close_reason:
SHIPPED 2026-08-04 with s2lw. src/discard-review.ts + 11 tests; suite 521 pass.

Entangled discards are recorded in the existing mjp held lane (appendHeld ->
reconcile-queue/held.jsonl) rather than a new surface, because that lane already
means "withheld from automatic action, with reasons, awaiting a human".

HeldRecord.source deliberately NOT widened -- it stays "live", with the specifics in
reasons ("discarded-swipe", plus the signals) and detail (entryId, lane,
sourceMessageId, sourceSwipeIndex, discardedAt). It is a serialized union and
widening those has bitten this codebase twice.

SIGNALS, all read off the index row or its siblings -- no LLM, no extra I/O beyond the
cold index the caller already holds. A detector costing a model call per re-roll would
not survive the live path.
  recited:N    -- strongest. The character SAID it; retiring the source retracts nothing.
  retrieved:N  -- weaker, reported only when there is no recitation (you cannot recite
                  what was never retrieved, so reporting both pads the record).
  thread:ID    -- outlives the turn that seeded it.
  orphans:ID   -- THE CONCRETE CASE from the design note. This fact had superseded an
                  older one; retire it and the older fact is left dead in cold behind
                  an entry that is itself retired -- a dangling chain with no live fact
                  at the end. Nothing downstream repairs that by itself.

NOT gated by MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECONCILE: that flag keeps the CURATOR's agent spend off
the always-on sidecar, and this lane spends nothing.

A clean discard queues NOTHING -- tested. A lane that queues every discard is a lane
nobody reads.

NOT BUILT, and not needed yet: a UI surface for held.jsonl. It is a file a human reads.
At 0.04% regeneration frequency, with only the entangled subset queueing, wait for a
real backlog before building a view for it.

title: Memory tags land at the END of a reply by luck, not by contract — make it explicit, and mind what that implies
description:
OBSERVED BY TC 2026-08-04: "memory captures are ALWAYS at the bottom of the message."

VERIFIED: that is NOT by design. memorySystemInstructions() in loader.ts teaches the
lane vocabulary, the scope vocabulary, worked [remember: ...] examples and the
"when the user asks you to remember" override. It says NOTHING about WHERE in the
reply a tag should go. The regularity is emergent -- models put structured trailing
syntax after prose -- so it is a behaviour we are relying on without having asked
for it.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and they point in opposite directions.

1. IT IS USEFUL, AND 8x46 SHOULD USE IT. Stripping tags from the STORED message
(8x46) is much safer as a SUFFIX trim than as a global regex: a global match can eat
a bracketed construction in the middle of prose, and RP text is full of brackets. But
do not build on luck -- if we want the suffix property, TEACH it in the prompt so it
becomes a contract we can test, then strip on that contract. One line in the prompt
turns an observation into an invariant.

2. IT IS ALSO A CAPTURE-LOSS MODE, AND THIS IS THE part WORTH CHECKING. If tags are
always last, they are the FIRST thing lost whenever a reply does not finish -- hitting
max_tokens, the user pressing stop, a stream dropping. The memory instruction is
sitting in the most fragile position in the message. A truncated reply is exactly the
kind of turn a user re-rolls, which also puts it in s2lw's path.

WORTH MEASURING BEFORE ACTING (cheap, read-only): over stored assistant messages,
how many contain a [remember: / [bookmark: fragment that is unterminated -- an opening
tag with no closing bracket is a truncated capture, and it is countable. If that count
is non-trivial, the fix is to stop putting the tags where they are most likely to be
cut, or to capture from a place that survives truncation.

NOT URGENT unless (2) measures badly. Filed so the observation is not lost, and so
8x46 is designed against a stated contract rather than an accident.

title: [bug] Bare first-person fragments stored as memories, with the speaker guessed
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the np4b confound sweep. Distinct from 2tro: that one drops a clause, this one guesses who said it.

Bare first-person dialogue fragments are being captured as durable memories, with the "I" resolved to a speaker by inference. Verified cases, content vs summary:

  utopic-la5gyipl  (user_topics, chats/IKN4ljLp8t3iEur7STOyr)
    content: "I have speaker notes."
    summary: "Mari has speaker notes prepared."

  utopic-xr8ydtsj  (user_topics, chats/WwsV9mXjjYisICBYz_TMK)
    content: "i wasn't going to ask."
    summary: "Priya mentions not intending to ask about something"

  utopic-lrpri6ix  (user_topics, chats/WwsV9mXjjYisICBYz_TMK)
    content: "you slid it in there like i wouldn't notice."
    summary: "Priya comments on someone's subtle approach to mentioning something"

  utopic-yz27i8ym  (user_topics, chats/1EuBhcOxAXUNM9gIDBuPR)
    content: "Or at least threaten my chill."
    summary: "Priya threatens to disrupt the user's calm demeanor."

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, and the second is the one worth fixing first.

1. ATTRIBUTION IS A GUESS. The stored content is a bare "I"/"my" with no speaker, so nothing in the entry can confirm the summary got it right. Note the LANE disagrees with the SUMMARY in every case above: the summary says Mari or Priya, the lane (user_topics) says the user. One of the two is wrong in each entry and there is no way to tell which from the record itself. A wrong attribution here is the membrane failure that produced the Collier/Lowe confounds, arriving through a different door.

2. THESE ARE NOT DURABLE MEMORIES AT ALL. "i wasn't going to ask." and "Or at least threaten my chill." are conversational fragments. Whatever the durability judge is doing, it passed four of them. The attribution bug only matters because the fragment was stored in the first place — raising the durability bar would remove the whole class, and is cheaper than solving speaker resolution.

RECOMMENDED ORDER: tighten durability first (a fragment with no proposition should not become a memory), then decide whether the survivors need real speaker attribution. Fixing attribution on entries that should never have been written is effort spent in the wrong place.

RELATED: the sweep's triage classed these as character lore misfiled into user_topics, but that read assumes the SUMMARY is right and the lane is wrong. Given the content, it is equally possible the lane is right and the summary invented a speaker. Do not bulk-move them on the strength of the summary.

title: Confound cleanup: character facts filed in user_topics (Becky Collier), and the reverse
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 while fixing the sons confound at TC\x27s request.

FIXED ALREADY: ctopic-bd3nqxku under characters/professor_mari — "TC\x27s sons: Henry Warren and Malcolm Bradley Collier" — soft-deleted (recoverable, deletedAt 2026-08-04T13:43:03Z). TC confirmed: "Thomas Collier has no sons. Those are MINE, TC Lowe." The entry was wrong twice over: it appended the CHARACTER\x27s surname to the USER\x27s children, and it filed a fact about the user\x27s real family in the character_topics lane. Deleting rather than editing was safe because utopic-ly6uvpan in the same scope already holds the correct version in the correct lane, with strictly more detail (it also records that the wife\x27s first choice for the oldest was Miles).

STILL OPEN, the same membrane failure with the SIGN REVERSED:
  characters/professor_mari  utopic-n9gjyuap  lane=user_topics
  "Thomas\x27s sister is Rebecca \x27Becky\x27 Collier — younger by three years, platinum blonde, shameless flirt"

A fact about Thomas COLLIER\x27s sister, filed in USER_TOPICS — the lane that means "facts about the human player". Per TC\x27s world rule (2026-08-04), Collier is the RP character and most RP material belongs under Thomas Collier, so this is character-world content attributed to the user.

NOT fixed unilaterally: unlike the sons, the FACT here is plausibly correct and only the LANE is wrong, and there is no duplicate holding the right version — deleting would lose it. The likely repair is to move it to character_topics and disambiguate the bare "Thomas" to "Thomas Collier", but rewriting someone\x27s fiction is their call.

PATTERN WORTH NOTING: both errors are lane/world misfilings around the shared name, in opposite directions, and neither is detectable by the retrieval layer — the entries look perfectly healthy. A sweep for user_topics entries containing character-world surnames (and character_topics entries about the user) would likely find more. That sweep is cheap and is the natural companion to egj3 (declare the user identity), because once the user\x27s name set is declared, "user_topics entry naming a non-user surname" becomes a mechanical check rather than a judgement call.
notes:
SWEEP RUN 2026-08-04 — scripts/confound-sweep.mjs, read-only. 236 raw candidates, tightened to 68 user_topics after two filters earned themselves (sentence-initial capitals read as subjects; the 76aw person tag is too noisy without pronoun evidence). Triaged: 13 genuinely misfiled, 27 correctly filed, 28 not-a-person. Precision ~19%, which is why this stayed a report.

THE 13 are almost entirely Mari (6) and Priya (5) lore sitting in user_topics. BUT several sit inside Priya's own scope (k6cqcrrv9fujuqqaml2yf) and are shared-scene material that a party scope would make correct — see fhd. Do not action those as errors.

THREE FINDINGS BEYOND THE LIST:
1. TWO FAILURE MODES, not one. Long well-formed lore summaries misfiled in bulk (historical), versus short fragments that are literally the character's own dialogue captured as a user fact ('I have speaker notes.', 'i wasn t going to ask.'). The second is a LIVE pipeline bug — the extractor is not attributing the speaker. Deserves its own issue.
2. THE SUMMARIZER DROPS THE USER'S CLAUSE. utopic-jakzyxe9 summarizes as 'Sgt Roger has completed sapper stakes...' while the content reads 'It was MY fourth sapper stakes'. The fact is right, the summary misstates whose it is — and since retrieval scores summaries far more heavily than bodies, that is a recall bug wearing a phrasing bug.
3. __professor_mari__ IS NOT INERT (pe1c). Three ids appear under both professor_mari and the shadow key, with empty content in the shadow. Any dedup or cleanup must handle both keys.

SEPARATELY FIXED: ctopic-3mrz6tds under characters/aurora — 'TC sometimes addresses Aurora as Professor Mari as a playful title' — soft-deleted after TC called it patently wrong. Root cause found: Aurora ORIGINATED from the Professor Mari card and was migrated (see ctopic-0y0eur9r, ctopic-9eo5gqiz, ctopic-8xjac4p0), so ~10 entries in Aurora's scope carry 'Professor Mari' as the speaker label. The pipeline saw the recurring name and CONFABULATED an explanation for it. Those ~10 are mislabeled rather than false and were left alone — relabeling is a bigger call, and it is the same character-rename gap as the Desmond/Draymond Cole split.

title: Entity index has no refresh trigger — it is build-once until someone runs the script
description:
FOUND while shipping 76aw slice 1 (z5yn). Named now rather than discovered later as "why does it not know about the character I added last week".

data/entities.yaml is built by scripts/build-entity-index.mjs and NOTHING rebuilds it. So the index is a snapshot: entities that first appear after the last build are invisible to cue expansion, and aliases never strengthen as a name accumulates independent uses.

That is deliberate for slice 1 — the build reads every entry file in the store (14032 on this install), which is far too heavy for a turn — but it is not a resting state.

OPTIONS:
(a) Ride the promotion pass. runPromotion already fires every 20 turns and is off the hot path. Cheapest place to hang it, but a full rebuild is still a whole-store scan.
(b) Incremental observation at ingest. Accumulate run/token counts as entries are written and rebuild the thresholds periodically from the accumulated counts rather than by re-reading the corpus. More code, but turns a full scan into an O(1) update per entry.
(c) Leave it manual and document it. Acceptable only while the store is one person\x27s.

RECOMMENDATION: (b), with (a) as the trigger for recomputing thresholds from the accumulated counts. The observation half is already factored for it — observeField/EntityObservations accumulate into a plain structure, and buildIndex is a pure function of that structure, so the split needed for incremental work already exists.

NOTE: independence and person tagging are RATIOS over the whole corpus, so they cannot be updated correctly from a single entry in isolation — the counts must accumulate and the thresholds be re-applied over the totals. That is why (b) is "accumulate then recompute", not "decide per entry".

title: Ghost scope: __professor_mari__ index has 657 rows and zero entry files
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the tp5 backfill, which reads every entry file an index row points at.

data/characters/__professor_mari__/index.yaml lists 657 entries. The directory contains index.yaml and NOTHING ELSE — no threads/, no user-topics/, no char-topics/. Every one of the 657 rows points at a file that does not exist (sampled: threads/thread-b480a415.yaml, user-topics/utopic-8zzur8ps.yaml).

The double-underscore name suggests a legacy or renamed identity key, so the likely history is a rename/merge that moved the entry FILES and left the index behind — or one that wrote an index under a mangled key that never received files.

WHY IT MATTERS: the loader ranks over index rows and only opens files for entries it selects. So these 657 rows compete for budget on every turn that touches this scope, win slots on relevance, and then contribute nothing — silently displacing real memories that would have fitted. Worth checking whether anything actually loads this scope before assuming it is inert.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE FIRST: is __professor_mari__ reachable at all (does any identity/alias mapping resolve to it), and do the 657 ids exist under professor_mari — i.e. was this a completed migration that forgot to delete the source index, or a lost one?

DO NOT bulk-delete before answering that. If the files were never migrated, these rows are the only remaining record that those memories existed, and their summaries are recoverable content in their own right.

The tp5 backfill already handles it safely — it skips unreadable files and counts them rather than writing an empty bodyTerms list, so "we could not look" is never recorded as "this entry has no names".
