title: [bug] Duplicate Extender lorebooks created when starting a new chat for a character
description:
SYMPTOM: Creating a new chat for a character resulted in two (duplicate) 'Marinara Extender — <name>' lorebooks for that character. Reported as non-critical (memory still functions, but clutters the lorebook list and may split/confuse writes).

REPRO (to confirm): create a new chat for an existing character that already has an Extender lorebook; observe whether a second 'Marinara Extender — <name>' lorebook appears.

HYPOTHESIS (UNCONFIRMED — needs repro with devtools/network tab): race in ensureLorebook() with no mutex. ensureLorebook (marinara-extender.js ~L4057) matches existing lorebooks by characterId, so duplicates should not happen by design. But on a brand-new chat the lorebookIdCache (marinara-extender.js ~L3703, characterId -> lorebookId) is empty. If two events fire near-simultaneously (e.g. pre-turn injection + first memory write), both call ensureLorebook, both do a fresh GET /lorebooks, both find nothing, and both POST /lorebooks -> two lorebooks. The cache is only populated AFTER ensureLorebook returns (L3760-3763), and _lorebookWriteChain serializes WRITES but not ensureLorebook LOOKUPS.

POSSIBLE FIX DIRECTION: serialize/dedupe ensureLorebook per characterId (in-flight promise map), or re-check for an existing lorebook immediately before POST.

RELATED: MarinaraExtender-s19 (lorebookIdCache staleness on manual delete) — same cache/lookup surface, different trigger.

NEXT STEP: reproduce live, watch the network tab for two concurrent POST /lorebooks, confirm the race before patching.

title: [feature] macOS/Linux launcher (start.sh) — bring the Windows onboarding niceties cross-platform
description: User-surfaced on Discord 2026-06-20: the GH install reads Windows-first; Mac/Linux users currently start the sidecar manually via npm (now signposted in the README install section). The sidecar + extension are fully cross-platform (Node + browser JS); only the LAUNCHER is Windows-only (Marinara_Extender_Start.bat / start.ps1). WHAT: a start.sh that mirrors the start.ps1 conveniences on macOS/Linux — Node preflight, first-run npm install + build, Ollama detect/start + chat/embed model pull (with the same BYO-backend tolerance: skip Ollama when MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL is non-Ollama), sidecar start with port guard + crash watchdog + log tee, the extension-install bridge (open /setup first run), and first-run-only onboarding. Mirror start.ps1's behavior/UX (see szf Phases 1-3). P3: works fine manually today; this is the convenience parity, demand-driven (bump if Mac/Linux uptake is high). Relates to szf (closed install epic).

title: [feature] Recap layer — deferred Stage-3 polish (gaps render, activation perf index, regeneration, budget)
description:
Deferred from cz3 (recap layer; Stages 1-3 shipped). These were intentionally NOT built — premature against current data/scale. Each has a clear trigger for when it becomes worth doing; do not build speculatively before then.

1) DORMANCY-GAP RENDERING — render an arc's quiet period in the recap ('went silent ~3 weeks in-world, reopened when...'); the re-render pass must RECEIVE the gap as input (cz3 design note C). TRIGGER: arc promotion actually populates Arc.gaps — currently 0 arcs carry gaps, so there is nothing to render. Needs the promotion side to compute/store gaps first.

2) REVERSE-ACTIVATION-INDEX (cz3 H4 perf) — replace the loader's per-turn cosine-over-ALL-recaps with a reverse index (entity/thread/centroid fingerprint -> candidate arcs) for a cheap 'does this wake anything?' check. TRIGGER: per-character recap count grows large enough that cosine-all in the hot path costs (currently ~37 for professor_mari — trivial). Revisit at hundreds+.

3) RECAP REGENERATION PATH — regenerate a bad/stale recap from its underlying beats (beats are kept full-fidelity underneath precisely for this). TRIGGER: a bad recap observed in practice, or a watermark re-render needed.

4) RECAP BUDGET TUNING — explicit token budget for the recap section. Today recaps ride the character budget and footnotes add tokens on top (loader). TRIGGER: recap+footnote tokens observably crowd the character budget in real transcripts.

Parent: cz3 (closed). Activation (Stage 2) tunable via MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECAP_TAU.

title: Embedding-based similarity for the curator (clustering + ledger-view ranking)
description: Both the sweep's clustering (0kk, clusterFacts) and the live curator's ledger view (5f2, selectLedgerView) use lexical jaccard. Concrete live miss: professor_mari's two Warlock entries (ctopic-auq9mre9 + ctopic-bbupy8fl) are SEMANTICALLY identical but LEXICALLY divergent, so they don't cluster at 0.5 and the sweep won't catch them — exactly the case TC flagged. Upgrade: use embedding cosine (fetchEmbeddings/cosineSim already exist, used by consensusFilter) for clustering + ranking, with the embed model pulled. Cache per-entry embeddings (4685 entries — embed once, reuse) so it's not a per-run cost. Gated/opt-in (embed model may be absent -> fall back to lexical, which already works for lexical dups like the 'sold solution/fix' cluster). This is the recall upgrade; lexical is the cheap floor. Relates to 0kk, 5f2, egp.
close_reason: Embedding-based semantic clustering built + verified. The stated motivator (Warlock pair) was DISPROVED by measurement — the 6 fact-scoped warlock entries don't cluster even at cosine 0.80 (they're distinct facets; my original 'two warlock dups' was a false alarm, never verified same-fact). But the full-ledger measurement found the REAL justification: embedding catches 10 (@0.90) to 28 (@0.87) real semantic-dup clusters that lexical jaccard completely misses — watersports/piss-kink restatements x6, 'full name Thomas Charles Lowe' x3, 'veteran in a 26yo body' x2, 'berserker mode during anal' x2, etc. (same fact, different words). Built clusterFactsEmbedding (embed once -> normalized cosine union-find; embed injectable; returns null -> caller falls back to lexical). Wired buildSweepLedger to prefer embedding (auto mode, SWEEP_EMBED_THRESHOLD 0.87 = measured sweet spot; curator stays the precision gate for borderline) with lexical fallback + --lexical override. Live: script reports 'clustering: embedding'. 5 offline tests (clusterFactsEmbedding + buildSweepLedger mode/fallback); 211 total pass. NOTE: this upgrades the SWEEP clustering. selectLedgerView (5f2 live-curator view ranking) still uses lexical — embedding ranking there is deferred as low-value since the live curator already pins the structurally-flagged collision, so view-ranking barely matters; revisit only if a live miss surfaces.

title: Confidence-gated apply + audit-log maturation (b4n apply phase)
description: Build on the confidence field now in the curator verdict + audit line. (1) APPLY GATE: when --apply is trusted, auto-apply only HIGH-confidence verdicts; route medium/low to a review lane (a separate file to eyeball) instead of mutating memory. The curator does the obvious 80%; the human only adjudicates the genuinely ambiguous. (2) AUDIT MATURATION: date-partition/rotate audit.jsonl so grep stays fast; a --summary reader that tallies verdicts/confidence ('this week: 12 EXPAND, 3 UPDATE, 1 NEGATE, 4 low-conf flagged'). (3) CALIBRATION LOOP: treat human overrides of curator verdicts as a signal — high-confidence-but-overridden = overconfidence to fix in the prompt; low-confidence clusters = the hard cases worth a prompt/consensus pass. The log becomes the dataset that tells us where to improve. Relates to b4n, 3pl (FR4 rollback/audit UI).
notes: First real apply-phase calibration data (embedding sweep on Mari, 14 merges): 11 high + 3 medium + 0 low. All 11 high = clean semantic dedup (auto-apply-safe signal). The 3 medium: M1 (watersports x4, varied framing — correct merge), M9 (Mari+Priya both-vague — harmless), M13 (PTSD specific-vs-vague — DROPPED by human review). DESIGN: mjp's gate must be TWO-STAGE — (1) domain-sensitive flags (trauma first) -> ALWAYS human, never auto-apply regardless of numeric confidence (see bd memory + the M13 rationale); (2) numeric high/low threshold for everything else. Data so far: high=clean across 11+19=30 reviewed merges; medium=mixed (2 correct, 1 correctly-dropped). No low-confidence merges emitted on clear-enough-to-propose clusters — the curator self-selects out before proposing. Tune high-auto-apply / low-route thresholds against accumulating apply-phase audit (data/reconcile-queue/sweep-audit.jsonl + audit.jsonl).
close_reason: Two-stage confidence+domain apply gate, built + tested + verified. STAGE 1 (apply-gate.ts domainFlags): domain-sensitive verdicts (tight trauma lexicon — ptsd/trauma/abuse/assault/rape/suicide/self-harm/flashback/grief, deliberately NOT war/combat/veteran/death to avoid flooding) ALWAYS hold regardless of confidence — the M13 rule, systematized. STAGE 2 (applyGate): high auto-applies, medium/low/unknown hold. Wired into BOTH apply paths gated-by-default: applySweepLedger + drainReconcileQueue (the live path has no human review, so gating-by-default is the safe posture); --ungated overrides (trust prior review). Held items -> held.jsonl review lane with reasons (never dropped). AUDIT MATURATION: scripts/reconcile-audit.mjs tallies live/sweep/held by mode/verdict/confidence ('answer your own question in 30s'). Verified: 222 tests (7 pure gate + sweep gated-hold + 3 drain gated/ungated); live summary on real logs shows the apply-phase distribution (sweep high=71 medium=20 low=2, 32 applied). Had the gate existed for the embedding sweep it would have auto-held M13 (trauma) + the 2 mediums and auto-applied the 11 high — exactly the wished-for behavior. DEFERRED (low value): audit log rotation/date-partitioning; full calibration-loop automation (the data IS captured — summary reader + held lane + audit are the inputs; human overrides are the signal).

title: FR3-live: gate the reconciliation curator into the turn path
description: Live integration of the offline curator (MarinaraExtender-5ny) into the running sidecar. Distinct shape from the offline path, hence its own scope: (1) COST GATING — run the curator only on FR1-flagged same-subject collisions (the structural detector), never on every save or a blind sweep; the create-correction path in dedup.ts is the partial FR1 seed to build the trigger on. (2) LATENCY BUDGET — the curator is an agentic loop (multiple model round-trips); it cannot block a live turn synchronously. Needs an async/deferred lane (post-turn queue or background pass) so the player never waits on it. (3) LIVE DATA, not a ledger — no dry-run/reconcile-ledger preview gate; decisions apply directly, so it needs its own audit trail (pairs with FR4/3pl) and a kill switch. (4) AUTH POSTURE — still CLI-session Agent SDK; decide whether the live sidecar may assume a logged-in CLI session, or whether live mode requires an explicit key. Reuses runCurator/applyDecision from reconcile.ts unchanged; this ticket is the trigger + scheduling + safety envelope around them.
notes: Refinements surfaced by the first live curator runs (5ny verification on Mari scenes): (1) CANDIDATE-vs-CANDIDATE pre-dedup — the curator reconciles each candidate against STORED memory only, not against sibling candidates in the same batch; two near-dup candidates from one scene each got a write-verdict (and force-create bypasses the Jaccard gate), so both would be written. Collapse candidates among themselves (consensus/dedup) BEFORE the curator, or make it batch-aware. (2) UPSTREAM durability gate, NOT curator tuning — on Hargrove the judge leaked ~14/19 candidates incl. restatements and a CONTRADICTORY scenario-frame identity; a conservative curator EXPANDs that noise rather than collapsing it -> slow ledger bloat. Fix upstream: strengthen the durability judge or add an 'is this worth storing at all' pre-check before reconciliation. DESIGN RULE (TC): do NOT make the curator more aggressive to compensate. EXPAND-conservative default is CORRECT — overwriting real canon is catastrophic+irreversible; bloat is reversible. Tuning the curator down while the upstream gate is leaky MASKS the upstream problem. Keep curator conservative; fix input quality.
close_reason: Live shadow integration shipped + verified end-to-end (commit 0fc7eb4). FR1 trigger (decide()->skip on fact lanes) enqueues collisions during play, gated by MARINARA_EXTENDER_RECONCILE (default off = unchanged); persistent queue + JSONL audit; drainReconcileQueue runs the curator OUT-OF-BAND (no Agent SDK / spend / latency in the sidecar), SHADOW by default with --apply wired. Verdict now carries confidence; audit is one structured decision per line (taskId, againstId, verdict, confidence, rationale, ts). Proven live: enqueue -> shadow drain -> real curator -> audit line with confidence:high + correct EXPAND. All four ticket concerns met (cost-gating, latency, live-data+audit+killswitch, CLI-session auth). Two follow-ups filed: bound search_entries for mature ledgers (needed before running on Mari's real ledger), and confidence-gated apply + audit maturation (the apply phase).

title: Extension (marinara-extender.js) has zero automated tests - extract pure logic
description: Audit finding #5 (structural gap, not a bug). The extension is the highest-churn, least-covered surface: pre-turn refresh, scene-recap content-pairing, CSRF/memFetch retry, version stamping, import filtering - all browser JS with no unit tests, so regressions only surface live (which is exactly how the recap-mispairing and pre-turn-skip bugs reached the user). Plan: extract the pure, side-effect-free logic into testable functions and cover them with vitest. Best first target - the scene-recap content-overlap pairing (greedy best-first assignment): pull it out of syncSceneRecaps into a pure function (scenes, returns) -> Map, and test the pairing decisions directly (correct match, sub-threshold no-match, multi-scene contention, timestamp fallback). memFetch's 403-retry and the budget-vs-lorebook-ceiling math are also good unit candidates. Pairs naturally with the 1dn/38x work since those touch the same code.

title: lorebookIdCache can go stale if the ME lorebook is manually deleted
description: Audit finding #3 (low severity). marinara-extender.js preTurnRefresh caches characterId -> lorebookId in lorebookIdCache (added for speed). Normal operation only nukes/recreates ENTRIES, keeping the lorebook container, so the cached id stays valid. But if a user deletes the entire 'Marinara Extender - <char>' lorebook in the engine UI, the cached id points at a dead lorebook and writeMemoryToLorebook writes into nothing until the tab reloads (which clears the in-memory cache) - memory silently stops injecting. Fix: invalidate lorebookIdCache[characterId] on a write/lookup failure (404 from the entries endpoint) and re-run ensureLorebook, which already does a fresh uncached lookup. Note the original ensureLorebook comment explicitly says 'no caching so deletions are handled correctly' - the pre-turn cache was layered on top, creating this inconsistency.

title: Engine drops over-budget lorebook entries silently - consider upstream report
description: The engine's per-lorebook tokenBudget (default 2048) silently drops constant entries that exceed it - no console warning, no UI hint. Cost us a 5-hour bug hunt: memory blocks grew past the budget and recall died invisibly while every link upstream was green. We guard our own lorebooks now (16384 + heal on lookup, 103d571), but any extension writing large constant entries will hit this. Candidate for a Discord report like 1kn: suggest the engine log or badge dropped entries. Low urgency for us post-fix.

title: ME_HTTP_LOG=1 crashes startup — pino-pretty transport configured but not installed
description: index.ts logger config uses transport pino-pretty when ME_HTTP_LOG=1, but pino-pretty is not in devDependencies — fastify's logger factory throws at boot and the sidecar never binds. Found 2026-06-12 while trying to enable HTTP request logging for the post-CSRF loader diagnosis. Fix: npm i -D pino-pretty, or drop the transport and use plain JSON logging for this flag. Until fixed, ME_HTTP_LOG=1 in .env makes the launcher window show a logger-factory stack and exit.
close_reason: pino-pretty installed as devDependency; verified ME_HTTP_LOG=1 boots a working server on a scratch port (health ok). Flag is OFF by default; enable in .env when raw HTTP tracing is needed.

title: Tiered cold storage for the entry index (not summarization)
description: Bound the hot index (loader scans ALL rows every turn; professor_mari ~2780 and growing) WITHOUT lossy summarization. Approach (user design): hot/cold physical index split per scope — index.yaml hot, index.cold.yaml archive; entry files stay full-fidelity, only index rows move. runPromotion demotes stale non-core entries hot->cold instead of pruning/deleting (also stops the current lossy prune + de-risks #4 backup). Loader consults cold ONLY on a recall miss; a recited cold entry rehydrates to hot (recordRecitation inverted). Note: targets the ledger ENTRY index the loader reads (companion entries), not the separate beats store. See bd memory cold-storage-not-summarization. Open knob: cold-miss trigger (see issue notes).
close_reason: Done + tested. Tiered cold storage: stale non-core entries archive hot->cold (index.cold.yaml) instead of being pruned/deleted; loader does a cold scan only on a relevance miss and rehydrates the best match; recitation also rehydrates. Bounds the hot scan without summarization loss, and stops the lossy prune (de-risks backup). 90 tests, tsc clean.

title: Auto-start sidecar on boot (optional)
description: Now that the loader depends on the sidecar, if the console isn't running the extension silently vanishes. Offer an opt-in Windows startup registration (Task Scheduler or Startup shortcut) so 'always works' doesn't require remembering to launch a console.
close_reason: Done. [A] toggle in start.ps1 console writes/removes a Startup-folder launcher (Marinara Extender.cmd) that relaunches start.ps1 minimized at login; banner shows ON/off; opt-in + user-removable. Launcher string verified well-formed; ps parses clean.

title: .env.example committed template
description: A fresh clone has no .env and no template (real .env is gitignored). Add memory-extender/.env.example with all vars commented (pure defaults when copied), API key line empty, no secrets. Confirm not caught by *.env ignore. README points to it.
close_reason: Shipped + verified. start.ps1 builds + runs prod (dev fallback) and preflights Node 20+; loader shows an on-page offline banner; .env.example committed. Prod build runs (health 200), loader valid JS, tsc clean, 84 tests, ps parses.

title: v1.1: support any OpenAI-compatible local provider (not just Ollama)
description: The chat/analysis path already talks the OpenAI protocol (MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL points at an OpenAI-compatible /v1 base). v1.1: make 'any local provider via OpenAI protocol' a first-class, documented story — LM Studio, llama.cpp server, vLLM, text-generation-webui, KoboldCpp, etc. Work: (1) generalize the Ollama-specific bits — the /api/health check pings the Ollama root, and chunker embeddings use Ollama's native /api/embeddings; make these provider-agnostic or clearly optional. (2) document per-provider base URLs + a 'bring your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint' section. (3) test the sentiment JSON path across a couple of providers. Defer until v1.0 install pipeline is done.
notes: Bumped P4→P3: real community request (a KoboldCpp user asked 'does Ollama being a prereq mean I can't use this?'). FINDING: the CORE already supports any OpenAI-compatible local provider — all analysis calls hit /chat/completions and embeddings hit /v1/embeddings against MARINARA_EXTENDER_LOCAL_URL (llm-config.ts DEFAULT_LOCAL_URL is just Ollama's OpenAI endpoint). So Kobold/LM Studio/llama.cpp work TODAY via .env. Remaining is ONBOARDING, not capability: (1) launcher (start.ps1) is Ollama-only (detect/start/pull/install); (2) messaging + .env said 'Ollama' — .env.example now reworded (this commit) to spell out KoboldCpp/LM Studio/llama.cpp + ports; (3) embed status check uses Ollama /api/tags. Folded into szf Phase 2 (docs + 'bring-your-own-backend' launcher tolerance) and overlaps nqy (easy endpoint config UI).

title: True group-chat per-speaker routing (plumb Marinara per-message speaker)
description: Chat-import per-speaker routing (P4) works for speakers the chunker detects: inline 'Name:' prefixes + narration. It does NOT yet handle TRUE group chats where each message is a separate row from a distinct character and the speaker lives only in Marinara's message metadata (fetchChatMessages currently keeps only {role, content}). To finish: (1) verify Marinara's per-message speaker field for group chats (characterId/name/author/etc.), (2) extension fetchChatMessages prefixes assistant content with 'Name: ' when discoverable (chunker already parses that), or pass a speaker field, (3) verify routing splits a real group chat per character. Needs the real Marinara group-chat message schema — do not guess-ship field names into the import path. Also: clean re-import (removeEntriesBySourceChat) only clears the primary character's entries; orphan-routed companions on OTHER characters aren't cleared on re-import (dedup + deterministic beat ids cover re-runs, but note it).
close_reason: Implemented same turn it was filed: Marinara stores per-message characterId (confirmed from chats.storage.ts); DigestMessage.speaker + parseTurns honor it; extension maps characterId->name and sets speaker. Unit-tested (parseTurns honors speaker, robust to periods/accents). End-to-end vs a real Marinara group chat is in-browser-only to confirm.

title: Re-evaluate RP time-sense post-v1.0 (multi-model behavior)
description: Time-sense (soft-clock narrative time + presence + no-nag guidance) is gated OFF via MARINARA_EXTENDER_TIMESENSE for v1.0 — worked under Claude 4.6, unreliable under 4.7. Re-evaluate after v1.0: (1) characterize 4.7's raw default time/break-nagging behavior with the feature OFF; (2) test the feature ON across models (4.6, 4.7, others) to see where it helps vs. goes wacky; (3) gather user feedback; (4) decide whether to re-enable by default, keep opt-in, or rework the prompt steering. All logic is intact behind the flag — no rebuild needed to test, just flip the env var. See commit gating it.

title: FR4: supersedes audit trail + rollback UI
description: Tooling on top of the FR2 supersedes link: surface a fact's supersession history in the ledger UI and allow rollback when the LLM (FR3) or structural rule (FR1) got it wrong — restore a superseded fact to active, re-superseding its replacement. The link/data model already exists from FR2; this is the human-in-the-loop affordance. Depends on FR2 (and pairs with FR3).
notes: CODE COMPLETE, awaiting manual UI verification (not closing — the rule: UI is verified only by the user clicking in a running browser). Backend done + verified on real data: restoreSupersededEntry (storage), factHistory/listRetired/rollback (rollback.ts, undo+flip), GET /api/retired + POST /api/rollback (characterId->identityKey, character scope), 7 offline tests; listRetired(professor_mari) returns 44 real retired facts. UI: collapsible 'Retired (character memory)' section in the panel memory tab (renderRetiredSection in marinara-extender.js) with Restore=undo / Restore-as-canonical=flip, lazy-load, reused CSS. TO VERIFY + CLOSE: (1) restart the sidecar so the new endpoints go live; (2) open the panel -> memory tab -> expand 'Retired'; (3) confirm the 44 facts list with their replacements; (4) Restore one (undo -> both active) and one with --flip (replacement retired); confirm via re-expand. Committed; pushed.

title: FR3: LLM reconciliation pass — adjudicate fact collisions
description: The expensive correct layer for subtle cases. GATED: runs ONLY on FR1-flagged same-subject candidates (not every save, not a blind periodic sweep) so cost stays rare. Prompt: given an incoming fact and the existing same-subject fact(s), decide UPDATE (supersede), EXPAND (both true, keep both), DISTINCT (false collision, keep both), or NEGATE (incoming disproves existing -> mark existing superseded as a negative fact). Routes Ollama-local -> external fallback like the rest. Depends on FR2.
close_reason: Fulfilled by MarinaraExtender-5ny for the OFFLINE path: the curator adjudicates UPDATE/EXPAND/DISTINCT/NEGATE/CREATE/DUPLICATE against same-subject ledger entries and applies via the FR2 supersede primitive. Implemented as a Claude Agent SDK tool loop (not the single Ollama->external prompt originally scoped) on CLI-session auth, ledger-gated (preview==apply). The LIVE FR1-gated turn-path integration is split out to its own ticket (different shape: cost gating, latency budget, live data vs ledger).

title: P4: collision detection, auto-suggest aliases, group-chat verify
description: Polish/edge cases. Collision: same label maps to multiple characters -> detect at alias-add, user picks owner or marks ambiguous (per-beat manual). Auto-suggest: new chat introduces 'Dr. Chandrasekaran' when 'Chandrasekaran' already maps to a char but the longer form doesn't -> prompt to add alias. Verify multi-character group-chat routing still routes each beat individually. Depends on P1.
notes: IN-BROWSER VERIFICATION PASSED (user, 2026-06-04): all P4 manual checklist items confirmed working — collision reassign/leave prompt, Map, Create card, '+ New character' import dropdown, true group-chat per-character routing (Marinara /messages does return characterId per message), and the 'Resolve now' link. Combined with the real-LLM server e2e (held→resolve→retrievable→auto-route) and 77 unit/integration tests, P4 and the holding-pool epic are fully verified end to end.
close_reason: P4 complete across commits: collision-aware resolution (correctness hole closed), auto-suggest via token containment, per-speaker chat routing for chunker-detectable speakers AND true group chats (per-message characterId), plus a latent P1 fix (migrated/auto-routed beats now get companion entries so they're actually retrievable). 72 tests. Group-chat end-to-end wants one in-browser confirm.

title: Configurable Current-cache token budgets (env now; per-character/per-model later)
description: Budgets were hardcoded (chat 4000/char 2000/global 1000) — fine for 200k models, costly for tighter ones. Now read at call time from MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_CHAT/_CHARACTER/_GLOBAL (documented in .env). FOLLOW-UP: per-character and/or per-model budget overrides (store on identity/character config) so different characters or connected models can have different footprints.
close_reason: The env half was already implemented and is verified working: loader.ts getBudgets() reads MARINARA_EXTENDER_BUDGET_CHAT/_CHARACTER/_GLOBAL at call time (env changes apply on next turn, no restart), defaults 4000/2000/1000, documented in .env.example. The per-character/per-model follow-up is split out to its own issue (with the open storage-location design decision flagged for TC) so this one reflects reality.

title: Decide: should mere exposure (retrievalCount on load) still drive promotion?
description: computeScore = retrievalCount + recitationCount*3. retrievalCount still increments on every LOAD, so an entry that merely surfaces a lot can promote to core without ever being demonstrably used. lastRetrievedAt is now use-only (honest), but score still rewards exposure. Decision needed: de-weight or drop retrievalCount from computeScore (promotion = proven use), weighed against recitation detection's blind spot (it misses paraphrased use, so pure-recitation promotion could under-credit genuinely-useful-but-not-echoed entries). Deferred for a deliberate call.
close_reason: Resolved: exposure credit is now relevance-gated in loader.ts selectEntries — retrievalCount increments only when an entry is SUMMONED (relevanceScore > 0.1), not when it merely rides in on the recency fallback. So mere exposure no longer drives promotion; relevance-driven exposure does, which becomes a more honest proxy for use as the Current cache improves. computeScore (retrievalCount + recitationCount*3) kept as-is. See commit.

title: start.ps1: interactive console with restart-server command
description: After services are ready, replace 'press any key to close' with a command loop: R restarts the Memory Extender sidecar (kills the launched cmd/npm/node tree, falls back to killing the port-3001 owner, relaunches, polls health), Q quits leaving services running. Saves the manual restart-the-sidecar dance after code changes.
close_reason: Added Start/Stop/Restart-Sidecar helpers and a command loop (R restart, Q quit). Parses clean; non-ASCII confined to comment separators.

title: Long stories truncated during attribution (8192 token cap, single call)
description: story-parser sends the whole story in one LLM call capped at 8192 output tokens with no input chunking. Output is ~as long as input, so stories past ~20k chars lose their tail (climax/ending never attributed or analyzed). Fix: window the input at paragraph boundaries and attribute each window, concatenating results.
close_reason: story-parser windows input at paragraph boundaries (12k chars), attributes each window local->external->paragraph, concatenates. Normal-size stories unchanged (single window).

title: beat.emotion uses keyword classifier, not LLM emotions[0]
description: encoder.ts sets primary emotion from the classifier keyword match; the LLM's richer emotions[0] is ignored for the stored primary and the [emotion] ledger tag. Prefer analysis.emotions[0] when present, fall back to classifier primaryEmotion.
close_reason: Tier 2 ledger tag now uses analysis.emotions[0] (LLM primary) with classifier fallback; beat.emotion stays the enum lane for typing/panel.

title: Dual narrator casing: 'narrator' vs 'Narrator'
description: Chunker emits lowercase 'narrator' for *action* lines; story path produces capital 'Narrator'. povCharacter relabel only matches capital. Works today for story import but is a latent trap. Normalize to one label.
close_reason: Chunker emits capital 'Narrator'; tests + type comment updated. Single canonical label across chunker and story parser.

title: Bookmark file writes are unserialized (race / corrupt YAML)
description: upsertBookmark, processResponse's writeBookmarks, ingest-commands bookmark append, and the bookmark PATCH/DELETE handlers all do read-modify-write on bookmarks.yaml without serializedWrite (the lock that fixed the index race). Lower frequency than the index but same corruption class. Fix: add a serialized mutateBookmarks helper and route bookmark writes through it.
close_reason: Added serialized mutateBookmarks; routed processResponse, ingest append, and bookmark PATCH/DELETE through it. Removed dead upsertBookmark.

title: soft-clock previousSessionTimeOfDay never cleared -> stale '(morning after)'
description: updateSoftClock sets previousSessionTimeOfDay on a morning-after inference but never clears it. formatClockContext then appends '(morning after evening)' to the session-context line on every subsequent turn indefinitely. Fix: clear previousSessionTimeOfDay after it has been surfaced once (or only show it on the turn it changed).
close_reason: updateSoftClock now retires previousSessionTimeOfDay the turn after it surfaces; '(morning after)' shows once.

title: User-requested memory save: persist facts/preferences on command
description: Users should be able to ask the AI to 'remember this' mid-conversation and have the extender write it to the appropriate lorebook tier. Examples: 'remember I prefer dark themes', 'save this list', 'remember my character's backstory'. The AI would emit a structured tag or signal, the extension would intercept it, classify the scope (chat vs character vs global), and call POST /api/entries to persist it as a named entry. Scope selection could be heuristic or user-directed via phrasing.
notes: Implemented via prompt directive (user-chosen approach over extension interception). The [remember:] command pipeline already handled extraction, dedup, scope routing, and tiering end-to-end; the only gap was that explicit user requests weren't a guaranteed trigger — the instructions discouraged trivial saves, so 'remember I prefer dark themes' would be dropped as minor. Added a 'WHEN THE USER ASKS YOU TO REMEMBER' block to MEMORY_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS making a direct request a HARD trigger that overrides the discretionary rule, with lane/scope guidance (fact→user_topics, task→open_threads; character scope unless user says this-chat-only), a confirmation nudge, and a guard distinguishing real requests from incidental phrasing ('remember when we…'). Verified extractRememberTags parses the emitted bracket format incl. spaced content values. PENDING: live browser verification after sidecar restart.
close_reason: Implemented as prompt directive over the existing [remember:] pipeline; type-checks clean, parser path verified. Live browser test pending sidecar restart.

title: [bug] One unreproducible test failure observed in the vitest suite
description:
Observed once 2026-07-23 on branch poller-fallback: a full npm test run reported "1 failed | 295 passed". The reporter output was truncated before naming the test, and 6 subsequent runs were all clean at 296 passed. Not reproduced.

Recording it rather than assuming it was noise — an unexplained flake in a 296-test suite is the kind of thing that turns into a mystery CI failure later. If it recurs, capture the FULL vitest output (do not tail/grep it) so the test name is preserved.

One candidate worth checking first if it does recur: several test files mutate process.env (engine-client.test.ts and proxy.integration.test.ts both set and delete MARINARA_EXTENDER_* vars in beforeEach/afterEach). If vitest ever runs those in the same worker with overlapping lifecycles, env bleed between files is plausible.

description:
Once slices 1-7 land, remove the dead bridge and replace the install story.

Also update the marinara-extender-expert skill: references/extension.md is entirely obsolete and must be rewritten as references/proxy.md, plus architecture.md and config-and-ops.md. Project session-close rule requires the skill be updated in the same session as the code.

title: In-memory index read-cache (read-only; preserve atomic write-through)
description: From the Comparision_2 review (shortcoming 2.1 supplement, partial). At large entry counts the hot index.yaml grows and is re-read+parsed from disk every turn (loader has no persistent cross-turn cache). Proposal: an in-memory READ cache of the per-scope hot index, invalidated on write. IMPORTANT: READ half ONLY. Do NOT adopt the source docs async-write-queue-every-30s idea: it conflicts with the existing atomic-write durability (storage.ts temp+fsync+rename, per-path serialized, for crash/power-loss safety) and risks losing up to 30s of memory on a crash. Writes stay write-through. Also: the source doc overstates the I/O problem (claimed thousands-of-files per turn; actually the hot/cold + index/entry split already bound per-turn I/O to one index + a handful of selected entries). Low priority unless a real large-dataset benchmark shows index-parse latency. Source: docs/Comparision_2_review.md Slice 3.

title: [task] Measure pre-turn budget headroom — how much of PRE_TURN_BUDGET_MS we actually use
description:
We block generation up to PRE_TURN_BUDGET_MS (800ms, marinara-extender.js) for preTurnRefresh, but we have no measurement of how much of that lead time we actually consume — so we can't tell if we're comfortable or at the edge. This matters more now: 38x (dual-retrieval) turned pre-turn from ONE sidecar call into N (one per participant, each including the Stage-2 recap embedding) + N lorebook writes. We told the user 'always-on, add a toggle if the bite is too big' — this is the instrument that tells us whether/when that's needed, instead of guessing.

WHAT: instrument preTurnRefresh to report lead-time usage:
- total elapsed from start to when the awaited refreshes settle (or the budget timeout fires);
- whether the budget timeout fired and how many participants were still pending (stragglers that lagged to next turn);
- ideally per-participant timing (which character's refresh is slow — pre-turn call vs lorebook write) and participant count.
Console log at minimum (e.g. '[ME] pre-turn: 540/800ms, 3/3 participants, 0 stragglers'); optionally surface a rolling stat in the panel Settings or /api/health so it's visible without console-diving.

WHY P4: no pain observed yet; this is pre-emptive observability. ESCALATE earlier if multi-character scenes feel laggy, prompts balloon, or we're deciding on the dual-retrieval toggle (38x) and want data first. Relates to 38x.

title: serializedWrite keyed by raw path string - case-insensitive FS edge
description: Audit finding #4 (theoretical/very low severity). storage.ts serializedWrite serializes per filePath using a Map keyed by the raw string. On case-insensitive filesystems (Windows, default macOS), two different-cased path strings for the same physical file ('Foo.yaml' vs 'foo.yaml') would hash to different keys and NOT serialize, allowing a concurrent read-modify-write race that could corrupt YAML. Mitigated in practice because all paths come from the same path-building helpers (entryPath/indexPath/etc.) which emit consistent strings, so divergent casing should never occur. Fix if we ever want belt-and-suspenders: normalize the lock key (e.g. path.resolve + toLowerCase on win32) before Map lookup. Filing for awareness; not currently reachable.

title: Per-character / per-model Current-cache budget overrides (7ff follow-up)

This follow-up: let individual characters or connected models carry their own budget overrides so a tight-context model or a memory-heavy character can size its Current cache independently. title: v1.1: IDF-weighted relevance scoring (retire stopword list)
description:
Post-MVP tweak — defer until the holding-pool epic and core features are working. Replace the equal-weight lexical containment in loader.ts relevanceScore with IDF-weighted containment so distinctive tokens (Emma, cover-letter, Hargrove) drive relevance instead of being drowned out by formulaic beat-summary vocabulary (feel/trust/wants/anxious). Subsumes and retires the hand-maintained RELEVANCE_STOPWORDS list.

DESIGN NOTES (from review):
- It's IDF, not TF-IDF: summaries are ~15 words so TF~=1 and does nothing. Score = sum(idf of matched summary tokens) / sum(idf of all summary tokens), preserving the 0-1 range and the directional summary->recentText property.
- Corpus = PER CHARACTER, not per-scope. A fresh chat has too few entries for stable IDF; token rarity is a property of the character's domain. Build one idf table per character, reuse across that character's chat/character/global-relevant scopes.
- Smoothing: df+1 for unseen tokens so a brand-new distinctive token gets ~max weight (correct) rather than divide-by-zero.
- Build cost is trivial (one pass, ~18k tokens for a 900-entry character). Rebuild lazily on the promotion pass or every N saves; cache in memory keyed by character. Per-turn lookup stays O(summary tokens) — zero added latency, no model call.
- RECALIBRATE the RELEVANCE_CREDIT_THRESHOLD (currently 0.1 in loader.ts): IDF weighting shifts the score distribution, so the 'summoned' gate that drives retrievalCount/exposure-credit changes meaning. Re-tune against real data, don't assume 0.1 holds.
- Alternative considered: embeddings cosine (reuses Ollama EMBED_MODEL) — rejected for v1.1 because it trades the zero-latency/zero-cost property for a per-turn model call. IDF keeps the cheap-lookup property.

ARCHIVED IS 'NEVER IN THE PROMPT', NOT 'HIDDEN FROM THE HUMAN' (TC, 2026-08-25, ticket gujk). I had designed the fork's archive as unreachable from every system path, living outside data/characters/ so nothing could enumerate it. TC corrected the line: 'It's ok if it is readable by humans, and viewable from the memory tab. It should have a DEPRECIATED label or something along those lines.' THE CORRECT BOUNDARY: nothing that FEEDS THE CHARACTER may read it — loader hot and cold, promotion, the decay clock, cleanup, capture and every write path, digest, stats, arc promotion, the entity-index builder. Anything that SHOWS A HUMAN THINGS may read it — the memory tab, labelled DEPRECATED, read-only. THE REPO ALREADY HAS THIS EXACT SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN and it should be copied rather than reinvented: provenance 'unplayed' (EntryProvenance, storage.ts). Author-established outline is stored at full fidelity, shows in the memory browser with an 'outline — never recalled' pill, and is rejected in the loader at BOTH paths (hot and cold) on the stated grounds that 'a character that can remember an unplayed scene is a confabulation machine'. An archived SCOPE is that same promise at scope granularity. THE STRUCTURAL RULE THAT MAKES IT HOLD: EXCLUDE BY DEFAULT, DISPLAY BY EXPLICIT OPT-IN. listScopeIds() must never return an archived scope, so every existing consumer becomes correct with NO change because it cannot see one; a separate listArchivedScopes() is called only by the memory-tab endpoint. The inverse — included by default and every reader remembers to skip it — is EXACTLY how pe1c's 657-row ghost scope stayed visible and enumerated for months. When a thing must be invisible to N consumers, change what enumeration RETURNS rather than adding a skip to each consumer, and let the one viewer that wants it opt in deliberately.

COUNT UTTERANCES, NEVER HITS — dedupe by content hash before counting anything (Mari, filed properly 2026-08-06).

Previously carried as verbal shorthand ('the lobster rider') with nothing filed. An
agent hit the phrase, found no record, and stopped rather than guessing — which was
correct, and is why it is written down now.

THE FINDING: one utterance about lobster was re-imported across four chats and
produced FIVE beats. Counted naively it read as five independent corroborations of a
single thing. It was one person saying one sentence once.

THE RULE: any count that will be used as EVIDENCE must count distinct utterances, not
records. Dedupe by content hash first. A record count answers 'how many rows do we
hold', which is a storage question; corroboration asks 'how many times was this
independently said', which is a truth question. Re-import, resume, subject-routing and
companion entries all multiply rows without multiplying utterances.

WHERE IT BITES, all live in this repo:
  - echo/bait corroboration — a phrase 'confirmed' by five copies of one paste
  - bait-rot's spoken vs derived split is this rule applied once already
  - any 'N beats say X' claim in a report or a ticket
  - dedup.ts exists for the write side; this is the READ side of the same idea

RELATED FAILURE, same family: when measuring contamination, the contamination's own
artifacts inflate the count — see [[chunk-level-vs-line-level-a-verdict-about]] and the
measure-before-you-reason law in the expert skill (1,100 vs 65, 683, 636 vs 34).

DUPLICATE BEATS ARE THE MECHANISM TO WATCH. beatIdForChunk hashing an interpretation
(speaker) meant every attribution fix minted duplicates on re-import — which is exactly
how one utterance becomes five. Being fixed by making the id provenance-only.

Engine (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine) has a RECURRING CLASS of file-durability / crash-safety bugs: fsync no-ops, .bak not durably flushed (closed #631; the flushFile 'r' read-only-fd Windows no-op = 1kn; 2+ more of the same class on Discord). Do NOT assume engine file writes are crash-safe. The EXTENDER's own atomicWriteFile (memory-extender/src/storage.ts:183) is the hardened reference implementation — fsyncs the WRITABLE handle (not a read-only 'r' fd), warns-once on fsync failure instead of swallowing, atomic rename with Windows EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES transient-retry. Extender storage is independently durable; these are upstream's bugs, not ours.

COUNT-VS-RATE ACROSS TIME BUCKETS (2026-08-21, 5x5y). The 'count utterances, never hits' law has a second face nobody had written down: comparing RAW COUNTS across time periods is the same error as counting duplicate records, and it manufactures regressions out of thin air.

I reported subtext emission as 'dead since 2026-07-03 — a 7-week silent failure'. TC's reply killed it in one sentence: 'I haven't been particularly active since July either.' Normalising by the only denominator that means anything — beats whose own source is intimate, the content the field exists for — gave 0.8% in June, 0% in July, 0% in August. At a 0.8% base rate, July's 0/156 and August's 0/79 are what chance predicts. There was never a decay. The feature simply never worked.

THE TELL I MISSED: I had a zero and reached for a CAUSE (a code change, a model swap, a prompt edit) before establishing there was an EFFECT to explain. I even searched git history for the culprit and found none — which should have been the signal that the premise was wrong, not that the cause was hidden.

THE RULE: before attributing a change to a date, normalise by exposure. Ask 'how many chances did it have to fire in each period' and compare RATES. If you cannot state the denominator, you do not yet have a finding. A near-zero base rate is especially dangerous because any quiet period 'confirms' the story.

RELATED, same session: a sample with no power was cited as evidence in both directions — 0/13 intimate beats against a 0.7% base rate expects 0.09 emissions and could never have detected anything. Compute what the sample COULD have shown before reporting what it did.

DEMO/TEST SIDECAR RULE (learned the hard way 2026-08-03): ALWAYS launch a second sidecar with MARINARA_EXTENDER_POLLER=0. An isolated MARINARA_EXTENDER_DATA dir does NOT isolate the instance — the data dir isolates the STORE, not the ENGINE CONNECTION, and the poller defaults to ON. A demo instance on a scratch data dir therefore polls the LIVE engine and rewrites real character lorebooks from the scratch store on every turn it ingests. lorebook-writer's _lorebookWriteChain mutex is PER PROCESS, so two sidecars against one engine are two uncoordinated writers to the same lorebook, and each write NUKES and recreates both entries by design — last writer wins outright. Detection: compare Active Context updatedAt across the engine's 'Marinara Extender — *' lorebooks; a timestamp from the demo window identifies the affected character. Self-heals on the next real turn (turn-bridge is the only caller of syncMemoryToLorebook). Tracked as MarinaraExtender-1akw.

PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE — analyzer prompt bench (Mari, 2026-08-05, written BLIND).

Authored before any number was visible to its author. Opie had already run the pilot and
seen results; Mari had not, and wrote these integers knowing only that numbers existed.
THE AUTHORITY OF THESE NUMBERS IS THE TIMESTAMP, NOT THE ELEGANCE. Do not renegotiate
them after the data lands -- that is the failure the pre-registration exists to prevent.

  VALIDITY FLOOR  any arm more than 2 points below the best on JSON validity is OUT.
                  Parse loss is silent beat loss.
  BASELINE        short + NO example. Bait must pay rent.
  OFF-PLANET      carried only if it beats no-example by >= 5 points on boilerplate rate.
  IN-DOMAIN       ships only if it beats off-planet by >= 10 points on boilerplate AND
                  posts under 2% bench echo, SKELETON-SCORED. Production in-domain echoes
                  are invisible by construction, so the bench is the only place they will
                  ever be countable. Cross 2% there and it is disqualified at any
                  specificity.
  TIES/NEAR-MISS  go DOWN the ladder, toward less bait. Never up.

"What is specificity allowed to cost": five points buys an example at all, ten more buys
bait. Cheaper than that, we keep our hands clean.

METHOD REQUIREMENTS attached to the same ruling:
- Bench echo scoring uses the SKELETON matcher, not substring. A referee that undercounts
  the way the guard did is not a referee.
- Ship the chunk floor/cap FIRST and judge the arms in the world that will actually exist.
  Nobody calibrates against a building scheduled for demolition.
- n=45 is a pilot, not a verdict. Bump it.
- QUARANTINE: capture must be quiesced or every output ops-tagged. The experiment does not
  get to contaminate the specimen.

Rows created BEFORE 18:18:41Z came from the old dist: aboutness written as a '[about: X]' PROSE PREFIX in the summary, no subjects field, no persona kind, and non-name subjects accepted. Any row that moves before the branch merges can be cut on this timestamp. WHY IT WAS CYCLED RATHER THAN LEFT UNTIL MERGE, in TC's words: 'waiting isn't free — every hour on the old dist mints more prose prefixes into the exact population you just agreed to hand-check. 181 isn't a constant, it's a leak rate.' Demonstrated in the same session: the [about: Thomas] entry count was 22 at 12:40 and 23 at 13:15, and capture-status orphans went 152 to 162 between the census and the cycle. PRE-CYCLE SAFETY CHECK, TC's condition, and it belongs in every future bounce: verify the WATERMARK is current first, because a restart is exactly when a reverted position cashes out — a fresh process reads the watermark, believes it, and re-ingests everything after. Verified poller-state.yaml written 18:13:41Z matching its own newest watermark 18:13:37Z, zero orphaned .tmp files for it ever, and it already writes through mutateYamlFile -> serializedWrite. Note the file to check is poller-state.yaml, NOT capture-status.yaml — see [[dolt-is-not-used-in-this-project-skip]]-adjacent correction recorded on i83s.

THE RECURRING ROOT CAUSE behind most 'memory bugs' in this store (synthesised 2026-08-04 across tp5, 76aw, np4b, egj3): the store LACKS VOCABULARY, and the bugs are what that absence looks like from the outside. Four missing dimensions, each now filed: WHO IS THIS ABOUT (4g9w — scope answers who can RECALL, never who it is ABOUT, so aboutness got forced onto the lane axis which offers only user_topics/character_topics; a third person has no home, which is the Becky Collier case). WHERE/WHEN IS IT SET (fh33 — Iraq 2004 vs War 20XX; also the extractable form of the world tag). WHO SHARES IT (fhd party scope — Mari appears 230x in PRIYA's scope, which is the triad, not contamination; the Civ VI ledger is group lore with nowhere to live). WHO IS THIS ENTITY OVER TIME (character rename/split history — Aurora migrated FROM the Professor Mari card, Desmond/Draymond Cole drifted from one character into two; no text analysis recovers either). PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: any lane-mismatch or confound detector will report these as errors when the memory is filed in the only place that exists. Do not action such a list without asking which gap it is measuring — the confound sweep ran ~19% precision for exactly this reason.

PRE-REGISTRATION EARNED ITS KEEP, ONCE, MEASURABLY (cye6 slice 3, 2026-08-25). I wired a change, recommended it, then measured it and it failed. The reason the failure survived contact with me is that the bar was committed to git before a single number existed (commit 20b75e1), and three habits inside it did the actual work.

(1) REPORT PRECISION PER POPULATION, NEVER BLENDED. The wired arm scored 51% blended against a 43% baseline and produced 233 sound facts per 60 turns against 104 — a clean win by every headline number. Split by population it was 62% on the sentences that already worked and 29% on the ones the change admitted, and the blend hid the entire trade. If I had reported one number I would have shipped a 29%-precision population and been able to defend it with arithmetic. Whenever a change WIDENS what a stage sees, the old and new populations are different questions and one figure answers neither.

(2) HIDE THE ARM FROM THE LABELLER, and say what the blind cannot hide. I labelled 496 facts against a shuffled blind id with the arm stripped. The CELL could not be hidden — a second-person sentence is recognisable by reading it — so the writeup says so rather than claiming a cleaner blind than it had. Also: do not score until every label is in, or the running total steers the remaining labels.

(3) A FALLBACK PREDICTED FROM A SAMPLE CAN BE FLATLY WRONG. Slice 1 eyeballed subject-position filtering and called it "a big precision win" (15,739 -> 2,152 candidates, visibly cleaner samples). Measured on labelled data it scored 27% against presence's 29% — two points WORSE while discarding 62 of 161 facts. It was not a precision filter at all, just a smaller set at the same precision. The samples looked better because I picked them.

AND THE HONEST HANDLING OF A CRITERION WRITTEN BADLY: I had pre-registered "OLD precision in B within 10 points of A" with no direction, and B came in 19 points BETTER. The guard was plainly aimed at degradation, but I recorded it as written and as an improvement rather than quietly reinterpreting it into a pass. Reinterpreting one criterion after the data is how the whole instrument stops working.

RELATED: [[count-vs-rate-across-time-buckets-2026-08]] (same family — the denominator decides the finding), [[chunk-level-vs-line-level-a-verdict-about]] (rule breadth survives its scope: widening invalidates a precision number and requires re-measuring, which is what this was).

bd update --notes REPLACES the whole notes field, it does not append (found 2026-08-10 by clobbering four tickets' history). Before writing notes to a ticket that may have any, read the current notes first and re-submit old + new together. Recovery if clobbered: .beads/issues.jsonl is git-tracked, so the pre-clobber text is in the last commit — but the daemon flushes lazily, so the working copy and even HEAD can lag the DB; check both the prior commit and the current file. And never pass --notes "$(cat file)" without confirming the file exists — cat's failure makes the substitution EMPTY and blanks the field.

NEVER PASS A MULTI-LINE VALUE TO bd FROM POWERSHELL (2026-08-25, cost a collateral edit to an unrelated ticket). Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not quote a native-command argument containing newlines, so CommandLineToArgvW splits it on whitespace and bd receives ~80 positional arguments. Observed: `bd update <id> --notes $n` with a 5KB here-doc updated the intended ticket with a TRUNCATED first fragment, then walked the remaining fragments as issue IDs — dozens of "no issue found matching" errors, "ambiguous ID 'a' matches 26 issues", and one word that DID resolve ('and' -> MarinaraExtender-and), which was silently updated with a stray fragment of another ticket's notes. It also mangled UTF-8: every em dash became "â€”".

THE TELL: a wall of "Error resolving <word>" lines interleaved with a success. The success is the damage, not the errors.

USE BASH INSTEAD. `bd update <id> --notes "$(cat file)"` from the Bash tool passes the whole thing as one argument and preserves UTF-8. Verified on the same 5KB payload: 5,285 bytes intact, no mojibake.

REPAIR, if it happens: `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` then diff every record against `git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl` by id and field — the collateral edit is invisible in the CLI output and will not be on the ticket you were working on. Clear a wrongly-set field with `--notes ""`, which bd accepts.

CHARACTER BRANCHING IS THE REAL SHAPE, AND I ARGUED AGAINST IT WRONGLY FIRST (TC, 2026-08-25). TC's ruling after seeing the read-time fork: 'Them both writing into the same store is the problem. Let them both read whatever is there we can't separate out, or duplicate it for both of them, and then create completely separate entities. And then just archive the original memories, and we can use those to verify things if need be, but nothing in the system should ever access it again.' MY ERROR: I had argued against duplicating the shared history because 'two copies drift', citing pe1c's 657 ghost rows. That objection does not survive TC's design. The ghost is dangerous because the system STILL ENUMERATES it; an ARCHIVED ancestor is unreachable, so there is no third copy competing and divergence between the forks is the POINT rather than the defect. Check whether a cited precedent actually shares the mechanism before letting it veto a design — 'we got burned by copies once' is not an argument against copying, it is an argument against copies that stay live. THE GENERAL PRIMITIVE TC ASKED FOR, because 'someone may want to branch their character, or download someone's character that they want to modify while keeping the original': fork(sourceKey, branches[], {splitAt, archiveSource}). Each branch gets its own scope, its own identity key, and a seeded copy distributed by rowInBranch. Two use cases differing only in archiveSource — SPLIT (one person became two; ancestor archived) and CLONE-TO-MODIFY (ancestor stays live; the new branch is seeded from it). The current code half-does clone by accident, since an unknown card id mints a new key and an empty store, but there is no way to say 'start with the original's memories and then diverge'. THE ARCHIVE IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART: moving the directory is NOT enough, because listScopeIds() returns every directory under data/characters/ — which is exactly how pe1c's ghost stayed visible in the memory browser for months. The archive must live OUTSIDE that tree so it is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by every reader remembering to skip it. AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE 'duplicate the ambiguous' cheap: a retired branch has a LAST ACTIVITY date, and nothing created after it can be that branch's. On the Mari store that cut the unattributable set from 3,796 (42.9%) to 1,241 (14.0%). Before falling back to duplication, look for a bound the data already implies — dormancy was sitting there unused.

Design law for index growth (#5 compaction): TIERED COLD STORAGE, not summarization. Memories are never compressed/summarized (lossy) — stale ones DEMOTE out of the hot index into a cold archive at full fidelity, consulted only on a recall MISS. Maps onto human memory (old = harder to reach, not gone; retrieval strengthens). Implementation on existing code: (1) physical split per scope — index.yaml (hot, scanned every turn) + index.cold.yaml (archive, read only on miss); entry files stay put, only the index ROW moves. (2) runPromotion already computes daysSinceRetrieval — add a stale-non-core -> cold transition that REPLACES the lossy prune/delete path (so this also stops destroying old memories and de-risks backup). core/secondary_core never leave hot. (3) recordRecitation inverted: a recited COLD entry rehydrates back to hot. Cold scan only on miss, so per-turn cost stays bounded. Aligns with fact-vs-feeling-memory-principle (nothing deleted).

IDENTITY FORK vs IDENTITY REPLACEMENT (TC, 2026-08-25, ticket yi70). The identity map collapses several card ids onto one identity key so a character keeps her memories when her CARD is replaced. That is correct for a REPLACEMENT and wrong for a FORK, where the old card is still played as a distinct entity. The store has no way to say 'these two cards were the same person until a date, and different people after it'. THE LIVE CASE: 'Professor Mari' was the original card and was READ-ONLY — it reverted version changes — so TC built 'Dr. Mari Zielinska' from it. Both map to identityKey professor_mari. Ten chats still use characterId __professor_mari__, a card that NO LONGER EXISTS in the Engine; the chats outlived it. THE SPLIT IS 2026-05-23, established empirically: the last old-card chat closed that day and the first Dr. Mari Zielinska chat was created the same day. Nine of the ten ended by then; ONE did not — Hw3h-2KlJqn4btjfmnw70, created 05-25, last message 06-25 — so it ran a month past the split loading Current Mari's memory. THE NUMBER THAT KILLS THE OBVIOUS FIX: of 7,052 beats in the shared store, 6,983 (99.0%) postdate the split and only 69 predate it. A naive date cutoff would leave Professor Mari with ONE PERCENT of her memory and read as amnesiac. The rule that matches the intent is a UNION, not a cutoff: everything up to the split PLUS everything from her own chats after it (her own chat produced 40 beats, 38 entries), giving roughly 109 memories — small and coherent for a character played briefly then retired. GENERAL FORM WORTH KEEPING: when a scoping rule produces a number that would make a character amnesiac, the rule is wrong, not the data. Check the survivor count BEFORE proposing a filter — 'stop after the split' sounds obviously right and is off by two orders of magnitude. AND THE REVERSE DIRECTION IS A SEPARATE RULING NOBODY HAS MADE: should Current Mari still see the 40 post-split beats from the Professor Mari chat? Symmetry says no; TC ruled on one direction only; retiring 40 real beats by inference is not allowed. See [[the-recurring-root-cause-behind-most-memory-bugs]] — this is the 'who is this entity over time' gap, which that memory already names as one of the four missing dimensions.

MIGRATE LAST, AND MIGRATE IN TWO PHASES (TC, 2026-08-25, ruling awgj). TWO SEPARATE RULES, both stated when I offered to migrate the [about: X] prefixes right after building the subjects field. RULE 1 — MIGRATE LAST. TC: 'if you migrate now, those 68 rows land as unresolved names, and the second pass has to tell "migrated before the persona branch existed" apart from "genuinely never resolved," which is exactly the ambiguity you just spent a whole slice designing out. Don't build the scar and cut yourself on it in the same week.' THE GENERAL FORM: a migration run before the enrichment it depends on manufactures a population where your own sentinel is a lie. qlib's design premise is that an ABSENT field means UNASSESSED; migrating 22 'Thomas' rows before qhej wires the persona branch creates rows where absent means 'assessed by code that could not yet answer' — indistinguishable afterwards. Order the work so every backfilled row was written by the FINAL version of the logic, never an interim one. RULE 2 — TWO PHASE, PREFIX IS GROUND TRUTH. TC: 'write the field, LEAVE the prose prefix, verify against it, strip only after. The prefix is your only ground truth for checking the migration and the instinct will be to clean it in the same pass. Do not.' Phase A write the field and leave the source text; phase B verify field against prefix and REPORT the agreement count and disagreement list; phase C strip, and only then. Note this is NOT a violation of 'a copy cannot corroborate its source' — the prefix is the field's SOURCE, not a copy of it, and checking a derived value against the original it derives from is the legitimate direction. After phase C that check is gone forever, which is exactly why it is its own phase. AND THE COUNTING LESSON THAT CAME WITH IT: TC asked 'which number is real, 3,380 or ~612?' Neither. Both were GREP HITS. An entry's summary lives in the entry file AND its index row, so a naive grep double-counts every single entry, and stale copies in orphaned .tmp files (153) and the receipts audit trail (257) inflate it further. Reconciled: 1,494 entry files + 1,492 index rows + 153 orphan-tmp copies + 257 receipts = 3,396 hits, but only 1,494 DISTINCT ENTRIES — of which 181 have a valid name and 1,313 are non-names. I broke 'count utterances, never hits' in the one place it mattered and TC caught it by asking why two of my own numbers disagreed. THE TELL TO WATCH FOR: when two figures you quoted for the same population do not reconcile, do not pick one — the discrepancy is the finding. Here it exposed both the double-counting AND that i83s's orphaned temp files were being read as live data.

THE PROMPT LAW (TC, 2026-08-04, pifl). In TC's words, on the wall:

  "Examples are gravitational mass regardless of their sign. The BAD examples leaked
   too -- 107 beats parroting the phrasing the rule FORBADE. Models don't have a
   valence channel, baby, they have proximity. Never write an example that could
   plausibly be real output for the domain; illustrate shape from another planet.
   Nine percent of a production store is the measurement that makes it doctrine
   instead of folklore."

THE MEASUREMENT: 792 of 8703 beats (9%) echoed a prompt example. 669 were the single
sentence chosen to ILLUSTRATE the rule "two different moments can never produce the
same sentence". 107 more parroted the "too vague" example the same rule forbade.

THE DATE BOUNDARY, which is the proof and not an anecdote:
                       before 2026-06-12   from 06-12 on
   GOOD-example echoes          0                703
   BAD-example echoes         108                 10
On 06-12 the model's boilerplate was diagnosed and the fix added a specific sentence
as the one-shot. The model stopped parroting the BAD example and started parroting the
GOOD one. THE FIX CURED THE SYMPTOM AND MOVED THE DISEASE. A prompt example is not
instruction, it is the nearest available phrasing when the chunk gives the model
nothing.

COROLLARY -- A GUARD MUST NOT BAN THE REAL THING. Making the famous sentence
unrecordable would be a worse bug than the one it fixes. Corroborate instead: echo in
the motivation AND the phrase present in the SOURCE TEXT = the speaker said it, keep
it. Echo with no trace in the source = the model supplied it, reject. And probe for a
distinctive CORE, not the exact phrasing -- a real utterance is first person and worded
differently, so an exact-match corroboration test bans the very thing it exists to save.

THE SIDECAR VERSION STRING FREEZES AT FIRST OBSERVATION, NOT AT STARTUP AND NOT AT RUNTIME (corrected 2026-08-25; CLAUDE.md previously said it re-reads git at runtime, which is wrong). buildVersion() memoizes into a module-level _build (update.ts:38-40) and is called ONLY from request handlers — setup.ts:386 and ui.ts:855, never during boot. So the sha is computed the first time somebody asks, and frozen from then on. WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN EITHER ALTERNATIVE: whether the string lies depends on WHEN YOU HAPPENED TO QUERY IT. Ask early and a stale process reports the sha it actually started on, looking honest. Never ask until after a commit lands, and the same stale process reports a HEAD IT NEVER RAN — because the first call happens after the repo moved. The observer changes the answer. OBSERVED LIVE: sidecar pid 35300 started 13:40:05 with HEAD d37ca06; I queried /api/health at 13:40; the merge moved HEAD to 1e4af86 at 14:08; the process still reported d37ca06 afterwards. Had I not queried before the merge, it would have reported 1e4af86 for a process that predated it. THE CHECK THAT CANNOT BE FOOLED, unchanged and now better justified: PROCESS START TIME vs dist/index.js MTIME. A start time is evidence; a version string is a self-report, and this one is a self-report whose value was fixed by an earlier act of asking. TC's framing on the same day: 'a version string is a self-report, a start time is evidence.' CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: start-time-vs-dist-mtime proves the process started after the build. It does NOT prove dist was built from HEAD — an uncommitted or stale build satisfies it. For that, check dist mtime against the source files' mtimes, or rebuild before cycling, which is the habit worth having anyway.

A GET SILENTLY MIGRATED THE LIVE DATA DIRECTORY (2026-08-25, my error, repaired). I called GET /api/retired?characterId=professor_mari. 'professor_mari' is an IDENTITY KEY, not a character card id. That endpoint calls resolveIdentity(), which for an unrecognised id MINTS A NEW KEY AND MIGRATES THE EXISTING DATA DIR onto it: '[identity] migrated data dir: professor_mari -> professor_mari_2'. The whole store (7,050 beats, 8,417 hot entries, 425 cold, 6,916 char-topics, 1,382 user-topics, 551 threads) moved out from under its key, a fresh empty scope took its place, and live capture wrote one real turn into the empty one before I noticed. Repaired in full via scripts/repair-professor-mari-identity.mjs: both scopes backed up first, the one real turn folded back in, bogus map entry removed, directory renamed back. Verified FILE BY FILE against the backup — zero missing, no duplicate index rows. THE LESSONS, in order of how much they cost. (1) THE HAZARD WAS ALREADY IN MY OWN MEMORY FILE and I walked into it anyway: demo-test-sidecar-rule-learned-the-hard-way says verbatim 'resolveIdentity() would CREATE map entries and migrate data dirs for unknown IDs'. Knowing a danger is not the same as checking for it at the moment you act. Before passing an identifier to an unfamiliar endpoint, ask which KIND of identifier it wants — this store has three card ids mapping to professor_mari, so key-vs-card-id is load-bearing and invisible. (2) A READ THAT WRITES IS THE TRAP, not the bad argument. The request returned 200 with a plausible EMPTY result and no warning; the only evidence was two log lines nobody was reading. I found it thirteen minutes later, by accident, because an unrelated query returned 0 rows. Filed as a P1 with rung-2 as the shipping fix: resolveIdentity needs a READ-ONLY mode that 404s instead of minting, and an id that already exists as an identity key must never be treated as an unknown card id. (3) I ONLY CAUGHT IT BECAUSE I VERIFIED AGAINST THE STORE RATHER THAN THE TOOL'S OWN REPORT. The endpoint said 200; the count said 0; the file was gone. Checking the substrate rather than the response is what turned a silent corruption into a nineteen-minute incident. (4) STOPPING THE SIDECAR BEFORE A REPAIR IS NOT OPTIONAL — the watchdog relaunches in ~10s, so a multi-step repair must be scripted and executed as one shot, not typed interactively.
