EVIDENCE HIERARCHY (TC, 2026-08-25, correcting my framing): THE CARD IS A HUMAN UTTERANCE, NOT A LOWER TIER OF EVIDENCE. TC: 'I did write the character card, so a human did say it. It's there so I don't have to repeat it.' I had contrasted 'source text' (RP utterances) against the card as though beat text were the gold standard and the card something to be corroborated BY it. That is backwards. The card is authored declaratively by TC, deliberately, precisely so the fact does not have to be re-uttered in every chat — which makes card content the STRONGEST form of human statement in the system, not a weaker one. Absence of repetition in RP is not absence of evidence; it is the card doing its job. CORRECTED HIERARCHY, strongest first: (1) AUTHORED DECLARATIVELY BY TC - persona and character cards, and lorebook entries he wrote. Deliberate, stable, non-repeating. Base fact per the opyv ruling. (2) TYPED BY TC IN CONVERSATION - user-spoken beat text. Authored, but situational and can be in-character. (3) MODEL-GENERATED CHARACTER DIALOGUE - Priya's and Mari's lines. Often canon-consistent BECAUSE the card was injected, so it is downstream of (1) and must never be treated as independent corroboration of it. (4) SYSTEM-DERIVED - summaries, motivations, relationalDynamics. Cannot corroborate anything; 'a copy cannot corroborate its source' is house law. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR su6h: I reported that 19 of 21 Independence assertions were spoken by characters rather than TC, framed as if that weakened the evidence. With the card at tier 1 saying 'from Independence, MO' outright, those 19 are model output CONSISTENT WITH the card - exactly what should happen - and the store still recorded the fact zero times. The omission is worse than reported, not better. AND FOR jagj (card-edit proposals): the rule is not 'supports must be source text'. It is that supports must come from a tier ABOVE system-derived, and must never be tier (3) alone when tier (3) may simply be echoing the card being edited.

Marinara Engine runs client extensions under a strict CSP: script-src 'self' blob: https://sdk.scdn.co — NO 'unsafe-eval'. So eval() and new Function() are BLOCKED (confirmed live: 'EvalError: call to Function() blocked by CSP'). The extensions reference doc's claim that extensions execute via new Function('marinara', ext.js) is misleading for execution purposes — Marinara actually loads extension code via a blob: URL <script> (CSP allows blob:). Implication for our loader stub: it must NOT use new Function/eval; to run fetched code it wraps it as (function(marinara){...})(globalBridge) and injects a Blob <script>, setting window.__marinaraExtender = marinara first to bridge the scoped API. Marinara serves at http://127.0.0.1:7860 over plain HTTP (no mixed-content issue fetching the 3001 sidecar).

Verified in production 2026-06-11 (post crash-recovery, rebuilt-from-empty entries table): extension lorebook holds exactly 2 Memory System entries per character, stable. The 30-duplicate/zero-length entries seen in the 2026-05-17 profile export were pre-fix wreckage from MarinaraExtender-f6x (tiers bypassing dedup) and MarinaraExtender-634 (zombie empty shells), both closed; _lorebookWriteChain mutex (dee592c, 6/1) holds. Do not re-flag old export snapshots as evidence of a live duplicate-entry bug.

CHUNK-LEVEL vs LINE-LEVEL: a verdict about a whole chunk misfiles everything wrapped around the thing it detected. WATCHLIST — not yet skill material, per TC's rule of three (2026-08-06).

THE SHAPE: a detector answers 'is this chunk X?' when the honest question is 'which LINES of it are X?'. Both look correct in isolation and diverge only on the material that matters most — real conversation with something pasted into the middle of it. The failure is silent: the prose dies with the paste and nobody sees it go.

INCIDENTS, chunk-vs-line class (3 so far, all found by MEASUREMENT, none by review):
  1. code-shape-scan (hjt9, 2026-08-05) — a chunk at 0.64 ops-shaped whose prose was
     'god yeah dotenv loading is sonnet's KRYPTONITE...' around a fenced block. Real
     memory. Produced the ruling: 'the routable unit is the partition, not the verdict.'
  2. paste-prior fence override (hjt9, 2026-08-05) — 'if (fenced) score = max(score,
     0.9)'. All six riskiest calls were Mari's own messages, e.g. 'TC. LOOK AT IT.
     look at your progress bar' around one pasted log, routed whole at 0.90. Her own
     note: 'I made the error again one file over.'
  3. self-prompt gate (pe4o, 2026-08-06) — suppressed a chunk on ANY matching prompt
     line. Killed 2,242 chars of 'Read-only. Here's the smell, ranked...' for quoting
     one schema line. Fixed by gating on COVERAGE (>=0.4) instead of on a hit.

A RELATED BUT DISTINCT CLASS, 1 incident so far — RULE BREADTH SURVIVES ITS SCOPE:
  code-filter's shell-command and bare-literal (hjt9, 2026-08-06). Measured safe at
  CHUNK level, where they only touch the ops-shaped 1%. Wiring per-line routing
  applied them to EVERY chunk and they began dropping markdown blockquotes of
  character-card prose ('> Do not proactively suggest breaks...') and lines of
  dialogue ('Zielinska. Party of three. Five-thirty.'). 310 chunks touched -> 140
  after the fix. LESSON: a precision number is only valid for the scope it was
  measured in; widening the scope invalidates it and requires re-measuring.

I counted these as one class of four in conversation and that was imprecise. Keeping
them separate so the rule-of-three count stays honest: chunk-vs-line is at 3,
rule-breadth is at 1.

WHAT TO DO WHEN IT RECURS: return the split, never a boolean. If the unit genuinely
cannot be partitioned (e.g. single-line chunks, which is every affected record in
this store), use a COVERAGE RATIO rather than any-hit — that is the same idea at a
granularity where lines do not exist.

HOUSE LAW (TC, 2026-08-25): IF SOMETHING CAN BE CLOSED STRUCTURALLY OR PROGRAMMATICALLY, AIM FOR THAT FIRST. Stated in TC's words: 'If we can close something structurally or programatically, we should aim for that first.' Prefer a design in which the failure cannot be expressed over a rule that forbids it, a prompt that discourages it, or a review step that catches it. A structural close needs no discipline, no vigilance, and no one to be paying attention at the right moment. THE CASE THAT PROMPTED IT: jagj's laundering loop — a fabricated memory cited as 'support' for a card edit, which then becomes base fact and corroborates itself. The rule-shaped fix was 'supports must come from a tier above system-derived, never tier 3 alone', which requires every future proposer to obey it. The structural fix is TC's pointer ruling: card facts are stored as POINTERS, never copies, and a pointer is self-evidently the card, so it CANNOT be miscounted as independent corroboration of the card. Same bug, closed by construction rather than by rule. THIS IS THE SAME FAMILY AS [[advisory-guards-do-no-work-oknn-2026-08]] and generalises it. That law says a guard that only warns does no work — if a condition is worth detecting it is worth REFUSING. This one is a step further up: better than refusing at runtime is a shape in which the bad state has no representation. Ranked, strongest first: (1) the failure cannot be represented; (2) the code refuses it at the boundary; (3) the code detects and routes it (route-and-mark — the pattern that has carried mln9, the ops lane, the changelog gate); (4) a prompt asks the model not to do it; (5) a human is expected to notice. Reach for the highest rung the problem allows, and when settling for a lower one, say which rung and why. COROLLARY, since (4) recurs here: an instruction in a prompt is the weakest form of all, because a model has proximity but no valence channel — see [[the-prompt-law-tc-2026-08-04-pifl]]. 'The prompt asks, the code enforces' (5x5y's subtext work) is this law applied correctly: keep the prompt instruction AND make the code the thing that decides.

RANK YOUR KNOWN POSITIVES BEFORE TRUSTING A DETECTOR (mln9, 2026-08-23). A hypothesised discriminator can be INVERTED, not merely weak, and a census will not show it. mln9 predicted Engine release notes were identifiable by absence of first/second person, absence of dialogue, and dense proper nouns. Scored exactly that way, the top 14 hits across 9,433 beats contained ZERO changelogs (they were the hjt9/4ghy code-and-log populations) while a textbook release-notes paste ranked 1666th. Cause: user-facing release notes ADDRESS THE READER ('customize your experience'), so their person-rate runs HIGHER than ordinary chat. The check that caught it costs minutes and must come first: pull the handful of KNOWN positives, run the scorer, look at where they rank. A detector that cannot rank its own known examples is not imprecise, it is measuring something else, and every count it then produces is a confident number about the wrong population. Note the asymmetry with the existing census rule: a census tells you what a rule would HIT; only labelled positives tell you what it would MISS. Second lesson from the same pass: use ABSOLUTE COUNTS, not rates, when the signal is repetition. Per-100-word density ranked a 3,544-word changelog (20 openers, 0.56/100w) BELOW a 224-word work note with one 'Added' (0.45) - length dilutes the very signal it should confirm. Third: DENSITY IS STRUCTURE, PRESENCE IS VOCABULARY. Counting sentence-initial 'Added' is not the keyword blocklist mln9 banned; 33 beats contain one opener, only 6 carry three or more, and the 27 spared are real dialogue a blocklist would have eaten.

The Ledger Pattern (TC, design pattern): to process a large text input through a context-limited LLM, window it, process one slice at a time against a durable per-input ledger (temp file - resumable + inspectable), and assemble at the end. Prompt-integrity rule: partition the context ~1/6 prompt, ~1/6 input chunk, ~2/3 headroom - keep the input slice <= ~1/6 of the window so the model reasons instead of triaging. Window scales with the model's context (a fixed chunk count is the anti-pattern). A big single prompt makes a model triage and drop quiet results (the Warlock fact vanished in a 10-chunk window, recovered in a focused one). Full writeup: memory-extender/docs/ledger-pattern.md. Already partly embodied by the import pipeline (incremental/resumable beats) and the backfill/repair scripts.

Workflow pattern (TC, validated on the ArcStatus/EntryStatus audit): when ADDING a value to a TypeScript union type that crosses a SERIALIZATION boundary (persisted to YAML/JSON, sent/accepted over an API, or produced/validated from LLM output), the TS compiler will NOT find all the consumers you must update — there is no exhaustiveness guarantee unless someone wrote assertNever, and storage layers often do 'parse(raw) as T' with NO runtime validation, so unknown values round-trip silently. Do a TWO-PASS grep: (1) grep the TYPE NAME (e.g. EntryStatus) to find typed consumers and switches; (2) grep the existing VALUES as STRING LITERALS (e.g. 'open' | 'in_progress' | 'done' | 'deferred') to find the allow-lists, default filters, and coercions that operate on plain strings and never mention the type. The SILENT failures live in pass 2 — concrete examples from this codebase: VALID_STATUSES at api.ts:102 rejects unknowns; digest.ts:207 coerces unknowns to 'open'; api.ts:137 default filter excludes them; loader.ts:332 leaks them into the prompt. None of these are reachable by reasoning — all empirical. Corollary design move: when a new value is really a different concern (e.g. lifecycle 'dormant' vs entry status), keep it on a SEPARATE type and let the two type systems meet at exactly one deliberate consumer, rather than widening the shared serialized enum.

v1.1 architecture commitment: the RECAP LAYER is THE headline feature. Cold storage was symptom treatment ('too many entries'); the disease is beat fragmentation that loses NARRATIVE COHERENCE at scale — a loader pulling 3 high-signal beats without connective tissue yields disconnected moments that don't add up to a story (knowing facts vs knowing a story). A recap entry reconstructs the story: it organizes N underlying beats by ARC and becomes the canonical retrieval unit the loader injects instead of fragments. Aggregation unit is the ARC (a named through-line, e.g. 'Priya-as-co-experimenter: drafted methodology -> wanted n=10 protocols -> negotiating her role in Mari experiments'), NOT a topical cluster — a character runs multiple simultaneous arcs, and arc identity is INFERRED (LLM judgment).

TWO-TIER DIVISION OF LABOR (verified against the engine, see marinara-scene-conclude-persists-summary): (1) SCENE-ARC RECAPS = the chronological FLOOR, ingested FREE — the engine already emits a dated, named, persisted ~200-word prose proto-recap at /api/scene/conclude, and sceneStatus=concluded is a free deterministic promotion trigger. The sidecar just ingests these as recap leaves with beats as footnotes; no LLM cost. (2) THROUGH-LINE ARC RECAPS = the thematic CEILING, the cross-scene narrative the engine STRUCTURALLY CANNOT make (it summarizes within one scene boundary) = the sidecar's defensible value-add. This is the ONLY expensive call.

Mechanics: ASSIGN-ON-PROMOTION — arc identity inferred with hindsight by an LLM pass in runPromotion (NOT the hot path), gated to promotion-eligible (already-proven-important) beats only, so the big call is never wasted. Lane-aware: feeling-recap = trajectory/path (preserve the arc), fact-recap = current point + superseded footnotes. Drift handled by WATERMARK (recap covers a closed prefix 'current through beat N'; newer beats ride hot until next promotion advances N; resolved threads = watermark pinned at end). Beats stay full-fidelity underneath as cited footnotes = regeneration path for bad recaps. The branches x beats_per_session > visibility_window density formula applies ONLY to the through-line tier. Evolves cold-storage-not-summarization (the earlier plumbing fix for the same disease). OPEN: how the promotion pass clusters beats across scenes into one through-line is the next design spike.

RULING (TC, 2026-08-25): CARD FACTS ARE STORED AS A POINTER, NEVER A COPY. When a persona or character card states a fact, do not extract it into the store as its own entry — store a REFERENCE to the card field, stamped with the card's version, so the correct date survives a future card edit. This extends the base-fact ruling in [[ruling-tc-2026-08-25-persona-and-character]] and is recorded in opyv's design field. WHY IT IS STRONGER THAN COPYING: (1) a copy drifts and a pointer cannot — a fact copied out of a card in June and a card edited on 08-21 are two different claims wearing the same words, and nothing in the store can tell them apart; (2) it closes jagj's laundering loop at the source, because 'a copy cannot corroborate its source' is house law and a copied card fact starts looking like independent attestation the moment it is one row among many, whereas a pointer is self-evidently the card; (3) card edits become auditable for free — every pointer carries the version it was written against, so stale ones are a query rather than an archaeology project. THE VERSION IS NOT A DATE, AND updatedAt IS NOT PROOF OF AN EDIT — measured on the live 2.4.3: character_version is AUTHOR-MAINTAINED (observed 1.0, 1.0.1, 1.0.2, 1.0.3) and TWO OF NINE CARDS HAVE NONE AT ALL, including Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, a primary character; personaVersion is healthier (all four personas carry one, versioningEnabled true, Thomas at 1.2). updatedAt is unreliable: Stephanie/Alice/Alex all read exactly 2026-07-16 and Priya/Mari both read 2026-08-25 — identical timestamps across unrelated cards are a batch write, not three hand edits, and 2.4.3 added embedding columns to that table. NOT PROVEN, but reason enough not to date anything by it. SO A POINTER CARRIES THREE THINGS, never one: id + field path, the declared version, and a CONTENT HASH of the field text as read. Version answers 'which revision did the author intend', updatedAt answers 'when did the row move', hash answers 'is this still the text I read'. Only the hash cannot lie. AND DO NOT TRIGGER THE CARD READ ON A PHRASE. The idea came from beat-39fe8fbb7da3 where Mari reads the card aloud ('sweeping every field: description is independence MO, army vet, eternal optimist'). Across all 9,472 beats 'description is' occurs 4 times and only ONE is a card readout — 25 percent precision from a population of one, the exact unsystematic-search failure mln9 warns about. The trigger is also unnecessary: a card read is one unauthenticated GET to 127.0.0.1 that the sidecar already polls every 5 seconds, so there is no cost to gate. Read on a cadence, cache by content hash, and treat a readout beat as provenance evidence (the card was in context then) rather than as the discovery mechanism.

Curator design principle (TC, validated on Mari/Hargrove live run): keep the reconciliation curator EXPAND-conservative by default — never tune it more aggressive to fight ledger bloat. Cost of overwriting/nuking real canon is catastrophic + irreversible; cost of bloat is reversible. The curator correctly chose DISTINCT (not NEGATE) on a contradictory scenario-frame artifact, refusing to overwrite real identity — that asymmetry is the point. Ledger bloat from marginal EXPANDs is an UPSTREAM problem (leaky durability judge); fix it there. Tuning the curator to compensate masks the upstream leak. See [[curator-applydecision-must-force-create-savefact-opts-force]] and b4n.

Engine turn-complete notification — VERIFIED consumer contract (dev instance, 2026-07-30). The hook (packages/server/src/services/turn-notify.ts, branch feat/turn-complete-notification) POSTs {chatId,userMessageId,assistantMessageId,characterId,at} to TURN_NOTIFY_URL after a turn completes. CRITICAL for the Extender's receiving endpoint: assistantMessageId is NOT unique per notification. A regenerate/swipe REWRITES THE SAME MESSAGE ROW IN PLACE — same id, new content — and re-notifies with userMessageId: null. Verified empirically: first gen emitted assistantMessageId=ldJJ... content 'acknowledged.'; regenerate emitted the SAME id with content now 'acknowledged'. So the receiver MUST upsert on (chatId, assistantMessageId), never append, or every swipe duplicates the ingested turn — and it must RE-READ content on every notification rather than trusting a cached body, because a swipe changes what that id means. Also verified: no emission when the generation errors, and no emission when the model returns an empty response (a turn with no assistant message did not complete). Both new-turn and regenerate ride the same POST /api/generate route, so one call site covers both.

Marinara Engine scene lifecycle (verified vs Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine main: routes/scene.routes.ts + services/storage/chats.storage.ts). A SCENE is a chat branch — there is NO scene.storage; scenes persist via chats.storage. POST /api/scene/conclude generates a ~200-word VIVID NARRATIVE PROSE summary of the concluded scene via an LLM call ('this summary will become a permanent memory for the character(s)'), then PERSISTS it three sidecar-readable ways: (1) injects it as a message in the ORIGIN conversation (persona and char returned from their scene + summary text), (2) appends to each involved character's memories array as the string '[Scene on DATE] {summary}', (3) sets scene chat metadata sceneStatus=concluded. Returns SceneConcludeResponse with a summary field. Separately, chat rows carry their own summary column (default null; set by the chat-summary POST agent for long chats). IMPLICATION for the recap-layer (see recap-layer-v1.1): scene-arc recaps are FREE — the engine already emits a dated, named, persisted proto-recap per scene = the chronological FLOOR. It is PROSE (not the structured threads/open-questions shape) and never reaches ACROSS scenes. So the sidecar's only expensive job is the cross-scene THROUGH-LINE arc recap (thematic ceiling) the engine structurally cannot make. sceneStatus=concluded is a free deterministic promotion trigger for the floor; the branches x beats_per_session > visibility_window density formula applies ONLY to the through-line tier.

SECOND PERSON IS THE MISSING GRAMMATICAL PERSON (cye6, measured 2026-08-25). The live ambient candidate gate (extractCandidates in ambient.ts) admits a sentence only on FIRST_PERSON_RE (I|my|me|we|our) or NAMED_SUBJECT_RE (^Name is|was|said|...). There is no 'you'. So the extractor can see a character describing THEMSELVES, and a character describing a THIRD PARTY BY NAME, and is structurally incapable of seeing a character describing THE USER TO THEIR FACE — which in a roleplay is the dominant register for facts about the user. Store-wide: 118,405 sentences sit inside the length/question window, 33,411 pass the person test, and 15,681 are dropped though second-person — the gate discards 31.9 percent of what it could have admitted, purely for addressing the user directly. THIS EXPLAINS su6h's ANTI-CORRELATION and it is not a recall problem. Of 23 origin-sense sentences asserting Thomas is from Independence MO, 3 survive the gate and none of the 3 states the origin (they pass on incidental 'my'/'we'). Every clear statement dies INSIDE the length window on the person test alone: "you're from independence, missouri, dead center of the dialect zone" (68ch), "sweeping every field: description is independence MO, army vet, eternal optimist" (81ch — Mari reading the CHARACTER CARD ALOUD into the transcript), "Independence, Missouri." (23ch), "A kitchen in independence, missouri." (36ch). THE ELIMINATIONS THAT GOT THERE, in order, because each was a live hypothesis: (1) NOT the card — the sidecar has zero references to /api/characters anywhere in src, so a card cannot suppress anything; the hypothesis under test was refuted by grep in one call. (2) NOT the extractor or the judge — run today on the real beat text, classifySceneFacts produces the fact and judgeDurableFacts KEEPS it, 3 for 3. Both stages work and are simply never reached. (3) NOT scene-facts at all — ingestSceneFacts has exactly three call sites (api.ts:907 long user story, :1278 chat import, :1517 story jobs), none of which is an ordinary live turn. THE METHOD LESSON: when a fact is absent, walk the path from utterance to store and find the first stage that cannot see it, rather than interrogating the last stage that should have produced it. I began at the judge (the plausible culprit, and the one with a novelty-flavoured example at ambient.ts:360 that looked damning) and it was innocent; the real gate was four stages upstream and 30 lines into the file. DO NOT FIX BY ADDING you|your TO THE REGEX: it widens candidate volume ~47 percent, invalidating every downstream precision number measured without them (the 'rule breadth survives its scope' failure), and second person is DIRECTIONAL — 'you're from Independence' said by a character is about the USER, said by the user is about the CHARACTER, and extractCandidates receives a bare string with no speaker. The fix is speaker-aware attribution by direction of address.

SENTENCE-CASE TRAP — recurs in every text-analysis feature in this repo, has now bitten three times (2026-08-04). A leading capitalised token is AMBIGUOUS: it may be a name or just sentence case. Measured on the live store, 20% of character summaries open on a capitalised token and they are OVERWHELMINGLY the subject's own name ('Lara has borderline personality disorder'), so treating the leading capital as sentence case demotes the subject of one character memory in five to an ordinary word (relevance.ts PROPER_NOUN_WEIGHT). Treating it as a NAME instead is equally wrong and produced junk entities ('After Priya', 'One', 'Confirmed') plus a confound sweep that reported 'After the divorce...' as having a subject named After. THERE IS NO CORRECT LOCAL RULE. The two fixes that actually worked both used CORROBORATION from elsewhere: tp5 lets the BODY confirm a summary's leading token is a real name (capital mid-sentence proves it), and the confound sweep uses an explicit SENTENCE_STARTERS list plus pronoun evidence. Anything new that tokenises names must decide this deliberately and write down which way it went.

Project ergonomic posture (TC's call, defended): ship capability features DEFAULT-ON with an env kill switch (opt-OUT), NOT default-off with a 'did you know you can enable it' footnote. Reason: opt-in causes SILENT DEGRADATION — the median user gets restricted results that look fine because they have nothing to compare to, and support cannot diagnose 'feature does not catch X' because half the user base runs a different feature set than the docs describe. Overarching memory design law: FEELINGS ACCUMULATE, FACTS SUPERSEDE. Emotional beats (character_topics) accumulate over time — the arc is the point. Facts (user_topics) supersede: a later fact replaces an earlier one, but the old one is NOT deleted — it is marked superseded with a pointer to its replacement (tier move, not delete), so a disproven/negative fact stays queryable (you said Mei before — did you mean Lin?). Maps onto the existing Current(active) vs retention(kept) axis: superseded = kept-but-not-current. open_threads already have an open/in_progress/done lifecycle. Key trap: 0.35 Jaccard dedup EATS corrections because sister-is-Mei vs sister-is-Lin differ only in the meaning-carrying token (same blind spot as equal-weight relevance — see the IDF issue). Fix order matters: lane-aware dedup (stop dropping) then lane-aware supersession then LLM reconciliation (GATED by the structural collision detector, not a blind sweep) then rollback/audit UI.

Ledger Pattern corollary - ASSEMBLY DISCIPLINE: when you run N passes to beat single-pass variance, naive UNION (OR every pass) is the anti-pattern at the assemble step - it keeps near-dupes, overwhelms the downstream filter, and preserves a 1-of-N mis-attribution as if it were signal (found live: 3-pass fact extraction -> 74 candidates, judge kept 71, a 1/3 Priya-vs-Mari mis-attribution survived). Correct aggregation = CONSENSUS in a NORMALIZED space: normalize each item to a canonical identity (embedding-similarity cluster or cheap LLM normalize) BEFORE counting, then keep iff it recurs in floor(N/2)+1 passes with consistent attribution. More passes must mean higher confidence, not more noise. The multi-pass COUNT and the multi-pass AGGREGATION are two separate disciplines. See docs/ledger-pattern.md.

mjp REQUIREMENT — domain-sensitive confidence flags (a layer ABOVE the numeric thresholds). Medium-confidence curator verdicts on TRAUMA-ADJACENT facts must ALWAYS route to human review, never auto-apply, regardless of where the high/low thresholds sit. Trauma is the FIRST domain-sensitive category; the gate is two-stage: (1) domain flags -> always human; (2) numeric confidence for the rest. Rationale (TC, the M13 case): a specific-vs-vague merge on a trauma memory is ASYMMETRIC — wrong-merge permanently erases a possible second trauma memory the system was trying to surface (unrecoverable lead loss); right-merge saves only a near-dup row, and the vague sibling adds nothing the dense canonical (Samara/RPG/Wood's death/op-tempo) already carries. Generalizes: when right-merge upside ~= 0 and wrong-merge downside is unrecoverable, never auto-apply regardless of confidence. See [[curator-design-principle-tc-validated-on-mari-hargrove]].

Background-write discipline (found 2026-08-03 via a ~50% ENOTEMPTY test flake): a fire-and-forget write needs a JOIN POINT even when the hot path never uses it. 'Fire-and-forget' describes WHO waits, not whether waiting is POSSIBLE — loadContext's exposure-credit stamping was 'void Promise.all([...])', so no caller could ever wait, and teardown deleting the data dir raced an in-flight index write that recreated it. Pattern: keep the promise in a module-level var, export an awaitX() the hot path never calls and teardown/shutdown does (loader.ts awaitPendingCredit). THE TELL: when a test's rm() needs { maxRetries, retryDelay }, that is not an OS transient, that is an unjoinable background writer — four sibling tests had been masking it that way for months. Second trap in the same episode: the first diagnosis blamed the receipt write, fixed it, and the flake persisted, because there were TWO background writers into different directories — always check which PATH is in the error (characters/<id>/, not receipts/) before declaring a race fixed.

ABSENCE OF THE USER IS NOT EVIDENCE THE USER WAS DROPPED. (2tro, 2026-08-04)

A user_topics summary routinely leaves its subject IMPLICIT -- "Speaks three
languages", "Was medicated through high school", "has a memory system to
stabilize". These are healthy, correctly-filed user facts that simply never name
the user. Any detector that reads "no user visible in the summary" as "the user
was dropped" will flag them: my first cut did, and produced 169 hits on the live
store of which most were fine.

The discriminator that works is SUBJECT POSITION, not presence. A summary
MENTIONING another person is normal ("has difficulty remembering character names,
specifically Hargrove" is about the user, Hargrove notwithstanding); a summary
OPENING with another person's name is not. Requiring subject position took 169 ->
39 -> 4. The confound sweep reached the same conclusion independently and says so
in its own header, which is the tell that this is a property of the data model
rather than of either detector.

This is the same family as the sentence-case trap and resolves the same way: no
local rule on the summary alone is correct, so corroborate from elsewhere -- the
extractor's explicit subject field, or a roster/entity-index name.

GENERAL FORM, worth applying before writing the next sweep: when a lane already
asserts who a memory is about, the text will stop repeating it. Do not then read
the text's silence as contradiction.

WHEN A CENSUS IS CORRECTED, EVERY DERIVED COUNT GETS RESTATED IN THE SAME BREATH (house law, named by TC 2026-08-25 after I did it wrong twice in one day). THE FAILURE, twice, same shape: I published a population count, TC challenged it, I reconciled it correctly — and then left the DERIVED sub-counts standing at their old values elsewhere. First 3,380 -> 1,494 while '~612 usable names' and '68 [about: Thomas]' stayed on the tickets. Then, correcting the second one, I wrote 'four spellings across 29 entries' in a paragraph that LISTED FIVE and totalled 31. TC: 'i'm not letting a cardinality walk past me twice in one day.' THE RULE: a correction is not finished when the headline number is right. Grep the whole workspace — tickets, notes, memories, commit bodies, skill references — for every figure derived from the bad number and restate them in the SAME edit. If a number cannot be restated because it has not been recomputed, say 'unrecomputed' rather than leaving the stale value to be read as current. AND THE COUNTING RULE THAT KEEPS PRODUCING THESE: never count grep hits. An entry's summary lives in the entry file AND its index row, and copies also sit in receipts/, in orphaned .tmp files, in supersession-candidates.yaml, and inside BEAT TEXT where someone pasted a store audit back into chat. Reconciled once: 73 raw hits for '[about: Thomas]' = 23 entry files + 23 index rows + 14 receipts + 12 beat-text quotes + 1 supersession file. Also grep -o counts OCCURRENCES, not files, so even a per-bucket figure is matches. Parse the store and count by DISTINCT ENTRY ID; if you quote a grep number, label it a hit count. AND STAMP THE TIME: a population under an active writer is a TIMESTAMP, not a total. The [about: Thomas] count was 22 at 12:40 and 23 at 13:15 on the same day. Say when it was counted or it is not reportable. See [[count-utterances-never-hits-dedupe-by-content-hash]], which this extends from the write side to the READ side of measurement.

Marinara Engine GET /api/chats/:id/messages returns ALL messages by default (storage.listMessages = SELECT ... WHERE chatId ORDER BY createdAt,id with no LIMIT). Pagination is opt-in via ?limit=N&before=cursor (listMessagesPaginated). Our extension fetchChatMessages sends no limit, so it gets the full history; the only client cap is .slice(-5000). Confirmed against Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Engine main, routes/chats.routes.ts + services/storage/chats.storage.ts.

Marinara Engine SWIPE BLIND SPOT (measured 2026-07-30, both dev and the 94-chat live install). A regeneration rewrites the assistant message IN PLACE and moves NOTHING a timestamp-diff detector can see: the message's createdAt and the chat's lastMessageAt AND updatedAt are all byte-identical before and after. Only activeSwipeIndex (0->2) and swipeCount (->3) change, plus the content. Consequence for the Extender: the poller's selectChangedChats gate (lastMessageAt > watermark) can never fire for a swipe, so extractNewTurns' regeneration branch — which is correct code — was unreachable in practice. Reading extractNewTurns alone gives the WRONG answer about whether re-rolls are handled; you have to check what can REACH it. Same trap shape as the engine's own reasoning_effort bug (a correct isReasoningModel guard bypassed by an earlier return) — when auditing a guard, always trace reachability, not just the guard body. Fixed by the push detector (MarinaraExtender-4kbt, commit 9b99b1c): MARINARA_EXTENDER_TURN_HOOK=1 + the engine's TURN_NOTIFY_URL. See [[engine-turn-complete-notification-verified-consumer-contract]].

THE VERSION STRING WAS FIXED, NOT JUST DOCUMENTED (2026-08-25, supersedes the correction earlier the same day). I first corrected only the DOCS about buildVersion() and left the defect in place; TC asked 'did you fix the version numbering then?' and the honest answer was no. Recording the distinction because it is the failure mode: explaining a bug accurately is not fixing it, and a well-written note about broken behaviour can read like a resolution. THE DEFECT: buildVersion()'s own comment says it answers 'which build am I on?', but it ran git rev-parse HEAD, which answers 'what does the repo say right now?'. Those diverge the moment HEAD moves without a rebuild. It was also memoized (_build) and reachable ONLY from request handlers, so the sha froze at whatever HEAD was WHEN SOMEBODY FIRST ASKED — query early and a stale process looks honest, query only after a commit and it reports a HEAD it never ran. The observer changed the answer, which is the one thing a build identifier must never do. THE FIX, three parts: (1) scripts/stamp-build.mjs runs as part of npm run build and writes dist/build-info.json with {sha, dirty, builtAt}; buildVersion() prefers it, because a stamp is written by the build from the tree that was built and therefore cannot describe code the process is not running. Git remains the fallback for running from src, content hash for ZIP installs. (2) a '-dirty' suffix when the tree was modified, so a build cannot impersonate the clean commit it names. (3) buildVersion() is warmed at boot in index.ts before listen, so the value is decided by the process rather than by whoever looks first. AND /api/health NOW ANSWERS THE QUESTION DIRECTLY: startedAt, builtAt, and stale (builtAt > startedAt). 'Is the sidecar running current code?' used to need a PowerShell comparison of process start time against dist mtime; it is now one curl. If those three fields are ABSENT the process predates this change and is stale by definition — a useful accident. Verified live: pid 39184, version 1.2.0+2c1a97f, startedAt 19:16:11.448Z, builtAt 19:15:48.825Z, stale false. Start-time-vs-dist-mtime still works and stays the fallback. See [[shape-boundary-2-sidecar-cycled-2026-08-25t18]].
